- Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu says that Israel has struck bridges and railways in Iran allegedly used by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)] [src: (Reuters via The Standard)]
- U.S. and Israeli warplanes strike Iranian military targets on Kharg Island that results in several massive explosions. [src: (Metro)] [src: (NBC News)]
- At least five people are killed after a rocket fired from Kuwait landed in Basra, southern Iraq. [src: (Shafaq)]
- 2026 Lebanon war
- Three people are killed and several are injured by an Israeli airstrike in Maarakah, Tyre District, Lebanon. [src: (Daily Sabah)]
- One person is killed by an Israeli drone strike in Deir ez-Zahrani, Nabatieh District, Lebanon. [src: (Daily Sabah)]
- One person is killed by an Israeli strike in Zebdin, Nabatieh District, Lebanon. [src: (Daily Sabah)]
- The Israeli military says that 36 soldiers were injured over the past two days, bringing the total casualties to 411. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Israel deploys the 98th Division to southern Lebanon, raising the force there to five divisions. [src: (AA)] 
- 2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war
- The Afghan foreign ministry says that talks between the Taliban–led government of Afghanistan and Pakistan in Ürümqi, China, to end the conflict have been "useful". [src: (ABC News)]
- 2026 attack on Israeli consulate in Istanbul
- One gunman is killed, while two other perpetrators and two policemen are injured in a shootout outside of the Israeli consulate in Istanbul, Turkey. The two injured perpetrators have been captured and detained by police. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Nigerian bandit conflict
- Armed attackers kill at least 50 people in a village in Shiroro, Niger State, Nigeria, including local hunters, militia members, and civilians. [src: (AFP via Macau Business)]
Arts and culture
- Destruction of cultural heritage sites during the 2026 Iran war
- The semi-official Mehr News Agency reports that a suspected Israeli–U.S. missile struck the Rafi'-Nia synagogue in central Tehran. [src: (Dawn)]
- This year's Wireless Festival in London, England, is cancelled and all tickets are refunded after its headliner, American rapper Kanye West, is banned from entering the United Kingdom by the Home Office on the grounds that "his presence would not be conducive to the public good" amid controversy over his past antisemitic comments on Jews and Adolf Hitler, and his association with neo-Nazis. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (CNN)]
Business and economy
- The Japanese House of Councillors enacts the country's largest state budget in history worth ¥122.3 trillion (€664 billion). [src: (Euronews)]
Disasters and accidents
- Mediterranean Sea migrant smuggling
- The International Organization for Migration reports that at least 990 deaths have been recorded in 2026 across the Mediterranean Sea, making it one of the deadliest starts to a year since 2014, with over 180 people feared dead or missing in the latest shipwrecks since 28 March. [src: (AFP via The Daily Star)]
- The death toll from a large fire at a petrochemical plant in Tatarstan, Russia, five days ago, rises to 12, including a firefighter. Dozens of others were injured. [src: (Reuters)]
- Three people are killed and another is reported missing after a scaffolding collapse at a steel plant in Kawasaki, Kanagawa Prefecture, Japan. [src: (The Japan Times)]
- A TGV train collides with a military lorry on a level crossing at Nœux-les-Mines, France. The train driver is killed and 27 people are wounded. [src: (Liverpool Echo)]
- The death toll from natural disasters, including heavy rain, storms and floods, rises to 188 in Afghanistan and Pakistan. [src: (AFP via The Daily Star)] [src: (Business Recorder)]
International relations
- Cuba–United States relations
- 2026 Cuban crisis
- Cuban president and First Secretary of the Communist Party Miguel Díaz-Canel warns the United States that his forces will wage a guerrilla warfare campaign if the U.S. military invades and occupies the country. [src: (CBS News)]
- Cross-strait relations
- At the invitation of paramount leader Xi Jinping, Kuomintang chairperson Cheng Li-wun begins the first visit to China by a Taiwanese opposition leader since 2016. [src: (AP)]
- Iraq–Kuwait relations
- Protestors storm the Kuwaiti consulate in Basra, Iraq, after a rocket attack launched from Kuwait killed three people in Basra. [src: (Türkiye Today)]
Law and crime
- Aftermath of the Afghanistan War
- War crimes in Afghanistan
- Australian Army veteran and Victoria Cross recipient Ben Roberts-Smith is arrested by police at Sydney Airport for alleged war crimes committed between 2009 and 2012 during his deployment to Afghanistan. [src: (Reuters)]
- Corruption in South Sudan
- South Sudan president Salva Kiir Mayardit sacks National Legislative Assembly speaker Jemma Nunu Kumba and her deputy Parmena Awerial Aluong after his ruling party backed a no-confidence vote accusing them of corruption and mismanagement. [src: (Pan African Visions)] [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- Protests against the 2026 Iran war
- Protests against the 2026 Iran war in the United States
- A protest is held outside the White House in Washington, D.C., U.S., after the ceasefire announcement, calling for President Trump's removal from office and accusing him of war crimes. [src: (India TV)]
- Iran calls on the population to form human chains around critical infrastructure such as power stations and bridges ahead of a U.S. deadline that threatens their destruction. [src: (The Hill)]
- Human chain protests are held across bridge and power plant structures in Iran to protest against Trump's threats against civilian infrastructure. [src: (The Telegraph)]
- Citizens in Ilam, Iran, form a human chain protest against Trump's threats against key infrastructure in the country. [src: (Away The Voice)]
- 2026 Vietnamese presidential election
- The National Assembly of Vietnam re-elects General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Tô Lâm as president for the 2026–2031 tenure, and Lê Minh Hưng as prime minister. [src: (Xinhua)] [src: (Viet Nam News)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 April 8
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi confirms the two-week ceasefire between Iran and the United States, which includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The ceasefire is ratified by the Supreme National Security Council (SNSC). [src: (Shafaq)] [src: (Khaleej Times)]
- The SNSC announces that negotiations between Iran and the U.S. will start on Friday in Islamabad, Pakistan, with the U.S. contingent to be led by vice president JD Vance alongside senior presidential adviser Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff. [src: (Axios)] [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and U.S. president Donald Trump both claim that the ceasefire does not include Lebanon, despite contrary statements from both Iran and Pakistan on their versions of the ceasefire agreement. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (BBC News)] [src: (The New York Times)]
- White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt states that Netanyahu and Trump will continue discussions on potentially including Lebanon in a ceasefire arrangement. [src: (AFP via Aaj News)]
- After the announcement, an Israeli military spokesperson states that Israel is still launching attacks on Iran. [src: (CNN)]
- Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian says the ceasefire with Israel and the U.S. has been violated as a result of the bombings of Iranian islands and Lebanon. Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf later echoes the remarks, citing the attacks as well as the "denial of Iran to enrich uranium." [src: (CNBC)] [src: (Forbes)] [src: (G1)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
- The Bahraini military intercepts six missiles and 31 drones. [src: (Yemen Online)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
- Kuwait's interior ministry reports fires at several oil facilities, power plants, and desalination plants after an Iranian drone attack. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar
- The Qatari military intercepts seven ballistic missiles and multiple drones. [src: (DPA via Yahoo News)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia
- Saudi Arabia's East–West Crude Oil Pipeline is hit in an Iranian attack. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
- The Emirati military intercepts 17 ballistic missiles and 35 drones. [src: (The National)]
- After the announcement of a ceasefire, Iran launches ballistic missiles at Bahrain, Israel, Kuwait, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates. [src: (CNBC News)] [src: (CNN)]
- Iranian agencies report explosions from the Lavan and Sirri islands of unknown origin. Iran accuses Kuwait and the UAE of the attacks and launches retaliatory attacks against those countries in response. [src: (Ynet)] [src: (Wanaen)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Thailand confirms the three crewmen on a vessel that was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz in March have died. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- MarineTraffic reports the first ships that have passed through the Strait of Hormuz since the ceasefire announcement, namely the Greek-owned bulk carrier NJ Earth and Liberia-flagged Daytona Beach. [src: (CNBC)] [src: (Euronews)]
- Iran closes Strait of Hormuz maritime traffic to oil tankers over Israeli attacks in Lebanon, claiming that Lebanon is included in the ceasefire. [src: (G1)] [src: (Forbes)]
- Bahrain, Iraq, and Syria reopen their airspace after weeks of closure. The Damascus International Airport and the Bahrain International Airport begin resuming flights. [src: (Khaleej Times)] [src: (BNA)] [src: (AA)]
- Hezbollah–Israel conflict
- 2026 Lebanon war
- 2026 Israeli Beirut strikes
- At least 254 people are killed and 1,165 others are injured in a wave of Israeli strikes on Lebanon, including in southern Lebanon, Beirut, and the Bekaa Valley. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (BBC News)]
- The IDF announces that its strikes in Lebanon are one part of a new operation called "Eternal Darkness". [src: (Ynet)]
- The Israeli military says that it has halted strikes against Iran, but state that they will continue fighting Hezbollah in Lebanon. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- The Lebanese army closes a bridge in the Tyre District after receiving a warning of a possible Israeli strike on the structure. The bridge is the last crossing linking areas north and south of the Litani River in the area, where many residents remain despite evacuation notices. [src: (AFP via The Times of Israel)]
- Israeli–Palestinian conflict
- Gaza war
- Killing of journalists in the Gaza war
- An Israeli airstrike in Sheikh Ijlin, Gaza City, Palestine, kills two people, including Al Jazeera correspondent Mohammed Wishah. [src: (AFP via Philippine Daily Inquirer)]
- Afghanistan–Pakistan border skirmishes
- 2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war
- Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning says that Afghanistan and Pakistan has agreed on a comprehensive plan to end tensions after seven days of talks in Ürümqi, China. The two countries also agree to avoid any escalations in their current conflict. [src: (AFP via The Straits Times)] [src: (Reuters)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- Tariffs in the second Trump administration
- U.S. president Donald Trump threatens to impose 50% tariffs on countries that supply military weapons to Iran. [src: (CNBC)]
- Danish shipping company Maersk says that they will take a "cautious approach" for vessels to cross the Strait of Hormuz despite the ceasefire and says that they have not provided security certainty as to when normal operations would resume. [src: (Reuters)]
- German shipping company Hapag-Lloyd says that it still does not plan to resume transiting the Strait of Hormuz despite the two-week ceasefire. They also say that it would need 6–8 weeks for recovery and for normal operations to resume. [src: (Insider Paper)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Oil prices plunge below US$95 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average surges past 1,000 after the ceasefire announcement. [src: (AP)]
International relations
- Belarus–North Korea relations
- Belarus plans to open an embassy in North Korea by August 1 after president Alexander Lukashenko visited the country in March following a decree signed by prime minister Alexander Turchin. [src: (Caliber.az)]
Law and crime
- 2026 attack on Israeli consulate in Istanbul
- Turkish police arrest 198 suspects across 34 provinces in operations targeting the Islamic State following a fatal shootout outside the Israeli consulate in Istanbul on April 7. Several suspects are placed in pre-trial detention as part of the investigation. [src: (AFP via Yahoo News)]
- Gilgo Beach serial killings
- Rex Heuermann admits in court to killing eight women and discarding their bodies between 1993 and 2010 in New York, United States. Heuermann is expected to receive a sentence of life in prison without parole when he is sentenced on June 17. [src: (AFP via RTHK)] [src: (NBC News)]
- Illegal drug trade in the United States
- A U.S. court sentences Jasveen Sangha to 15 years in prison for distributing ketamine that resulted in the death of actor Matthew Perry in 2023, as part of a wider investigation into a network supplying controlled substances. Authorities also charge and sentence other individuals, including medical professionals, in connection with the distribution of the drug. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Politics and elections
- Protests against the 2026 Iran war
- Anti-war protesters gather outside the U.S. embassy in Ottawa, Canada, to protest against the Iran war despite the ceasefire along with the wars in Lebanon and Gaza. [src: (CTV News)]
- Around 50,000 protestors across over 150 locations, including around 30,000 outside the National Diet Building in Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo, Japan, protest against the war and proposals by prime minister Sanae Takaichi plan to revise Article 9 of the constitution. [src: (CNN)] [src: (Kanagawa Shimbun)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 April 9
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- After pressure from the United States, Israel agrees to hold direct talks with Lebanon in Washington, D.C., but refuses to observe the Iran war ceasefire in Lebanon. [src: (Axios)] [src: (AA)]
- German chancellor Friedrich Merz announces that Germany will resume direct negotiations with Iran to support a ceasefire between Iran and the U.S., with talks planned in Islamabad, Pakistan, involving a German delegation. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian says that supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei had approved the ceasefire. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
- The Bahraini military intercepts seven drones from Iran. [src: (AA)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
- The Kuwaiti military reports that drones attacked several vital facilities and caused significant damage to a national guard base. [src: (AA)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy announces alternative routes for ships crossing the Strait of Hormuz, citing risks of sea mines in the main shipping channel. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- Abu Dhabi National Oil Company CEO Sultan Al Jaber says that the strait is still not open because Iran has been restricting and controlling traffic. [src: (CNBC)]
- Gabon-flagged oil tanker MSG crosses the Strait of Hormuz according to MarineTraffic, making it the first non-Iranian oil tanker to cross the waterway since the ceasefire was announced. [src: (Gulf Today)]
- Iranian officials killed during the 2026 Iran war
- Former Iranian foreign minister Kamal Kharazi dies from injuries sustained during an Israeli–U.S. airstrike on his home on April 1. [src: (Ynet)]
- Hezbollah–Israel conflict
- 2026 Lebanon war
- Hezbollah launches rockets at the Israeli kibbutz of Manara, citing Israeli and American violations of the ceasefire linked to the Iran war. [src: (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]
- At least seven people are killed by a wave of Israeli airstrikes and artillery shelling across Lebanon. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- The Israeli military says that it has killed Lebanese Resistance Brigades commanders Maher Qassem Hamdan and Ali Yusuf Harshi, personal secretary and nephew of Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Hezbollah says that its fighters are engaged in "point-blank clashes" with Israeli troops in Bint Jbeil, Lebanon. [src: (Al Arabiya)] 
- Lebanese authorities update the losses from the previous day's attacks to 303 killed and 1,150 injured. [src: (AA)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russia–United Kingdom relations, Russian sabotage operations in Europe
- British defence secretary John Healey says three Russian Navy submarines engaged in covert operations against the UK in the North Sea near its undersea cables and says counter-measures are underway. [src: (BBC News)]
- The Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War says that Russia has returned 1,000 bodies of fallen individuals to Ukraine as part of repatriation efforts. [src: (Interfax Ukraine)]
- Russian president Vladimir Putin declares a ceasefire for the weekend in Ukraine for Orthodox Easter. [src: (AP)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Darfur campaign
- The Sudan Founding Alliance says that over 56 civilians, including 17 children, are killed and 107 are injured in a Sudanese drone strike on a wedding celebration in Kutum, North Darfur, Sudan. [src: (The Sudan Times)]
- The World Food Programme announces the return of its Sudan office in Khartoum for the first time in three years amidst a hunger crisis caused by the war. [src: (Sudan Tribune)] [src: (Sudan Horizon)]
Arts and culture
- The Al-Aqsa Mosque, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, the Western Wall, and other holy sites in the Old City of Jerusalem reopen for the first time since the war with Iran started on February 28 after being closed by authorities due to security concerns. [src: (Israel National News)] [src: (Middle East Eye)] [src: (The Times of Israel)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development announces plans to allocate €5 billion to support economies affected by the Iran war, focusing on financial systems, businesses, and infrastructure in Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, and Lebanon. [src: (Reuters via London South East)]
- Gulf Air, the flag carrier of Bahrain, announces a plan to return its operations hub to Bahrain International Airport after having relocated to King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia, during the Iran war. [src: (Aerospace Global News)]
- Oil prices rebound amidst concerns about the ceasefire, with U.S. and Brent Crude oil back up to nearly US$100 per barrel. [src: (NBC News)]
- Saudi Arabia reports that the recent Iranian attack on a pumping station of the East–West Crude Oil Pipeline reduced its throughput by 700,000 barrels per day. [src: (CNBC)]
- Mining in Venezuela
- Venezuela's National Assembly approves a reform of mining laws that allows greater private investment in the country's mineral sector, with the bill advancing to constitutional review. The measure forms part of broader economic changes aimed at increasing foreign participation in natural resource industries. [src: (Le Monde)]
- USAID in the second Trump administration
- The OECD reports that official development assistance from its member states declined by 23.1 percent in real terms to US$174.3 billion, marking the largest recorded annual decrease, with the reduction largely driven by cuts from the United States. [src: (AFP via Indo Premier)]
Disasters and accidents
- European migrant crisis
- Four people are killed and 38 are rescued after an inflatable dinghy of migrants capsized near Calais, off the coast of northern France. [src: (Reuters)]
International relations
- Cuba–Russia relations, 2026 Cuban crisis
- Russian deputy foreign minister Sergei Ryabkov meets with Cuban president Miguel Díaz-Canel in Havana to discuss bilateral relations amid ongoing tensions between Cuba and the U.S. over energy and economic measures, and following the recent arrival of a Russian oil shipment to Cuba despite U.S. restrictions. [src: (AFP via Daily Sun)]
- India–Qatar relations
- Indian oil and gas minister Hardeep Singh Puri visits Qatar to discuss the prioritization of energy exports, as the country is India's largest supplier of liquefied natural gas and liquefied petroleum gas. [src: (OilPrice.com)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Iraq–United States relations
- United States deputy secretary of state Christopher Landau summons the ambassador of Iraq to protest the Iraqi government's failure to prevent militia attacks on American personnel. [src: (AA)]
Law and crime
- Corruption in Nepal
- Nepal issues an arrest warrant for former prime minister Sher Bahadur Deuba and his wife, former foreign minister Arzu Rana Deuba, for alleged money laundering. [src: (AFP via CNA)]
- Pakistan enforces a lockdown in the Capital Territory to prepare for Iran–U.S. ceasefire talks. [src: (Times of India)]
Politics and elections
- The Supreme Court of Russia designates the human rights group Memorial as an extremist organization and bans its activities following a petition by the Ministry of Justice. [src: (AP via Laredo Morning Times)]
Science and technology
- International Space Station program 
- Isar Aerospace's "Onward and Upward" mission, which had been due to launch from Andøya Space port in Andøya, Norway, is postponed for a third time due to a possible leak. [src: (isaraerospace.com)] [src: (NRK)]
- Ngogo chimpanzee war
- A study published in the Science journal finds that 28 chimpanzees, including 19 infants, have been killed during an ongoing chimpanzee war in Kibale National Park, Uganda. [src: (NBC News)]
- North Korea and weapons of mass destruction
- The Korean Central News Agency reports that North Korea has tested various military technologies throughout the week, including a surface-to-surface tactical ballistic missile identified as Hwasongpho-11 Ka. [src: (Yonhap News Agency)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 1
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- The Bermuda-flagged LNG tanker Gaslog Shanghai, which was carrying LNG oil from Qatar, is reported to have been among the two vessels hit yesterday in the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (Arab Times Kuwait)] [src: (Bloomberg)]
- A tanker near Oman is hit by an unknown projectile. [src: (CNBC)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
- The Kuwaiti defense ministry reports that its military has detected and intercepted Iranian drones entering the country's airspace. [src: (Kuwait Times)]
- United States embassies in the Middle East warn Americans to depart the region amidst fears of a potential escalation in the war. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- U.S. president Donald Trump cancels a planned attack against Iran, citing progress in ceasefire negotiations. [src: (Axios)] [src: (The Japan Times)]
- Gaza war
- Casualties of the Gaza war, Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip
- Israeli airstrikes kill three Palestinians in Gaza City, bringing the total casualties in the past 24 hours to seven. [src: (Al-Ahram)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Gaza peace plan
- A Board of Peace official reports that Hamas will disarm its weapons in the coming days. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- Hezbollah–Israel conflict
- 2026 Lebanon war
- The Israeli military says it has killed several Hezbollah fighters in an Israeli-held area of southern Lebanon, despite a ceasefire framework between Israel and Lebanon. [src: (AFP via South China Morning Post)]
- Red Sea crisis
- The Houthis in Yemen deny reports of imposing tolls on vessels passing through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Foreign involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian war
- The Washington Post reports that Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu blocked a request by former United States senator Lindsey Graham to transfer an Iron Dome system from the U.S. to Ukraine. [src: (Haaretz)]
- Kyiv strikes
- Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko says an overnight Russian missile attack has killed at least nine people and injured 24 others, while damaging buildings and causing fires across several districts of the Ukrainian capital. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Naval warfare in the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Ukrainian forces sink a Rosatom-owned container ship in the Black Sea, forcing its 17-member crew to abandon it. Rosatom says it had been transporting civilian goods, including frozen food and construction materials. [src: (BBC News)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Battle of Khartoum
- Egypt and Sudan reach an agreement on a 16-month plan to rehabilitate the Jebel Aulia Dam south of Khartoum, including the construction of a temporary bridge, after the dam was damaged in November 2023 during shelling by the Rapid Support Forces. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Terrorism in Colombia
- 2026 attack on the Norte de Santander Police Command
- A truck bomb explodes beside a police station in Cúcuta, Norte de Santander, Colombia, injuring eleven police officers and three civilians. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Terrorism in Russia 
- 2026 Moscow bombing
- A woman attempts to set off a bomb inside a coffeehouse in Moscow, Russia, but is stopped at the entrance and detonates the explosive. Three people are killed, including the perpetrator, and 21 more are injured. [src: (CNN)]
Arts and culture
- Iraq in the 2026 Iran war
- The Arba'in Shia Islam pilgrimage in Iraq is held amidst the Iran war, with Iranian pilgrims attending the event. [src: (Al-Monitor)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 United States wildfires
- 2026 Washington wildfires
- The Old Trails wildfire in northwestern Spokane, Washington, United States, burns over , destroying many structures. Residents near Fort Spokane are told to evacuate. [src: (CNN)] [src: (News.az)]
- 2024–2026 Cuba blackouts
- Cuba reports a partial collapse of the national power grid, leaving western provinces without electricity after transmission lines fail between Matanzas and Pinar del Río. [src: (Xinhua)]
- 2026 Aerodiana Cessna 208 crash
- Thirteen people, including eleven tourists, are killed when a small aircraft crashes near the Nazca Lines, Peru, after departing Pisco, Ica. [src: (Firstpost)]
- 2026 Broad Peak avalanche
- All ten climbers, including Nirmal Purja, are confirmed deceased after an avalanche at Broad Peak in Pakistan on July 30. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Health and environment
- 2026 heat waves
- Protesters block parts of the main highway connecting Port Sudan and Khartoum in Suakin and Jubayt over severe power cuts amidst a heat wave reported by the in Red Sea State, Sudan. [src: (Sudan Tribune)] 
International relations
- Morocco–Spain relations
- 2026 Morocco–Spain border incident
- Moroccan security forces clash with hundreds of migrants as they attempt to storm the Spanish enclave of Melilla. Several Moroccan security personnel are reportedly injured while more than 50 migrants are detained. [src: (Yeni Safak)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Twin Falls shooting
- Four people are killed, including the perpetrator, and seven others are injured in a mass shooting at an In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls, Idaho, United States. [src: (CNN)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Cyberwarfare during the 2026 Iran war
- The U.S. FBI opens an investigation after the U.S. state of Michigan reports a cyberattack on its water systems, including whether Iran was behind the cyberattack, a day after Minnesota reported a similar breach. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (ABC News)]
- Four workers are killed in a mass shooting in Nyanga, Western Cape, South Africa, while they were repairing a flat tyre. [src: (The Witness)]
Sports
- 2030 FIFA World Cup controversies
- UEFA gives FIFA president Gianni Infantino an ultimatum to resign or face an emergency no-confidence vote following Infantino's plan to sell stakes in FIFA Forward Enterprise, which he has rescinded amidst backlash. [src: (BBC Sport)] [src: (The Telegraph)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 10
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran
- The United States Central Command says that they have redirected 55 vessels linked to Iran since reinstating the blockade in July. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- Impact of the 2026 Iran war on Iran
- Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei appoints new leaders for Iran's military to replace their predecessors after they were killed during the initial Israel and U.S. airstrikes, including Ali Abdollahi as chief of staff, Kioumars Heydari as deputy commander, and Hossein Taeb as Basij commander. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)] [src: (Al-Monitor)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Аt least 13 people are killed, including a child, and 39 others were injured in a Ukrainian drone attack on an oil refinery in Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, Russia. [src: (Reuters)]
- Libyan crisis
- , head of military intelligence for the Libyan National Army, is assassinated as a bomb exploded inside his car in Benghazi, Libya. [src: (AFP via RFI)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Colombia earthquake
- A earthquake strikes Chocó Department, Colombia, causing widespread and heavy damage, and leaving at least 288 people dead. [src: (El Pais)] [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Reuters)]
- The Cathedral Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary in Manizales is confirmed to be among the buildings damaged after one of the towers collapsed following the earthquake. [src: (The Independent)] [src: (The City Paper Bogota)] [src: (El Colombiano in Spanish)]
- Wildfires in 2026
- A recent wildfire at the Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park in East Java, Indonesia, is extinguished after were burnt. However, new hotspots are also reported near the caldera. [src: (Reuters)]
- The Philippine civil defense office reports that at least 16 people were killed across Luzon, including seven in Baguio, by floods, landslides and weather-related accidents after nine days of heavy monsoon rain, while three others remain missing. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- The World Health Organization reports that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo started in February before its declaration, with some cases attributed to malaria and typhoid. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
International relations
- Colombia–Israel relations, Colombia–Syria relations
- Colombia becomes the second country to recognize the Golan Heights, a region in southwestern Syria that has been under Israeli occupation since 1967, as part of Israel's sovereignty. [src: (AFP via CNA)] [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Nonthaburi shootings
- Nonthaburi Provincial Administrative Organization president Thongchai Yenprasert is killed in a shooting at a government building in Nonthaburi province, Thailand. Former parliament member Chalong Riewrang is taken into custody over corruption. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (AFP via CNA)] [src: (Thairath)]
- Murder of Mir Raza Ali
- The government of Sindh, Pakistan, announces that a judicial commission headed by a judge of the Sindh High Court would investigate businessman Mir Raza Ali's death. The decision followed a recommendation by the Sindh Assembly. [src: (Dawn)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Russian legislative election
- Upon petition from Rodina, the liberal Yabloko party is barred from participating in the 2026 Russian legislative election on charges of unregistered funding, a controversial copyright infringement, and extremism by the Supreme Court of Russia. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (The Moscow Times)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 11
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war
- Pakistani defence minister Khawaja Asif says that a deal between Iran and the United States is "close", including an arrangement over the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (Bloomberg News)] [src: (CNBC)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran
- The Wall Street Journal reports that a U.S. military helicopter has fired at the rudder of the Panama-flagged container ship Vela ​Nova after crews ignored the naval blockade re-imposed in July, contradicting British maritime management that it was hit by a missile in the Gulf of Oman. [src: (Reuters)]
- Red Sea crisis
- Operation Rough Rider
- The U.S. Department of Defense reports to Congress that the U.S. military strikes against Houthi rebels in Yemen in 2025 killed 153 civilians and injured another 243. [src: (The Hill)]
- The Yemeni government reports that six people have been killed in strikes on a cargo ship by the Houthis in the Bab-el-Mandeb. [src: (The New York Times)]
- Gaza war
- The Israeli Army Radio reports that the Israel Defense Forces launched a strike targeting a Hamas sniper near the Yellow Line in the Gaza Strip, its first strike on the enclave in 10 days. [src: (AIN)] [src: (The Times of Israel)] [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- Sudanese Civil Wars
- Sudanese civil war
- Blue Nile campaign
- A heavy attack on civilians by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North (SPLM-N) is reported in Geissan in Sudan's Blue Nile state, including on the main market, surrounding farms, and other shops. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- The International Organization for Migration reports that 2,300 people in the Blue Nile region has been displaced following recent clashes. [src: (Middle East Monitor)]
- Attacks by the RSF and SPLM-N are also reported in Qaysān on its provincial headquarters and a market. [src: (Sudan Tribune in Arabic)]
- Sudanese nomadic conflicts
- Around 60 people are killed and around 50 others injured in an armed attack during a cattle raid in Tonj North County, Warrap State, South Sudan. [src: (AFP via Arab News)] [src: (Radio Tamazuj)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Colombia earthquake
- The casualty toll from the earthquake in Colombia yesterday increases to over 240 people killed, 570 injured, and at least 3,000 others still missing. President Abelardo de la Espriella declares a national state of emergency. [src: (The Guardian)]
- At least 44 people are killed when a ferry sinks on Lake Kariba, Zimbabwe. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- Search operations for the landslide from Sunday conclude in Baguio, Philippines, placing the final death toll at ten people. Meanwhile, the national police places the nationwide toll from the tropical cyclones and monsoons at 26. [src: (ABS-CBN News)] [src: (Philippine Daily Inquirer)]
- At least 18 people are killed and around 30 others are injured in a two-vehicle collision in Ismailia Governorate, Egypt. [src: (Al Ahram)]
- Four people are killed and five others are injured after an old residential building collapses in Cairo, Egypt. [src: (Gulf News)]
- Three people are killed following a commercial building fire in Giza, Egypt. [src: (Al Ahram)]
International relations
- Syria and weapons of mass destruction
- The Syrian transitional government confirms their cooperation with the International Atomic Energy Agency to purge nuclear materials at a hidden facility following a report by Axios on such plan after an agreement between Israel, Syria, and the United States. Conversely, Israel threatens to bombard the site again if the materials remain, and to prevent access to the site. [src: (AA)] [src: (Axios)] [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
Law and crime
- Presidency of Ahmed al-Sharaa, War crimes in the Syrian civil war,‪ Prosecution of Syrian civil war criminals
- The Criminal Court in Damascus, Syria, sentences deposed president Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher to death in absentia, and former Daraa political security director Atef Najib in person, and issue international arrest warrants for all for premeditated murder and crimes against humanity. [src: (AFP via The Standard)] [src: (The National)]
- Capital punishment in Lebanon
- The Lebanese parliament votes to abolish the death penalty. [src: (BBC News)]
- A United States Marine Corps soldier is released from Russia after having been detained there since 2022. [src: (Kyiv Independent)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Hungarian presidential election
- Former Supreme Court president András Baka is elected as Hungarian president through a supermajority and is scheduled to take office on 19 August. He ran uncontested as the Tisza Party's candidate, as neither Fidesz nor its partner KNDP nominated a candidate. [src: (Reuters)]
Sports
- Thousand Martyrs' Cup, Palestinian sports during the Gaza war
- Palestinian Football Association president Jibril Rajoub announces that all football and sport activities will resume in September following a three-year suspension that began after the outbreak of the Gaza war. [src: (Al Jazeera)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 14
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Gaza war
- Gaza war hostage crisis
- The Israel Defense Forces announce that Al-Qassam Brigades commander Muhammad Bassam Mushtaha, who was accused of taking hostages during and after the Hamas–led attacks against Israel on October 7, was killed in a recent airstrike last month in northern Gaza. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- Heavy fighting erupts in El Obeid, North Kordofan, Sudan, between the Sudanese Armed Forces and Rapid Support Forces (RSF). Clashes also break out in Umm Arda. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Around 14 people are reported to be killed following an attack by RSF militants on the North Kordofan town of Umm Arda. [src: (AFP via Arab News)] [src: (Xinhua)]
- Colombian conflict
- A Colombian soldier is killed and four more wounded following a drone strike in the rural area of El Carmen, Norte de Santander. [src: (El Colombiano in Spanish)]
- Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
- A constable policeman is killed and another is injured after a group of suspected insurgents attacked a police post in Bajaur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. [src: (Dawn)]
- Mexican drug war
- Three gunmen are killed and a child is wounded in an attempted ambush on a highway in La Piedad, Michoacán, Mexico. Authorities seize four long guns, magazines, ammunition, and improvised explosives. [src: (El Heraldo de México in Spanish)]
- War in the Sahel
- American missionary Kevin Rideout is released from captivity after being kidnapped by an unidentified organisation front in Niger nine months prior. [src: (The New York Times)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Croatia wildfires
- One person dies and at least 40 others are injured after a severe wildfire breaks out on Croatia's coastline. [src: (BBC News)]
- 2026 Flores earthquake
- At least 47 people are killed and several more are injured when a earthquake strikes the coast of the island of Flores in East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia. [src: (AP)]
- A earthquake strikes the province of Granada in Spain, with damage reported in Granada and the surrounding area, and being felt in Madrid. [src: (The News International)]
- Sixteen people are killed and 40 others injured on the Yaounde-Bafoussam highway after a passenger bus crashed into a parked truck carrying planks in Mbam-et-Inoubou, Cameroon. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Thai rescuers find a French tourist and his two sons alive after they spend more than 16 hours at sea when their rented jet ski capsizes off Ko Samui. The family receives medical checks and is discharged. [src: (CBS News)]
- Heavy rainfall persists in Eastern China due to the remnants of Typhoon Dolphin, resulting in flooding in Zhejiang province, China, killing atleast one. [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- Internet censorship in France
- The Constitutional Council of France blocks a bill proposing a ban on social media access for minors under the age of 15. President Emmanuel Macron orders prime minister Sebastien Lecornu to re-work the draft legislation and resubmit it to the Council. [src: (RFI)] [src: (Business of Fashion)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 political prisoner release in Venezuela
- Venezuela releases 131 detainees under alternative custody measures as part of a national reconciliation program following former president Nicolás Maduro's removal. Human rights group Foro Penal confirms that at least 45 of those freed are political prisoners. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
Sports
- 2026 NFL season
- In American football, the National Football League suspends Atlanta Falcons linebacker James Pearce Jr. for eight games for violating the league's personal conduct policy after his arrest in February on domestic violence charges. [src: (AP)] [src: (WAGA-TV)]
- 2026 Volta a Portugal
- In road bicycle racing, the eighth stage at the Volta a Portugal race is neutralised after British cyclist Finlay Tarling is killed in an accident during the race. [src: (The Athletic via The New York Times)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 16
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war, Russia–NATO relations
- 2026 drone incidents in Romania 
- A Spanish F/A-18 Hornet jet shoots down a Russian drone in Romanian airspace. The drone was downed near Galați after entering from Moldova. [src: (Politico)]
- Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Ukrainian forces launch 822 drones at Russia, including over 600 towards Moscow, killing at least seven people and injuring 39 others. A Wildberries warehouse is also destroyed. Russian officials say it is the largest Ukrainian drone attack launched this year. [src: (BBC News)]
- Insurgency in Balochistan
- Seven suspected members of the Pakistani Taliban are killed in a intelligence-based joint operation in Kharan District, Balochistan, Pakistan. [src: (The Express Tribune)]
- Mali War
- 2026 Mali offensives
- Tuareg separatist Azawad Liberation Front releases six wounded Malian troops. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- Myanmar civil war
- Rakhine offensive
- Two civilians are killed and several homes are damaged by a government airstrike in Thandwe, Rakhine State, Myanmar. [src: (Narinjara News)]
- Sudanese civil war
- The African Union (AU) holds a meeting with Sudanese officials in an effort to end the war, marking the first talks by the AU in the country since the military led by Abdel Fattah al-Burhan seized power in the October 2021 coup. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
Business and economy
- The Federal Government of Somalia announces that Somali Airlines will resume flights beginning next month, ending a 35-year pause after the country entered a civil war in 1991. [src: (Bloomberg)] [src: (Dawan Africa)] [src: (Airline Geeks)]
Disasters and accidents
- The death toll of the Lake Kariba vessel capsizing in Zimbabwe from last week rises to 72 after twelve more bodies are recovered. [src: (AP)]
- A passenger bus carrying tourists from Poland crashes in to a ditch in Mezőkeresztes, Hungary, killing 12 people and injuring ten more. [src: (AP)]
- Ten people are killed after a tourist bus overturns near Petrópolis, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. [src: (Xinhua)] [src: (O Globo )]
- Five teenagers are killed and four others, including a child, are injured in a head-on collision caused by a wrong-way driving vehicle on the M9 motorway in County Kildare, Ireland. [src: (BBC News)]
- St. Nicolas' Church is completely destroyed by a fire at the Museum of Folk Architecture in Sanok, Podkarpackie Voivodeship, Poland. [src: (TVP World)]
Law and crime
- Three people, including a teenager, are killed and two others are injured in a shooting in Isla Cristina, Andalusia, Spain. Police investigate the attack as a possible dispute between rival drug-trafficking groups and search for the gunman. [src: (Reuters)]
Sports
- 2026 IFAF Women's Flag Football World Championship, Canada at the 2028 Summer Olympics
- In flag football, Canada's women's team defeats the defending champion United States to win its third IFAF Flag Football World Championship title. Additionally, the men's football team qualifies for the upcoming Summer Olympics. [src: (Global News)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 17
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region
- Kurdistan Region prime minister Masrour Barzani reports that Iran has launched a drone attack on the Kurdistan Regional Government’s (KRG) prime minister’s office. No casualties are reported. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- A Russian Banderol cruise missile explodes in Ștefan Vodă District, Moldova, after entering from Ukrainian airspace, triggering a wildfire in a corn field. Moldovan authorities condemn the strike as "a serious violation of Moldova’s sovereignty". [src: (The New Voice of Ukraine)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- The Sudanese Armed Forces says that it has shot down a long-range drone used by the Rapid Support Forces in Sudan's North Kordofan state, the second drone shot down this month in the region. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- South Sudanese president Salva Kiir meets with Darfur governor Minni Minnawi in Juba, South Sudan, to discuss efforts to end the conflict in Sudan. [src: (Eye Radio)]
- Somali Civil War
- Constitutional crisis in Somalia, Controversies of Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
- Several fighters from both sides are killed after Somali federal forces and opposition groups clash in the South West State. Two civilians are also killed. Militias loyal to former state president Abdiaziz Laftagareen enter the regional capital Baidoa, challenging two battalions of the Somali National Army loyal to Somali president Hassan Sheikh Mohamud. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (Garowe Online)] [src: (i24 news)]
- Nigerian bandit conflict
- At least 22 people are killed in a mass shooting in Kebbe, Sokoto State, Nigeria. [src: (Tribune)]
- Terrorism in Afghanistan
- An explosion is reported at a school in the Dashte Barchi neighborhood of Kabul, Afghanistan, injuring several people. The perpetrator is unknown. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Pacific hurricane season
- A 90-year-old woman is confirmed dead in Nāʻālehu, Hawaii, United States, and over 100,000 people remain without power after Hurricane Lala struck the state. [src: (AP)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- 2026 Pacific typhoon season
- Floods and landslides caused by the southwest monsoon and Tropical Storm Kujira kill at least 23 people and displace thousands across the Philippines. [src: (AA)]
- A crowd crush at the Ashokdham Temple in Bihar, India, kills at least seven people and injures 19 others. [src: (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]
- Seven people are killed and several others are injured after a fire breaks out in a hotel in Birbhum District, West Bengal, India. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Humanitarian NGO Emergency rescues 50 migrants from a wooden boat in international waters off Libya and recovers seven bodies. Two survivors require urgent medical evacuation, and 29 of those rescued are unaccompanied minors. [src: (Reuters)]
- Three people are killed when a private helicopter crashes on Sifnos, South Aegean, Greece. [src: (AP)]
- Torrential rainfall causes widespread flooding in Geoje-si, South Gyeongsang, South Korea, killing at least one. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (The Guardian)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- The United Nations reports that at least 2,325 people have died from the current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, making it the deadliest in the country's history. [src: (DW)]
- Seventh cholera pandemic
- A city official reports that at least 500 people have been hospitalized for severe diarrhea, with nearly 150 testing positive for cholera, in Yangon, Myanmar. [src: (AFP via CNA)]
- California's energy commission approves the United States's first energy-efficiency standards for replacement tires, aiming to reduce rolling resistance and lower driver fuel costs by 2029. However, manufacturers warn the strict limits could eliminate up to 70% of current replacement tire options by 2033. [src: (The New York Times)] [src: (Fox Business)]
International relations
- France–Iran relations
- Iran says it barred two French embassy employees from returning for allegedly violating the Vienna Convention through activities supporting Iranian civil society. France says their work involved programs for civil society, students, and artists. [src: (Reuters)]
- South Korea–United States relations
- United States president Donald Trump orders the Department of Defense to substantially reduce the Ulchi-Freedom Guardian military exercises with South Korea, citing their cost and his relationship with North Korean supreme leader Kim Jong Un. The drills begin as scheduled. [src: (AFP via The Straits Times)]
Law and crime
- War on drugs
- Mexican drug war
- Members of the Mexican Navy seize 3.2 million doses of cocaine floating off the coasts of the state of Michoacán. This action represents a financial blow of Mex$340.2 million (US$20.11 million) to organized crime. [src: (López Doriga in Spanish)]
- Indonesia's National Narcotics Board, police, and customs arrest 10 Myanmar nationals after seizing 2.6 metric tons of liquid methamphetamine from a Tanzanian-flagged vessel in waters off the Riau Islands. [src: (Reuters)]
- Opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia, Protests against the Russo-Ukrainian war
- A Russian court sentences Yabloko deputy chairperson Lev Shlosberg to 11 years and one month in prison for discrediting the armed forces and spreading disinformation after he publicly condemned the Russo-Ukrainian war. [src: (Reuters)]
- Discord suspends live streaming, screen sharing, and video calls in Brazil to comply with an order from the national data protection authority following the death of a 13-year-old girl allegedly encouraged to kill herself during an online broadcast. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- The trial of Duane "Keffe D" Davis for his alleged role in the murder of rapper Tupac Shakur begins in Las Vegas, Nevada, United States. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (CNN)]
Politics and elections
- Immigration policy of the second Trump administration
- United States Customs and Border Protection (CBP) commissioner Rodney S. Scott pauses construction of a $1.7 billion border-security project in Big Bend National Park, Texas, while the CBP reviews the plan amid bipartisan local opposition and environmental concerns. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- Former South Korean prime minister Kim Min-seok is elected as the new leader of the Democratic Party with 54.08% of the vote against its former leader Jung Chung-rae. [src: (The Diplomat)] [src: (The Korea Herald)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 18
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reports that a cargo vessel has come under attack off the Omani coast in the Strait of Hormuz, leaving one dead. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- United Arab Emirates in the 2026 Iran war
- The United Arab Emirates's defence ministry detects two missiles fired from Iran towards the country, including one that fell outside territorial waters and another that fell within it. [src: (Gulf News)] [src: (Khaleej Times)] [src: (Emirates 24/7)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war, Russia–United Kingdom relations
- British prime minister Andy Burnham confirms that the United Kingdom will continue to militarily support Ukraine after Russia warned the UK will face "consequences" for allowing Ukraine to use British-made drones to strike targets deep inside Russian territory. [src: (BBC News)]
- Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
- A Russian ballistic missile strike kills ten civilians and injures eight others in Pechenihy, Kharkiv Oblast. Several homes are completely destroyed. [src: (AP)]
- Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant crisis
- A drone strike hits a bus stop near the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant in Enerhodar, killing one plant worker and injuring several others. [src: (Reuters)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Blue Nile campaign
- The Sudan Doctors Network reports that recent attacks in Geissan of Sudan's Blue Nile region has displaced over 5,000 people to Damazin. [src: (Sudan Horizon)]
- Darfur campaign
- The Rapid Support Forces launches a major crackdown in Nyala, South Darfur, its largest security and military mobilization since seizing the city in 2023. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Nigerian bandit conflict
- At least 24 bandits are killed by a force of Nigerian Army, State Security Service, and vigilante groups during a foiled kidnapping attempt in Bakori, Katsina State, Nigeria. [src: (Daily Post)]
- Fourteen kidnapping victims are rescued by the Nigerian Army in Sabuwa, Katsina State. [src: (The Punch)]
- Mexican drug war
- Five gunmen are killed by members of the Mexican Army after an encounter in Los Palillos locality, Los Reyes, Michoacán. [src: (Latinus in Spanish)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- Iran–United Arab Emirates relations
- The United Arab Emirates suspends commercial exchanges, and financial transactions with Iran after Iran launched two ballistic missiles at the country. [src: (Time)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Zamboye mine collapse
- At least 100 people are killed when a gold mine collapses in Zamboye, Baboua, Central African Republic, at the border with Cameroon. [src: (RTÉ)]
- At least eight people are killed and more than 20 others are injured after a vehicle rams into a truck in Madhya Pradesh, India. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Five people are killed and 17 others sustain injuries after a parapet wall collapses due to excessive rainfall during a college entrance celebration in Changning County, Sichuan, China. [src: (Xinhua in Chinese)]
- Four people are killed and 16 others are injured when a passenger bus crashes due to a brake failure in Kirehe District, Eastern Province, Rwanda. [src: (IGIHE)]
- Three people are killed after an explosion at a thermal power plant in Baniyas, Syria. [src: (Xinhua)]
- A second earthquake strikes the province of Granada, in Spain. Damage and injures are reported in Granada and the surrounding area, while the Alhambra is evacuated. [src: (BBC News)]
Health and environment
- The UK Health Security Agency confirms that an outbreak of salmonella in the UK has left one person dead and hundreds more ill. The outbreak is believed to be linked to imported eggs. [src: (BBC News)]
International relations
- United States and the International Criminal Court
- The United States imposes sanctions on International Criminal Court (ICC) president Tomoko Akane and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye over their alleged involvement in proceedings against officials from countries that do not recognize ICC jurisdiction. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Ateneo de Zamboanga University shooting
- A student is killed while nine other people are injured in a mass shooting at a junior secondary school building of the Ateneo de Zamboanga University in Zamboanga City, Philippines. The perpetrator, also a student, later kills himself. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (The Philippine Star)]
- Imprisonment of Imran Khan
- Pakistan's Supreme Court orders imprisoned former prime minister Imran Khan transferred from the central jail in Rawalpindi, Punjab, to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad for medical examinations following a petition by his lawyers concerning his health. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- Singapore begins requiring major Internet messaging platforms to restrict unsolicited contacts and social media services to verify advertisers and block suspected scam advertisements under new anti-scam rules, with penalties of up to S$1 million (US$780,000) for non-compliance. [src: (AFP via The Manila Times)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Zambian general election
- Zambian president Hakainde Hichilema is declared the winner by the electoral commission, re-electing him to a second term. [src: (AP)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 19
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign
- Axios reports that the U.S. military has created a new shipping lane in the Strait of Hormuz to help ships transit through the waterway, including the facilitating of 10 million barrels of oil per day. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)] [src: (Axios)]
- Gaza war
- Gaza peace plan, Qatar as a mediator in conflict
- Qatari prime minister and foreign minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani meets with Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya and other senior leaders in Doha, Qatar, to discuss the situation in the Gaza Strip and other occupied Palestinian territories. [src: (Doha News)]
- War crimes in the Gaza war, Gaza genocide
- The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) launches an investigation into troop conduct for their roles in the 2024 killing of five-year-old Palestinian girl Hind Rajab, her family, and 15 paramedics. [src: (AP)]
- Around ten people are reported killed in an Israeli airstrike on a police station in Gaza City. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- The IDF says that the Air Force have targeted two Hamas commanders, including one who participated in the October 7 attacks, along with Hamas tunnels in the Gaza Strip. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- The IDF also confirms that they have killed four Nukhba force commanders from the Al-Qassam Brigades wing of Hamas in an airstrike on a cafe yesterday in Gaza City. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)] [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Kyiv strikes
- Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy says that a Russian missile and drone attack on Kyiv killed at least 15 people and injured 40 others, damaging residential buildings, a children's hospital, and a school. [src: (ABC News)] [src: (BBC News)]
- Mexican drug war
- Nine CJNG members, including four ringleaders, are arrested during a military operation in Tinaja de Vargas y Colesio, municipality of Tanhuato and Ecuandureo. Among the detained is Heraclio Guerrero aka "Tio Lako", leader identified as behind the operation of cartel training camps and the offensive during the 2026 Jalisco operation. [src: (CNN en Español in Spanish)] [src: (Democrata)]
- The United Nations reports that 36 humanitarian workers and contractors in South Sudan have been killed since the start of the year, surpassing the 31 killed last year. [src: (AP)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- Iranian economic crisis, Economic D-Day
- U.S. president Donald Trump announces an economic war against Iran, along with new sanctions for countries trading with Iran. [src: (The Hill)]
- The Office for National Statistics reports that inflation in the United Kingdom rose to 2.9% last month amidst the Iran war. [src: (The Guardian)]
- Economy of the United States
- The United States Department of the Treasury reports that the national debt surpassed $40 trillion for the first time the previous day, and is currently at $40.047 trillion. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (CNBC)] [src: (AP)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Mount Ololokwe helicopter crash
- Six passengers, including Ecuadorian intelligence head Michele Sensi-Contugi and his wife, and the pilot are killed in a helicopter crash on Mount Ololokwe in Samburu County, Kenya. [src: (NBC News)]
- At least 52 people are killed when a boat carrying farm workers capsizes in Goronyo, Sokoto State, Nigeria. [src: (Lagos Television)]
- Twenty-three people are killed and five others are injured in a head-on collision between a bus and a truck on the BR-373 near Ipiranga, Paraná, Brazil. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (UOL)]
- Nine people, including eight Bangladeshi nationals, are killed and six others are injured in a hotel fire in Kolkata, West Bengal, India. [src: (AP)] [src: (The Independent)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak
- Amidst the ongoing measles outbreak in Bangladesh, health minister M. A. Muhit says that the outbreak will need 2-3 months for it to be under control. [src: (Jagonews24)]
- In a study from the Bangladesh Shishu Hospital & Institute, around 82% of children who died from measles during the outbreak in Bangladesh did not receive adequate or exclusive breastfeeding during their first 6 months of their life. [src: (Dhaka Tribune)] [src: (The Business Standard)]
- Four more children are reported to have died from measles in 24 hours, bringing the death toll in the country from the outbreak past 922. [src: (The Business Standard)]
- Merck and Moderna report that their cancer vaccine candidate showed positive results in their late-stage trial in preventing a recurrence of melanoma, including in high-risk patients. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (CNBC)]
Law and crime
- Former Liberian vice president Jewel Taylor is charged for drug trafficking, money laundering ‌and other offenses as part of an investigation of a transnational narcotics network. [src: (Reuters)]
Science and technology
- A U.S.-led research team grows human brain organoids for seven years, the longest reported period, and finds that their cells continue maturing in patterns similar to normal brain development. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Sports
- 2026 Sydney Swans player investigation
- In Australian football, the Sydney Swans suspend five of their players for the remainder of the season who are under police investigation over allegations of sexual assault against multiple women. [src: (ABC News Australia)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 2
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- Iranian lawmaker Hassan Ghashghavi says that efforts to restore the Islamabad Memorandum deal between Iran and the United States are underway. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- 2026 Iran–Oman negotiations
- Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi says that Iran and Oman are nearing a deal to manage the Strait of Hormuz after the U.S. halted its recent strikes against the country. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Gaza war
- The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) confirm that they killed three militants in separate strikes last week, including a Jaish al-Islam militant in Gaza City, a Hamas commander in the Jabalya Battalion, and a Palestinian Islamic Jihad militant. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- Hezbollah–Israel conflict
- The IDF's 401st Brigade says that they have destroyed 1,200 Hezbollah tunnels and concluded their mission in southern Lebanon, ending their eight-month deployment. [src: (Israel National News)] [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- Ethiopian civil conflict
- Ethiopia-TPLF clashes
- New clashes are reported across the Tigray Region in northern Ethiopia between the Ethiopian federal army and Tigray People's Liberation Front, four years after the previous war in the region ended, prompting hundreds to flee to war-torn Sudan amidst fears of a new civil war. [src: (BBC)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Several Ethiopian refugees are reportedly killed after projectiles have hit refugee camps across the Ethiopia–Sudan border. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Darfur campaign, Darfur genocide
- A drone strike hits a customary court in Kabkabiya District, North Darfur, Sudan, killing at least 37 people. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
- Police say a suspected suicide bombing outside a police station in Kabal, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, killed at least 17 people, including seven officers and the suspected bomber, and injured at least 34 others. [src: (Reuters)]
- Mali War, Mali–Russia relations
- The BBC reports that Russia shipped military equipment to the Malian government on the sanctioned cargo vessel Mikhail Britnev last month. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (RBC-Ukraine)]
- Papua conflict
- Five road construction workers are killed in an ambush by armed separatist insurgents at a workers' camp in Tolikara Regency, Highland Papua, Indonesia. [src: (Antara News)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Greece wildfires
- Two people are killed when two firefighting helicopters collide near Athens, Greece. [src: (BBC News)]
- 2026 Morocco–Spain border incident
- Spanish officials say at least 72 people died during the mass migrant crossing from Morocco into the autonomous city of Ceuta. [src: (Reuters)]
- Six people are killed and 27 more injured in a traffic collision between a bus, a camper, and three cars in Colli sul Velino, Province of Rieti, Italy. [src: (Xinhua)]
- A ferry catches fire off the coast of Madura, Indonesia, leaving at least five people dead and 41 others missing. [src: (BBC News)]
Health and environment
- South Korea's weather agency records in Yangsan, South Gyeongsang, the country's highest temperature since observations began. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
International relations
- Foreign relations of the Dominican Republic, Foreign relations of Venezuela
- The Dominican Republic and Venezuela agree on a framework to gradually restore diplomatic relations, which deteriorated after the Dominican Republic questioned the results of the 2024 Venezuelan presidential election. [src: (AFP via Jamaica Observer)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Brazilian general election
- Incumbent Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva formally announces his candidacy for a fourth term as the Workers' Party's nominee in October’s presidential election. [src: (AFP via France 24)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 20
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 United States military buildup in the Middle East
- The arrives in the Middle East to relieve the amidst a nine-month deployment and reports of mental health challenges among the crew and supply shortages on the aircraft carrier during the Iran war. [src: (AP)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Data from Kpler shows that seven ships have passed through the Strait of Hormuz, with four entering and three exiting the waterway. [src: (Reuters)]
- Gaza war, Palestinian war crimes
- The Israel Defense Forces accuses Hamas of using the Nasser Hospital in Khan Yunis to carry out interrogations and torture Palestinians. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- Mali War
- 2026 Mali offensives
- Human Rights Watch reports that Africa Corps forces summarily killed nine civilians, including four children, in Mali last month. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (HRW)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- The Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North led by Abdelaziz al-Hilu regains control of Kauda, South Kordofan, following two days of clashes with Otoro fighters. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Myanmar civil war
- Unexploded ordnance from past fighting is detonated after being tampered with in Maungdaw Township, Rakhine State, Myanmar, injuring ten children. [src: (Burma News International)]
Business and economy
- LSEG data shows that a vessel in France is loading wheat destined for Sudan, marking the first export of wheat from France to Sudan since August 2008. [src: (Baird Maritime)]
Disasters and accidents
- Security Aviation Flight 45
- Eight people are killed when a Cessna 441 Conquest II aircraft crashes at the Cape Newenham Long Range Radar Site in Western Alaska, United States. [src: (AA)] [src: (AP)] [src: (KTUU-TV)]
- A earthquake strikes the Parinacochas province in Peru. [src: (AP)]
- Four railway workers on the Tōbu Nikkō Line are killed after being struck by a Limited express train in Kanuma, Tochigi Prefecture, Japan. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (The Japan Times)]
- Mauritania's coast guard rescues more than 300 migrants, including 40 children, from an overcrowded boat off the country's coast after finding them in distress. [src: (AFP via L'Orient–Le Jour)]
- At least 13 Tunisians are missing and two are rescued after their boat capsized off Tunisia while sailing toward Italy, according to the Tunisian Observatory for Human Rights. One survivor is in critical condition. [src: (Reuters)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- The World Health Organization says that the Democratic Republic of the Congo will receive 70,000 doses of the Ebola vaccine candidate developed by Merck to combat the Ebola outbreak in the country. [src: (CNBC)] [src: (Africanews)]
International relations
- Ecuador–United States relations, Mexico–United States relations
- The U.S. Treasury Department issues sanctions on 15 people allegedly involved in a drug trafficking network shipping thousands of kilograms of cocaine from Ecuador through Mexico to the United States. [src: (AP)]
Law and crime
- 2025 Mexican fuel smuggling scandal, Argentina–Mexico relations
- Argentina deports a Mexican Rear Admiral accused of leading a fuel-smuggling network inside the Mexican Navy to Mexico after the Mexican government withdraws its extradition request. He is taken to the Altiplano maximum-security prison, where his brother and alleged co-leader, Vice Admiral Manuel Roberto Farías Laguna, is also imprisoned. [src: (Infobae in Spanish)]
- Corruption in China, Chinese real estate crisis
- A Chinese court sentences Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan to life imprisonment for financial fraud, bribery, and embezzlement, and fines Evergrande and its real estate arm a combined ¥15.8 billion (US$2.35 billion). [src: (AFP via CNA)]
- Two ANC members including a former Knysna councillor are shot dead, one day after a sitting Knysna councillor is shot dead in a suspected internal ANC faction fight in Knysna, Western Cape, South Africa. [src: (Knysna-Plett Herald)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Bangladeshi presidential election
- The Jatiya Sangsad elects Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as the President of Bangladesh in the first contested presidential election in 35 years. Alamgir will take office tomorrow. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (AP)] [src: (Dhaka Tribune)]
- Cameroon President Paul Biya returns to the country following a two-and-a-half-month absence. [src: (Africanews)]
- Syrian Kurdish leader Mazloum Abdi says the integration of Kurdish military, security, and administrative institutions into the Syrian state is complete following an agreement reached with president Ahmed al-Sharaa in January. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Sports
- In American football, the National Football League fines the Dallas Cowboys and the New Orleans Saints $500,000 each after they started a brawl after a joint practice session at the Cowboys' facility in Oxnard, California, United States. [src: (AP)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 21
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Kryvyi Rih strikes
- Russian drone strikes on a shopping center in Kryvyi Rih, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Ukraine, kill at least 16 people and injure more than 130 others, including 22 children. [src: (Reuters)]
- Mykolaiv strikes
- A Russian strike on a neighborhood in Mykolaiv Oblast, Ukraine, kills four people, including three children, according to Ukrainian interior minister Ivan Vyhivskyi. [src: (Ukrinform)]
- Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
- Pakistani forces raid multiple militant hideouts, killing 12 suspected Pakistani Taliban militants in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and 37 suspected Baloch separatist militants in Balochistan. [src: (AP)]
- Myanmar civil war
- Resistance fighters and a local activist say Myanmar's military deployed hundreds of troops around the proposed Dawei Special Economic Zone in the Tanintharyi Region, burning villages and pushing resistance groups back as the government seeks to revive the project. [src: (Reuters)]
- At least 14 people are reportedly killed and 20 others are injured after Myanmar's military launched an airstrike on a Buddhist monastery compound in Myaung Township during a religious gathering. [src: (AFP via CNA)]
Arts and culture
- Ethiopian civil conflict
- The annual Ashenda festival in Mekelle, Tigray Region, Ethiopia, is cancelled over drone strike fears. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Binance)]
- American fantasy film The Odyssey reaches US$1.35 billion at the worldwide box office to become the highest-grossing R-rated film, surpassing Deadpool & Wolverine. [src: (The Guardian)]
Business and economy
- The Panama Canal announces it will limit the number of ships allowed to cross the passage over the next month due to El Niño causing droughts in the region. [src: (DW)]
Disasters and accidents
- The death toll of a boat capsizing off the coast of Zambezia Province, Mozambique from August 16 rises to 12 after five bodies of those unaccounted for are found by search teams. [src: (Club of Mozambique)]
- Three people are killed and six more wounded in an explosion at a house in the Ain al-Qasab village of Idlib, Syria. [src: (AA)] [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- Five people are reported missing and eight others are injured after a fire at a restaurant with apartments in Thusis, Grisons, Switzerland. [src: (AFP via Kuwait Times)] [src: (BBC News)]
Health and environment
- Project Elephant
- India's Supreme Court orders states to protect elephant corridors, identify and remove obstructions, and prohibit groups from using fire to drive wild elephants away amid increasing habitat loss and human-elephant conflict. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Around 16 people in Sudan's Red Sea state have reportedly died from a heat stroke amidst a rise in temperatures in the state. [src: (Middle East Monitor)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Fagersta school stabbing
- A person is killed and three other people are injured in a mass stabbing, carried out with a sword, at a high school in Fagersta, Sweden. The perpetrator is arrested at the scene. [src: (Reuters)]
- Capital punishment in Japan
- Japan executes a 58-year-old man for a 2009 arson attack that killed five people at a pachinko parlor in Osaka. It is the first execution under Sanae Takaichi's premiership. [src: (AFP via The Star)] [src: (The Japan Times)]
- Lawsuits involving TikTok
- TikTok agrees to pay $400 million to settle a U.S. Justice Department lawsuit alleging violations of federal children's privacy law through the collection of personal data from users under 13 without parental consent. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- War crimes in the Gaza war, Humanitarian aid during the Gaza war, Gaza genocide
- Turkish justice minister Akın Gürlek announces that Turkey has issued an Interpol arrest warrant for Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu for his role in attacks on activists seeking to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza. [src: (France 24)] [src: (Reuters)]
- The Hong Kong Court of First Instance convicts Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung of incitement to subversion over their leadership of a group that organized annual Tiananmen crackdown vigils. They face up to 10 years in prison. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- The Russian justice ministry designates independent news outlet Mediazona a "foreign agent" for a second time, accusing it of publishing false information about law enforcement. [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- In Mexico, Sinaloan governor Rubén Rocha Moya resumes office after a four-month suspension while contesting U.S. drug-trafficking charges and an extradition request. Mexican prosecutors say they find insufficient evidence linking him to criminal conduct. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Sports
- 2026–27 Malaysia Super League
- In association football, Johor Darul Ta'zim claims a world record for the longest unbeaten run in top-flight league play, reaching 109 matches after defeating Kuching City 3–0 in Malaysia's Super League. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- 2026–27 DFB-Pokal
- 85 people were injured, including 35 police officers, after Kaiserslautern fans launched flares towards the main stand, while Mannheim fans stormed the pitch, causing the match between Kaiserslautern and Mannheim to be temporarily interrupted. [src: (Goal)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 22
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
- Israeli invasion of Syria
- The Israeli Army Radio reports that the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) launched a drone strike against a militant in southern Syria whom they accuse of prepping an improvised explosive device (IED) attack against Israeli troops currently occupying the region. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- Syrian state media reports that an IED struck a bus carrying security forces on the Maarounah–Al-Tall road near Damascus, injuring several passengers. [src: (AFP via Arab News Japan)]
- Gaza war
- Tunnel warfare in the Gaza Strip
- The IDF says that Sharif al-Hasanat, an alleged Hamas company commander affiliated with the Deir al-Balah Battalion of the Al-Qassam Brigades, was killed in an airstrike in Gaza, violating the ongoing ceasefire. [src: (The Times of Israel)] [src: (JFeed)]
Business and economy
- Canada–United States relations
- 2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico
- The United States imposes 50% tariffs on about US$20 billion of Canadian goods after trade talks fail to produce an agreement. Canadian prime minister Mark Carney says Canada will impose equivalent retaliatory tariffs. [src: (AFP via Daily Tribune)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Sudan's industry ministry establishes a high-level committee to rehabilitate industrial zones in Khartoum State that were damaged during the ongoing civil war along with helping shuttered factories resume production. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Zamboye mine collapse
- The Central African Republic's government closes down a gold mine site in Zamboye that killed over 100 people after it collapsed, citing non-compliance with regulatory procedures. [src: (AP)]
- The Indian Coast Guard launches a rescue operation after a Panama–flagged cargo bulk carrier sunk off the coast of eastern India. [src: (Reuters)]
- Seven people are killed, including two police officers, and several others are injured in a three-vehicle collision on the A66 road in Middlesbrough, North Yorkshire, England. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Five people are killed in a head-on road collision along the Lagos–Badagry Expressway near Lagos, Nigeria. [src: (The Daily Post Nigeria)]
International relations
- Pastoral trips made by Pope Leo XIV
- Pope Leo XIV makes a half-day papal visit to San Marino, including meeting with the Captains Regent, the local religious community, and visiting the Basilica of Saint Marinus. [src: (Vatican News)] [src: (Holy See)]
Law and crime
- The Pacific Islands Forum Fisheries Agency reports that authorities in Kiribati, Palau, and Papua New Guinea have detained four Chinese and Indonesian fishing vessels for alleged illegal fishing or licence violations during a regional enforcement operation across the Pacific Ocean. [src: (AFP via Daily Tribune)]
- American far-right activist Jake Lang, who was pardoned last year for his role in the January 6 riot at the United States Capitol, is arrested during a protest in Minneapolis, Minnesota, U.S. [src: (The Detroit News)] [src: (Minnesota Star Tribune)]
Science and technology
- A humanoid robot at the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, China, runs 100 meters in 9.39 seconds, surpassing a record set by Usain Bolt of 9.58 seconds at the World Athletics Championships in 2009. [src: (NBC News)]
Sports
- 2026 IndyCar Series
- In open-wheel racing, the Freedom 250 Grand Prix kicks off in Washington, D.C. on the National Mall to commemorate the 250th anniversary of the U.S. Declaration of Independence, with former NASCAR driver Jeff Gordon winning the International Race of Champions.
