[src: (The Athletic via The New York Times)] [src: (Motorsport)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 23
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Iran claims to have blacklisted 45 tankers in the Strait of Hormuz that breached its rules for crossing the waterway, with the Persian Gulf Strait Authority threatening fines, detainments, and confiscations against the named vessels. [src: (Reuters)]
- The Iran parliament's National Security and Foreign Policy Commission approves a draft allowing Iran to charge ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- Gaza war
- Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip
- Two Israeli airstrikes kill two people, including a four-year-old boy, in the Gaza Strip in violation of the October 2025 ceasefire. [src: (Reuters)]
- Somali Civil War
- Controversies of Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
- At least ten people are killed and several others injured in clashes between federal forces and residents protesting a controversial demolition and forced eviction in Yaaqshid neighbourhood of Mogadishu. [src: (FTL Somalia)] [src: (Garowe Online)] [src: (Shabelle Media)]
- The Turkish Armed Forces carries out an airstrike in Garmaal, Puntland, killing at least four people, in response to the previous hijacking of a Cameroon-flagged vessel by Somali pirates, which was transporting military equipment to the Camp TURKSOM in Mogadishu. The authorities of Puntland identified the victims as civilian fishermen. [src: (Somali Guardian)]
- Kivu conflict
- M23 campaign
- The Democratic Republic of the Congo and the M23 rebel group agree on a roadmap for further peace negotiations under the Doha Framework Agreement after talks in Switzerland. [src: (AFP via The Hindu)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Sudan's defence ministry says that the country's armed forces (SAF) have shot down a "hostile" drone from Ethiopia entering its airspace, which was seen flying over the Blue Nile region. [src: (Saudi Gazette)] [src: (Sudan Horizon)]
- The SAF-allied Joint Forces says that they have destroyed a Rapid Support Forces convoy in the northern desert bordering Libya, along with capturing several vehicles and drone equipment. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Haitian crisis
- At least 47 people are killed and over 50 others are kidnapped by armed gangs in Kenscoff, Ouest department, Haiti, in one of the largest mass kidnappings in the conflict. [src: (AP)]
- Mali War
- The Tuareg-led Azawad Liberation Front releases 22 Malian soldiers, some held for more than three years, in exchange for at least eight of its fighters and several civilian detainees. [src: (AFP via Macau Business)]
- Mexican drug war
- Iván Manjarrez, a La Línea ringleader accused of controlling illegal logging in the Chihuahua Mountains, is killed during a security operation in Bocoyna Municipality, Chihuahua, Mexico. [src: (El Heraldo de Chihuahua in Spanish)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 United States wildfires
- 2026 Nevada wildfires
- The Hawk Fire near Reno, Nevada, U.S., grows to more than 20 square miles (53 sq. km.) and spreads across the Peavine Peak of Humboldt–Toiyabe National Forest, prompting evacuations. [src: (PBS)] [src: (Reuters)]
- A earthquake strikes southern Ibaraki Prefecture in Japan, injuring 45 people. [src: (The Nikkei)] [src: (FNN)]
- At least 30 people are killed and six more are wounded when a landfill collapses in Conakry, Guinea. [src: (BBC News)]
- The Indian Coast Guard and Navy's Eastern Naval Command reports that two crew members from the Panama-flagged MV Ocean Winner have been rescued after it sank off the coast of Bay of Bengal in eastern India. [src: (Times of India)] [src: (New Indian Express)]
- Four people are found dead after a fire at a restaurant in Thusis, Switzerland, two days ago. The search and rescue operation are concluded. [src: (RSI)]
Law and crime
- Billings, Montana massacre
- Eight people, including four children, are killed in a domestic shooting and house fire in Billings, Montana, United States. The gunman kills himself at the scene. [src: (AP)]
- The Israel Defense Forces's Duvdevan Unit says that they arrested four Palestinians over the weekend, including two allegedly affiliated with the Islamic State. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Kazakh legislative election
- Kazakhstanis vote to elect 145 members to the 1st convocation of the unicameral Kurultai following the passage of the new constitution on 15 March. Contesting parties must get at least five percent of the vote in order for lists to gain proportional representation. [src: (AP)] [src: (DW)]
Sports
- 2026 IndyCar Series
- Freedom 250 Grand Prix
- In open-wheel racing, American auto racing driver Kyle Kirkwood wins the IndyCar Freedom 250 Grand Prix event at the National Mall in Washington D.C., United States. [src: (The Athletic via The New York Times)] [src: (The Indianapolis Star)]
- 2026 WNBA season
- In basketball, former National Basketball Association player Enes Kanter Freedom is ejected from a WNBA game between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena after being confronted by Natasha Cloud for his controversy in declaring for the 2027 WNBA draft. [src: (AP)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 24
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Operation Southern Spear
- United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear
- The United States Southern Command's Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere launches a strike on a vessel in the eastern Pacific Ocean on alleged drug traffickers, killing two people. [src: (CNN)] [src: (PBS)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian war, Ukraine–United Kingdom relations
- British prime minister Andy Burnham, during a visit to Kyiv, confirms that he has approved supplying Ukraine with the classified blueprints to produce Storm Shadow cruise missiles despite Russian threats against such a move, which will give Ukrainian forces the ability to strike key targets deep inside Russian territory. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (The Japan Times)]
- Kharkiv strikes
- A Russian missile strike on the outskirts of Kharkiv kills three people and leaves eight others wounded. [src: (TRT World)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Darfur campaign
- Drone strikes by the Sudanese Armed Forces hits several Rapid Support Forces Paramilitary targets in Nyala, South Darfur, Sudan, hours after a cargo aircraft landed in the area. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- South Sudanese Civil War
- Jonglei clashes
- Two peacekeepers from Ethiopia of the United Nations Mission in South Sudan are killed in an ambush by unknown gunmen in Jonglei State, South Sudan. Three more peacekeepers, two policemen and two civilians are also wounded. [src: (RFI in French)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- International sanctions against Iran
- United States sanctions against Iran
- U.S. treasury secretary Scott Bessent announces Operation Economic Outcast, a campaign involving new sanctions against Iran, in an effort to isolate the regime. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Politico)]
- Iranian economic crisis
- The Iranian rial reaches 2.02 million rials ahead of the U.S. dollar, a record-low, ahead of U.S. sanctions. [src: (Time)]
- France–Saudi Arabia relations
- French president Emmanuel Macron and Saudi Arabia crown prince Mohammed bin Salman reach an agreement to build a Dragon Ball Z theme park worth €6 billion (US$7 million) in Paris, France. [src: (France 24)] [src: (CNBC)]
Health and environment
- 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
- The Arkansas Department of Health reports seven new cases of cyclosporiasis in the state, including the first cases in Ashley and Cleburne counties, amidst a decline in the outbreak across the United States. [src: (Arkansas Democrat-Gazette)]
International relations
- Syria–United States relations
- The United States formally removes Syria from its designated state sponsors of terrorism list. [src: (AFP via The Straits Times)] [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
Law and crime
- War crimes in the Syrian civil war
- Syria's Grand Mufti Ahmad Badreddin Hassoun is found guilty of committing war crimes spanning nearly 14 years of civil war under Bashar al-Assad's former regime and is sentenced to life in prison. [src: (AP)] [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (DW)]
- Former British snooker player Graeme Dott is found guilty of sexually abusing two primary school children. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (The Guardian)] 
- South African police arrests four people in connection of the murder of former professional boxer Zolani Tete. [src: (Sahara Reporters)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Kazakh legislative election
- The Central Election Commission of Kazakhstan declares the preliminary results from yesterday's election, stating that Ädilet secured 71% of the vote. [src: (Reuters)]
Sports
- In tennis, Philippine tennis player Alexandra Eala becomes the highest-ranked female player in Southeast Asian history after reaching rank 18. [src: (Yahoo! Sports)] [src: WTA)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 26
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- 2026 Iran–Oman negotiations
- The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps say Iran and Oman have agreed to share revenues from the Strait of Hormuz and define their respective maritime areas, while negotiations continue over reopening the waterway amid the war. [src: (AFP via The Borneo Post)]
- Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi says that Iran will not allow military vessels to transit through the strait under the proposed agreement. [src: (AP)] [src: (Military.com)]
- Gaza war
- The Israel Defense Forces says that they have killed several Hamas members in airstrikes in the Gaza Strip city of Jabalia, including on a structure allegedly used as a storage facility for weapons. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- An overnight Ukrainian drone attack "completely destroys" a Wildberries depot in Tambov Oblast, Russia. [src: (Reuters)]
- A man and a 14-year-old child are killed in Lipetsk Oblast, and a woman is killed in Belgorod Oblast, in Ukrainian drone strikes. The Russian defence ministry says its forces have shot down 426 Ukrainian drones overnight. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Luhansk Oblast campaign
- Nine people are killed after a Ukrainian strike on a bus in Russian-occupied Luhansk. [src: (Reuters)]
- Central African Republic Civil War
- Cambodia deploys 184 peacekeepers, including 28 women, to the Central African Republic as part of a peacekeeping mission by the United Nations. [src: (Khmer Times)] [src: (Xinhua)]
Arts and culture
- 2026 anti-immigrant movement and xenophobia in South Africa
- A spokesperson for Malian singer Salif Keita confirms that he has cancelled all upcoming concerts in South Africa over its response to anti-migrant protests in the country. [src: (Channels TV)] [src: (Arbiterz)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Nepal–Tibet floods
- Flash floods and mudslides along the Trishuli River impact between Nepal and Tibet, China. At least 160 people are killed, hundreds are injured and 463 others, including over 200 tourists, are reported missing in Nepal, while Chinese Communist Party officials report three deaths and 265 missing in Tibet, severely affecting Gyirong County and its port. [src: (AFP via Jamaica Observer)] [src: (AP)] [src: (BBC News)]
- Nepali officials say bridges, roads, power stations, and entire villages have been swept away by the flash flooding with some areas still completely cut-off from search and rescue efforts. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (The National)]
- At least 15 infants are killed and another is injured after a fire at a state-run hospital in Islamabad, Pakistan. [src: (The Globe and Mail)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- Twelve people are killed and at least 54 others are injured as wildfires spread across northeastern Algeria during a severe heat wave, with deaths reported in Béjaïa, Jijel, and Tizi Ouzou provinces. [src: (AFP via Gulf News)]
Health and environment
- Artificial intelligence in healthcare
- The University College London reports that neurosurgeons in London, England, have performed the first AI-assisted brain surgery at the National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery in a 48-year old patient who was diagnosed with a brain tumor in 2024. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (Sky News)] [src: (UCL)]
- Nineteen cases of Japanese encephalitis are confirmed in Madhesh Province, Nepal, causing six deaths. [src: (Nepal News)]
- The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approves the daraxonrasib drug as a treatment for metastatic pancreatic cancer, making it the first RAS inhibitor drug to be approved for the disease. This came after a previous study showed that it nearly doubled the survival rate for patients compared to chemotherapy. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (Reuters)]
International relations
- South Korea–United States relations, Japan–United States relations
- The U.S. Pacific Command announces that the United States will conduct trilateral military exercises with South Korea's armed forces and Japan's self-defense forces despite U.S. president Donald Trump scaling back on the recent Ulchi-Freedom Guardian exercises. [src: (AA via TRT World)] [src: (Korea Herald)]
Law and crime
- Aftermath of the September 11 attacks
- The U.S. military trial for al-Qaeda militant Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, the alleged mastermind of the September 11 attacks, is set for June 2028 alongside three co-conspirators. [src: (NBC News)] [src: (Sky News)]
- Lawsuits involving Meta Platforms
- Meta Platforms agrees to pay up to $16.7 billion to settle claims by 29 U.S. states over alleged harms to young users and to impose new usage limits and safeguards for teenagers on its social media platforms Facebook and Instagram. [src: (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]
- Terrorism in the United States
- The United States designates the Italy-based Autistici/Inventati, the UK-based Palestine Action, and pro-Palestinian group Masar Badil as terrorist organizations, citing alleged involvement in politically motivated violence and extremist activity. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Russia orders the arrest of German Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung journalist , charging him in absentia over comments interpreted as calling for the killing of Russians, a crime punishable by up to six years in prison. [src: (News.az)]
- Two people are killed and nine others are seriously injured in a vehicle-ramming attack against pedestrians after a fight near a train station in Caen, Normandy, France. The perpetrator is arrested. [src: (France 24)]
Politics and elections
- Immigration policy of the second Trump administration
- The United States Department of State suspends immigrant visa appointments at all embassies and consulates worldwide while training consular staff on screening applicants for potential dependence on public benefits. [src: (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]
- Deogratius Ndejembi is appointed as Vice President of Tanzania, replacing Emmanuel Nchimbi who resigned yesterday. [src: (The Tanzania Times)]
Sports
- Pro Bowl Games
- In American football, the National Football League announces the elimination of the Pro Bowl Games. [src: (The New York Times)] [src: (Reuters)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 27
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Gaza–Israel conflict
- Gaza war
- Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip
- Three Palestinians are reported to be killed in strikes in the Gaza Strip, violating the October 2025 ceasefire. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Gaza war hostage crisis
- The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) and its Spokesperson's Unit confirms Al-Qassam Brigades commander Ismail Mohammad Ibrahim Barim, who held Edan Alexander, Avera Mengistu, and Matan Zangauker as hostages, was killed in a strike in Khan Yunis. [src: (The Times of Israel)] [src: (Israel National News)] [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- The IDF also confirms that they have recently killed two Hamas militants that invaded the Re'im Base in Re'im during the October 7 attacks in separate strikes in the Gaza Strip, including a body guard to former leader Yahya Sinwar and a Nukhba forces militant. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- It is reported that Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu held secret meetings with Hamas during the 2014 Gaza War. The Prime Minister's Office denies the reports. [src: (The Times of Israel)] [src: (Ynetnews)]
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- Qatar as a mediator in conflict
- Qatari prime minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani talks with Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi in Tehran, including on the Strait of Hormuz and efforts to end the war. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign
- United States Central Command commander Brad Cooper says that the military has cleared all Iranian naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and its routes. [src: (The Hill)]
- Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei says that Iran is preparing a set of conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz after mediators called for them to do so. [src: (Reuters)]
- The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reports that a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was hit by an "unknown projectile", causing a fire that was later extinguished. [src: (Marine Insight)]
- Sudanese Civil Wars
- Sudanese civil war
- Blue Nile campaign
- Sudan's army repels a Rapid Support Forces attack on the town of Al-Keli in the Blue Nile region. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Battle of Khartoum
- Sudan's Security Affairs Coordination Committee lifts the curfew and state of emergency on the capital Khartoum after two years. [src: (Middle East Monitor)] [src: (BBC)]
- Around 12 people are reported killed in a airstrike near the border with Chad. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Sudanese nomadic conflicts
- Around 49 people are killed in a cattle raid on the Machar-Pakuek cattle camp in Mading Juer Boma in Tonj North County of South Sudan's Warrap state. [src: (MENA via The New Arab)]
- Kivu conflict
- M23 campaign
- Four people are killed after an unconfirmed civilian or military airplane is shot down with a surface-to-air missile near Minembwe, Democratic Republic of the Congo. [src: (Noveau Media)]
- Mexican drug war
- NORAD and the U.S. Northern Command say that the U.S. military used a laser weapon against three drones belonging to Mexican drug cartels. [src: (Military Times)]
Business and economy
- South Korean company SK Gas pays a record US$5.3 million for priority passage of the LPG tanker G. Spirit through the Panama Canal before El Niño-related transit restrictions reduced daily crossings. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Disasters and accidents
- Wildfires in 2026
- 2026 Canadian wildfires
- In Canada, British Columbia ends its state of emergency previously imposed on August 8 in response to wildfires that killed one person. [src: (The Canadian Press News)] [src: (CTV News)]
- A section of the Trans-Canada Highway in the Fraser Canyon reopens after being closed for seven weeks due to the wildfires. [src: (Redfm)] [src: (CTV News)]
- Algerian president Abdelmadjid Tebboune declares three days of national mourning after 12 people were reported to be killed in wildfires in northeastern Jijel. [src: (Africanews)]
- 2026 Flores earthquake
- The death toll from the earthquake that struck the Flores island in East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, rises to 111, with 176,000 people displaced. [src: (A News)] [src: (AA)]
- 2026 Nepal–Tibet floods
- The United States Geological Survey says a glacial collapse and debris flow, not an earthquake, caused the seismic event near the Nepal–Tibet border and subsequent flooding that killed at least 392 people and left over 900 more missing. [src: (BBC News)]
- Six people die after a pump boat carrying 13 passengers capsizes while crossing the Mapanuepe Lake in San Marcelino, Zambales, Philippines. Three others remain missing. [src: (The Philippine Star)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- The Democratic Republic of the Congo begins vaccination for the Ebola outbreak in Kisangani, Tshopo, with healthcare and front line workers among the first to receive the vaccine. [src: (Africanews)]
- The World Health Organization declares the Ebola outbreak in Uganda over after the country went 42 days without a new case of the virus. [src: (Euronews)]
- 2026 European heatwaves
- Germany's Robert Koch Institute estimates 15,800 heat-related deaths during summer 2026, the highest total in a decade of monitoring, as repeated heat waves push temperatures above . [src: (Kurdistan 24)]
International relations
- Malaysia–Myanmar relations
- Malaysia says that 1,476 Burmese people will be voluntarily repatriated on September 29 in the first phase of a return program agreed with Myanmar, using Myanmar naval vessels. [src: (AFP via The Manila Times)]
Law and crime
- Two people are killed in a stabbing at a private school in Gosen-Neu Zittau, Brandenburg, Germany. A suspect is arrested. [src: (Xinhua)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Zambian general election
- Zambian presidential candidate Brian Mundubile surrenders to police and is questioned over an alleged national security threat after two weeks in hiding following the disputed presidential election, in which he finished second. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Forced contraception of women in Greenland
- Denmark's parliament passes legislation granting 300,000 kr. (US$46,758) in compensation to each Greenlandic woman affected by non-consensual contraception administered under a Danish birth-control program in the 1960s and 1970s. [src: (BBC News)]
- U.S. president Donald Trump signs an executive order directing federal agencies to call Lake Ontario "Lake America." The change applies only to U.S. federal usage; Canada need not adopt it, and no international authority exclusively determines names of shared waters. [src: (AP)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- King Rukidi IV of Uganda's Tooro Kingdom, the youngest person to reign as a monarch, dies at the age of 34. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (NTV Uganda)]
Science and technology
- August 2026 lunar eclipse
- A near-total partial lunar eclipse occurs over Africa, the Americas, and Europe. [src: (TimeandDate)]
- The Korea AeroSpace Administration says that the Nuri will launch 15 satellites, a record, into space from the Naro Space Center in South Korea's Goheung County on October 7. [src: (Korea Times)] [src: (Yonhap)]
Sports
- 2026 Diamond League
- In athletics, Brazilian Alison dos Santos and American Masai Russell break the world records in men's 400 metres hurdles (45.80 seconds) and women's 100 metres hurdles (12.09 seconds), respectively, at the 2026 Weltklasse Zürich in Zurich, Switzerland. [src: (Reuters)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 28
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Sudanese civil war
- Blue Nile campaign
- Sudan's Rapid Support Forces says that they have seized the Bakori and Surkum Sudanese Army bases in the southeastern Blue Nile region alongside Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Kordofan campaign
- Emergency Lawyers, an independent group documenting atrocities in Sudan, reports that eight civilians have been killed in drone strikes in the Sowdari District of North Kordofan. [src: (AP)] [src: (Asharq Al Awsat)]
- Gaza war
- Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Gaza war
- The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) says that they have killed three Palestinian militants, including Islamic Jihad (PIJ) senior member Qais Bitawi, in a drone strike in the Israel-occupied West Bank city of Jenin. The PIJ later confirms Bitawi's death. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Kyiv strikes
- A Russian drone strike hits a supply depot in Bucha, Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine, triggering explosions and a fire, killing at least 37 people and forcing the evacuation of almost 400 residents. Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy says explosives stored near homes worsened the disaster. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (CNN)]
Arts and culture
- American country singer-songwriter Dolly Parton becomes the most-streamed artist globally following her death, according to data from Luminate. [src: (AP)]
Business and economy
- The Japanese finance ministry says it spent a record ¥15.4 trillion (US$96 billion) between July 30 and August 26 to support the yen, marking the country's largest monthly currency intervention on record. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Disasters and accidents
- Twenty-seven people are killed and seven people are injured after a vehicle carrying churchgoers collides head-on with a truck in Chivhu, Zimbabwe. [src: (MSN)]
Health and environment
- Seventh cholera pandemic
- Nigeria records 65,000 cases of cholera, across 35 states, alongside 10,000 cases of diphtheria. Additionally, NCDC director Jide Idris reports a decline in cholera cases but also warn that transmission of cases remain ongoing. [src: (The Nation NG)] [src: (Daily Trust)]
International relations
- United States–Venezuela relations
- The United States and Venezuela agree to expand U.S. access to Venezuelan oil reserves under a deal involving US$100 billion in private investment, while Venezuela retains ownership of its petroleum resources. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Law and crime
- Corruption in Ecuador
- An Ecuadorian court convicts former president Lenín Moreno of bribery linked to the construction of the Coca Codo Sinclair plant in Napo Province. His wife, Rocío González Navas, and daughter are also found guilty. [src: (Reuters)]
- Protests against Donald Trump
- Demonstrators gather in Washington, D.C., United States, to protest against the Trump administration's alleged efforts to rollback voting and civil rights, 63 years after the March on Washington rally by civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr. [src: (Reuters)]
- Scam centers in Cambodia
- The Cambodian government says that they have closed more than 700 online scam centers and arrested nearly 30,000 suspects, including 15 senior officials and law-enforcement officers, during a year-long crackdown on cybercrime networks. [src: (Euronews)]
- Two men steal a 200-carat platinum-and-diamond necklace from the Museum of Applied Arts in Vienna, Austria, after smashing a display case with a hammer and fleeing, according to Austrian police. [src: (AFP via CBS News)]
- Two teenagers are arrested in Israel for allegedly pledging allegiance to ISIS and plotting an attack on security forces at the Temple Mount and an IDF base in northern Israel. [src: (Ynetnews)] [src: (The Times of Israel)]
Politics and elections
- Death and state funeral of Harald V
- King Harald V of Norway dies at the age of 89 after a 35-year reign and is succeeded by his son Haakon VIII. [src: (AP)] [src: (BBC News)] [src: (CNN)]
- Forced contraception of women in Greenland
- Greenland establishes a truth and reconciliation commission after experts conclude that a decades-long Danish contraceptive program violated Inuit women's rights but disagree on whether it constituted genocide. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Serbia justice minister Nenad Vujić says that convicted war criminal Ratko Mladić will be buried with state and military honors following his death at the United Nations Detention Unit at the Hague. [src: (CNN)] [src: (Serbian Times)]
Sports
- 2026–27 NHL season
- In ice hockey, the Colorado Avalanche sign defenceman and alternate captain Cale Makar to an eight-year extension worth US$163.2 million, the largest contract in National Hockey League history. He is the first player to exceed $20 million in average annual value. [src: (The Athletic via The New York Times)] [src: (CBS Sports)] [src: (ESPN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 29
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- A tanker is struck by a unknown projectile while transiting through the Strait of Hormuz near Khasab, Oman, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- Gaza war
- Attacks on health facilities during the Gaza war
- Israel strikes the Shuhada al-Aqsa Hospital in the Deir al-Balah area of the Gaza Strip, killing three people, in violation of the October 2025 ceasefire. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) stated that they targeted a Hamas commander who, according to it, was hiding within the compound of the hospital. [src: (MENA via The New Arab)]
- The IDF confirms that they have killed Nukhba Force commander Hani Abd al-Hai Fakhri Mazloum and Hamas sniper Hassan Zidan Hassan Deiri in separate strikes in the northern Gaza Strip. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- A Ukrainian drone attack on Shebekino, Belgorod Oblast, Russia, kills three people and damages residential buildings, according to the regional emergency response center. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Somali Civil War
- Piracy off the coast of Somalia
- The Cameroon-flagged Turkish cargo ship MV LUTUF, which was hijacked on August 17, is freed by Somali and Turkish forces off the coast of Somalia. Conversely, the Puntland ministry of security says a ransom was paid. [src: (AP)] [src: (Garowe Online)] [src: (Hiiraan Online)]
- 2026 Nigerien coup attempt
- Nigerien television confirms that dissenting elements of the Niger Armed Forces attempted a coup in the nation's capital, Niamey. Attacks are reported on Diori Hamani International Airport and the Presidential Palace. [src: (AP)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Mali War
- Tuareg rebels free 60 Malian soldiers in exchange for army officer-turned-defector Inkinane Ag Attaher. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Nepal–Tibet floods
- Nepal–United States relations
- The U.S. State Department says that the U.S. will provide US$3.6 million in humanitarian aid to Nepal in wake of the floods. [src: (Malay Mail)]
- The death toll from flash floods in Nepal rises to 669, with more than 2,400 people reported missing. [src: (NBC News)]
- 2026 Grand Canyon flood
- A flash flood in the Grand Canyon National Park in Arizona, United States, leaves about 15 people missing and prompts the evacuation of at least 62 others. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- A person is rescued while four people are missing when a sport utility vehicle plunges into a river after a bridge in Tarlac City, Philippines, collapses. The bridge has been serving as an alternative route as another partially collapsed days prior amid monsoon rains. [src: (Philippine Daily Inquirer)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Icelandic European Union membership negotiations referendum
- Iceland rejects restarting membership negotiations with the EU in a referendum. [src: (RÚV)]
- Pope Leo XIV publishes a motu proprio to amend the Code of Canons of the Eastern Churches, granting them the ability to remove their respective Patriarchs via a two-thirds vote with papal approval, if the relationship between them and the council is broken beyond repair. [src: (Vatican News)] [src: (National Catholic Register)]
Sports
- 2026 Women's FIH Hockey World Cup
- 2026 Women's FIH Hockey World Cup final
- In field hockey, Argentina beat the Netherlands in the final after a 1–1 draw and a penalty shoot-out to secure their third Women's World Cup title. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Women's NORCECA Volleyball Championship
- Canada at the 2028 Summer Olympics, Volleyball at the 2028 Summer Olympics
- In volleyball, the Canadian women’s national team qualifies for the upcoming Summer Olympics in Los Angeles, California, U.S., their first qualification since 1996 following a victory against the Dominican Republic in the Women's NORCECA Volleyball Continental Championship. [src: (CBC)]
- Moses Itauma vs Filip Hrgovic
- In boxing, Filip Hrgović defeats Moses Itauma by ninth-round stoppage to win the vacant IBF heavyweight title. Hrgović becomes the first Croatian heavyweight boxing world champion. [src: (AFP via The Philippine Star)]
- In tennis, former player Roger Federer is inducted into the player category, while former player and current sportscaster Mary Carillo is inducted into the contributor category of the International Tennis Hall of Fame respectively. [src: (Sports Business Journal)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 3
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Gaza war
- Gaza peace plan
- A Board of Peace envoy meets Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and urges a halt in strikes across the Gaza Strip. However, they also announce that Israel will not withdraw from the enclave until Hamas completely disarms. [src: (The New Region)] [src: (The Washington Post)]
- Casualties of the Gaza war
- The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs reports that dozens of children and civilians have been killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza over the weekend, violating the ongoing ceasefire. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Two Palestinian civilians are killed in an Israeli missile strike near a mosque which targeted a civilian vehicle southwest of Gaza City. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- Gaza war hostage crisis
- The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) claim that they have killed Palestinian Islamic Jihad commander Mahmoud Fatair, who took part in the abduction of Rom Braslavski, in the Deir al-Balah area of the Gaza Strip during the Nova music festival massacre on October 7, 2023. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- The IDF claim that they have killed two Hamas militants in separate airstrikes in central Gaza and the Shati camp in Gaza City respectively, violating the ongoing ceasefire. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- Red Sea crisis
- Shipping data shows that two tanker ships carrying oil from Saudi Arabia, the Suezmax Malta-flagged Lesvos and the VLCC Desh Vaibhav, have exited the Red Sea through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait. [src: (Reuters)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- At least seven people, including three children, are killed and 40 others are injured when drone debris falls on a crowded beach in Gelendzhik, Krasnodar Krai, Russia. [src: (CNN)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Venezuela earthquakes
- The death toll from the two earthquakes that hit Venezuela in June exceeds 6,000 people according to figures from lawmaker Jorge Rodríguez. [src: (Reuters)]
- At least fourteen people are killed in a series of floods in southern India. [src: (Reuters)]
- Guatemala's disaster agency declares a nationwide orange alert following a major eruption of Fuego volcano and begins evacuating two nearby villages. [src: (AFP via RNZ)]
Health and environment
- 2020–2026 H5N1 outbreak
- Scotland's NatureScot denies a 2026 licence for hunting northern gannets on Sula Sgeir, citing possible harm to the local gannet population after recent bird-flu deaths. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- 2026 European heatwaves
- Italy experiences its fourth heatwave of the summer with the health ministry issuing red alerts for a record 25 cities. [src: (AA)]
- 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
- Michigan, U.S., reports the first two deaths of the current cyclosporiasis outbreak, which is caused by cyclospora cayetanensis. [src: (AP)]
Law and crime
- COVID-19 pandemic in Poland
- The Polish health ministry appeals a Brussels court ruling that ordered the country to accept and pay approximately €1.3 billion for unwanted COVID-19 vaccine doses produced by Pfizer and BioNTech. [src: (Politico EU)]
- South African news outlets report that over 170 people have been murdered in the Western Cape, South Africa in the past 2 weeks. [src: (Independent Online)]
Politics and elections
- Human rights in Russia
- Russian opposition politician Boris Nadezhdin, who attempted to contest the 2024 presidential election on a platform against the Russo-Ukrainian war, announces that he has fled the country to France following growing pressure on him and his family. [src: (The Moscow Times)]
Sports
- 2026 WTA Tour
- 2026 Mubadala DC Open
- In tennis, Alexandra Eala becomes the first Filipino player and the first player from Southeast Asia to win a WTA Tour title after defeating Jessica Pegula 4–6, 6–4, 6–0 to win the women's singles title at the 2026 Washington DC Open. [src: (AFP via RFI)] [src: (ESPN)]
- In horse racing, Churchill Downs Incorporated and the New York Racing Association announce a new championship series for 3-year old Thoroughbreds beginning in 2027, involving the Kentucky Derby and Belmont Stakes, but notably omitting the traditional middle leg of the U.S. Triple Crown, the Preakness Stakes. [src: (Courier Journal)] [src: (The Daily Gazette)]
- Major League Soccer, the top flight of men's soccer in the U.S. and Canada, announces that Larry Berg, currently a co-owner of Los Angeles FC (LAFC) in that league, will succeed Don Garber as league commissioner at the start of 2027. Berg will sell his interest in LAFC before assuming his new position. [src: (AP)] [src: (The Guardian)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 30
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
- Iran launches ballistic missiles at U.S. military bases in Jordan. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- A spokesperson for the United States Central Command reports that the U.S. military has launched strikes on two Iranian rocket launchers at Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz that were used by Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, its first strikes against the country since July. [src: (Axios)] [src: (NBC News)]
- Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
- Syrian security forces says that they have killed Firas Abdul Karim Hammoud, a army commander who served under ousted former Syrian president Bashar al-Assad, after he opened fire on forces as they tried to arrest him. [src: (Asharq Al Awsat)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- A Ukrainian missile strike on Belgorod, Russia, kills two people and injures 16 others, according to regional acting governor Alexander Shuvaev. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (Xinhua)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign, Battle of Barah
- Sudan's doctors network reports that five civilians are killed and thousands are displaced during attacks by Rapid Support Forces in Bara, North Kordofan. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- 2026 Nigerien coup attempt
- Niger's army says that they have regained control of an airbase after it was attacked by mutinous soldiers yesterday. [src: (Reuters)]
- Mexican drug war
- Mexican security forces kill Los Reyes cartel leader Luis Enrique Barragán Chávez and his bodyguard during an operation in Tocumbo, Michoacán, after coming under gunfire. [src: (AA)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Indonesia wildfires
- 2026 East Malaysia haze, Endangerment of orangutans
- An orangutan named Sampurna is reported to be rescued from a haze fire zone in Ketapang, West Kalimantan, on Indonesia's Borneo island. [src: (Reuters)]
- The Japanese military ship JS Kunisaki departs from a port in Kure, Hiroshima, to help fight wildfires in Indonesia. [src: (Tempo)]
- 2026 Grand Canyon flood
- The body of one man is found near the Colorado River while 15 other people remain missing after a flash flood at Bright Angel Creek in the Grand Canyon in Arizona, United States. [src: (Euronews)]
- 2026 Nepal–Tibet floods
- Following the floods that killed over 1,000 people in Nepal and Tibet, several countries and organizations pledge over $19.8 million total in emergency humanitarian aid, including Canada, the European Union, the United Kingdom, the United States, and the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Society. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Sinking of the Filo Jet
- At least eight people are killed and 18 others are missing when a passenger ferry sailing from Northern Cyprus to Turkey capsizes in the eastern Mediterranean sea. The ship was carrying 259 passengers and 8 crew members, of which 237 people have been rescued. [src: (Sky News)] [src: (Reuters)]
- The body of the last missing individual aboard a boat capsized on Thursday on Mapanuepe Lake in San Marcelino, Zambales, Philippines, is recovered, concluding search operations with the final death toll at nine. [src: (Philippine Daily Inquirer)]
International relations
- 2026 state visit by Xi Jinping to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt
- Chinese leader Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan arrive in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, for the upcoming Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit and a state visit. [src: (AFP via RFI)] [src: (Xinhua)]
Law and crime
- One person is killed and five others are injured in a mass shooting at a rave in Aarau, Aargau, Switzerland. The perpetrator is on the run. [src: (CNN)]
- Two people are killed and nine injured during a mass shooting at a gathering in Trenton, New Jersey, United States. [src: (AA)] [src: (NBC News)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Guinea-Bissau constitutional referendum
- Bissau-Guineans vote on a constitutional referendum that proposes to expand presidential powers. [src: (AP)]
- 2026 Zambian general election
- Zambian presidential candidate Brian Mundubile is charged with treason amid an election dispute. [src: (BBC News)]
- The Korean Central News Agency reports that general No Kwang-chol has been dismissed as defence minister of North Korea, with Korean People's Army General Political Bureau director Kim Song-gi replacing him. [src: (AFP via CNA)] [src: (NK News)] 
Science and technology
- NASA launches the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope aboard a Falcon Heavy rocket from Florida, United States, to survey the universe, study dark matter and dark energy, and search for exoplanets and supernovae. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Space.com)]
Sports
- 2026 Men's FIH Hockey World Cup
- In field hockey, Germany defeats Spain 1–0 in the final to secure their fourth FIH Men's World Cup title. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 World Rowing Championships
- In rowing, the 2026 World Championships conclude in Amsterdam, Netherlands, with the host nation as the most successful team with 4 gold medals and 10 medals overall. [src: (BBC Sport)] [src: (World Rowing)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 31
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) says that a supertanker caught fire after hitting two naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC accuses the United States of responsibility for the attack, which the United States Central Command on an X post denies. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (Reuters via Arab News)]
- Saudi shipping company Bahri says that two Filipino crew members were killed after unidentified projectiles struck the oil tanker SIDR while it transited the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]
- United Arab Emirates in the 2026 Iran war
- The United Arab Emirates defense ministry reports that an Iranian drone has been intercepted over the country's airspace. Additionally, Iran's army says that they have attacked the Al Minhad Air Base, which the UAE denies. [src: (AP)]
- Gaza war
- Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip kill ⁠at least five people. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Aerial warfare in the Russo-Ukrainian war, Kyiv strikes
- Ukraine tightens security measures for Kyiv's public transport, schools, and parliament amid increased Russian drone attacks, including restrictions on large school gatherings, possible remote learning, and expanded shelter arrangements. [src: (AFP via Bangkok Post)]
- Myanmar civil war
- Twelve civilians are killed in an attack by alleged armed People's Defence Force members after they claim to have entered a village in Mahlaing Township, Mandalay Region, Myanmar. [src: (Myanmar Digital News)]
- Colombian conflict
- A car bomb outside a police station in Los Patios, Norte de Santander, Colombia, kills one civilian and injures 11 others, including two officers. Police attribute the attack to the National Liberation Army. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Mexican drug war
- A car bomb outside a police station in Ojocaliente, Zacatecas, México, leaves ten people injured. Authorities arrest one suspect related to the attack. [src: (AA)]
Arts and culture
- Dale Sanders reclaims his record of being the oldest person to hike the entire Appalachian Trail, one of the world's longest hiking-only trails, after completing it at age 91. [src: (AP)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Nepal–Tibet floods
- It is reported that school principal Rajendra Dawadi saved over 900 students and 16 faculty members at the Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School in Bidur, Nuwakot District, Nepal, 10 minutes before flash floods hit the area last week. [src: (AP)] [src: (Reuters)]
- The death toll from the flash floods in Nepal has reached past 950. Additionally, hundreds are reported to be feared stuck in hydropower tunnels in wake of the floods. [src: (AP)] [src: (CBC)]
- 2026 Grand Canyon flood
- The death toll from the flash flood in Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona, United States, last Saturday rises to two, while the number of people missing falls from more than 20 to one after park rangers locate most of those previously unaccounted for. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- 2026 Indonesia wildfires
- The Mount Sinabung stratovolcano in North Sumatra, Indonesia, erupts, sending ash 3,500 meters into the air. Residents and visitors around Lake Lau Kawar are ordered to evacuate. [src: (AA)] [src: (Antara News)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- The total amount of cases of ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceeds 6,000. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- A data from the Methane Alert and Response System reports that Turkmenistan has started the process of clearing methane leaks from its oil and gas facilities. [src: (The Guardian)]
International relations
- 2026 Bishkek SCO summit
- The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit is held in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, which coincides with the country's Independence Day and the opening ceremony of the 2026 World Nomad Games. [src: (The Times of Central Asia)] [src: (Xinhua)]
- Greece–Israel relations, 2020s European rearmament
- Israel and Greece sign a 3 billion (US$3.48 billion) arms export deal that will enable the Israeli defense ministry to build the "Achilles Shield", a multi-layered air defense array similar to the Iron Dome, made entirely by Israeli systems, including David's Sling, SPYDER, and Barak MX. [src: (DW)] [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- India–Pakistan wars and conflicts
- The Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague, Netherlands, orders India to comply with the Indus Waters Treaty and restrict work on two hydroelectric projects that could violate it. India rejects the ruling and maintains that the treaty remains suspended. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Italy–Spain relations, 2026 Ceuta migrant crisis
- Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni announces that Italy will extend its suspension of the Schengen free movement agreement with Spain for another 15 days in response to the migrant crisis event at the Ceuta border fence with Morocco. [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- Corruption in South Korea, Unification Church and politics
- A South Korean court sentences Unification Church leader Hak Ja Han to two years in prison for bribing officials, including former first lady Kim Keon Hee, in an effort to obtain policy favors. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Kidnapping of Shelly Kittleson
- A judiciary in Iraq sentences Kata'ib Hezbollah member Amir Rahim Jabbar to 15 years in prison for his role in the kidnapping of American journalist Shelly Kittleson. [src: (Asharq Al Awsat)]
- Murder of Tupac Shakur
- A jury in Las Vegas, Nevada, United States, finds former Crips gang leader Duane Davis guilty of first-degree murder for orchestrating the murder of rapper Tupac Shakur during a drive-by shooting in Paradise in 1996. [src: (ABC News)] [src: (BBC News)]
- 2026 Times Square stabbing
- A woman stabs two people in Times Square, New York City, U.S., killing a Bank of America vice president and injuring another person, before police fatally shot her after she refused commands to drop her knives. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Three people are killed in a mass shooting at a shooting range in Danilovgrad, Montenegro. The perpetrator then opened fire against police officers in the near city of Herceg Novi, before killing himself. [src: (Balkan Insight)]
- A tribunal of first instance in Brussels, Belgium, orders biometrics company Semlex and 13 other defendants to stand trial over alleged corruption, money laundering, and tax fraud linked to a passport contract in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. [src: (Reuters)]
- A suspect is arrested in relation to a mass shooting over the weekend at a rave in Aarau, Aargau, Switzerland, which killed a woman and injured five other people. [src: (DW)]
Politics and elections
- 2025–2026 Kosovo political deadlock
- Kosovo's Vetëvendosje and Democratic League parties agree to support former Constitutional Court judge Bekim Sejdiu for president, potentially ending nearly two years of political deadlock and enabling the formation of a new government. [src: (Reuters)]
Science and technology
- AI boom
- Adobe Inc. reaches a US$4 billion deal to offer free access to AI tools in Saudi Arabia with its Ministry of Communications and Information Technology and Humain. [src: (Reuters)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 4
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire, Qatar as a mediator in conflict
- Mediators from Qatar reports that progress has been made in efforts to end the war between the United States and Iran. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- The Liberian-flagged bulk carrier Minoan Pioneer is reported to be missing in the Strait of Hormuz after it was struck by a unknown projectile northeast of Oman. [src: (Seatrade Maritime News)] [src: (Al Arabiya)] [src: (Haaretz)]
- Shipping data show that Iraq has exported over 30 million barrels of crude oil through the strait between July 4 and August 4. [src: (Asharq Al-Awsat)]
- It is reported that the United States Army has used most of its ATACMS and Precision Strike missiles during the war in Iran including Operation Epic Fury. [src: (Military Times)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Gaza war
- Casualties of the Gaza war
- A mass funeral is held for 112 bodies that were recovered from a Israeli strike in the Sabra neighborhood of Gaza City during the early weeks of the war. [src: (Haaretz)]
- Red Sea crisis
- Yemen's internationally recognized government says a projectile attack sank the Indian-flagged cargo ship MSV Faize Noore Oliya in the Red Sea near the coast of Hodeidah, with all 14 crew members rescued. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Darfur campaign
- Rapid Support Forces senior commander and brigadier general Mahdi Adam Ismail, also known as Jebel Moon, is confirmed to be killed during clashes with the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Joint Forces in West Darfur, Sudan. His death is confirmed by Sudan Liberation Movement leader and Darfur governor Minni Arko Minnawi. [src: (Sudan Tribune)] [src: (Sudan Nabaa)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- Health Canada announces it has given Moderna the green light for authorization to launch a clinical trial for a mRNA Ebola vaccine aimed at targeting the Bundibugyo strain of the ebolavirus. [src: (CBC)]
- 2026 European heatwaves
- Austria records in Vienna, the highest temperature in the country's history, as a heat wave also brings wildfires and historically low Danube water levels. [src: (Xinhua)]
International relations
- Brazil–United States relations
- The United States revokes the visa of Brazilian ambassador Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti to reciprocate Brazil's denial of visas to two U.S. diplomats. The State Department says the action does not expel Viotti from the country. [src: (AFP via New Straits Times)]
Law and crime
- Colombian conflict
- The Colombian Special Jurisdiction for Peace charges 27 former FARC members, including ex-commander Timoleón Jiménez, with crimes against humanity and sexual violence committed during the conflict, including killings, disappearances, displacement, and rape. [src: (AFP via The Manila Times)]
- Kyrgyz president Sadyr Japarov signs a law banning the use of cremation for deceased human bodies in Kyrgyzstan. [src: (AKIPress)] [src: (Kabar)]
- South Sudanese police arrest 60 suspected gang members in a series of operations targeting criminal gangs, drug trafficking and youth delinquency in Juba. [src: (Sudans Post)]
- Four people are killed and four others are injured in a shooting spree by a rogue Russian soldier in Sevastopol, Russian-occupied Crimea. [src: (CBS News)]
- A 37-year-old man is killed in Plovdiv, Bulgaria after being lured through a dating app by a group of teenagers posing as an underage girl. [src: (BTA)]
Sports
- Expansion of the WNBA
- In basketball, the Women's National Basketball Association announces that the expansion team in Cleveland, Ohio, U.S., will be called the Sirens. The organization will debut in 2028. [src: (The Athletic via The New York Times)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 5
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- 2026 Iran–Oman negotiations
- Iran and Oman reach an agreement understanding on geographic coordinates for shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (Euronews)]
- 2026 Lebanon war
- 2026 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire
- Talks between Israel and Lebanon are on pause following alleged leaks and will resume tomorrow. [src: (Al-Monitor)]
- Hezbollah–Israel conflict
- The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) says they have launched strikes in southern Lebanon after alleged ceasefire violations by Hezbollah. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- Two Israeli soldiers are killed in action and four others are wounded in an improvised explosive device bombing in Majdal Zoun, South Governorate, Lebanon. [src: (Anadolu Ajansı)]
- Gaza war
- IDF chief Eyal Zamir visits the Gaza Strip to conduct an assessment in the enclave. He also states that the military will continue to operate proactively. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Kyiv strikes
- Russian forces launch dozens of ballistic missiles and drones at Kyiv, Ukraine, killing at least 17 people, including eight civilians at a railway station in Kyiv Oblast, and wounding dozens more. None of the missiles were intercepted by Ukrainian forces due to a shortage of Patriot missiles, according to president Volodymyr Zelenskyy. [src: (The Guardian)]
Disasters and accidents
- Five people are killed after two vehicles collided head-on and burst into flames on the Stuart Highway, Australia. [src: (Xinhua)]
Health and environment
- The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approves Moderna's mRNA influenza vaccine for people aged 50 and older. [src: (Time)] [src: (Reuters)]
International relations
- International sanctions against Iran
- The United States Treasury Department lifts sanctions against Fly Baghdad, which were previously imposed in 2024 over its links to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Quds Force. [src: (Al-Monitor)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Pastoral trips made by Pope Leo XIV, Argentina–Holy See relations, Holy See–Peru relations, Holy See–Uruguay relations
- The Holy See Press Office announces Pope Leo XIV will make an apostolic journey to Argentina, Uruguay, and his home country of Peru, in November, marking his first trip to Latin America in his papacy. [src: (AP)] [src: (Holy See)]
Law and crime
- Crime in Karachi
- Murder of Mir Raza Ali
- Sindh Police detain 19 people for questioning as part of the investigation into the murder of Karachi entrepreneur and Wafflix founder Mir Raza Ali. [src: (Daily Pakistan)] [src: (ARY News)]
- Far-right politics in Germany
- The Hanseatic Higher Regional Court in Hamburg, Germany, convicts seven members and one supporter of a right-wing extremist group called Last Defense Wave and sentences them to prison for attempted murder, arson, aggravated assault, and being members of a terrorist organisation for planning and carrying out arson and bomb attacks on asylum seeker shelters. [src: (AP)]
- War on drugs, Illegal drug trade in Latin America, Crime in Spain
- The Spanish Civil Guard and the Ecuadorian National Police announce they have arrested 44 people and confiscated 21 tons of cocaine as part of a multiyear investigation on a drug trafficking ring financed by investors in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. [src: (AP)]
- A drone loaded with explosives is found and defused at Leipzig/Halle Airport in Germany, while a cargo Boeing 757 had a collision with another supposed UAV at the same airport. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (DW)]
Politics and elections
- Aftermath of the July Uprising
- Former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina announces that she plans to return to the country from exile in New Delhi, India, despite facing a death sentence for her role during a violent crackdown on protesters that led to her resignation two years ago. [src: (Sky News)]
Science and technology
- 2026 SpaceX lunar impact
- The spent upper stage (COSPAR ID 2025-010D) of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket collided with the Moon near Einstein Crater. [src: (The Guardian)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 6
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Gaza war
- Ugandan authorities approve a measure to send troops from Uganda to the Gaza Strip as part of the International Stabilization Force proposed by the Board of Peace to secure the enclave following the war. [src: (NBC News)]
- Yemeni civil war
- The Houthis announce a military offensive against Saudi-backed government forces in Marib Governorate and Hadhramaut Governorate, with over 30 soldiers being killed in two missile attacks. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Ukrainian forces launch drone attacks on two oil refineries in Russia, the Yaroslavl refinery and a Bashneft-Novoil refinery in Bashkortostan, causing large fires at the facilities. [src: (BBC News)]
- Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
- Six people are killed in Russian airstrikes across Ukraine, including three civilians in Kharkiv Oblast, while a total power outage occurs in the city of Kherson after critical infrastructure was targeted overnight by Russian drones. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Antikor)]
- Ethiopian civil conflict
- 2026 Ethiopia–TPLF clashes
- It is reported that the situation on the border between Ethiopia and Sudan is calm following recent clashes between the Ethiopian Army and Tigray People's Liberation Front that sparked fears of a new conflict four years after a peace agreement was signed in 2022 to end the war in Tigray. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Haitian conflict
- The United Nations Integrated Office in Haiti reports that 613 people were killed and 375 others injured between March 6 and July 31 amid intensifying gang violence across the country. [src: (Caribbean Broadcasting Corporation)]
- Two people are killed and 13 others are injured when an explosive device detonates on a passenger minibus in Jaramana, Syria. [src: (AA)]
Business and economy
- Proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance
- The Competition and Markets Authority of the United Kingdom clears Paramount Skydance's US$110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, while culture secretary Lisa Nandy declines a public-interest review after receiving commitments on editorial independence. [src: (AA)]
Disasters and accidents
- Civil officials state that ten children passengers are reported missing after a wooden boat capsized on the Lulua River, Demba Territory, Kasai-Central, Democratic Republic of the Congo. [src: (AA)]
- Six people are killed and 19 others are injured after a bus crashed in Constantine Province, Algeria. [src: (Xinhua)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- Congolese health authorities monitor passengers from a boat near Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, after a traveler died from Ebola complications. [src: (The Washington Post)]
International relations
- 2026 Morocco–Spain border incident
- Ceuta mayor-president Juan Jesús Vivas confirms that at least 100 people died during last week's migrant surge into the Spanish autonomous city of Ceuta, while around 3,500 to 5,000 undocumented migrants remain in the city. [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- Mexican drug war
- Iguala mass kidnapping
- Former Guerrero governor Ángel Aguirre Rivero is arrested on charges of forced disappearance and obstruction of justice. He is accused of ordering the concealment of security camera footage that showed police intercepting a bus carrying students in Iguala in 2014, who have never been found. [src: (Reuters)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 7
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Operation Urja Suraksha
- Indian shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal reports that more than 4,000 seafarers from India have been repatriated and 62 Indian vessels have successfully transited through the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran war. [src: (Lokmat Times)] [src: (India New England News)]
- The Abu Dhabi National Oil Company reports that 15 of its vessels have been attacked by missiles or drones while transiting through the Strait of Hormuz since the war with Iran started on February 28. [src: (Reuters)]
- Gaza war
- Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Gaza war
- Israeli forces withdraw from the Qalandiyah refugee camp and Kafr 'Aqab neighborhood in occupied West Bank following a two-day raid, with Palestinian Authority reporting 51 injuries. [src: (Haaretz)]
- Yemeni civil war
- Houthi attacks in Marib, Yemen, kill at least eight government soldiers and two civilians and injure 26 others, as the group launches missiles, drones and shelling against military positions, residential areas, and refugee camps. [src: (AFP via The Manila Times)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Odesa strikes
- A Russian drone strike hits the Chornomorets Stadium in Odesa, Ukraine, with Odesa Oblast governor Oleh Kiper reporting that two people are injured in the strikes. [src: (Kyiv Independent)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- Sudanese armed forces repel a surprise drone attack by the Rapid Support Forces in Dilling, South Kordofan. Additionally, five civilians are reported to be killed in El Obeid, North Kordofan. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
Disasters and accidents
- Twenty people are killed and several others are injured after a fuel tanker overturns in Bangui, Central African Republic. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Sixteen people are killed and dozens others are injured in two separate road accidents in Sylhet Division and Bogra District, Bangladesh. [src: (Xinhua)]
Health and environment
- 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
- Michigan health officials lift an advisory against the consumption of lettuce in the U.S. state after reporting a decline in cases of cyclosporiasis, which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis. [src: (Reuters)]
- Brazil's National Institute for Space Research reports that deforestation of the Amazon rainforest fell to from August 2025 to July 2026, a 37% annual decline and the lowest level since the institute's satellite monitoring began in 2016. [src: (AFP via The Straits Times)]
International relations
- International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war
- The United States Senate votes 86–11 to pass a bill imposing sanctions on Russia's energy revenues, financial institutions, officials, and shadow fleet, while authorizing tariffs of up to 100% on major buyers of Russian oil and gas. The legislation will head to the U.S. House of Representatives for a vote. [src: (Reuters)]
- Pakistan–Saudi Arabia relations, Pakistan–Turkey relations, Saudi Arabia–Turkey relations
- Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey mutually sign the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, declaring that an attack on one will constitute an attack on all three. [src: (Al Arabiya)]
- Mexico–Peru relations
- The governments of Mexico and Peru reinstate diplomatic relations after agreeing to allow former Peruvian prime minister Betssy Chávez to seek asylum in Mexico. [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- Crime in Karachi
- Murder of Mir Raza Ali
- A judge of the Karachi High Court in Pakistan allows the exhumation of Mir Raza Ali's body. [src: (Dawn)]
- 2026 Nonthaburi shootings
- Nine people are killed, including the shooter, and 15 others are injured in a shooting spree between a home and the Debsirin Nonthaburi School in Bang Kruai district, Nonthaburi province, Thailand. [src: (AP)] [src: (The Guardian)]
Politics and elections
- Inauguration of Abelardo de la Espriella
- Abelardo de la Espriella is sworn in as the president of Colombia after winning the presidential election in June. [src: (AP)]
Science and technology
- Investigation of UFO reports by the United States government
- The U.S. defense department releases more classified videos and files of unidentified flying objects, including an incident in the Gulf of Oman in 2021 when United States Air Force pilots encountered a swarm of "cold orbs", describing each orb as measuring around 4 feet (1.2 metres) in diameter and moving in irregular patterns. [src: (BBC News)]
Sports
- 2026–27 Ukrainian Premier League
- The Ukrainian Premier League's FC Chornomorets Odesa announces on Telegram that its match against FC Kolos Kovalivka is postponed after its home stadium was hit by a Russian strike. [src: (Intent)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 8
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- The Abu Dhabi National Oil Company says that one of their vessels was attacked by a missile while transiting through the Strait of Hormuz during the early hours. No injuries were reported. [src: (Khaleej Times)]
- Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr says that Iran will reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the United States lifts sanctions against the country, ends the naval blockade, and halts military action against the country. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Kyiv strikes
- Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy reports that a 3-year-old boy and his grandparents were killed by a drone strike by Russian forces in Kyiv. [src: (Reuters)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Darfur campaign
- Darfur governor Minni Minnawi says that the SAF-allied Joint Forces have repelled an attack in Sudan's West Darfur state. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Kordofan campaign
- A tribe leader in the Nuba Mountains in South Kordofan accuses the Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North of launching attacks on Otoro villages in Kauda. Additionally, four aid workers are reported to be detained. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
Disasters and accidents
- Wildfires in 2026
- 2026 United States wildfires
- 2026 Utah wildfires
- The National Interagency Fire Center reports that two people were killed yesterday in a Sikorsky S-64 Skycrane helicopter crash in Fishlake National Forest, Utah, U.S., while trying to battle the Widemouth 2 fire. [src: (The New York Times)] [src: (The Hans India)]
- 2026 Canadian wildfires
- In Canada, British Columbia declares a state of emergency after 105 wildfires were reported across the province. [src: (DW)]
- 2026 Pacific typhoon season
- Typhoon Dolphin makes landfall in the Ryukyu Islands of Japan, which encompass the entirety of Okinawa Prefecture and parts of Kagoshima Prefecture. Additionally, China shuts down ports and ferry routes in preparation for the typhoon. [src: (The Japan Times)]
- A helicopter crashes in Tijuca National Park in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, killing three Colombian tourists and the pilot. [src: (AFP via Gulf News)]
- Satellite images show that the British-sanctioned oil tanker Caroline Bezengi, believed to be part of the Russian shadow fleet, which was carrying 1 million barrels of oil, is leaking oil and sinking further off the coast of Oman, after an explosion was reported on the vessel on June 8. The oil leaks have reportedly reached the shore of Al-Qibliyah Island. [src: (AP)]
International relations
- 2026 Morocco–Spain border incident, Italy–Spain relations
- Spain imposes temporary border checks on travelers from Italy after Italy introduced similar controls on arrivals from Spain amid a dispute over migration policy following the mass arrival of migrants in Ceuta. [src: (AP)]
Law and crime
- 4 men and one woman are shot and killed in a house in Langa, Cape Flats, Cape Town, South Africa on Saturday night. [src: (EWN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 9
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Gaza war
- Gaza peace plan
- Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejects a United States-led plan for peace accepted by Hamas, saying Israel will not withdraw forces until Hamas fully disarms. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- Yemeni civil war
- At least eleven people are killed and at least 40 others are injured in a Houthi missile and drone attack on Mokha, Taiz Governorate, Yemen. [src: (MENA via The New Arab)]
- The Governor of Al-Hudaydah Governorate, Yemen, survives an assassination attempt after the Houthis shelled his residence in Al Khawkhah district. [src: (Yemen Online)]
- Mali War
- 2026 Mali offensives
- Around ten Malian soldiers are reportedly killed in a Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin attack in central Mali. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- Authorities say that they have repelled an attack by militants on a military base in San, Mali. [src: (BBC)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Blue Nile campaign
- Mass graves of 25 civilians executed by the Rapid Support Forces are discovered in Kurmuk in Sudan's Blue Nile region. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Colombian conflict
- Colombian president Abelardo de la Espriella reports that military forces killed four FARC dissidents in Meta and two Gulf Clan members in Antioquia. [src: (AFP via The Daily Star)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Canadian wildfires
- Police report that a woman was killed while evacuating the Summerland wildfire in British Columbia, Canada, which has burned more than and forced over 20,000 people to evacuate. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- 2026 Pacific typhoon season
- Typhoon Dolphin makes landfall in eastern China, evacuating 1 million people and cancelling 1,300 flights from Shanghai. Monsoon rains are also reported in parts of the Philippines, causing flooding. [src: (South China Morning Post)] [src: (The New York Times)] [src: (AP)]
- At least 16 migrant workers are killed in a major fire at a sofa manufacturing factory in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. [src: (Reuters)]
- Six people, all members of the same family, are killed after an intoxicated truck driver collides head-on with their vehicle in Dhar district, Madhya Pradesh, India. [src: (The Hindu)]
- Five people are killed, at least three others survive, and five are still missing in a landslide that hits a residential area in Baguio, Philippines. [src: (Philippine Daily Inquirer)]
Health and environment
- 2026 cyclosporiasis outbreak, Salmonellosis in the United States
- Taylor Farms extends its recalls to products containing jalapeños after they were linked to the ongoing salmonellosis outbreak in the United States. Taylor Farms currently has a recall for iceberg lettuce linked to cyclosporiasis. [src: (Ars Technica)] [src: (HuffPost)]
- The Hong Kong Observatory records in the city, the highest temperature since records began in 1884. [src: (AFP via Malay Mail)]
International relations
- Russia–Syria relations
- Russia and Syria reach a memorandum of understanding to reorganize Russia's presence on the Syrian coast, including transferring civilian facilities to Syrian state management and converting Russian military bases into joint training centers. [src: (SANA)]
Law and crime
- At least eleven people are killed and two others are injured in three separate shootings in Cape Town, South Africa. [src: (AA)]
- Afghanistan's intelligence agency arrests two staff members of the United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan in Herat, according to the office of UN secretary-general António Guterres. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- Suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan is arrested upon arrival at Baldonnel, County Dublin, Ireland, following his extradition from the United Arab Emirates, and is brought to the Special Criminal Court in Dublin. Kinahan is charged with directing the operations of a criminal organisation from 2015 to 2017. [src: (RTÉ)]
- The boat operator involved in a capsizing that killed two people, including a 5-month-old toddler, and injured 12 others near the Statue of Liberty, New York City, United States on August 8 has been arrested on 13 counts of reckless endangerment. [src: (ABC)]
Politics and elections
- Impact of the 2026 Iran war on Iran
- Iranian state media reports that Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei met president Masoud Pezeshkian in July, his first publicly reported meeting since taking over, amidst ongoing speculation about his health and future. Additionally, a rare video is released of him. [src: (Middle East Monitor)] [src: (Reuters)] [src: (Shafaq)]
Sports
- 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup
- In association football, Malawi's women's national football team defeats Ghana 2–1 at the Women's Africa Cup of Nations in the quarter-finals at Al Medina Stadium in Morocco, qualifying for the upcoming FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil and will make their debut at the tournament. [src: (Nyasa Times)] [src: (Ghanaweb)] [src: (ESPN)]
- 2026 CONCACAF U-20 Championship
- Mexico defeats the United States 2–0 at the Estadio Azteca to win the CONCACAF Under-20 Championship, its second in a row after winning the previous one. [src: (ESPN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 February 1
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Insurgency in Balochistan, India–Pakistan relations
- 2026 Balochistan attacks
- Pakistani military and Balochistan Police forces announce the end to a 40-hour counterterrorism operation which resulted in the deaths of 145 Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) insurgents, 18 civilians, and 18 security personnel. The Pakistani government accuses India of backing the BLA. [src: (AP)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Dnipro strikes
- A Russian drone strike hits a minibus transporting mineworkers in Dnipro, Ukraine, killing at least 15 people and injuring seven others. [src: (BBC News)]
- Boko Haram insurgency
- Nigeria reports that its forces have killed a senior Boko Haram commander known as Abu Khalid, describing him as the group's deputy leader in the Sambisa Forest, and ten other fighters during a raid in Borno State. [src: (Reuters)]
- Sudanese civil war
- A Sudan Airways passenger flight lands at Khartoum International Airport, Sudan's main international airport, for the first time since the war began in 2023, resuming limited operations after renovations and earlier drone attacks. [src: (AFP via Al-Ahram)]
Arts and culture
- 68th Annual Grammy Awards
- At the 2026 Grammy Awards, Kendrick Lamar wins five awards and surpasses Jay-Z as the most awarded hip-hop artist in Grammy history, while Bad Bunny's Debí Tirar Más Fotos becomes the first Spanish-language album to win Album of the Year. [src: (AP)] [src: (The Hollywood Reporter)]
- "Golden" from the film KPop Demon Hunters becomes the first K-pop song to win a Grammy after winning Best Song Written for Visual Media. [src: (AP via ABC News)]
- Steven Spielberg becomes the 22nd competitive EGOT awardee after winning a Grammy for Best Music Film for producing Music by John Williams. [src: (AA)]
Disasters and accidents
- Storm Kristin
- Portugal launches a €1 billion (US$1.2 billion) loan program to rebuild uninsured storm-damaged factories and a €500 million ($593 million) facility for short-term liquidity, while the government extends the state of calamity in about 60 municipalities amid forecasts of further heavy rain and flooding. [src: (Reuters)]
- Nine people are killed and 21 others are injured, including seven critically, after a bus rolls off a road and crashes in Antalya province, Turkey. [src: (AP)]
- Four people are killed and 28 others are injured after a bus carrying wedding guests collides with a truck and overturns in Lodhran District, Pakistan. [src: (Dawn)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Costa Rican general election
- Costa Ricans vote to elect the president and all 57 members of the Legislative Assembly. From a field of 20 candidates, Laura Fernández of the Sovereign People's Party (PPSO) wins the presidency with 48% of the vote. [src: (BBC News)]
- Epstein Files, Relationship of Peter Mandelson and Jeffrey Epstein
- Peter Mandelson resigns from Labour Party (UK) after the United States Department of Justice releases files showing that convicted child sex offender Jeffrey Epstein made £55,000 ($75,000) in payments to Lord Mandelson in three separate transactions in 2003 and 2004. [src: (BBC)]
- Tens of thousands of people gather in Prague, Czech Republic, in support of President Petr Pavel in his dispute with foreign minister Petr Macinka and his party Motorists for Themselves. [src: (AP)]
Sports
- 2026 Australian Open
- In tennis, Spanish player Carlos Alcaraz defeats Serbian player Novak Djokovic in the men's singles final 2–6, 6–2, 6–3, 7–5, to win his first Australian Open title, becoming the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam in singles. [src: (AFP via ABS-CBN)] [src: (ESPN)]
- 2026 European Men's Handball Championship
- In handball, Denmark defeats Germany 34–27 and becomes European Champions in addition to being the reigning World and Olympic Champions. [src: (DW)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 February 10
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Israeli–Palestinian conflict
- Gaza war
- Five Palestinians are killed by Israeli strikes and gunfire on the Gaza Strip. [src: (RTÉ News)] 
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Two people are killed in a Russian airstrike on Sloviansk, Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine. [src: (The Kyiv Independent)]
- Boko Haram insurgency, Nigeria–United States relations
- A United States military official confirms that the U.S. will deploy 200 soldiers to Nigeria to help train the Nigerian military and provide logistical support against Boko Haram and other Islamic terrorist groups. [src: (AA)]
- Syrian conflict
- Four people are killed and eight others are wounded after their vehicle strikes a land mine in Deir ez-Zor Governorate, Syria. In a separate incident, a tractor triggers a land mine in the village of Taanah, Aleppo Governorate, killing one person. [src: (MENA via The New Arab)]
Arts and culture
- Ireland launches a permanent basic-income programme for the arts that pays 2,000 creative workers €325 (US$387) per week for three years, following a government trial that began in 2022, and which culture minister Patrick O'Donovan describes as the first permanent scheme of its kind worldwide. [src: (Reuters)]
Business and economy
- Connections of Jeffrey Epstein
- Canadian pensions funder La Caisse suspends all future ventures with multinational logistics company DP World following the disclosure by the U.S. Department of Justice that its CEO Sultan Ahmed bin Sulayem had maintained close ties with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. [src: (The Gazette)]
- United States embargo against Cuba, Cuba–Mexico relations, Canada–Mexico relations, United States trade war with Canada and Mexico
