- The first day of direct negotiations and the sixth round of peace talks between Israel and Lebanon begins at the U.S. embassy in Rome, Italy. [src: (AA)] [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- Gaza war
- The Israeli military strikes a police station in Gaza, killing eight people, according to Gaza's civil defence agency and Al-Shifa Hospital, violating the ongoing ceasefire. [src: (AFP via CNA)]
- Iraqi conflict
- Withdrawal of United States troops from Iraq
- Iraqi prime minister Ali al-Zaidi and the U.S. defense department says that all remaining American troops will withdraw from Iraq by September 30, ending a 23-year presence in the country that started with the 2003 U.S. invasion. [src: (AP)] [src: (DW)]
- Sudanese civil war
- 2026 Blue Nile campaign
- The Sudanese Armed Forces say that the 4th Infantry Division's 13th Brigade have taken control of the Blue Nile town of Fashfoun following days of clashes with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces and the Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North. [src: (TRT Afrika)] [src: (Yeni Şafak)]
- Colombian conflict
- Colombia's military says it has rescued 39 civilians kidnapped by the National Liberation Army on a highway in Chocó Department, with two soldiers killed during the operation. [src: (AFP via Vanguard)]
Arts and culture
- A Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton nicknamed Gus sells for US$50.1 million at Sotheby’s in New York City, United States, setting an auction record for a dinosaur fossil. [src: (AFP via CNA)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2024–2026 Cuba blackouts, 2026 Cuban crisis
- Cuba suffers its third nationwide blackout in less than 10 days and fifth of 2026, as the state utility reports a complete grid failure amid fuel shortages caused by the ongoing U.S. imposed blockade, that complicate power restoration. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- Seven people are killed and three others are injured after two vehicles collided head-on just outside Ramadi, Iraq. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Six people are killed after a gas-laden truck caught fire and exploded at a checkpoint along a federal highway in Kogi State, Nigeria. [src: (The PunchNG)]
- Six workers are killed in a fire at a building under construction in Brussels, Belgium. [src: (BBC News)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak
- The Directorate General of Health Services reports that seven more children have died from measles in Bangladesh in the past 24 hours, bringing the total death toll from the disease in the country to 766. [src: (The Business Standard)]
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) announces that it will test the Gilead Sciences antiviral for the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus. [src: (CNBC Africa)]
- The World Health Organization reports that 80% of cases of Ebola in eastern DRC are from unknown chains of transmission. Additionally, the death toll from Ebola reaches 700. [src: (AP)] 
- 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
- The U.S. CDC reports 7,000 cases nationwide of cyclosporiasis, which is caused by cyclospora cayetanensis. [src: (NBC News)]
- The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services reports 3,300 cases in the state, up from 2,640 the previous day. [src: (The Detroit News)]
Law and crime
- Shootings by U.S. immigration agents in the second Trump administration
- The U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement suspends vehicle stops related to immigration enforcement following the recent fatal shootings of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston, Texas, and Joan Sebastian Guerrero in Biddeford, Maine. [src: (Reuters)]
- International Criminal Court investigation in Darfur
- A prosecutor at the International Criminal Court drop charges against former rebel leader Abdallah Banda over his role in a 2007 attack on African Union peacekeepers during Sudan's Darfur conflict. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
Politics and elections
- AI boom
- Japan approves election rules requiring AI-generated images and videos on social media to be labeled and prohibiting false or distorted information about candidates, with the measures taking effect in March. [src: (AFP via The Straits Times)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 15
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign
- 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran
- The United States Central Command (CENTCOM) says that American forces have redirected two commercial vessels since the blockade resumed. [src: (AA)]
- CENTCOM says that American forces disabled the Curaçao-flagged oil tanker M/T Belma as it was heading towards an Iranian port in the Persian Gulf amidst the blockade. An 18 second video confirms that a U.S. aircraft disabled the vessel. [src: (AA)] [src: (Stars and Stripes)]
- India in the 2026 Iran war
- Operation Urja Suraksha
- India's Directorate General of Shipping warns companies not to deploy Indian sailors onto vessels transiting through the Strait of Hormuz after two Indian seafarers were killed in separate ship attacks in the waterway. [src: (The Indian Express)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed "until the United States ends its acts of aggression". [src: (Euractiv)]
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says that ceasefire negotiations aimed at ending the war have not closed despite renewed fighting between Iran and the U.S. [src: (The New York Times)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region
- The Directorate General of Counter Terrorism of the Kurdistan Region Security Council reports that international coalition forces have intercepted seven drones in Erbil, Kurdistan Region, Iraq. [src: (Kurdistan24)]
- Three drones are reportedly shot down near the U.S. consulate in Erbil. [src: (Shafaq)]
- CENTCOM announces the U.S. has launched new strikes against Iran for a fifth consecutive day aimed at coastal defense systems, cruise missile storage, and launch sites in the Greater Tunb Island. [src: (AFP via NDTV)] [src: (Politico)]
- Gaza war
- Gaza peace plan
- Morocco signs an agreement with the Board of Peace to join the International Stabilization Force for Gaza. [src: (Reuters)]
- Nirim attack, Gaza war hostage crisis
- Israel's military claims to have killed a militant from the Hamas branch Al-Qassam Brigades that participated in the abduction of soldiers Col. Asaf Hamami, St.-Sgt. Tomer Yaakov Ahimas, and Sgt. Kiril Brodski during the October 7 attacks on the Nirim kibbutz. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)] [src: (Haaretz)]
- Yemeni civil war
- Saudi Arabia–United States relations
- The U.S. State Department approves a potential US$1.96 billion deal in arms sales to Saudi Arabia amidst the current Iran war and potential re-escalation with the Houthis. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Darfur campaign
- The Sudanese Armed Forces-allied Joint Forces announce that they have recaptured the Orshi Reservoir area in North Darfur, a month after the Rapid Support Forces seized the area. [src: (AA)]
- A drone strike by the Rapid Support Forces hits a power station in the town of Al Dabbah in Sudan's Northern State. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
Disasters and accidents
- Seven people are killed and one person is missing after a rubber dinghy explodes near Liaoning Province, China. [src: (Xinhua)]
- One person is killed and 24 others are missing after a passenger boat sank off the coast of Sulawesi, Indonesia. [src: (Xinhua)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Canadian wildfires
- IQAir ranks Toronto, Ontario, Canada, as having the worst air quality among major cities worldwide as smoke from wildfires in northwestern Ontario reaches the city, prompting the Canadian environment ministry to advise residents to remain indoors. [src: (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- The total amount of cases of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceed 2,000. [src: (Medical Xpress)]
- Sudanese cholera epidemic
- Sudan's health ministry reports that the total amount of cholera cases in north and west Kordofan has increased to 1,547. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
International relations
- United Kingdom–European Union relations
- Effect of Brexit on Gibraltar
- The United Kingdom and the European Union remove the land-border fence between Gibraltar and Spain under a post-Brexit treaty, allowing free movement while introducing joint British-Spanish checks at Gibraltar's airport and port. [src: (AP)]
- Afghanistan and the United Nations
- United Nations secretary-general António Guterres appoints Bangladeshi diplomat Rabab Fatima as the next head of the United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- Papua New Guinea–Taiwan relations
- Papuan foreign minister Justin Tkatchenko announces the immediate closure of Taiwan's representative office in Port Moresby, citing Papua New Guinea's adherence to the One China policy, while saying the decision does not affect contracts between Taiwan's CPC Corporation and natural gas in Papua New Guinea. [src: (AFP via The Straits Times)]
Law and crime
- Bhutanese refugees scam
- A district court in Kathmandu, Nepal, sentences former deputy prime minister Top Bahadur Rayamajhi to four years in prison and former home minister Bal Krishna Khand to two years for roles in forging documents for a fraudulent Bhutanese refugee resettlement scheme. [src: (Reuters)]
- Cannabis in Kenya
- Kenya's High Court rejects a Rastafarian petition seeking a religious exemption from cannabis laws, ruling that the group does not show the laws violate religious freedom. [src: (AFP via NDTV)]
- Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda conflict
- The Democratic Republic of the Congo establishes a council composed of mostly international war crimes lawyers to advise state institutions seeking accountability and reparations for victims of violence in the country's east. [src: (Reuters)]
- Detention of Craig and Lindsay Foreman
- The family of British national Craig Foreman says an Iranian court has added two years to his 10-year espionage prison sentence for speaking to the media, as he and his wife Lindsay continue a hunger strike. [src: (CBS News)]
- Moroccan prosecutors release journalist Ali Lmrabet after questioning him over online posts allegedly defaming unnamed individuals and institutions, while the criminal investigation continues. [src: (Reuters)]
- U.S. president Donald Trump announces that American citizen Dena Karari has been released from Iran after being detained on espionage charges since 2024. Her lawyer, Jared Genser, also confirmed her release. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (NBC News)]
Politics and elections
- France's National Assembly gives final approval to a bill allowing eligible adults with incurable, life-threatening illnesses to obtain lethal medication under strict conditions. The measure awaits Constitutional Council review before taking effect. [src: (AP)]
Science and technology
- Discoveries of exoplanets
- Astronomers directly image the exoplanet Beta Pictoris d next to its star, located 63 light-years away, using NASA's James Webb Space Telescope and European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope. It is also reported to be fainter than its sibling Beta Pictoris b. The discovery is published in the The Astrophysical Journal. [src: (ABC News)] [src: (Space.com)]
- Internet in South Africa
- American technology company Amazon partners with South African internet provider Herotel to launch Amazon Leo satellite internet service in 2027, marking its first such African agreement. [src: (AFP via The Manila Times)]
Sports
- 2026 ESPY Awards
- The ESPY Awards is held at the David H. Koch Theater in New York City, U.S., with the 2025–26 New York Knicks winning five awards, including the Best Team award after winning their first NBA championship since 1973, while point guard Jalen Brunson wins the Best Male Athlete and Best Championship Performance awards. [src: (NBC News)] [src: (Reuters)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 16
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- 2026 Iran war
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says that Iran is still interested in an agreement with the United States. [src: (Reuters)]
- July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
- The United States Central Command launches new strikes against Iran for a sixth consecutive night in an effort to degrade Iranian military capabilities. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- Explosions are reported in Iran's Qeshm Island, Bushehr, Ahvaz, and Bandar Abbas, including a bridge in Bandar Khamir. A truck on the bridge is reported to be targeted, killing the driver. [src: (Turkiye Today)]
- Tasnim News Agency reports that American fighter jets attacked the Iranshahr Airport in the Sistan and Baluchestan province. [src: (Ynetnews)] [src: (MTV)]
- Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war
- The Kuwaiti defense ministry reports that the military intercepted and destroyed 32 drones entering the country's airspace. [src: (Arab Times Kuwait)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Sudanese refugee crisis
- Around 1,000 Sudanese returnees in Egypt are reported by a local committee to have returned to Sudan. [src: (Middle East Monitor)]
- The Sudanese Armed Forces says that they have destroyed around 205 combat vehicles, military supply trucks, and four strategic drones belonging to the Rapid Support Forces in the past two weeks. [src: (AA)] [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Insurgency in Cabo Delgado
- Five insurgents are revealed to have been killed and several others injured in recent clashes last month involving the Mozambican Army and the Islamic State near Catupa, Cabo Delgado, Mozambique. [src: (Moz24)]
Business and economy
- TotalEnergies and its partners inaugurate the 216 MW Hydra solar-and-battery project in the Northern Cape, South Africa, which is the largest hybrid renewable energy project on the continent. [src: (Renewables Now)] [src: (Business Insider)]
Disasters and accidents
- Twenty-one people are killed and several others are injured after a bus lost control and veered off the road in Kapchorwa, Uganda. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Fourteen people are killed and five others are injured after a minibus plunged into a deep ravine in Cajamarca, Peru. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Eleven people are killed and 19 more injured in a fire at a care facility in Algiers, Algeria. [src: (BBC News)]
- Six members of a family are killed after a fire engulfed their house in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province, Pakistan. [src: (Xinhua)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- The Ugandan health ministry reports that Uganda has discharged its last patient diagnosed with Ebola, triggering a 42-day countdown clock on when it can be declared free of the virus. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
- The Washington Post links the iceberg lettuce produced by Taylor Farms and supplied to American fast food chain Taco Bell as a source of the current cyclosporiasis outbreak in the United States, which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (The Washington Post)]
- Taco Bell removes lettuce from some of their restaurants following reports that the Food and Drug Administration has opened an investigation into iceberg lettuce supplied to them. [src: (The Hill)]
- The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services reports that the amount of hospitalizations in the state linked to the cyclosporiasis outbreak has surpassed 100 people. [src: (ABC News)]
- Zambia's health ministry declares an end to its cholera outbreak, which started in August of last year, after four weeks without a case. [src: (Lusaka Times)]
International relations
- Papua New Guinea–Taiwan relations
- Taiwan says that its representative office in Port Moresby will continue operating and assisting Taiwanese nationals, rejecting Papua New Guinea's decision to close it and stating that the move was made without prior consultation. Papuan foreign minister Justin Tkatchenko says that his ministry informed Taiwan of the closure "weeks ago". [src: (AFP via The Straits Times)]
- Sudan–United Arab Emirates relations, War crimes during the Sudanese civil war
- Sudanese justice minister Abdallah Dirif says that the government will launch lawsuits against the United Arab Emirates in international courts for its role in supporting war crimes by the Rapid Support Forces in the ongoing civil war. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
Law and crime
- Corruption in Thailand
- The Thai interior ministry identifies irregularities in the mandatory examination results of 5,814 civil servants and considers suspensions, while police arrest three suspected organizers following a joint investigation with the anti-corruption commission. [src: (AFP via The Straits Times)]
- Huachicol fiscal, Organized crime in Mexico
- Ernesto Ruffo Appel, former governor of Baja California, Mexico, is arrested on charges related to organized crime and fuel smuggling. [src: (Gringo Gazette)]
- Unification Church and politics
- South Korea's Supreme Court upholds People Power Party lawmaker Kweon Seong-dong's two-year prison sentence for accepting ₩100 million (US$67,400) in illegal political funds from the Unification Church, removing him from the National Assembly. [src: (AFP via The Straits Times)]
- Former Autostrade per l'Italia (ASPI) CEO Giovanni Castellucci is convicted and sentenced to 12 years in prison for his role in the 2018 collapse of the Ponte Morandi in Genoa, Liguria, Italy, which killed 43 people. [src: (ANSA)] [src: (TrasportoEuropa)]
Politics and elections
- Dismissal of Mykhailo Fedorov
- Protests take place in Kyiv and other cities across Ukraine against president Volodymyr Zelenskyy's decision to replace defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov with major-general Yevhenii Khmara. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Ukrainian Air Force deputy commander Pavlo Yelizarov resigns from his position in protest of Fedorov's removal as defense minister. [src: (BBC News)]
Science and technology
- Astronomers report the first observationally confirmed atmosphere around a rocky exoplanet within its star's habitable zone, after detecting helium escaping from the upper atmosphere of LHS 1140 b, a super-Earth approximately 49 light-years from Earth. [src: (Space.com)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 17
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
- Iran says that it has launched ballistic missile and drone strikes at targets in Bahrain, including a drone vessel depot, an artificial intelligence center used for targeting, and the Al-Sakhir Air Base, as part of the 11th phase of its Saegheh operation. [src: (AA)] [src: (Middle East Monitor)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
- Jordan reports having intercepted projectiles fired from Iran. [src: (AA)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
- Iranian strikes damage a desalination plant and a power plant in Kuwait, according to the Kuwaiti energy ministry. [src: (AP)] [src: (CNBC)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Oman
- The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy launches attacks on radar facilities in Oman. [src: (AA)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Syria
- Iranian state media reports that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps have targeted a United States Special Operations Command in Al-Tanf in response to the killing of Iranian soldiers in Iranshahr, Sistan and Baluchestan province. [src: (Arab News)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar
- The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Aerospace Force launches an attack at Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar, and claims to have caused damage to equipment there, while Qatar's armed forces claim to have intercepted Iranian attacks. [src: (AA)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- The U.S. military's Central Command (CENTCOM) confirms that they have destroyed the Chah Bahar Shahid Kalantari Port surveillance tower in Chabahar Port yesterday, which was allegedly used by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps for tracking commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region
- Iranian drone strikes near Erbil, Kurdistan Region, Iraq, kill eight Kurdish rebels and injure several more. [src: (AFP via The Times of Israel)]
- The U.S. CENTCOM launches strikes against Iran for a seventh consecutive night. [src: (The Guardian)]
- Gaza war
- Around eight Palestinians are reported to be killed in an airstrike on a funeral in central Gaza. [src: (AA)]
- The Israeli military and Shin Bet confirm that they have killed Hamas commander Anas Mahmoud Ahmad Hamdan, who served as a "right-hand man" of former Al-Qassam Brigades commander Mohammed Deif, in an airstrike in Khan Yunis, Gaza Strip. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- War in the Sahel
- An attack on a military deployment in Téra, Tillabéri Region, Niger, kills 16 soldiers and injures 23 others, while state media reports that security forces have killed 15 attackers. [src: (AFP via The Economic Times)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis, Iraq–Syria relations
- Iraq and Syria sign a memorandum of understanding to rehabilitate the Kirkuk–Baniyas pipeline to bypass to the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- Iraq-United States relations
- The United States Chamber of Commerce announces that Iraq has signed roughly $60 billion worth of agreements and partnerships to bypass the Strait of Hormuz and accelerate American investment in the Iraqi oil sector. [src: (AP News)]
Disasters and accidents
- Wildfires in 2026
- 2026 United States wildfires
- 2026 Minnesota wildfires
- The United States Forest Service reports that wildfires in northern Minnesota has reached over 77,000 acres, prompting evacuations in the area. [src: (KARE TV)] [src: (KAAL)]
- 2026 Canadian wildfires
- Over 900 wildfires are reported across Canada, including 43 new active blazes, prompting evacuations across the country. [src: (CTV News)] [src: (BNN Bloomberg)]
- The U.S. state of Connecticut's Department of Energy and Environmental Protection deploys firefighters to assist with wildfire efforts in Quebec, Canada. [src: (CT.Gov)] [src: (WVIT)]
- 2026 Chiapas earthquake
- A earthquake strikes near the coast of Chiapas, Mexico. Tsunami warnings are issued and at least two people are injured. [src: (ABC7)] [src: (BBC News)] [src: (The Weather Network)]
- 2026 Venezuela earthquakes
- The confirmed death toll from the doublet earthquakes that struck northern Venezuela in June rises to 5,069 people. [src: (AP)]
- Krokstadelva fire
- A large fire breaks out among terraced houses in Krokstadelva, Drammen, Norway, spreading rapidly between multiple housing blocks and prompting mass evacuations. The municipality declares a crisis and calls in fire crews from eight neighboring municipalities. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (VG)]
- Eight people are killed, ten others are rescued and 34 are reported missing when a landslide buries multiple houses and residential buildings in Pengshui, Chongqing, China. [src: (ABC News)] [src: (India Today)]
- Four people are killed and nine others are injured after a head-on collision between two overspeeding cars along the N-25 National Highway in Wadh, Balochistan, Pakistan. [src: (Dawn)]
- A nine-vehicle pile-up in Deli Serdang, North Sumatra, Indonesia, kills at least four and injures eight others. [src: (Xinhua)]
- A storm in Chile kills three people, injures seven others, damages more than 800 homes, displaces hundreds, and leaves around 400,000 people without electricity across 10 regions. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (Xinhua)]
- A nine-story building under construction near Conakry, Guinea, collapses due to heavy rainfall, killing three people and injuring several others. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Two citizens are killed from weather-related incidents and 53,000 homes are reported to be without power during severe thunderstorms across several regions of France. [src: (AA)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak
- The death tolls from the measles outbreak in Bangladesh reaches 780 after one child is reported to have died from the disease by the Directorate General of Health Services. [src: (Dhaka Tribune)]
- 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
- Taylor Farms recalls their iceburg lettuce, traced through a farm in Mexico, amidst the ongoing cyclosporiasis outbreak in the United States, which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis. [src: (Forbes)]
- Michigan, U.S., surpasses 5,000 cases of cyclosporiasis. [src: (The Detroit News)]
International relations
- Hong Kong–United States relations
- The United States allows its national emergency over Hong Kong's national security law to expire while retaining the underlying executive order and most related sanctions. [src: (AFP via New Straits Times)]
Law and crime
- A civilian dies while a police officer and the suspected gunman are wounded in a shooting in Nørresundby, North Jutland, Denmark, after officers responding to a reported fire are met with gunfire. [src: (AP)] [src: (TV2)]
- The Ontario Court of Appeal finds Canadian far-right activist and Freedom Convoy organizer Pat King guilty of intimidation and orders a re-sentencing. [src: (CBC)] [src: (Toronto Star)]
- Japan enacts a law criminalizing public damage, removal or defacement of the national flag, punishable by up to two years in prison or a ¥200,000 (US$1,200) fine. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Turkish authorities detain 67 irregular migrants and five other suspected smugglers following a sailboat interception off the coast of Muğla, Turkey. [src: (Xinhua)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Labour Party leadership election
- Andy Burnham is elected as the new leader of the British Labour Party. He will formally succeed Keir Starmer as prime minister on Monday. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (CNN)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- Dismissal of Mykhailo Fedorov
- Protests continue for a second day in Kyiv, Ukraine, near the Presidential Office Building, demanding the return of Mykhailo Fedorov as Minister of Defence and the resignation of Oleksandr Syrskyi as the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine. [src: (Reuters)]
- Japanese imperial succession debate
- Japan's National Diet amends the Imperial Household Law to allow unmarried male descendants of former imperial branches to rejoin the family and permit royal women to retain status after marrying commoners, while preserving male-only succession. [src: (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 18
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
- The Bahraini military intercepts projectiles fired from Iran. [src: (DPA via Yahoo News)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
- The U.S. Central ​Command (CENTCOM) reports that two American troops have been "killed in action" in Jordan, bringing the total casualties for American troops to 16. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (The Wall Street Journal)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
- Kuwait says Iranian attacks have struck a second power and desalination plant in two days, causing a fire and shutting several generating units, while other attacks injure firefighters and a worker and temporarily disrupt flights from Kuwait International Airport. [src: (AFP via Vanguard)]
- An oil facility is damaged, according to the Kuwait Petroleum Corporation. [src: (PBS)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia
- Axios reports that Iran has launched a ballistic missile at a United States base in Saudi Arabia, making it the first direct attack by Iran on the country since targeting a petrochemical complex in Jubail. [src: (Financial Times)]
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
- Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi says that the United States has violated the terms of the Islamabad Memorandum and that Iran is "no longer implementing them". [src: (PBS)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, in a statement published by IRNA, report that two oil tankers have exploded after hitting mines south in the Strait of Hormuz. However, the U.S. Central Command disputes the claims on X as "false". [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- The Philippine foreign affairs department reports that four Philippine-registered vessels carrying 81 seafarers have safely transited through the Strait of Hormuz. The vessels are identified as the MV Lyng Trader, MV Western Doncaster, MV Vivian Trader, and MV Eva Fuji. [src: (GMA Network)]
- July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
- In the seventh day of renewed U.S. strikes, civilian infrastructure, including a desalination plant in Jask, are damaged, cutting off the access to water for 10,000 civilians. [src: (IRNA)] [src: (BBC Persian (in Persian))]
- Communications services in Iran's Hormozgan province are disrupted after U.S. strikes damaged 116 radio towers there. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (BBC Persian (in Persian))]
- The U.S. CENTCOM launches a new wave of strikes for an eighth consecutive night against IRGC targets in response to two American service members killed in Jordan. [src: (The Hill)]
- Mali War
- 2026 Mali offensives
- The Al-Qaeda-linked Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin and Tuareg Azawad Liberation Front rebels ambush a Malian military convoy in the Gao Region of Mali. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (AP)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war, Aerial warfare in the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Moscow Oblast governor Andrey Vorobyov and Tambov Oblast head Yevgeny Pervyshov say Ukrainian drone attacks killed seven workers and injure 49 others at Wildberries warehouses in Kotovsk and Elektrostal, Russia, while another strike ignites an oil facility. Ukraine says the warehouses support Russian drone production. [src: (Reuters)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Arab League secretary general Nabil Fahmy and U.S. envoy Massad Boulos reach an agreement to establish a regular framework for joint coordination for a ceasefire in the ongoing civil war in Sudan. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
- An insurgent is killed and five others are injured during a counterterrorism operation that foiled a terrorist plot in Wana, South Waziristan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. [src: (Dawn)]
Business and economy
- Belgium–Israel relations, International reactions to the Gaza war
- Belgium approves an import ban on goods from Israeli settlements. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- Kuwait Airways reschedules most of its flights due to the country's airspace being closed amidst ongoing Iranian attacks. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- Iran's Hormozgan province water and wastewater company announces that United States airstrikes have damaged desalination equipment, cutting off water to about 10,000 people. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
Disasters and accidents
- Krokstadelva fire
- Over 100 houses burn down in a fire in the Krokstadelva municipality of Norway. [src: (NOS)]
- Nine people are killed and nine others are injured after an unauthorized firecracker factory explodes in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India. [src: (NDTV)] [src: (Xinhua)]
- Five people are killed and two others are injured in a workplace accident in Thanh Hóa province, Vietnam. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Five people, including three women, drown in the Godavari River whilst fishing near Polavaram district, India. [src: (The Hindu)]
- Four people are killed, four more are missing, and seven others are injured after torrential rains and flash floods hit a mountainous village in Lai Châu province, Vietnam. [src: (AA)]
Law and crime
- Turkey–Islamic State conflict
- Turkey's interior ministry announces the arrest of 119 people linked to ISIS. [src: (AFP via Al Arabiya)]
Politics and elections
- Magyar Government
- Hungarian president Tamás Sulyok signs the 17th amendment to the nation's constitution, which will end his term in office at midnight the following day. [src: (BBC News)]
- Jens Spahn resigns as leader of the governing CDU/CSU alliance in Germany's Bundestag amid criticism after he and his husband became parents through surrogacy, despite Germany's ban and his party's opposition to the practice. [src: (AFP via Channels TV)]
Science and technology
- Space industry of India
- Skyroot Aerospace successfully launches Vikram-1, India's first privately built orbital rocket, from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Andhra Pradesh, carrying small satellite payloads into low Earth orbit on its maiden flight. [src: (AFP via Asharq Al-Awsat)]
Sports
- 2026 FIFA World Cup
- In association football, England beats France 6–4 in the highest-scoring third-place playoff in FIFA World Cup history, securing their best result since winning the tournament in 1966. [src: (BBC Sport)]
- French footballer Kylian Mbappé scores twice to become the highest-scoring player in World Cup history, and the first player to score 10 goals in a single World Cup since Germany's Gerd Müller in 1970. [src: (BBC Sport)]
- 2026 Diamond League
- At the London Athletics Meet, British runner Josh Kerr sets a new world record of 3:42.66 for the mile. The previous record of 3:43.13 by Hicham El Guerrouj had been set in 1999. [src: (BBC Sport)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 19
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio says that diplomatic solutions are "still on the table" if Iran ceases attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- Iraq in the 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region
- The Kurdistan Freedom Party reports that eight Iranian Kurdish rebels have been wounded after a drone strike from Iran hit a camp near Erbil, Kurdistan Region, Iraq. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- The United States Central Command (CENTCOM) announces that an American service member has been killed in northern Iraq during a "controlled" detonation of a downed Iranian drone, bringing the total amount of American casualties to 17. [src: (The Hill)] [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
- The Israeli military uses the Iron Dome to shoot down fragments from an Iranian missile fired at Aqaba, Jordan, after the Aegis was reportedly used to shoot down the missile. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)] [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
- The U.S. CENTCOM launches strikes against Iran for a ninth consecutive evening amidst a rise in American casualties. [src: (CNBC)] [src: (The Kabul Tribune)]
- Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
- SDF–Syrian transitional government clashes
- The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reports that 530 people, including 76 civilians, have been killed in clashes between the post-Assad Syrian Army and the Syrian Democratic Forces over the past months. [src: (Shafaq)]
- Mali War
- 2026 Mali offensives
- Around 50 Malian soldiers are reported to have been killed in Anéfis, Mali, by the Al-Qaeda-linked Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin and Tuareg Azawad Liberation Front rebels. [src: (The Hindu)] [src: (The News Pakistan)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Odesa strikes
- Ukrainian officials say Russian forces struck a Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship carrying corn off Odesa, killing ten crew members from India and Syria. Eight others are rescued, while the vessel continues burning. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Huancayo earthquake
- At least six people are killed and 21 others are injured when a earthquake strikes the town of Pumpunya in Chongos Bajo District, Chupaca province, Department of Junín, Peru. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (notiPerú)] [src: (El Comercio Perú)]
- Four people are killed, four others are unaccounted for, and several houses are swept away after a landslide triggered by heavy rainfall hits Mon District, Nagaland, India. [src: (NDTV)]
- Sixty-seven people are rescued and 66 others are reported missing when passenger ferry MV Barima capsizes and sinks near the Pomeroon River in Guyana. [src: (AP)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- Canada bars foreign nationals who have visited the Democratic Republic of the Congo within the previous 21 days, citing the Ebola epidemic. [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Delhi Jantar Mantar protests
- Students hold protests in several cities across India after activist Sonam Wangchuk is arrested and taken to a hospital during his hunger strike calling for education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over the 2026 NEET exam paper leak, with a march on Parliament planned for the following day. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Financial Express)]
- 2026 São Toméan presidential election
- Santomeans vote to elect the country's president. Incumbent president Carlos Vila Nova seeks a second term in office. [src: (Reuters)]
Sports
- 2026 Esports World Cup
- League of Legends in esports
- In esports, Dplus KIA defeats Karmine Corp 3–0 to win the League of Legends title at the 2026 Esports World Cup, extending South Korea's winning streak to three years and securing its first international title since 2020. [src: (DAZN)]
- 2026 FIFA World Cup
- 2026 FIFA World Cup final
- In association football, Spain win their second FIFA World Cup title after defeating the defending champions Argentina 1–0 after extra time in the final held at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, United States. Spain's captain Rodri is awarded the Golden Ball. [src: (France 24)] [src: (Yahoo! Sports)]
- Spain at the FIFA World Cup
- After winning the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Spain becomes the first country to hold both the men's and women's World Cups, having won the latter in 2023. The men's team extends their international football record of 38 consecutive unbeaten matches, surpassing Italy's record of 37. It also becomes the first team to field two teenagers, Lamine Yamal and Pau Cubarsí, both 19-year-olds, in a FIFA World Cup final. [src: (NPR)] [src: (Reuters)] [src: (FOX Sports)]
- Spanish manager Luis de la Fuente also becomes the oldest manager to win a World Cup title at 65 years old. [src: (Reuters)]
Science and technology
- AI boom
- Mathematician and Anthropic employee Levent Alpöge presents an explicit counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture in three-dimensional space that disproves the n-variable conjecture for n > 2 using the large language model Fable 5. The Jacobian conjecture for n = 1 remains true. [src: (VNexpress)] [src: (NewScientist)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 2
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Kurdish–Iranian crisis
- Western Iran clashes
- The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says that they have killed five members of the Democratic Party of Iranian Kurdistan near Piranshahr, West Azerbaijan, Iran. [src: (Reuters)]
- Gaza war
- Tunnel warfare in the Gaza Strip
- Israeli defense minister Israel Katz reports that the military has demolished 83% of Hamas tunnels in the Gaza Strip. [src: (The Times of Israel)] [src: (Ynetnews)]
- Seven Palestinians are injured in an Israeli strike on the Nuseirat refugee camp in the middle of the Gaza Strip. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- 2026 Lebanon war
- Hezbollah–Israel conflict
- The Israeli military says that the Egoz Unit commando group has killed a Hezbollah militant who emerged from a underground tunnel in Ali al-Taher in southern Lebanon. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- Syrian conflict
- Nine people are killed and 22 others are injured in a bombing at a coffeehouse in Damascus, Syria. No group has claimed responsibility. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Kyiv strikes
- Russian forces launch a major ballistic missile and drone attack on Kyiv, Ukraine, killing at least 30 people and injuring 98 others, and forcing more than 50,000 civilians to shelter underground. [src: (AP)] [src: (Kyiv Independent)]
- Terrorism in Indonesia
- Papua conflict
- The West Papua National Liberation Army says it set fire to a plane that landed with eight people in Highland Papua, Indonesia, after shooting and killing its American pilot. The Indonesian military announces the recovery of his body and that the plane's seven Papuan passengers returned unharmed. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Reuters)]
Arts and culture
- 2026 Écône consecrations
- The Holy See excommunicates the entire clergy of the Society of Saint Pius X for consecrating four bishops yesterday without the Pope's permission, barring the group from officiating marriages and hearing confessions. The Catholic laity are also warned that they will also be excommunicated if they attend SSPX masses. [src: (AP)] [src: (Vatican News)]
Disasters and accidents
- Sixteen people are killed and 20 others are injured when a passenger bus overturns in Dutywa, Eastern Cape, South Africa. [src: (CTV News)]
- Eleven people are killed in a collision between a truck and two cars on the Dushanbe-Kulob-Khorog highway near Vahdat, Tajikistan. [src: (Times of Central Asia)] [src: (Xinhua)]
- Ten monks are killed and more than 10 others are injured, some critically, when an 11-year-old boy drives a pickup truck into a pilgrimage walk in Mukdahan province, Thailand. [src: (AP)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- The Democratic Republic of the Congo begins treatment trials for Ebola. [src: (BBC News)]
- The World Health Organization says that Uganda has confirmed a Marburg virus case in a toddler in the Kyegegwa District during Ebola surveillance, with authorities monitoring contacts and reporting no symptoms among them. [src: (AFP via Jamaica Observer)]
International relations
- Canada–Philippines relations
- Canadian prime minister Mark Carney and Philippine president Bongbong Marcos agree to upgrade bilateral relations to a strategic partnership during a meeting in Vancouver. [src: (NHK)]
- Human rights in Burkina Faso
- The United Nations announces that it will close its human rights office in Burkina Faso after the country's military junta indefinitely suspends its operations, preventing the office from carrying out its mandate. [src: (Euronews)] [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- AI boom, Artificial intelligence industry in China
- Taiwanese prosecutors detain two Supermicro employees in an investigation into alleged document forgery and shipments of Nvidia artificial intelligence servers to China in violation of U.S. export controls. [src: (AFP via The Manila Times)]
- Corruption in Spain
- Spain's National Court charges the Civil Guard's director-general Mercedes González Fernández and her deputy with the offences of abuse of office and obstruction of justice in connection with the ruling PSOE's alleged operation against judges and prosecutors investigating cases of corruption involving party members. [src: (Demócrata)]
- Flamingo Revolution
- Police clash with demonstrators in Albania during a protest against the government and the Sazan Island Resort project. [src: (AP)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Algerian parliamentary election
- Algerians vote for 407 seats of the People's National Assembly amid a cost-of-living crisis and candidate bans upon the Hirak movement. [src: (AP)]
- Protests and uprisings in Tibet since 1950
- A man protesting against the annexation of Tibet by China lights himself on fire outside of the headquarters of the United Nations in New York City, United States. He is transported to Bellevue Hospital where he dies from his injuries. [src: (AA)] [src: (CTV News)]
Sports
- 2026 Wimbledon Championships
- In tennis, Alexandra Eala becomes the first Filipino woman to reach the third round of a Grand Slam tournament after defeating Australian player Maya Joint in the Wimbledon women's singles tournament. She will face reigning Wimbledon champion Iga Świątek next. [src: (ABS-CBN)] [src: (WTA)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 20
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign
- 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran
- The United States Central Command says that the U.S. military has redirected seven commercial vehicles and disabled one since the blockade on Iranian ports was reinstated on July 14. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- Greek shipping company Dynacom Tankers reports that two oil tankers, the Malta-flagged Panamax-sized tanker Kavomaleas and Liberian-flagged crude carrier Acheloos, were attacked off the coast of Oman near the Strait of Hormuz after being hit by unknown projectiles. [src: (Reuters)] 
- Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claims that two tankers have exploded after passing through the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (The Hill)]
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war, Qatar as a mediator in conflict
- Mediators Pakistan and Qatar propose a 10-day ceasefire in an effort to revive the Islamabad Memorandum signed last month. [src: (MENA via The New Arab)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian says that Iran is in a "full-scale war". [src: (The Guardian)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
- The Jordanian military says air defences intercepted three Iranian missiles targeting Jordan. [src: (AFP via Business Recorder)]
- The New York Times reports American soldiers were injured and several helicopters were damaged in Iranian strikes against Jordan. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)] [src: (The New York Times)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
- The Kuwaiti defense ministry reports that the military has intercepted ballistic missiles and drones entering Kuwait's airspace. [src: (Arab Times Kuwait)]
- July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
- The U.S. CENTCOM completes a 10th round of strikes against Iranian military command centers, missile and drone launch sites, maritime capabilities and air defense systems. [src: (Reuters)]
- Gaza war
- The Israeli military says that they have killed two Islamic Jihad militants in separate strikes in the Gaza Strip, in violation of the ongoing ceasefire. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- Hamas names Khalil al-Hayya as its new leader, replacing former leader Yahya Sinwar. [src: (Reuters)]
- Red Sea crisis
- Houthi-controlled Yemen declares a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia effective immediately, after accusing it of an "aggressive siege" against Yemen for nearly 12 years. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (CNBC)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Humanitarian impact of the Sudanese civil war
- Saudi Arabia–Sudan relations
- A plane operated by Saudi Arabia's King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center arrives in Khartoum, Sudan, with aid, food, and medical supplies amidst the civil war. [src: (Asharq Al-Awsat)]
- Sudan–United States relations
- The United States imposes new sanctions upon the Sudanese military junta, alleging the use of chemical weapons including chlorine gas in the civil war. [src: (RFI)]
- War against the Islamic State
- Iraqi insurgency
- The Iraqi military say that they have destroyed six ISIS hideouts in Kirkuk, Iraq. [src: (Iraqi News)]
Business and economy
- Canada–United States relations
- 2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico
- U.S. president Donald Trump signs another executive order imposing 50% tariffs on many Canadian goods, including USMCA-covered products, citing alleged discriminatory trade practices. The duties take effect in 30 days, with exemptions for energy, potash, and products under sector-specific tariffs. [src: (AFP via Vanguard)] [src: (CBC News)]
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
- The nationwide gas prices in the United States exceeds US$4 per gallon, the highest since June 17. [src: (AP)] [src: (NBC News)]
- Brent Crude oil surpasses US$90 per barrel as oil prices increase amidst the ongoing escalation, while West Texas Intermediate reaches $84.49. [src: (CNBC)]
Disasters and accidents
- Twenty people are killed, 80 others are injured and more than 100 people remain missing after heavy rains caused flash floods in eastern Afghanistan. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Twelve people are killed and 13 others are missing after a suspected methane explosion collapses part of a tunnel at a hydropower project along the Teesta River in Namchi, Sikkim, India. Rescue teams detect toxic gases while searching for those trapped. [src: (AFP via CNA)]
Health and environment
- Thousands of fish die in a canal in Sint Maarten in what officials describe as the largest fish kill in the country's history. A critical drop in oxygen levels is being blamed for the deaths. [src: (AP)]
Law and crime
- Illegal drug trade in the United States, Mexican drug war
- A federal court in New York, U.S., sentences Sinaloa Cartel co-founder El Mayo to life imprisonment and orders $15 billion in forfeiture after he pled guilty to charges related to leading the cartel. [src: (AFP via Le Monde)]
- Heavy clashes erupt between police and protesters in Bologna, Italy, after a 42-year-old Moroccan man, Abderrahim Fakir, was killed by police while being handcuffed the previous day. [src: (Il Sole 24 ore)] [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Delhi Jantar Mantar protests
- Indian riot police baton-charge protesters marching toward the Parliament House in New Delhi over irregularities involving the NEET. Thousands demand education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, while Delhi Police restrict internet access and say the demonstration lacked permission. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- 2026 Labour Party leadership crisis
- Sir Keir Starmer resigns as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, and is succeeded by Andy Burnham. [src: (CNN)] [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (The Telegraph)]
- 2026 São Toméan presidential election
- Santomean president Carlos Vila Nova wins re-election with 55.94% of the vote, while his main opposition candidate Nito Abreu comes second with 41.42% of the vote. [src: (Reuters)]
- Next Nicaraguan general election
- Nicaraguan co-president Daniel Ortega announces that the country will hold no further elections in order to "build a wall" against the political opposition. [src: (The Guardian)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 21
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
- The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says that they have launched strikes on Amazon's data center in Bahrain. [src: (CNBC)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
- The U.S. military confirms that a third service member, identified as 28-year-old Sgt. Angel S Rampersad of New York, was killed during a recent attack on the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, bringing the total American casualties to 18. [src: (Military Times)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Malta's sustainable mobility ministry confirms that the Greek-owned Malta-flagged oil tanker M/T Kavomaleas was "subject to an attack" in the Strait of Hormuz as it was navigating the southern corridor of the waterway. Additionally, all 23 crew members of the vessel are reported to be rescued. [src: (Malta Today)]
- A tanker is attacked by Iran in the coast of Oman near the Strait of Hormuz in the wake of the U.S. military conducting strikes for a 10th consecutive night yesterday, forcing crew to abandon ship. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations also confirms the attack. [src: (Military.com)]
- July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
- Israeli finance minister Bezalel Smotrich says that Israel will not join the United States in striking Iran. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- The United States Central Command confirms that they have launched an 11th round of strikes against Iran, against hangars and military targets such as military logistics infrastructure. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)] [src: (Reuters)] 
- Gaza war
- The Israeli military and Shin Bet states that senior Hamas Gaza City Brigade commander Adham Ibrahim Shaaban Nasman, who was involved in directing the October 7, 2023, attacks and taking hostages, has been killed in a Israeli airstrike in the city last weekend, despite the ongoing ceasefire. [src: (The Sunday Guardian)] [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- Local medics report that 12 Palestinians, including four children, have been killed in airstrikes across Gaza City, in violation of the ongoing ceasefire. [src: (BBC News)]
- Red Sea crisis
- Two oil tankers departing Saudi Arabia, Xin Long Yang and Rodos, turn around in the Red Sea and head for the Suez Canal instead of the Strait of Bab-el-Mandeb, after a warning by Houthi-controlled Yemen. [src: (Reuters)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Darfur campaign
- Around 21 people are reported to be killed in a drone strike by Rapid Support Forces in the Tina region of Sudan's North Darfur state near the border with Chad. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Communal conflicts in Nigeria
- Nigerian bandit conflict
- A survivor and local official say an armed gang abducted more than 40 people during raids on 11 villages in Maru, Zamfara State, Nigeria, over the weekend. The local government requests additional security forces. [src: (AFP via NDTV)]
- Residents say motorcycle-riding gunmen killed at least 24 farmers and wounded several others in attacks on villages in Talata Mafara, Zamfara State, before stealing livestock and leaving the area. [src: (Reuters)]
- Three women and a zonal commander are killed, while two youths are injured, as gunmen ambush a youth meeting in Omoku, Rivers State, Nigeria following a local community dispute. [src: (PunchNG)]
Business and economy
- Tariffs in the second Trump administration
- 2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico
- A spokesperson for Canadian infrastructure minister Gregor Robertson announces that Canada has cancelled a joint opening ceremony for the Gordie Howe International Bridge that will connect Detroit, Michigan, and Windsor, Ontario, after U.S. president Donald Trump announced 50% tariffs on Canadian goods. [src: (AP)] [src: (CBC)]
- Trump announces that imported generic drugs will remain tariff-free until August 2028, face a 100% tariff for one year, and a 200% tariff thereafter, citing efforts to move pharmaceutical production to the country. [src: (AFP via NDTV)]
- Russia stops issuing bonds after recent auctions failed to find buyers. [src: (Bloomberg)]
Disasters and accidents
- In Vietnam, a fire on a bus travelling from Lâm Đồng province to Ho Chi Minh City kills seven passengers and injures five others. [src: (Reuters)]
- The death toll from the sinking of passenger ferry MV Barima off the coast of Guyana two days ago rises to 53. Seventy-seven others were rescued, while over 55 remain missing. [src: (NEWS Source Guyana)] [src: (Demerara Waves)] [src: (Guyana Chronicle)]
- The Australian reports that Australian doctor Tareq Kamleh, who traveled to Syria to join the Islamic State, is found alive in a prison in Baghdad, Iraq. [src: (ABC News Australia)] [src: (The West Australian)]
Health and environment
- 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
- The U.S. state of Michigan reports 6,571 cases of cyclosporiasis, which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis. [src: (Reuters)]
- Venezuela's health ministry reports that the hantavirus killed three people in Anzoátegui, says no evidence indicates human-to-human transmission, and rejects any connection to two unexplained deaths among medical workers in Barinas. [src: (AFP via Jamaica Observer)]
International relations
- Lebanon–United States relations
- U.S. president Donald Trump authorizes U.S. airlines to resume direct flights to Lebanon, ending a suspension imposed after the 1985 hijacking of TWA Flight 847. [src: (The Independent)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Delhi Jantar Mantar protests
- Indian police detain Lok Sabha opposition leader Rahul Gandhi during education-reform protests in New Delhi after he called for prime minister Narendra Modi's resignation. Parliament adjourns as demonstrators demand accountability for examination scandals and education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's removal. [src: (AFP via The New Zealand Herald)] [src: (The Hindu)] [src: (The Times of India)]
- Two American tourists are injured, including one seriously, in a stabbing attack near the Acropolis in Athens, Greece. A 60-year-old Greek man is taken into custody. [src: (AP)]
Politics and elections
- Dismissal of Mykhailo Fedorov
- Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy dismisses commander-in-chief Oleksandr Syrskyi amid protests over the removal of defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov and appoints Joint Forces commander Mykhailo Drapatyi as Syrskyi's replacement. [src: (CNN)]
- Republican People's Party absolute nullity crisis
- Özgür Özel, the leader of the Turkish opposition Republican People's Party, who was ousted in May by a judicial ruling, announces that he will establish a new political party. [src: (AP)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- The French Parliament approves legislation allowing limited use of acetamiprid and flupyradifurone, pesticides banned nationally but permitted in the European Union. Environment minister Monique Barbut says she will resign over the measure. [src: (AFP via News.com.au)]
Science and technology
- The wreckage of Pan Am Flight 526A, a Douglas DC-4 that crashed into the sea off Puerto Rico in 1952, killing 52 people, is located by a veteran aviation search team. [src: (The Dallas Express via Yahoo News)]
Sports
- 2026–27 Premier League
- In association football, Chelsea sign attacking midfielder Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa for a British record transfer fee of £117 million. [src: (BBC Sport)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 22
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
- The Jordanian military reports that air defenses have intercepted 8 out of 10 projectiles fired by Iran against the country in Aqaba near the Israeli border, with two missiles landing in remote areas. [src: (ABC News)] [src: (CBC)] [src: (Ynetnews)]
- Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war
- The General Staff of the Kuwait Army reports that Kuwait's military and air defenses have been actively intercepting "hostile drones" from Iran. [src: (Arab Times Kuwait)] [src: (The Times Kuwait)]
- July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
- The United States military launches Tomahawk missile strikes on Iran's Larak Island. [src: (AFP via Al Arabiya)]
- The U.S. Central Command launches a new round of strikes against Iran, marking the 12th consecutive day of attacks. [src: (AP)] [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Financial Times reports that the tanker Kavomalaes, belonging to Greek shipowner George Prokopiou, was "highly likely" to have been captured in the Strait of Hormuz by Iran two days earlier. [src: (Forbes)]
- Gaza war
- The Israel Defense Forces and Shin Bet announces that they have killed three Hamas militants in the northern Gaza Strip, including one in the Hamas military wing that took part in the October 7 attacks on Israel. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)] [src: (Cleveland Jewish News)]
- Red Sea crisis
- Seven oil tankers departing Saudi Arabia's port of Yanbu change course away from the Strait of Bab-el-Mandeb after the Houthis announced a blockade on Saudi Arabian ports. [src: (The Washington Post)] [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war
- 2026 Kabul hospital airstrike
- Amnesty International calls for an investigation into a Pakistani airstrike against a drug rehabilitation center in Kabul, Afghanistan, as a possible war crime. [src: (The Washington Post)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- UNICEF reports that six people, including two children, have been killed and 30 people including children have been injured in a drone strike on a market in Al-Rahad, North Kordofan, Sudan. [src: (AA)]
- A Chadian official reports that a drone attack from Sudanese territory has attacked positions in Chad, injuring civilians and destroying vehicles and several shops. The attack is the fifth in recent months, following an incursion by Rapid Support Forces last January. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Allied Democratic Forces insurgency
- Sixteen civilians, most of whom gold miners, are killed during a village attack suspected to have been perpetrated by ADF forces in Mandeite locality, Mambasa, Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo. [src: (AA)]
- Southern Thailand insurgency
- Five soldiers are killed and six civilians are injured in a mass shooting by ten unknown gunmen at a security checkpoint in Narathiwat province, Thailand. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir
- A 35-year-old head constable is shot and killed in a militant attack in Anantnag, Jammu and Kashmir, India. The Resistance Front claims responsibility. [src: (NDTV)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
- Oil prices, including Brent Crude and West Texas Intermediate, rise to over US$95 and $86 per barrel, respectively, and the United States average gasoline price rises to $4.06 per gallon, amidst the ongoing conflict. [src: (CNBC)] [src: (NBC News)]
Disasters and accidents
- Seven people are killed after a truck collides with a medical transport van in Pernambuco, Brazil. [src: (Xinhua)]
- A Robinson R44 helicopter crashes in Sincan, Ankara, Turkey, killing the pilot and injuring the co-pilot. [src: (Turkiye Today)]
- In the United States, West Virginia governor Patrick Morrisey declares a state of emergency and announces that 100 National Guard troops have been deployed after flash floods caused by torrential rains were reported across the state, including the northern part. [src: (AP)] [src: (The Independent)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak
- The death toll from the ongoing measles outbreak in Bangladesh exceeds 800. [src: (The Business Standard)] [src: (Dhaka Tribune)]
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- African CDC director Jean Kaseya reports that the death toll from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached past 1,000. [src: (AP)]
- 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
- The number of reported cyclosporiasis cases in the U.S. state of Michigan exceeds 7,000. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (WDIV)]
- The fire department of Tokyo, Japan, reports 453 heat-related hospitalizations, its highest daily total since records began in 2010, as a severe heat wave kills one person and leaves four critically ill. The country's Fire and Disaster Management Agency reports at least 14 heat-related deaths nationwide over the previous week. [src: (AFP via Malay Mail)]
International relations
- Saudi Arabia–United States relations, Nuclear program of Saudi Arabia
- Saudi Arabia and the United States sign a civil nuclear cooperation agreement allowing Saudi Arabia to use U.S. reactor technology, enrich uranium, and reprocess nuclear waste. The pact excludes the IAEA Additional Protocol and proceeds to U.S. congressional review. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- Stabbing of Salman Rushdie
- The federal trial against Hadi Matar, the man who attempted to kill author Salman Rushdie in August 2022 in New York, United States, opens. If he is convicted, Matar faces a sentence of life in prison. He is already serving a 25-year state prison sentence in New York. [src: (AP)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- Unknown gunmen open fire at a police station in Canindeyú Department, Paraguay, killing three officers and wounding another. [src: (Abc.com)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Delhi Jantar Mantar protests
- Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi is released after police detained him outside prime minister Narendra Modi's residence yesterday during protests demanding education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and changes to the examination system. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Catholic Church in China
- Pope Leo XIV consecrates Fr. Joseph Chang Yanfeng as the bishop of Chifeng in the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China under the 2018 provisional framework, which cedes authority over its bishops to the Chinese government. [src: (Holy See)] [src: (Vatican News)]
Science and technology
- Exomoon candidates
- The European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope reports evidence of a possible exomoon-like object orbiting the brown dwarf CD-35 2722 B in the CD-35 2722 system, in a study published in the Nature journal. [src: (Space.com)] [src: (Phys.org)] [src: (Nature)]
|

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 23
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran
- The United States Central Command (CENTCOM) says it has redirected 12 commercial vessels and disabled one since the naval blockade on Iran resumed on July 14. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy says it has stopped three oil tankers from passing through the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
- The Islamic Republic News Agency reports that the U.S. military struck the Shalamcheh area near the Iran–Iraq border. Two people are reported to be killed and 11 are reported injured. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- The U.S. CENTCOM reports on X that they have conducted strikes against Iran for a 13th consecutive night amidst clashes over shipping routes, with explosions reported in Ahvaz, Bandar Abbas, and Qeshm Island. [src: (MENA via The New Arab)] [src: (WLS-TV)]
- Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war
- Kuwait's defense ministry reports that a drone has hit the Abdali area near the Iraqi border. [src: (KUNA via Arab Times Kuwait)] [src: (Kurdistan24)]
- Red Sea crisis
- The Houthis claim to have attacked two Saudi Arabian oil tankers in the Red Sea for their violation of the blockade by Yemen's Houthi-led armed forces. There are no reported casualties. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Shipping data shows that two Chinese very-large crude carriers carrying four million ​barrels of Saudi Arabian oil, the Singaporean-flagged VLCC Xin Long Yang and Chinese-flagged VLCC Cosnew Lake, are heading towards Bab-el-Mandeb strait. [src: (Reuters)]
- Germany's defence ministry moves the Frankenthal-class minehunter Fulda and the replenishment oiler Mosel from the coast of Djibouti to the eastern Mediterranean Sea, citing uncertainty over a planned Strait of Hormuz mission and concerns about prolonged deployment affecting the vessels. [src: (AFP via Al Arabiya)]
- Reuters reports that Iran sent Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps officers, along with drone- and missile-related equipment, on a Mahan Air flight to Houthi-controlled Yemen on July 13, in preparation for the blockade on Saudi Arabia. [src: (Reuters)]
- Sudanese civil war
- 2026 Blue Nile campaign
- Emergency lawyers report that a drone strike has killed several civilians in the Badia area of Sudan's Blue Nile State. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
- Oil prices, including Brent Crude and West Texas Intermediate, increase to over US$101 per barrel and to nearly $93 per barrel, respectively, after the escalation in the Red Sea. The United States gasoline national average increases to $4.09 per gallon. [src: (NBC News)]
- Foie gras controversy
- Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signs a law banning the production and sale of foie gras, citing animal cruelty. The measure effectively ends Brazilian imports of the product. [src: (Reuters)]
- Tariffs in the second Trump administration
- The United States imposes tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on imports from 60 trading partners, citing forced-labor concerns. The duties take effect Friday and exempt USMCA-covered goods and products already subject to sector-specific tariffs. [src: (AFP via Philippine Daily Inquirer)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 France wildfires
- More than 20,000 people are evacuated from their homes as wildfires spread in Gironde, France. More than 700 firefighters have been deployed to battle the fires. [src: (BBC News)] 
Health and environment
- 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
- Taylor Farms temporarily suspend operations at its processing facility in central Mexico after American health officials linked it to a current cyclosporiasis outbreak in the U.S., which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis. [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- 2025 shootings of Minnesota legislators
- United States federal judge John R. Tunheim sentences Vance Boelter to two life terms plus 40 years without parole for killing Minnesota state representative Melissa Hortman and her husband and wounding state senator John Hoffman and his wife in June 2025. [src: (AFP via The Manila Times)]
- International Criminal Court investigation in Darfur
- The International Criminal Court at The Hague, Netherlands, officially drops charges against former militia leader Abdallah Banda, who was previously charged for his role in a 2007 attack on African Union peacekeepers during Sudan's Darfur conflict. [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- Reactions to the 2026 Iran war
- The United States House of Representatives votes 214–208 to approve war powers legislation attempting to require the president of the United States to halt military action against Iran. The United States Senate votes 47–49 to stop the legislation from advancing. [src: (CNBC)] [src: (Reuters)]
Science and technology
- The International Mathematical Union awards the 2026 Fields Medals to Yu Deng, John Pardon, Jacob Tsimerman, and Hong Wang at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States. Wang becomes the third woman to receive the prize after Maryam Mirzakhani in 2014 and Maryna Viazovska in 2022. [src: (AFP via Le Monde)]
Sports
- In association football, Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger submit joint bids to host the 2032 Africa Cup of Nations under the Alliance of Sahel States. [src: (BBC Sport)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 24
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
- Bahrain's military says that they have intercepted a number of missiles and drones from Iran. [src: (Arab News)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
- Jordan's military says that they have intercepted seven missiles and six drones launched from Iran. No casualties or damage were reported. [src: (Al-Monitor)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
- Kuwait's army says that its air defenses confronted several attacks from Iran. [src: (Arab News)]
- Iran says it has attacked U.S. military bases in Bahrain, Jordan, and Kuwait, including the Isa Air Base, using Arash drones. [src: (Euronews)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran
- The U.S. military says its forces fired into a tanker's engine room and disabled the vessel after its crew repeatedly attempted to breach the American blockade of Iranian ports and ignored warnings. [src: (AFP via BSS)]
- The Indian embassy in Tehran reports that the Mozambique-flagged LPG tanker Disha with 28 Indian nationals on the vessel was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz. All 28 crew members were reported safe. [src: (The Hindustan Times)] [src: (India Today)]
- July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
- The United States strikes an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy naval academy in Ziba Kenar, Gilan province, Iran. [src: (Arab News)] [src: (Iran International)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region
- Drones target Erbil in Iraq's Kurdistan Region, with six drones reported to be intercepted. [src: (AP)] [src: (Kurdistan24)]
- The Wall Street Journal reports that Bahraini and Kuwaiti fighter jets attacked military targets inside Iran earlier in July, with air and intelligence support from the United Arab Emirates. [src: (The Wall Street Journal)] [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- Israeli–Palestinian conflict
- Gaza war
- The Israeli military reports that the air force has struck Hamas weapon depots, weapon manufacturing sites and tunnels in the Gaza Strip, and accuses the militant group of violating the ceasefire signed in October 2025. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- July 2026 West Bank unrest
- Clashes in Tell, Nablus, kill four Palestinians and two Israelis after a confrontation between settlers and locals in the town. Subsequent settler attacks in the West Bank injure at least 10 Palestinians. [src: (Haaretz)] [src: (The New York Times)]
- Red Sea crisis, Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
- The Houthis deny reports that they have closed the Bab-el-Mandeb and state that they are not seeking to close it, reaffirming that they have only established a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia. [src: (DW)] [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- Saudi Arabia strikes Houthi military sites in Hodeidah, Yemen, after a long hiatus in response to the movement's attacks on maritime shipping, while the militant group vows to retaliate. [src: (Reuters)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Ukrainian strikes on Wildberries warehouses
- A Wildberries logistic hub in Russia-occupied Crimea is hit by Ukrainian drones and catches fire. [src: (RBC-Ukraine)]
- Ukrainian drones also hit Wildberries logistics hubs in Saint Petersburg and Tver, Russia. [src: (Kyiv Independent)]
- Kyiv strikes
- Ukrainian officials say a Russian ballistic missile strike on a private training ground hosting a defence-industry event in the Kyiv Oblast killed 10 people and injured nearly 100. Prosecutors investigate possible negligence in organizing the event. [src: (Reuters)]
- Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- A Romanian F-16 ​fighter jet shot down a Russian Geran-2 drone near Padina, Buzău County, that had entered its airspace for the first ‌time. [src: (Euronews)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- The North Kordofan government reports that 15 civilians in the Burbur area south of El-Obeid, Sudan have been killed by a Rapid Support Forces drone strike. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
- At least 27 people are killed, including 12 militants, in an attack on a security check post in Tank District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. [src: (Hindustan Times)]
Business and economy
- Tariffs in the second Trump administration
- 2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico
- The Gordie Howe International Bridge, which connects between Detroit, Michigan, U.S., and Windsor, Ontario, Canada, ceremonially opens, with Canadian officials marking the opening ceremony of the bridge with the absence of American officials amidst ongoing trade tensions. [src: (Detroit Free Press)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance
- Paramount announces that they have agreed to delay its US$111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery amidst lawsuits from twelve U.S. state attorneys general. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (The Hill)]
Disasters and accidents
- Wildfires in 2026
- 2026 France wildfires
- French authorities evacuate more than 110,000 people from Cap Ferret, Gironde, by land and sea as an uncontrolled wildfire burns over 19,000 hectares, destroys 80 homes, and threatens the peninsula’s only access road. [src: (The Guardian)]
- 2026 Spain wildfires
- Spanish interior minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska declares a national emergency over wildfires in the Community of Madrid and the Province of Ávila, placing the Military Emergencies Unit in command. Authorities evacuate more than 10,000 people as three major fires remain uncontrolled. [src: (AA)]
- The death toll from the sinking of passenger ferry MV Barima off the coast of Guyana two days ago rises to 72. [src: (The Guardian)] 
- Thirteen people are killed and two others are injured after a heavy boulder rolled down a hill and hit moving vehicles in Chamba District, India. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Five people are killed and three others are injured when a soil collapse buries a house in Hongtong County, Shanxi, China. [src: (Reuters)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- Oxford University reports the first volunteer that has been injected with the Ebola vaccine aimed at targeting the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain of Ebola that is causing a outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. [src: (AFP via GMA News Online)]
- 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
- The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reports that the ongoing cyclosporiasis outbreak, which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis, has spread to an additional four states: Illinois, Kansas, Oklahoma, and Pennsylvania. [src: (CNBC)]
- The U.S. state of Michigan surpasses 8,100 cases of cyclosporiasis. [src: (CBS News)]
- Dengue fever outbreaks
- The Sudan Doctors Union reports a dengue fever outbreak in Sudan's Blue Nile state, killing 39 people and leaving 300 infected. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Measles resurgence in the United States
- The U.S. CDC reports 2,318 confirmed measles cases in the country during the first seven months of 2026, marking the highest annual total since 1991. [src: (AFP via Euractiv)]
International relations
- International sanctions against Iran
- Iran–European Union relations
- The European Union sanctions five Iranian judges over alleged human rights violations and Ashiyane cyber group founder Nima Salehi, whom it accuses of cooperating with Iranian authorities to suppress information. [src: (Reuters)]
- United States sanctions against Iran
- The U.S. treasury department announces sanctions against nine firms and four people associated with sanctioned Iranian financer Babak Zanjani after attempting to evade previous sanctions. [src: (Reuters)]
- International Criminal Court investigation in Venezuela
- Venezuelan foreign minister Félix Plasencia says the country will withdraw from the International Criminal Court (ICC), citing alleged geographic bias. The ICC says it has not received formal notice and that existing investigations and cooperation obligations remain unaffected. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- Mexico–United States relations, Mexican war on drugs
- The U.S. state department, in coordination with the Mexican finance ministry, sanctions over 50 Mexican individuals and companies allegedly linked to the Jalisco New Generation Cartel. [src: (Bloomberg)] [src: (El País)]
Law and crime
- 2020 Phala Phala robbery
- A South African court temporarily halts the parliament's impeachment inquiry into president Cyril Ramaphosa over the theft of US$580,000 from his farm, pending his challenge to a report finding possible constitutional violations. [src: (Reuters)]
- Karolkiewicz family murders
- Eight people are killed, including six children, in an arson and shooting attack at a house in Grand Haven Charter Township, Michigan, United States. [src: (ABC News)] [src: (The Indian Express)]
- Diplomatic sources say International Criminal Court member states voted to remove chief prosecutor Karim Ahmad Khan following sexual misconduct allegations. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (CNN)]
- Prosecutors say thieves stole a 2,500-year-old gold Celtic necklace from the Musée du Pays Châtillonnais in Châtillon-sur-Seine, Côte-d'Or, France, after breaking its display case during opening hours. The artifact belongs to the Vix treasure. [src: (AFP via The Manila Times)]
Politics and elections
- Protests against the dismissal of Mykhailo Fedorov
- For the ninth consecutive day, thousands continue to protest in Kyiv, Ukraine, demanding Mykhailo Fedorov's reinstatement as Minister of Defence. [src: (The Kyiv Independent)]
- Bangladeshi president Mohammed Shahabuddin resigns from office, citing health reasons. [src: (Reuters)]
