- Forty deputies of the Polish Sejm leave the Law and Justice party as part of a dispute between party leader Jarosław Kaczyński and member Mateusz Morawiecki. [src: (AP)] [src: (Polsat )]
Science and technology
- The SpaceX Starship test flight 13, the first to successfully deploy operational Starlink satellites, successfully lands in the Indian Ocean intact. [src: (CNN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 25
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Gaza war
- Attacks on refugee camps in the Gaza war, Killing of health workers in the Gaza war
- A Israeli airstrike reportedly kills a Palestinian medic at the Nuseirat refugee camp in the central Gaza Strip. [src: (Reuters via The Times of Israel)]
- An Israeli airstrike reportedly kills senior brigadier general Abdel-Nasser Al-Maqadma, the head of the Hamas police force in the North Gaza Governorate, Gaza. [src: (Asharq Al-Awsat)] [src: (Reuters)]
- The Israeli military confirms that they have killed several Hamas militants over the past few weeks, including a Nukhba forces cell commander who took part in the Kissufim massacre during the October 7, 2023 attacks. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- The naval forces of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claims to have stopped four vessels from transiting the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
- Iranian health ministry spokesperson Hossein Kermanpour reports no U.S. military strikes against Iran, after 13 consecutive nights of strikes by the U.S. Central Command against the country. [src: (NBC News)]
- The United States halts strikes against Iran after government officials reportedly saw a potential opening to resume diplomatic efforts and talks. [src: (Al-Monitor)] [src: (AP)]
- Red Sea crisis, Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
- Two people are injured by Saudi-led coalition airstrikes on Hodeidah, Houthi-controlled Yemen. A Patriot battery operated by the Greek military intercepts two ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis at Aramco facilities in Yanbu and Jizan, Saudi Arabia. [src: (CNBC)] [src: (NBC News)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Ukrainian officials say a Russian drone strike on a postal facility in Sumy has killed two people. [src: (AFP via BGNES)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- Darfur Joint Protection Force spokesperson Mutawakkil Ali Wakil confirms that, in coordination with the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), that the joint force have retaken control of Umm Sayala, North Kordofan, Sudan, with 38 members of the Rapid Support Forces confirmed to have been killed. [src: (Sudan Horizon)]
- The SAF and Darfur Joint Protection Force recapture Jebrat al Sheikh alongside the North Kordofan towns of Bara and Al-Baraka. Additionally, Darfur governor Minni Arko Minawi confirms the recaptures. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
Disasters and accidents
- Snyder Fire
- A fourth firefighter dies from injuries sustained in a wildfire at the Colorado–Utah border in the United States on June 27. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (KUSA)]
- 2026 Assam floods
- The death toll from the flash floods in Assam, India, rises to 62, after fourteen more fatalities are confirmed. [src: (NDTV)]
- At least 35 people are killed and 30 others are injured when two buses collide on the Deir ez-Zor–Damascus road in Syria. [src: (Reuters)]
- Two people are killed when a Tecnam P2010 aircraft crashes into a home in Ganderkesee, Lower Saxony, Germany. [src: (DPA via South China Morning Post)]
- One person is killed and at least 22 others are injured in a five-alarm fire in Flushing, New York City, United States. [src: (WNBC)]
International relations
- Brazil–United States relations
- Brazil denies visas to two U.S. state department officials seeking election-related meetings in Brasília, citing risks of "political exploitation". The U.S. state department says the visit concerns electoral integrity and freedom of expression. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Berlin Pride attack
- Abdul Ballout, a 21-year-old Lebanese-German, drives into a crowd at the pride festival in Berlin, Germany, killing a person and injuring 29 others. A suspect is on the run. [src: (CNN)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Brazilian general election
- Brazil's Liberal Party formally nominates Rio de Janeiro senator Flávio Bolsonaro, former president Jair Bolsonaro's son, as its presidential candidate in the upcoming election. [src: (AFP via Philippine Daily Inquirer)] [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Delhi Jantar Mantar protests
- Indian education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns after protests over alleged entrance-examination leaks and broader education-system irregularities. His resignation marks the Modi government's first major concession to the demonstrations. [src: (AFP via Le Monde)]
- The Bishop of Aberdeen in Scotland declares the sedevacantist Sons of the Most Holy Redeemer religious institute, an order associated with the Society of Saint Pius X, to be excommunicated, after they consecrated a bishop without Vatican approval. [src: (The Herald)] [src: (The Catholic Herald)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 26
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war, Qatar as a mediator in conflict
- Iran and the United States submit their responses to a proposal by Pakistan and Qatar to resume talks between the two countries. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy says it has prevented six ships from transiting the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (CNBC)]
- Iranian media reports that an oil tanker exploded in the Strait of Hormuz after it has hit a naval mine. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- Gaza war
- Humanitarian aid during the Gaza war
- Five aid convoys from the United Arab Emirates carrying 938 tonnes of humanitarian aid arrive in Gaza as part of Operation Chivalrous Knight 3. [src: (Gulf Today)] [src: (Sharjah24)]
- The Israeli military states that an Hamas unmanned aerial vehicle unit commander was killed in an airstrike yesterday in central Gaza, in violation of the ongoing ceasefire. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- Yemeni civil war
- Red Sea crisis
- Eleven vessels cross the Bab-el-Mandeb strait, according to shipping data from Kpler. [src: (Reuters)]
- Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
- The Houthis shoot down a Saudi Arabian reconnaissance drone in northwest Yemen. [src: (AFP via The Times of Israel)]
- Sudanese civil war
- The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) announces that they have recaptured the North Kordofan areas of Umm Qarfa and Juraikh. The SAF also seize control of the National Export Highway which connects Sudan's capital Khartoum and North Kordofan. [src: (Sudan Horizon)] [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- At least 30 people are killed and others are injured in an attack on a community by unknown gunmen in Kaura, Kaduna State, Nigeria. [src: (CTV News)]
Arts and culture
- UNESCO designates the Alamut Castle in Qazvin province, Iran, a World Heritage Site. [src: (Tehran Times)]
Disasters and accidents
- Vietnamese cargo ship sinks in the South China Sea along the Vietnamese coast. Forty-five people are rescued while 17 more are still missing. [src: (Reuters)]
International relations
- Argentina–Brazil relations
- Brazil recalls its ambassador to Argentina and summons Argentina's ambassador after Argentine president Javier Milei made remarks deemed derogatory about Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Supreme Court justice Alexandre de Moraes at a political event in São Paulo. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Iran–Ukraine relations, Ukraine in the 2026 Iran war
- The Iranian foreign ministry summons the Ukrainian chargé d'affaires in Tehran over an attack by Ukraine on an Iranian ship in the Caspian Sea that killed an Iranian sailor, calling it a "hostile and criminal act". [src: (CNBC)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Berlin Pride attack
- A suspect in a recent vehicle-ramming and mass stabbing attack in Berlin, identified as a 21-year-old German citizen of Lebanese descent, is shot and killed by police after allegedly rushing toward officers with a weapon. [src: (CNN)]
- 2026 Seattle Center shooting
- Three people are killed and four others are injured in a shooting during the annual Bite of Seattle festival in Seattle, Washington, United States. [src: (CNN)]
Politics and elections
- 2027 Salvadoran presidential election
- El Salvador's Nationalist Republican Alliance nominates former legislator Mayteé Iraheta for president, while the Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front nominates physician Rafael Aguirre. [src: (Reuters)]
Science and technology
- International Space Station expeditions
- Expedition 74, the joint NASA–Roscosmos–ESA expedition aboard the International Space Station, ends after the Soyuz MS-28 undocks and lands on Earth in Kazakhstan. [src: (CNN)]
Sports
- 2026 Formula One World Championship
- 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix
- In auto racing, Formula One announces that Malaysia's Sepang International Circuit will host the rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix in October, under an agreement signed between Bahrain and Malaysia. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 All-Ireland Senior Football Championship, Sports-related curses
- In Gaelic football, the All-Ireland Senior Football Championship concludes with Mayo defeating Kerry in the final to end one of sport's longest-running droughts and a 75-year wait for the title. [src: (ABC News Australia)] [src: (ESPN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 27
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Gaza war
- Mass detentions in the Gaza war
- Palestinian media reports that Israel has released 60 Gazan detainees back to the Gaza Strip. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) and Shin Bet state that Hamas' internal security head Wael Musa Khaled Ladawi was killed in a airstrike in the Deir al-Balah area of the central Gaza Strip, in violation of the ongoing ceasefire. [src: (The Jewish Chronicle)]
- The IDF claim that Palestinian Islamic Jihad Nukhba militant Amro Abu Alrish and Hamas commander Abd Al-Nasser Al-Aziz Maqadmeh were killed in separate strikes in Gaza, which violated the ongoing ceasefire. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- 2026 Iran war
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
- Iran and the United States pause strikes as the U.S. allows additional time for negotiations and Iran suspends retaliatory attacks against U.S. allies. [src: (AFP via The Manila Times)]
- Saudi Arabia in the 2026 Iran war
- Saudi Arabia's defense ministry reports intercepting drones fired by Iran-backed Iraqi militias from inside Iraq, which targeted oil facilities in eastern Saudi Arabia and the Riyadh area. [src: (France 24)]
- Yemeni civil war
- Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict, Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
- The Houthis launch a drone attack that damages the Abqaiq oil field in eastern Saudi Arabia. [src: (BBC Persian)] [src: (France 24)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- Siege of El Obeid
- Drone strikes are reported in El-Obeid, North Kordofan, Sudan, hours after the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) secured the National Export Highway, which connects Sudan's capital Khartoum and North Kordofan. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (The Defense Post)]
- The Sudanese Doctors Network reports that the main hospital in Jebrat al Sheikh District, North Kordofan, has been looted and turned into a military barracks. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- SAF general and leader Abdel Fattah al-Burhan visits the newly captured areas in North Kordofan alongside Sudan Shield Forces leader Abu Aqla Kaikal and Darfur Governor Minni Arko Minnawi. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- The Sudanese National Mine Action Center (NMAC) reports that 80% of war remnants have been removed from the Khartoum State and announces plans to expand survey and removal operations in Sudanese areas recently recaptured by the SAF. [src: (Sudan Tribune in Arabic)]
Arts and culture
- UNESCO designates the Amazon Theatre and Theatro da Paz, opera houses in the Amazonia region of Brazil, as World Heritage Sites. [src: (AP)]
Business and economy
- Canada–United States relations
- 2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico
- The Gordie Howe International Bridge, which connects between Detroit, Michigan, U.S., and Windsor, Ontario, Canada, officially opens to traffic after months of delay due to the countries' trade war and the U.S. imposition of tariffs on Canada. [src: (Detroit Free Press)] [src: (Global News)]
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- Singapore's monetary authority tightens its monetary policy for the second time in three months by increasing the Singapore dollar's appreciation rate against a trade-weighted currency basket, citing rising import costs and inflation risks caused by the Iran war. [src: (AFP via South China Morning Post)]
Disasters and accidents
- Wildfires in 2026
- 2026 France wildfires
- Wildfires continue in the Gironde region near Bordeaux, France, as president Emmanuel Macron describes it as "the worst fire-related crisis since World War II." [src: (AP)]
- 2026 Pacific hurricane season
- Hurricane Genevieve strengthens into a category 5 pacific hurricane, the first in the Pacific region since 2024. [src: (The Independent)]
- The death toll from heavy rains and flooding in Pakistan since June increases to 107 people killed and at least 344 others injured. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- A landslide occurs at the Gold Ridge Mine in Guadalcanal, Solomon Islands. Local media reports ten bodies recovered, while the National Referral Hospital says it expects more fatalities. [src: (AFP via BSS)]
Health and environment
- Sudanese cholera epidemic
- The General Coordination for Refugees and Displaced Persons in Darfur, Sudan, reports seven cholera cases across the region in displacement camps between July 5 and July 25. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approves a new blood test for colorectal cancer screenings in older adults, including those above age 45. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (MedPage Today)]
International relations
- Brazil–Lithuania relations
- The Lithuanian government registers a resolution to open an embassy in Brasilia, Brazil, in October. The country currently has a consulate-general in São Paulo. [src: (LRT)]
- Kuwait–Pakistan relations
- Kuwait approves the Kuwait–Pakistan Defence Cooperation Agreement, a five-year framework for defence cooperation between the two countries covering military training, exchanges, defence technology, logistics, and cooperation between their armed forces. [src: (Anadolu Ajansı)] [src: (Jordan News)]
- Romania–Russia relations, Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Romania recalls its ambassador to Russia, declares a Russian embassy employee persona non grata, and summons Russia's ambassador after three Russian drones violated Romanian airspace between July 24 and 26. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Chad states its intention to withdraw from the International Criminal Court, citing limited effectiveness and disproportionate attention to African cases. [src: (AFP via Courthouse News Service)]
Law and crime
- The Seoul Central District Court gives former South Korean president Yoon Suk Yeol an 18-month suspended sentence for false statements made during his 2022 election campaign. If upheld, the ruling may void his victory and require Yoon's People Power Party to repay campaign funds. [src: (AFP via The Japan Times)]
- Five people are killed and another is injured in a home invasion and shooting in Gugulethu, Cape Town, South Africa. [src: (News24)]
- Three women are wounded in a mass stabbing near the Porte de Clichy station in Paris, France. The perpetrator is detained. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (The Telegraph)]
Politics and elections
- Politics of Nicaragua
- Nicaraguan co-president Rosario Murillo announces that a legislative vote on a proposed constitutional reform that would exclude opposition parties from future elections has been postponed until September. [src: (AFP via GMA News Online)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 28
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Gaza war
- Gaza peace plan
- A Hamas delegation visits Cairo, Egypt, to resume negotiations on the implementation of the next phase of its ceasefire with Israel. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- 2026 Iran war
- The United States Central Command says that Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces have launched multiple ballistic missiles from Iran in a "surprise attack" against U.S. forces in the Middle East, and that all missiles were successfully intercepted. [src: (Politico)]
- Mali War
- 2026 Mali offensives
- Malian Armed Forces launch strikes against two armed vehicles and Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin and Azawad Liberation Front militants in the Ségou Region near Dagabory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko. [src: (APA)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- Human rights group Emergency Lawyers reports that recent airstrikes have targeted multiple locations in North Kordofan, Sudan, including a water station and civilian vehicles, killing dozens of civilians. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Sudanese refugee crisis, Darfur campaign
- The United Nations reports that over 20,000 people have been displaced in Sudan's Darfur region over insecurity and violence. [src: (Middle East Monitor)]
 Arts and culture
- 2026 Booker Prize
- The longlist for the 2026 Booker Prize is announced. [src: (The Guardian)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Kumamoto earthquake
- A earthquake strikes central Kumamoto Prefecture, Japan, causing a tsunami alert for the western Kyūshū coast. At least 13 people are killed. [src: (CNN)]
- Three more people are rescued from the Vietnamese cargo ship Khoi Nguyen 18 that sank on Saturday. Fourteen others remain missing with a multinational search still underway. [src: (AFP via The Canadian Press)] [src: (South China Morning Post)]
International relations
- International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war
- The United States Senate votes 86–12 to advance legislation imposing sanctions on Russia's energy revenues, financial institutions, officials, and shadow fleet, while authorizing tariffs of up to 100% on major buyers of Russian oil and gas. [src: (Politico)] [src: (Kyiv Post)]
Law and crime
- 2024 Apalachee High School shooting
- The gunman convicted of carrying out a school shooting at Apalachee High School in Winder, Georgia, United States, in 2024, receives four sentences of life in prison without the possibility of parole. [src: (AFP via Philippine Daily Inquirer)]
- Myanmar's military-backed parliament passes a law allowing the death penalty when coercion, unlawful detention, torture, or other abuse used to force victims into online scams results in death. The law also imposes severe penalties on scam-centre operators. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Taiwanese prosecutors detain an Nvidia employee in an investigation into alleged smuggling of advanced artificial intelligence chips to China through falsified transport documents. Authorities hold seven people over shipments of about 50 Supermicro servers that may violate U.S. export controls. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Peruvian general election
- Keiko Fujimori is sworn in as President of Peru after winning the general election in June. [src: (AP)] [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Victorian Labor Party leadership election
- In Australia, Victorian premier Jacinta Allan resigns, triggering a leadership spill. Ben Carroll is elected unanimously as the new Premier and Victorian Labor Party leader. [src: (ABC News Australia)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Women in Algeria
- Khalida Boufedeche is elected the first woman president of the People's National Assembly of Algeria. [src: (France24)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 29
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Gaza war
- Attacks on religious sites during the Israeli invasion of Gaza
- Israeli forces strike a mosque in Gaza City in violation of the ongoing ceasefire and accuses Hamas of using it to store weapons. [src: (The New York Times)]
- Hezbollah–Israel conflict
- 2026 Lebanon war
- Israeli forces accuse Hezbollah of launching a drone attack on its forces in the Ali al-Taher ridge of southern Lebanon, in violation of the ceasefire. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- Israeli forces also claim that their 401st Brigade Combat Team and Yahalom Unit have destroyed an underground headquarters belonging to Hezbollah, located near a UNIFIL post. [src: (Israel National News)] 
- 2026 Iran war
- Saudi Arabia in the 2026 Iran war, Iraq in the 2026 Iran war
- The Saudi Arabian Armed Forces and United States Central Command (U.S. CENTCOM) launch strikes against Iran–backed militias in Iraq in response to Iranian drone attacks against oil facilities in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province. [src: (Iraqi News)] [src: (Reuters)]
- The Popular Mobilization Forces reports that 20 militants have been killed in joint Saudi–U.S. strikes. [src: (The Defense Post)]
- Several members of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps are also confirmed to have been killed in the Saudi–U.S. strikes in Iraq. [src: (The New Region)]
- Egypt in the 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Damietta drone strike
- A drone strike targets the LNG storage tanker Energos Winter, which is leased by the Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Company, at the port of Damietta, Egypt. Additionally, another vessel is also targeted. The group responsible for the strike is currently unknown. [src: (The New York Times)]
- July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
- The U.S. CENTCOM launches strikes against Iran in retaliation of a attempted attack by Iran against Jordan. [src: (AP)]
- A senior officer in U.S. CENTCOM issues an internal email requesting troops to suggest "new creative and unconventional ways to pressure and punish Iran". [src: (CNN)]
- Red Sea crisis
- Data from Kpler shows that 39 commercial vessels have transited through the Bab el-Mandeb yesterday, the highest since July 19, while another five transited it today, including the VLCC Sophia and the Aframax tanker ​Ocean Laureate. [src: (Reuters)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- The Sudan Tribune reports that Rapid Support Forces militants retreating from Umm Sayala, Jabrat al-Sheikh, and Barah have launched retaliatory strikes in North Kordofan. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Somali Civil War
- Five soldiers are killed in a shootout with Al-Shabaab gunmen in Mandera County, Kenya. [src: (Garowe Online)]
- Terrorism in Pakistan
- Ten police officers are killed in a drone attack and ambush in Hangu district of northwest Pakistan. Pakistani authorities claim that 15 of the attackers were killed. [src: (Reuters)]
Disasters and accidents
- Wildfires in 2026
- Two firefighters are killed while battling a wildfire near Rethymno, Crete, Greece, while a third dies near Gytheio, Laconia, during a separate operation. [src: (AFP via Malay Mail)]
- A Bell 412 helicopter crashes while on a fire-fighting training operation in San Juan, Argentina, killing all seven occupants. [src: (AFP via NDTV)]
Health and environment
- Kenya Wildlife Service says preliminary tests indicated cyanide-contaminated tomatoes may have killed 15 elephants near Amboseli National Park over the past month, warning that livestock grazing in the area could also be exposed. [src: (AFP via The Manila Times)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Bolivian protests
- Bolivian prosecutors issue an arrest warrant for former president Evo Morales for allegedly organizing protests and roadblocks across the country in May and June. The investigation follows complaints alleging armed uprising and terrorism. [src: (AFP via Firstpost)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russia's Federal Security Service ​issues an arrest warrant on Telegram founder Pavel Durov for facilitating terrorist activity, alleging that Telegram helps Ukraine plan attacks in Russia. [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- China–Holy See relations, Catholic Church in China
- Pope Leo XIV consecrates Fr. Francis Xavier Duan Yongkun as the coadjutor bishop of Bameng in the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region under the 2018 provisional framework that cedes authority over its bishops to the Chinese government. [src: (Vatican News)]
- The government of Nauru announces the official change of name of the country from Nauru to Naoero. [src: (RNZ)]
Sports
- 2026 FIFA World Cup
- Argentina at the FIFA World Cup
- FIFA opens an investigation into the Argentina national football team over altercations during the World Cup final and the display of a banner of the Falklands. [src: (The Athletic via The New York Times)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 3
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Kyiv strikes
- Ukraine declares a day of mourning for the victims of the Russian bombardment of Kyiv on July 2 as the death toll rises to 30. [src: (DW)]
- Russian missile and drone strikes kill at least five people and injure ten others across Ukraine, including three people in Sumy when a drone struck their apartment building. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Crimea attacks
- Ukrainian forces strike nine substations across Russian-occupied Crimea causing power outages. Saky air base and Gvardeyskoye air base are also targeted with seven jets destroyed or damaged. [src: (The New Voice of Ukraine)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Eastern front of the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russia reports that its forces have captured the eastern Ukrainian city of Kostyantynivka, Donetsk Oblast. [src: (AFP via NDTV)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign, Siege of El Obeid
- United Nations human rights chief Volker Türk issues a "red alert" warning in El-Obeid, North Kordofan, Sudan, of a "catastrophe" and violence in the city. [src: (ABC News)] [src: (ModernGhana)]
- Sudanese foreign minister Mohi El-Din Salem says that the Sudanese government is ready to engage in "sincere initiatives" aimed at ending the civil war that started in April 2023. He also says that initiatives submitted by Sovereign Council chairman and military head Abdel Fattah al-Burhan to the United Nations last year must be a part of this process. [src: (AA)]
- Gaza war
- The Israeli military and Shin Bet state that Hamas militant Muhammad Na'im Jandiya, who allegedly took part in taking hostages during the attack on the Nahal Oz kibbutz in the October 7 attacks on Israel, has been killed in an airstrike in the northern Gaza Strip, violating the ongoing ceasefire. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)] [src: (Ynetnews)]
- Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
- Two policemen, including an additional station house officer, are killed, while a driver is injured, as gunmen open fire on a mobile patrol vehicle in Mohmand District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. [src: (Dawn)]
Disasters and accidents
- In Pakistan, a bus en route from Quetta to Islamabad plunges into a deep roadside ditch in Sherani District, Balochistan, killing 40 people and injuring eight others. [src: (Reuters)]
- Four people are killed, ten are missing and eight others are injured during the collision of a car with a bus, carrying Afghan refugees returning from Pakistan, on the Kabul–Nangarhar highway in Laghman Province, Afghanistan. [src: (Caliber.az)] [src: (Pajhwok)]
Health and environment
- 2026 heat waves
- 2026 European heatwaves
- Health officials in Belgium report a 39% increase of deaths, compared to the week prior, from heat waves in the country during June, while France saw a 29.1% increase. [src: (Euronews)]
- The French health agency reports that over 2,025 people in France have died in heat waves last month between June 22 and June 28. [src: (Le Monde)]
- 2026 North American heat wave
- Heat waves are reported across the eastern and central United States, with 23 states placed under heat warnings by the National Weather Service. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (The New York Times)] [src: (KGW)]
Politics and elections
- Impact of the 2026 Iran war on Iran
- State funeral of Ali Khamenei
- The state funeral of former Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei, who was killed in an airstrike on his compound by Israel and the United States during the first day of the Iran war on February 28, begins as his body lies in state at Tehran's Grand Mosalla. The funeral is expected to draw millions of attendees, including foreign dignitaries. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (The New York Times)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Armenia's parliament passes a law requiring citizens living abroad to meet stricter residency rules before voting, following reports of Russian efforts to influence the June election through Armenians living in Russia. [src: (Reuters)]
- The Royal Palace of Cambodia confirms that King Norodom Sihamoni has returned to the country from Beijing, China, after undergoing treatment and surgery for prostate cancer. [src: (AFP via The Straits Times)] 
- Moldovan prime minister Alexandru Munteanu resigns. [src: (Politico)]
Sports
- 2026 FIFA World Cup
- Egypt at the FIFA World Cup
- In association football, Egypt advances to the round of 16 of a FIFA World Cup for the first time after defeating Australia 4–2 on penalties, following a 1–1 draw after extra time, in the round of 32. [src: (RFI)]
- Argentina at the FIFA World Cup
- Argentine forward and captain Lionel Messi becomes the first player to make 30 FIFA World Cup appearances, score 20 World Cup goals, and score in eight consecutive World Cup matches (including the previous edition), after scoring in the team's 3–2 victory against Cape Verde in the round of 32. [src: (AP)] [src: (ESPN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 30
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire, Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war
- Pakistan foreign ministry spokesman Tahir Andrabi reaffirms that talks between Iran and the United States are still ongoing despite recent strikes by the U.S. military. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
- Jordanian air defenses shoot down five missiles from Iran. [src: (AP)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
- Kuwaiti authorities confirm that an Iranian attack targeted a building belonging to a Chinese company and killed one person. [src: (AFP via The Times of Israel)] [src: (Kuwait Times)]
- Egypt in the 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Damietta drone strike
- The Egyptian cabinet confirms a drone has hit two vessels yesterday at a port in Damietta, Egypt, including the LNG storage tanker Energos Winter. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Data shows that the QatarEnergy-controlled LNG tanker Al Areesh exited the Strait of Hormuz, becoming the first LNG vessel from Qatar visible on ship-tracking data to do so since July 11, when Al Hamra exited the strait from Das Island, United Arab Emirates. [src: (Reuters)]
- Gaza war
- Gaza peace plan
- Mediators and Hamas reach an agreement to implement the second phase of a United States-backed ceasefire signed in October last year during a meeting in Cairo, Egypt. [src: (Egyptian Gazette)]
- U.S. president Donald Trump announces that the Board of Peace has reached a deal for a complete disarmament of Hamas. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Jewish Insider)]
- Amidst reports of a new plan to disarm Hamas, Israel reaffirms that it will not withdraw from the Gaza Strip, including the Yellow Line, until the militant organization is completely disarmed. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- The Gaza Health Ministry reports that four people, including children, are killed in an Israeli strike in Gaza, in violation of the ongoing ceasefire. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- The Israeli military claims it has killed two Hamas militants in separate strikes in the Gaza Strip, including a Nuseirat Battalion commander and a Hamas platoon commander, violating the ongoing ceasefire. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- Red Sea crisis
- Saudi Arabia's government announces the establishment of the Multinational Maritime Defense Alliance with 14 countries signing the founding document in an effort to keep the Bab-el-Mandeb strait open. [src: (Middle East Eye)] [src: (Saudi Press Agency)]
- About 25 vessels cross the Bab-el-Mandeb strait according to data from Kpler shipping data. [src: (Reuters)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russian forces launch hundreds of drones and missiles at Ukraine, killing at least nine people and injuring more than 50 others, including six people killed in a ballistic missile strike on Kryvyi Rih. [src: (NBC News)] [src: (Fana News)]
- 2026 missile explosion in Poland, Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- An armed Russian Kh-101 cruise missile enters Polish airspace around Lublin, prompting NATO to scramble fighter jets in response. It later explodes in the countryside near Tarnawa-Kolonia. [src: (The Kyiv Independent)] [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (DW)] [src: (TVN24 in Polish)]
- Sudanese civil war
- War crimes during the Sudanese civil war
- The Associated Press reports that two former child soldiers said they were trained by Colombian mercenaries after being conscripted by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) during the ongoing civil war in Sudan. [src: (AP)] [src: (The Washington Post)]
- Kordofan campaign
- The Sudanese Air Force launches a series of airstrikes against RSF mobilizations and military positions in the north and west Kordofan. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Terrorism in Pakistan
- The death toll from yesterday's attack in the Hangu district of northwest Pakistan rises to at least eleven police officers. [src: (AP via ABC News)]
Business and economy
- The Intergovernmental Authority on Development trade bloc reopens its office in Khartoum, Sudan, resuming operations for the first time since the start of the country's civil war in April 2023. [src: (Sudan Horizon)] [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Kumamoto earthquake
- The casualty toll from the earthquake in Kumamoto on Kyushu, Japan, earlier this week rises to 35 people killed and over 134 injured. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Quetta coal mine explosion
- At least 34 miners are killed and more are reported missing after a methane gas explosion at a coal mine near Quetta, Balochistan, Pakistan. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- At least nine people are killed and several others are trapped after an explosion at a four-story building in Bhiwandi, Maharashtra, India. [src: (Hindustan Times)]
- Five people are critically injured and six are missing after a residential building collapses during a gas leak explosion in Messina, Sicily, Italy. [src: (SkyNews24)]
- Ten climbers are reported missing, including Nepalese mountaineer Nirmal Purja, after an avalanche on the Broad Peak in Pakistan. [src: (CNN)] [src: (The Indian Express)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- The death toll from the Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo rises to over 1,500 people killed. [src: (AP)]
- Singapore-based Hilleman Laboratories announces plans to advance an rVSV-based vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola into human trials after World Health Organization experts identified it as the most promising candidate for the epidemic. [src: (AFP via CNA)]
- 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
- The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services reports that the U.S. state has surpassed 10,000 cases of cyclosporiasis, which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis. [src: (CBS News MI)]
- Nuclear power in Hungary
- The Paks nuclear power plant in Hungary shuts down for the first time in 44 years amid a drought across the country and extremely low water levels on the Danube river. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (DW)]
International relations
- Morocco–Spain relations
- 2026 Morocco–Spain border incident
- Thousands of undocumented immigrants cross into the Spanish autonomous city of Ceuta from neighboring Morocco. The city's mayor-president, Juan Jesús Vivas, requests the Spanish government to declare a national emergency, but is refused by the interior ministry. [src: (AP)]
- Senior Italian politicians, including prime minister Giorgia Meloni, deputy prime minister Matteo Salvini, and foreign minister Antonio Tajani, call for Spain to be kicked out of the Schengen Zone or the suspension of the Schengen Agreement entirely, citing the alleged threat of undocumented immigrants spreading throughout the European Union. [src: (Politico EU)]
- Chile–Venezuela relations
- Chile and Venezuela restore diplomatic relations after a two-year suspension following Chile's call for a review of the 2024 Venezuelan presidential election results. [src: (AFP via The Manila Times)]
- International recognition of Abkhazia and South Ossetia
- Naoero announces it has withdrawn its recognition of Georgia's breakaway states Abkhazia and South Ossetia, terminating diplomatic relations with these entities "with immediate effect". [src: (Civil Georgia)]
Politics and elections
- Argentine president Javier Milei issues a decree seeking parliamentary approval to bar or expel foreigners accused of inciting hatred against Argentina or its people, while exempting protected political, academic, and ideological expression. [src: (AFP via Vanguard)]
Science and technology
- Cyberwarfare during the 2026 Iran war, 2026 Minnesota water system cyberattack
- The Minnesota IT Services reports a cyberattack across 30 municipal community water systems across the state, with American authorities accusing Iran of being behind the cyberattack. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (The New York Times)]
Sports
- 2026 FIFA crisis, 2030 FIFA World Cup controversies
- In association football, UEFA announces that it will boycott the 2030 FIFA World Cup, scheduled to be hosted by current champions Spain along with Morocco and Portugal, if FIFA president Gianni Infantino proceeds with plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors. [src: (Sky Sports)]
- International sporting sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
- In boxing, World Boxing lifts all restrictions on Russian athletes, allowing them to compete with their national symbols. [src: (Reuters)]
- In ice hockey, the International Ice Hockey Federation extends Russia's ban to the 2027 Men's Ice Hockey World Championships, and says that a decision will be made in November for the 2027 Women's Ice Hockey World Championships. [src: (ESPN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 31
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says that it struck two tankers trying to pass the Strait of Hormuz with aerial protection from the United States, and forced four others to turn around. [src: (The Guardian)]
- Recent evidence by The New York Times show that a U.S. strike yesterday on Qeshm Island hit a family home and killed three people. [src: (The New York Times)]
- Gaza war
- Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Gaza war, Israeli settler violence
- At least eleven Palestinians, including four children, are injured during a raid by Israeli settlers and soldiers in Nablus in the occupied West Bank. Israeli soldiers also detain at least ten people from Bethlehem, Nablus, Salim, and Tell. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Gaza war hostage crisis
- The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) confirms that they have killed a Mujahideen Brigades militant who was involved in the abduction of Avinatan Or and Noa Argamani during the Nova music festival massacre, and directing the abduction of Sudthisak Rinthalak during the October 7 attacks. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)] [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- Gaza peace plan
- Hamas says that they will disarm if Israel withdraws from and ends its military campaign in the Gaza Strip and if Israel and the U.S. honors the ceasefire agreement signed in October 2025. [src: (Middle East Eye)] [src: (The Washington Post)]
- The IDF says that killed two Hamas operatives accused of smuggling weapons into the Gaza Strip in separate strikes. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Two warehouses in Volgograd and Zelenodolsk, Tatarstan, are attacked and set on fire, causing damage estimated at US$1.5 billion, in the latest of a series of Ukrainian drone strikes targeting Russian online retailer Wildberries. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Kyiv Post)]
- Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir
- A migrant worker is fatally shot and another is injured by insurgents in Kulgam district, Jammu and Kashmir, India. [src: (The Indian Express)]
- Mali War
- Human Rights Watch reports that a Sukhoi Su-24 airstrike by the Russian paramilitary group Africa Corps in Mali's Mopti region killed eight civilians in June. [src: (Africanews)] [src: (AP)]
- Sudanese civil war
- The Sudan News Agency reports that the Group 26 unit of the Rapid Support Forces paramilitary group has surrendered its personnel and military equipment to the Sudanese Armed Forces. [src: (Middle East Monitor)]
Business and economy
- AI boom
- South Korea's KOSPI index rises by 18%, its largest single-day gain in history, amid a surge of investment in AI. [src: (The New York Times)]
Disasters and accidents
- A bus en route to Algiers, Algeria, plunges into a deep ravine in El Kerma after skidding off the road, killing 25 people and injuring 44 others. [src: (AP)]
- Twelve people, including five children, are killed and 66 others are injured after a bus overturns on the N1 highway near Trompsburg, Free State, South Africa. [src: (IOL)]
- Two bodies and a body part are recovered after an avalanche on the Broad Peak in Pakistan buried ten climbers yesterday, including Nirmal Purja, who remains missing. [src: (BBC News)]
Health and environment
- A cancer patient at the Christie hospital in Manchester, United Kingdom, becomes the first to receive the ZI-MA4-1 therapy. [src: (BBC)] [src: (The Independent)]
International relations
- Morocco–Spain relations
- 2026 Morocco–Spain border incident
- Ceutan mayor-president Juan Jesús Vivas says that around 60,000 undocumented migrants have entered the Spanish exclave in North Africa in the last 24 hours, as the death toll rises to 57. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (BBC News)]
- Videos on social media appear to show the Spanish Army deploying military vehicles towards the border with Morocco. [src: (Reuters)]
- French interior minister Laurent Nuñez announces that he has ordered increased controls at the border with Spain amid fears the thousands of migrants entering Ceuta could make their way to France. [src: (Politico)]
- Austrian chancellor Christian Stocker and Finnish interior minister Mari Rantanen join Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni in calling for Spain to be suspended from the Schengen Area in response to the mass arrival of migrants in Ceuta over the last 24 hours. [src: (AA)]
- Spanish authorities close the Melilla border crossing with Morocco after around 400 migrants stormed the border barrier. RTVE reports the sound of gunfire and explosions. [src: (AA)]
- Italy suspends Schengen border-free travel with Spain, introducing checks on air and sea passengers and strengthening controls with France along the France–Italy border. [src: (Reuters)]
- Spain's interior ministry says authorities have returned about 48,300 of roughly 50,000 migrants who entered Ceuta from Morocco. [src: (CBS News)]
- Belarus–Latvia relations
- Latvia announces the sudden closure of its border with Belarus, citing "technical reasons". [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- Crime in Karachi
- Murder of Mir Raza Ali
- Pakistani entrepreneur and Wafflix founder Mir Raza Ali Khan is found shot dead in Karachi, Pakistan, two days after he went missing. Police launch a murder investigation into the case. [src: (The Express Tribune)]
- 2019 Sri Lanka Easter bombings
- A Sri Lankan court sentences former police chief Pujith Jayasundara to death for negligence in failing to prevent the 2019 Easter bombings, which killed 279 people. Sri Lanka has not carried out an execution since 1976. [src: (AFP via The Star)]
- Indonesian authorities announces it arrested a Malaysia Airlines pilot for allegedly smuggling over of ecstasy and a package of methamphetamine into Jakarta's Soekarno–Hatta International Airport. [src: (AP)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Bulgarian presidential election
- The Bulgarian National Assembly sets 25 October as the date for the presidential election. [src: (AP)]
Sports
- 2030 FIFA World Cup controversies
- Carlos Cordeiro, senior FIFA executive and adviser to FIFA president Gianni Infantino, resigns in protest of Infantino's plans to sell stakes in FIFA Forward Enterprise to private investors, including American banking institution JPMorgan Chase, calling them "a bad deal for FIFA's members, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game". [src: (Sky News)]
- The Asian Football Confederation joins UEFA in opposing Infantino's plans and vows to boycott the next tournament if they go ahead. [src: (The Independent)]
- Infantino reverses his plan to sell stakes in the FIFA World Cup amidst backlash. [src: (ESPN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 4
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Oman reaches an agreement with France and the United Kingdom to ensure safe navigation through the country's waterways including the Gulf of Oman and Strait of Hormuz. [src: (CNBC)]
- Mali War
- 2026 Mali offensives
- The Al-Qaeda-linked Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin and Tuareg Azawad Liberation Front separatists launch coordinated attacks on the Malian communes and towns of Aguelhok, Anéfis, Gao, and Sévaré. The Malian army says it has repelled the assaults, while local sources report continuing fighting. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Battle of Kostiantynivka
- Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy and the General Staff of the Ukrainian Armed Forces deny Russia's claim that it captured Kostiantynivka, Donetsk Oblast, yesterday, saying Ukrainian forces still control the city and continue defensive operations there. [src: (Reuters)]
- Yemeni civil war
- Over 50 Houthi fighters and 16 soldiers are killed during clashes in Hodeidah, Yemen. Twenty-two more soldiers are also wounded. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Arts and culture
- United States Semiquincentennial
- The United States celebrates the 250th anniversary of the ratification of the U.S. Declaration of Independence in 1776. [src: (BBC News)]
Disasters and accidents
- Nine people are killed and eight others injured after a minibus collides with a truck between and Nechayane, Mykolaiv Oblast, Ukraine. [src: (Xinhua)]
International relations
- China–United States relations
- China releases pastor Jin Mingri, the founder of the Beijing Zion Church, after detaining him since October, with ChinaAid.org saying officials presented the release as a goodwill gesture following U.S. president Donald Trump's visit to China last May. [src: (AFP via New Straits Times)]
- Moldova–Russia relations
- A Russian cultural center in Chișinău, Moldova, closes after the government orders its shutdown, citing security concerns linked to Russian influence and drone incidents amid strained bilateral relations. [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Slovak referendum
- Slovaks vote in a referendum to decide whether to cancel life payments for prime ministers after their terms expire and whether to reopen the office of an anti-corruption agency. The referendum is invalidated due to low turnout. [src: (AP)]
Sports
- 2026 Wimbledon Championships
- In tennis, Alexandra Eala becomes the first Filipino singles player to reach the fourth round of a major tournament after defeating defending champion Iga Świątek in the third round of the Wimbledon Championships women's singles. [src: (AP)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 6
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Gaza war
- Gaza peace plan
- Hamas announces that its government will step down to facilitate the transition of a technocratic administration in the Gaza Strip, as stipulated in the Gaza peace plan of October 2025. In response, the Board of Peace states that it will assess the implementation of these steps. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- The Israeli military states that they have killed five Hamas militants who allegedly attempted to restore underground infrastructure in the northern Gaza Strip, west of the Yellow Line, including Hudhayfah Hussein Abdullah al-Hawajri, a Nukhba militant from the East Jabalia Battalion command, despite the ongoing ceasefire. [src: (Israel National News)]
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- According to shipping data from LSEG, around 10 Japan-linked ships, mostly managed by Mitsui O.S.K. Lines, are reported to have transited through the Strait of Hormuz using the route proposed by Iran. Data also show that a supertanker carrying Saudi crude oil headed for South Korea left over the weekend. [src: (Gulf Today)] [src: (Japan Times)]
- Mali War
- 2026 Mali offensives
- The Al-Qaeda-linked Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin and Tuareg Azawad Liberation Front rebels seize the northern Mali town of Anéfis. [src: (AllAfrica)] [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Ukraine's General Staff reports that drones have struck Russia's Omsk refinery in Omsk, Omsk Oblast in the Siberia region. [src: (Reuters)]
- Kyiv strikes
- At least 22 people are killed and 56 others are injured in a Russian ballistic missile and drone attack on Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine. Search and rescue efforts are underway in Kyiv to free civilians trapped under rubble. [src: (BBC News)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Siege of El Obeid
- The United Nations Human Rights Council orders an inquiry into alleged human rights violations around El-Obeid, North Kordofan, Sudan, warning that civilians face a risk of mass atrocities as the Rapid Support Forces encircles the city amid Sudan's civil war. [src: (AFP via Macau Business)]
- UNICEF reports that over 330 children have been killed in Sudan's civil war in the first six months of 2026. [src: (AP)] [src: (UCICEF)]
Business and economy
- 2022–2026 video game industry layoffs
- Microsoft cuts roughly 4,800 jobs, primarily within its Xbox and commercial sales divisions, while divesting game studios Compulsion Games, Double Fine, Ninja Theory, and Undead Labs. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (The Verge)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Cuban crisis, 2024–2026 Cuba blackouts
- Cuba experiences its third nationwide power outage of the year, with state utility Unión Eléctrica de Cuba reporting a total grid disconnection as the country faces severe fuel shortages and chronic failures in its electricity system. [src: (AFP via The Guardian)]
- 2026 Ezhou-Huanggang tornado
- At least 12 people are killed, hundreds are injured, and extensive damage is reported when a large wedge tornado strikes Ezhou and Huanggang, Hubei, China. [src: (Sohu in Chinese)] [src: (The Watchers)]
- Fifteen miners are killed and another is injured when part of a decommissioned gold mine collapses in Wadi Halfa, Northern State, Sudan, after miners entered the closed site. [src: (AFP via Asharq Al-Awsat)]
- At least nine people are killed, including children, and several others are injured in landslides at Rohingya refugee camps in Cox's Bazar District, Bangladesh. [src: (Demócrata)] [src: (TRT World)]
- Five people are killed and one injured after a fire at a residential building in Zhengzhou, Henan, China. [src: (PTI via The Hindu)] [src: (Xinhua)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- The total number of deaths from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceeds 500. [src: (ModernGhana)]
International relations
- Australia–Fiji relations
- Australia and Fiji sign a defence pact, making Fiji one of Australia's treaty-bound allies and committing both countries to consult on security threats and support mutual defence in the Pacific. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Kyrgyzstan–Pakistan relations
- Pakistani president Asif Ali Zardari begins a four-day visit to Kyrgyzstan after an invitation from Kyrgyz president Sadyr Japarov, making it the first official visit by a Pakistani president to the country in 21 years. [src: (Pakistan Observer)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Monaco bombing
- Anastasiia Berezovska, the suspect in a bombing targeting Ukrainian oligarch Vadym Iermolaiev and his family in Monaco on June 29, is found dead near Kyiv, Ukraine, with gunshot wounds to the head. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Pravda)]
- Riots between inmates from rival drug gangs at a prison in Negombo, Sri Lanka, kill 27 people, including four officers, and injure more than 100 others. [src: (AFP via Daily Tribune)]
- Corruption in the Philippines
- Philippine police ⁠separately arrest senator Rodante Marcoleta and three co-accused, including former party-list representative Mike Defensor, after an anti-graft court orders their arrest in relation to a plunder case filed by the Ombudsman. [src: (AP)] [src: (Philippine Daily Inquirer)]
- Crime in Bangladesh
- A crude bomb explodes during a post-march rally in Savar, Dhaka District, Bangladesh, while National Citizen Party convener Nabila Tasnid was giving a speech, injuring three. [src: (The Business Standard)]
- Óbuda scandal
- News outlet Telex.hu publishes the text of arrested Hungarian Socialist Party (MSZP) politician Gergő Czeglédy's 2024 testimony alleging the existence of a large corruption network involving members of the MSZP and Fidesz since 2006. [src: (24.hu )] [src: (HVG )] [src: (Daily News Hungary)]
Politics and elections
- Impact of the 2026 Iran war on Iran
- State funeral of Ali Khamenei
- Former Iranian president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad attends former supreme leader Ali Khamenei's funeral amidst questions surrounding his fate in the aftermath of an Israeli–U.S. airstrike on his home during the early stages of the war. [src: (Iran International)] [src: (The Jerusalem Post)] [src: (RFE/RL)]
- Iranian state television reports that Khamenei's body arrives in Qom, where he studied, ahead of a planned procession. [src: (AFP via Al-Ahram)]
- Second impeachment of Sara Duterte
- The impeachment trial of Philippine vice president Sara Duterte begins in the Senate. [src: (AP)] [src: (BBC News)]
Science and technology
- Samsung Electronics announces that Samsung Messages is being discontinued in the US on July 6 and directs users who have Android 12 or above to switch to Google Messages. [src: (9to5Google)]
Sports
- 2026 FIFA World Cup
- Spain at the FIFA World Cup
- In association football, Spain records its sixth consecutive FIFA World Cup clean sheet in a 1–0 win over Portugal in the round of 16, setting a tournament record, while goalkeeper Unai Simón extends his scoreless streak to 609 minutes. [src: (ANI)]
- 2026 Esports World Cup
- The third edition of the Esports World Cup opens in Paris, France. [src: (TNT Sports)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 7
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Three commercial vessels are reported to be attacked near the Strait of Hormuz, including the Qatari LNG tanker Al Rekayyat, which is owned by Nakilat. [src: (AP)]
- Al Rekayyat is reported to be at a risk of explosion following the attack. The attack marks the first time a vessel from Qatar was attacked since the war started on February 28. [src: (Al-Monitor)]
- The United States revokes the temporary sanctions waiver against Iranian oil issued as part of the Islamabad Memorandum after the attacks on the three vessels. [src: (AFP via CNA)] [src: (Axios)]
- U.S. forces strike Iranian air-defence, coastal surveillance, and missile sites after attacks hit three commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, with explosions heard in Bandar Abbas, Bandar Sirik, and Qeshm Island. Iran accuses the U.S. of violating their memorandum of understanding and warns of retaliation. [src: (AFP via CNA)]
- Gaza war
- Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip
- Israeli airstrikes and gunfire kill at least seven people, including a child, in the Gaza Strip, while Israel says the airstrikes targeted Hamas militants. [src: (Reuters)]
- The Israel Defense Forces and Shin Bet says that they have killed a Hamas Nukhba Force commander and another commander associated with the militant group's intelligence unit. [src: (JNS)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- Human rights groups say that 15 people have been killed in drone strikes in Sudan's North Kordofan state. [src: (AFP via Al-Arabiya)]
- The Sudanese Army says that it has shot down a Chinese-made FH-95 drone in North Kordofan, the third model shot down by the army. [src: (AA)]
- 2026 Damascus bombings
- One person was killed and 36 others are injured in two explosions near Four Seasons Hotel Damascus, Syria, where French president Emmanuel Macron stayed during his state visit to the country. Macron was not at the hotel during the explosions. [src: (AP)]
Disasters and accidents
- K2 Airways Flight 1732
- A K2 Airways Boeing 737-400 cargo aircraft goes missing off the coast of Pakistan with five people on board. [src: (The Independent)]
- Fourteen people are killed and 28 others are injured after a bus collided head-on with a trailer on the Kampala–Gulu Highway, in Northern Uganda. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Two people are killed and 14 others are injured after a bus veered off a road and struck pedestrians in Amadora, Portugal. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Two people are killed and seven others are missing after a massive landslide triggered by heavy rains hit a bridge in Wayanad District, Kerala, India. [src: (Xinhua)]
Health and environment
- Sudanese cholera epidemic
- The Médecins Sans Frontières deploys to the Darfur region amidst ongoing cases of cholera in the Kordofan states of West and North Kordofan. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
International relations
- 2026 Ankara NATO summit
- Greenland crisis
- At the NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey, U.S. president Donald Trump renews his calls for the United States to control Greenland, and says that the U.S. could remove troops from Europe over the dispute. [src: (CNBC)]
- Turkey–United States relations
- Trump says that the U.S. will lift sanctions against Turkey that were imposed in 2020 over its purchase of Russian defense missiles. [src: (Defense News)]
Politics and elections
- Iraq in the 2026 Iran war
- State funeral of Ali Khamenei
- Iraqi state television says that former Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei's remains has arrived in Iraq's Shi'ite holy city of Najaf for viewing following funeral ceremonies in Tehran and Qom, Iran. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2027 French presidential election
- French deputy Marine Le Pen announces her candidacy for president in the next election as the far-right National Rally's nominee. It will be her fourth bid for the presidency. [src: (CNN)]
Sports
- 2026 FIFA World Cup
- Argentina at the FIFA World Cup
- In association football, Argentine forward and captain Lionel Messi becomes the first player to score in nine consecutive World Cup matches (including the previous edition), after scoring in the team's 3–2 victory against Egypt in the round of 16. [src: (ABC News)]
- Switzerland at the FIFA World Cup
- Switzerland advances to the quarterfinals of the FIFA World Cup for the first time since 1954 after beating Colombia in a penalty shootout in the round of 16. [src: (CBS Sports)]
- 2028 Summer Olympics
- Doping in Russia, Russia at the Summer Olympics, International sporting sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
- The International Olympic Committee lifts its ban on Russian athletes, allowing them to take part in the upcoming Summer Olympics in Los Angeles, United States, after previously being banned from competing under its own flag for doping and the 2022 invasion of Ukraine. [src: (The Guardian)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 8
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- U.S. president Donald Trump says that the ceasefire between Iran and the United States is over and that airstrikes will continue. However, he also states that negotiations can continue. Pakistan's foreign ministry reaffirms its call for all sides to honor the recently-signed memorandum of understanding following Trump's declaration. [src: (AFP via The Times of Israel)] [src: (Asharq Al-Awsat)] [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
- The Bahraini military intercepts projectiles from Iran. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
- The Kuwaiti military intercepts two ballistic missiles and 13 drones from Iran. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- International Maritime Organization head Arsenio Dominguez reports that 6,000 seafarers are still stranded in the Strait of Hormuz and calls for a "maximum restraint and de-escalation" amidst renewal of the crisis. [src: (Middle East Eye)] [src: (Oman Observer)]
- Nakilat confirms that the Qatari LNG tanker Al Rekayyat was hit yesterday by projectiles near the Strait of Hormuz. No casualties are reported. Additionally, the tanker is reported to be stranded near the coast of Oman. [src: (Gulf Times)] [src: (Khaleej Times)] [src: (The Peninsula Qatar)]
- July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
- The U.S. military conducts new airstrikes against Iran, with at least 14 people killed in the last two days. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Iranian state media, including the Fars News Agency, releases footage of former supreme leader Ali Khamenei's compound after it was hit in an airstrike by Israel and the U.S. during the first day of the war. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Gaza war
- The Israeli military states that Nukhba commander Mohammed Emad Alrahman Abu Taima of the Al-Qassam Brigades, who is alleged to have taken part in the infiltration of the kibbutz Nirim during the October 7, 2023, attacks by Hamas, has been killed in an airstrike in the southern Gaza Strip. [src: (Cleveland Jewish News)] [src: (Israel National News)]
- Sudanese civil war
- 2026 Blue Nile campaign
- The Sudanese Army says that they have recaptured the Blue Nile town of Kurmuk. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- War crimes during the Sudanese civil war, Darfur genocide
- A probe by the United Nations fact-finding mission of Sudan finds that the Rapid Support Forces have committed mass killings, abductions ‌of women and girls, mass gang rapes, and forced starvation in the North Darfur city of El Fasher. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Human rights groups report that drone strikes in Sudan on civilian vehicles heading to social gatherings have killed 20 people in recent days. [src: (ABC News)] [src: (AP)]
- A drone strike by the Rapid Support Forces kills 10 people traveling to a wedding near Omdurman. [src: (AA)] [src: (MENAFN)]
- 2026 Damascus bombings
- The toll from yesterday's bombings in Damascus, Syria, increases to one person killed and 36 people injured. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Insurgency in Balochistan
- Pakistan's military says that three militant attacks in Balochistan since July 6 have killed 42 army and police personnel, while security forces have killed 54 militants in the incidents. [src: (Reuters)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- Brent Crude and West Texas Intermediate oil prices increase by at least 5% amidst the escalation in the Iran war, rising to US$78.01 and $73.86, respectively. [src: (CNBC)]
- Stocks on the Pakistan Stock Exchange witness a sharp decline following renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, with the KSE-100 Index falling to 4,626 points. [src: (Dunya News)] [src: (Arab News PK)]
Disasters and accidents
- Nine workers are killed and 14 others are rescued after heavy rain causes a garbage heap to collapse onto an administrative building at a waste-to-energy plant near Pune, Maharashtra, India, prompting a temporary suspension of operations. [src: (AFP via Dawn)]
- Seven children and a teacher are killed when heavy rain triggers a landslide during a class at Kutupalong refugee camp in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh. [src: (AFP via The Straits Times)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Two people are killed after an explosion in a fireworks factory in Borgorose, Rieti Province, Italy. [src: (Xinhua)]
Health and environment
- 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
- A cyclosporiasis outbreak, caused by cyclospora cayetanensis, is reported across the United States in 18 states, with Michigan reporting around 992 cases and Ohio reporting 177. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (The Columbus Dispatch)]
International relations
- Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
- Syria–United States relations, US-designated state sponsors of terrorism
- U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio notifies Congress that the U.S. will remove Syria as a "state sponsor of terrorism" after being listed as one since 1979 during the Assad regime. [src: (Al-Monitor)]
- Protests against the 2026 Iran war
- Pakistan–United States relations, 2026 attack on the United States consulate in Karachi, Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war
- The United States announces that it will resume regular consular services at its consulates in Karachi and Lahore after previously suspending operations over security concerns during violent protests in Pakistan, including an attack on the U.S. consulate in Karachi. [src: (Dawn)]
- Greenland crisis
- The prime ministers of Greenland and Denmark, Jens-Frederik Nielsen and Mette Frederiksen, respectively, reaffirm that Greenland is not for sale amidst a renewed push by Trump at the NATO summit to control the territory. [src: (RFI)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Ukraine–European Union relations, Polish Order of the White Eagle controversy
- The European Parliament passes a resolution expressing regret over the decision of Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy to name a military unit after the Ukrainian Insurgent Army, citing their responsibility for the massacres of Poles in Volhynia and Eastern Galicia. [src: (TVP World)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Sumatra blackout, Corruption in Indonesia
- Indonesia police perform raids on 12 places linked to three different cases. They found 74 kg of golds, and cash in form of Indonesian rupiah, Singapore dollar, and United States dollar totaling over US$3.7 million. [src: (Bloomberg)] [src: (Jakarta Globe)] [src: (Tempo)]
- Disappearance of ARA San Juan
- A court in Río Gallegos, Santa Cruz, Argentina, convicts former Argentine Navy commander Claudio Villamide for his role in the 2017 implosion of the submarine ARA San Juan, which killed all 44 people on board. [src: (Buenos Aires Times)]
- Norwegian police and international partners announce the arrest of 28 men across seven countries in an operation targeting suspected dark-web buyers of child sexual abuse material who allegedly used the cryptocurrency Monero, while Europol says three children are safeguarded. [src: (AFP via South China Morning Post)]
- 7 people are killed and 5 others are injured in two separate shootings in Mitchells Plain and Philippi, both located on the Cape Flats in Cape Town. [src: (SABC News)][src: (Xinhua)]
Politics and elections
- Iraq in the 2026 Iran war
- State funeral of Ali Khamenei
- State funerals for former Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei are held in Iraq's Shi'ite holy cities of Karbala and Najaf. [src: (AP)] [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- 2026 United States elections
- 2026 United States Senate elections
- U.S. Senate Democratic nominee Graham Platner suspends his campaign in the upcoming U.S. Senate election in Maine, leaving the Maine Democratic Party to seek a replacement challenger to incumbent Republican Susan Collins. [src: (Reuters)]
- Human rights in Thailand
- Thailand's parliament passes an amnesty bill covering political activists convicted since 2005 while excluding corruption and royal insult offences. The measure awaits royal approval. [src: (AFP via The Star)]
Sports
- 2026 FIFA World Cup controversies
- 2026 Trump–FIFA red card controversy
- Seventy-two lawmakers from the European Parliament call for an investigation into FIFA president Gianni Infantino after FIFA lifted the red-card suspension on American striker Folarin Balogun. [src: (Politico Europe)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 9
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
- The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Aerospace Force fires 10 ballistic missiles at the Al-Azraq air base in Jordan. [src: (AA)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
- The Kuwaiti General Staff of the Army reports that Kuwait air defenses has intercepted "hostile missile and drone attacks" on the country. [src: (AFP via The Times of Israel)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar
- Qatar is attacked by projectiles from Iran. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- A U.S. official says that technical talks will continue after two days of recent clashes between the two countries. [src: (Bloomberg)] [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- Israeli defence minister Israel Katz says that Israel is ready to launch further strikes against Iran if necessary. [src: (Armen Press)]
- Gaza war
- The Israel military says that Islamic Jihad commander 'Rashid al-Qadhi', who was allegedly in charge of the organization's weapon production division, was killed in a airstrike in the southern Gaza Strip. Additionally, Hamas sniper Abdullah Baha al-Din Razak al-Souti is said to have been killed in a separate strike in the northern part of Gaza, both despite the ongoing ceasefire. [src: (The Times of Israel)] [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- Mali War
- 2026 Mali offensives
- Battle of Anéfis
- The Azawad Liberation Front attacks a convoy carrying Malian soldiers and Russian Africa Corps fighters near Anéfis, Kidal Region. Security sources say Niger provided air support for Mali during the attack. [src: (Reuters)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- Siege of El Obeid, Sudan–European Union relations
- The European Parliament votes 476–28 with 96 abstentions to adopt a resolution calling on the European Union to designate the Rapid Support Forces as a terrorist organization and impose sanctions on individuals responsible for attacks on civilians in El-Obeid, North Kordofan. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Sudanese prime minister Kamil Idris and African Union envoy to Sudan Mohamed Belaiche hold talks in Khartoum to discuss efforts to achieve peace and stability in the country and coordinate initiatives for a ceasefire to end the civil war. [src: (AA)]
- 2026 Damascus bombings
- Syrian interior minister Anas Khattab and Rif Dimashq internal security commander Ahmed al-Dalati say security forces have captured an Islamic State-linked cell responsible for the two bombings in Damascus that killed one person and injured 36 others last Tuesday. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Colombian conflict
- Colombia's military says a drone attack on Tibú Airport in the Norte de Santander Department near the Venezuelan border injures three workers and damages the facility, blaming the attack on the National Liberation Army. [src: (The Defense Post)]
- Nigerian bandit conflict
- Nigerian troops kill more than 300 suspected kidnapping and cattle-rustling gang members during an operation that began yesterday in Gummi, Zamfara State. [src: (AFP via New Straits Times)]
Business and economy
- Aftermath of the September 11 attacks, Economy of New York City
- The proposed 2 World Trade Center breaks ground in Lower Manhattan in New York City, New York, U.S., 25 years after the original building was destroyed during the September 11 attacks. [src: (ABC News)] [src: (KTLO)]
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- QatarEnergy pauses efforts to restore liquefied natural gas (LNG) production at the Ras Laffan gas facility after an attack on an LNG carrier in the Strait of Hormuz, choosing to keep its operations at a minimum. [src: (AA)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Los Gallardos wildfire
- Twelve people are killed, eight others injured and 23 reported missing in a wildfire in Los Gallardos, Andalusia, Spain. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Huiteng Shoes factory fire
- Twenty-eight people are killed after a fire at a shoe factory in Jinjiang, Fujian, China. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Xinhua)]
- Five members of a family are killed in an apartment fire caused by a gas leak in Giza, Egypt. [src: (Xinhua)]
- At least four people are killed in a building collapse in New Delhi, India, due to rains related to the monsoon season. [src: (Reuters)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- The death toll from Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo reaches 600. [src: (NPR)]
Law and crime
- 2025 Tanzanian election protests
- Tanzanian police arrest 130 people for allegedly encouraging criminal activity after home affairs minister Hamad Masauni banned political rallies and deployed security forces to prevent planned protests seeking democratic reforms and accountability for election-related deaths. [src: (Reuters)]
- Terrorism in the United States
- The U.S. justice department announces that a federal grand jury has indicted eight men over an alleged plot to attack the UFC Freedom 250 event at the White House in Washington, D.C., last month. [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- Impact of the 2026 Iran war on Iran
- State funeral of Ali Khamenei
- The final stage of former Iranian supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's state funeral begins in his hometown of Mashhad after previously being delayed by an hour in which Iran said U.S. forces struck a railway bridge northeast in the country en-route to the funeral. [src: (The New York Times)]
- Khamenei's body arrives in the Imam Reza shrine for his burial. [src: (Al-Monitor)]
- 2026 New Caledonian legislative election
- Virginie Ruffenach, of the pro-France coalition, is elected president of the Congress of New Caledonia following elections. Ruffenach defeats of the pro-independence bloc with a 28 to 25 vote. [src: (Radio New Zealand)]
- Thousands of people protest in Budapest, Hungary, against the attempt by prime minister Péter Magyar to oust president Tamás Sulyok, whom Magyar accuses of failing to "live up" to his role by not opposing what he calls antidemocratic measures by former prime minister Viktor Orbán. [src: (AP)]
- Senegal's Constitutional Council strikes down a parliamentary bill that would expand the powers of the National Assembly and prime minister while limiting presidential authority, after president Bassirou Diomaye Faye challenges the measure. [src: (AFP via Indo Premier)]
Science and technology
- AI boom
- OpenAI releases the large language model tool GPT-5.6, with significant advancements in cybersecurity. [src: (Axios)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 June 1
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
- Red Sea crisis, 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Iran announces a pause on peace talks with the United States, and, alongside the Axis of Resistance, announces plans to "completely block" the Strait of Hormuz and threatens to close the Strait of Mandeb, ruling out any further talks until Israel ends its military operations in Lebanon and Gaza. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (CNBC)]
- Iranian parliamentary speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says that the U.S. naval blockade of Iran and the Israeli attacks on Lebanon are violations of the Iran–U.S. ceasefire agreement. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war, Iran–Pakistan relations
- Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi asks Pakistani foreign minister and deputy prime minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar to help facilitate de-escalation and express concern about Israel's violations of the ceasefire in Lebanon. [src: (AA)] [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Radio Pakistan)]
- U.S. president Donald Trump says that ceasefire negotiations are still ongoing, contradicting reports of Iran backing out of talks. [src: (The Hill)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign
- United States president Donald Trump says that Iran's pause on peace talks does not mean the U.S. will resume airstrikes, but the naval blockade will continue. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Iran–Japan relations
- Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian says that Iran will allow ships from Japan to pass the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (Dawn)] [src: (AFP via The Times of Israel)]
- Iran–Oman relations
- Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi says that Iran and Oman are the only two countries with the right to "exercise sovereignty" over the Strait of Hormuz, and that Iran implemented a new process for controlling maritime traffic in coordination with Oman. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war
- The U.S. Central Command intercepts two Iranian ballistic missiles targeting the U.S. military base in Kuwait that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says was used for on attack on Bandar Sirik, Iran. [src: (CNBC)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says that their naval forces have attacked the Panama-flagged "US-owned" container ship MSC Sariska in response to an alleged US attack on an Iranian ship in the Sea of Oman. [src: (AA)] [src: (AFP via Gulf News)] [src: (ANI News)]
- Hezbollah–Israel conflict
- 2026 Lebanon war
- 2026 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire
- U.S. president Donald Trump says that Israel and Hezbollah have agreed to dial back on fighting after holding a call with Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Hezbollah. [src: (PBS)]
- The U.S. embassy in Beirut confirms that Hezbollah has accepted a proposal by the United States for a “mutual cessation of attacks" after Israel threatened Beirut with strikes on the eve of a fourth round of peace talks. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- The Lebanese government receives confirmation about Hezbollah’s agreement to a new ceasefire with Israel. [src: (Times of Israel)]
- The Iranian military command warns residents of northern Israel to evacuate if the Israeli military strikes the Dahieh suburb of Beirut, Lebanon, in response to an Israeli evacuation order. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Staff Sergeant Adam Tzarfati of Maglan, a sayeret of the IDF's Commando Brigade, is confirmed to be killed in a Hezbollah drone attack in southern Lebanon. Three other soldiers are injured in the attack. [src: (Times of Israel)]
- Herder–farmer conflicts in Nigeria
- Nigerian bandit conflict
- An early-morning bandit attack in Kabba/Bunu, Kogi State, Nigeria, leaves two people dead and five injured, with 30 civilians kidnapped. Twenty-three civilians are later rescued by the Nigerian Army. [src: (Daily Post Nigeria)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- Fifty-eight people are killed in multiple Rapid Support Forces attacks over the past four days in various villages near Bara, North Kordofan, Sudan. [src: (Dabanga Sudan)]
- Mali War
- Eight people are killed and 42 others are injured after a bus struck a land mine on a road between Bamako and Kayes, Mali. [src: (Reuters)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
