- Herder–farmer conflicts in Nigeria
- Nigerian bandit conflict
- At least eight villagers are killed and 15 others were injured after more than a hundred Fulani bandits carried out a shooting in Plateau State. [src: (Daily Post)]
- Two policemen are killed after unidentified gunmen attacked them on a road in Anambra State. [src: (Daily Post)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- The National Umma Party says that ten people, including eight children, have been killed in a drone strike on two civilian vehicles driving on the Abu Zabad–Al-Fula road in West Kordofan state, Sudan. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Tribal clashes erupt in South Darfur between the Beni Halba and Salamat tribes, killing 50 people. [src: (Darfur24)] [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Allied Democratic Forces insurgency
- An Allied Democratic Forces attack kills at least 19 civilians in the Ruwenzori commune, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). [src: (Radio Okapi in French)] [src: (Radio Okapi in French)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iran war fuel crisis, Sri Lanka and the International Monetary Fund
- Sri Lanka increases fuel prices by up to six percent as part of economic reforms linked to its International Monetary Fund assistance program, which includes plans to phase out fuel subsidies and achieve cost recovery in the energy sector. [src: (AFP via The Hindu)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Angeles City building collapse
- The death toll from the collapse of an under construction nine-story building in Angeles, Pampanga, Philippines, on May 24, rises to twelve. [src: (The Philippine Star)]
- 2026 Namhkam Township explosion
- More than 55 people are killed, including six children, and 74 others are injured in an explosion at a building storing explosives for mining in Namhkam Township, Shan State, Myanmar. [src: (AP)] [src: (BBC News)] 
- Five people are killed, at least 19 others are injured and three are reported missing after a suspected shell from World War II explodes under a stilt house in Papua, Western New Guinea, Indonesia. [src: (CBS News)]
- Five people are killed and another is injured when an illegal mine collapses in Huize County, Yunnan, China. [src: (AP)] [src: (Reuters)] 
Health and environment
- Sudanese cholera epidemic
- Sudan holds an emergency meeting led by Health Minister Haitham Mohamed Ibrahim after the Federal Ministry of Health reports 308 cases and 77 deaths in West Kordofan from cholera since the outbreak in Sudan. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- A study published by The New England Journal of Medicine reports that the daraxonrasib, a RAS inhibitor drug that targets KRAS-mutated cancers, has doubled median overall survival in patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer as compared to chemotherapy. [src: (NPR)] [src: (Reuters)] [src: (NEJM)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Colombian presidential election
- The National Salvation Movement's candidate Abelardo de la Espriella wins the election and will face Iván Cepeda from Historic Pact in the runoff on 21 June. [src: (AP)] 
- President Gustavo Petro announces that it does not recognize the results due to doubts about the computerised vote-counting system. [src: (NBC News)]
- 2026 Guinean parliamentary election
- Guineans vote to elect 147 members of the National Assembly. [src: (AFP via Free Malaysia Today)]
- 2026 Maltese general election
- Preliminary results from yesterday's election revealed that the Labour Party, currently led by incumbent prime minister Robert Abela, won a record fourth consecutive term in government. [src: (Reuters)]
- Hungarian president Tamás Sulyok announces that he will not resign despite the prime minister Peter Magyar's ultimatum after accusing him of being an "Orbán puppet". [src: (Euronews)]
Sports
- 2026 Indian Premier League
- In Twenty20 cricket, the Indian Premier League concludes with Royal Challengers Bengaluru defeating the Gujarat Titans in the final at Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India. [src: (India Today)] [src: (Telegraph India)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 May 4
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign
- Operation Project Freedom
- The U.S. Central Command says that two US-flagged merchant vessels have passed through the Strait of Hormuz, the first vessels to cross the waterway since the start of Project Freedom. Additionally, CENTCOM also says that U.S. Navy guided-missile destroyers transited through the waterway. [src: (The Hill)] [src: (Axios)]
- Iranian media report that the Iranian navy struck a U.S. Navy warship with two missiles, after it ignored warnings off the coast of Jask. United States Central Command denies the claim that a ship was hit. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (CNBC)]
- A fire and explosion is reported on an anchored HMM vessel in the Strait of Hormuz near the United Arab Emirates. No casualties were reported. [src: (Yonhap)]
- A vessel belonging to Abu Dhabi National Oil Company is attacked by two drones in the Strait of Hormuz. No injuries were reported. [src: (Gulf News)]
- 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran
- The Pakistani foreign ministry says that the U.S. has evacuated 22 crew members on the Touska and will hand them to Iranian authorities. [src: (Reuters)]
- The IRNA confirms that the 22 sailors returned home to Iran at a border terminal in Sistan-Baluchistan. [src: (Pakistan Today)]
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations, Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi and Pakistani foreign minister Ishaq Dar hold a phone call to discuss Pakistan's efforts to revive ceasefire talks between Iran and the United States aimed at ending the war. [src: (AA)] [src: (Al Arabiya)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
- 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
- The United Arab Emirates reports that it has intercepted three missiles from Iran, with the 4th one falling into the sea. This is the first report of missile interceptions since the ceasefire began on April 7. [src: (Khaleej Times)]
- A strike on an energy facility in the Fujairah emirate injures three Indian nationals. [src: (AFP via LBCI)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Rapid Support Forces launch drone attacks at several targets in Khartoum, Sudan, including the Khartoum International Airport in Khartoum, Sudan. Drone strikes are also reported at the Signal Corps in Khartoum Bahri and Al-Markhiyat camp in northern Omdurman. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- The Sudan Army's air defenses intercept drone strikes at the airport. [src: (Yaffaps)]
Arts and culture
- 2026 Pulitzer Prize
- The Pulitzer Prize winners for 2026 are announced, recognizing excellence in journalism, books, drama, and music. [src: (NPR)] [src: (The New York Times)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- The Dubai International Airport in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, reports a 66% drop in passenger traffic in March 2026 amidst a disruption of air traffic in the Middle East due to the Iran war. [src: (Bloomberg)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Liuyang fireworks factory explosion
- At least 26 people are killed in an explosion at a fireworks factory in Liuyang, Hunan, China. [src: (Reuters)]
- Eight people are killed in a road accident in Dandong, Liaoning, China. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Seven people are killed and 13 others critically injured after a bus collided head-on with a trailer in Northern Uganda. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Three people are killed and 14 others are injured in a fire at a six-story apartment building in Manhattan, New York, United States. [src: (The New York Times)]
- At least two people are killed and three others are injured when an Embraer EMB-721 crashes into a residential building in Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais, Brazil. [src: (G1 in Portuguese)]
- Two people are killed after a fire swept through a residential area in San Mateo, Rizal, Philippines. [src: (Xinhua)]
International relations
- Austria–Russia relations
- Austria and Russian intelligence
- Austria expels three Russian diplomats over suspected espionage activities involving data interception from the Russian embassy and a diplomatic mission in Vienna. [src: (AP)]
- Australia–Japan relations
- Australia and Japan sign agreements on energy and critical minerals. [src: (Reuters)]
- European integration
- The 8th European Political Community Summit is held in Yerevan, Armenia, with leaders from nearly 50 countries participating. [src: (Euronews)] 
- Indonesia–Japan relations
- Indonesia and Japan signs a defense agreement including cooperation in defense industry and personnel training amid the lifting of Japan's arms export ban. [src: (JakartaGlobe)]
- Nigeria–South Africa relations, Xenophobia in South Africa
- Nigeria announces plans for the voluntary repatriation of its citizens from South Africa following reported attacks and safety concerns affecting foreign nationals. [src: (AFP via The Manila Times)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Leipzig car incident
- Two people are killed and 22 others are injured, including two seriously, after a car was driven into a crowd of people in Leipzig, Saxony, Germany. The perpetrator is arrested and the incident is being investigated. [src: (Reuters)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 May 5
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- U.S. secretary of state Marco Rubio and U.S. military leaders, including U.S. defense secretary Pete Hegseth, say that the ceasefire is holding despite recent attacks on the United Arab Emirates and Strait of Hormuz. [src: (Times of Israel)] [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign
- U.S. president Donald Trump announces a pause in Operation Project Freedom aimed at helping ships transit the Strait of Hormuz, citing Pakistan's request to do so and progress in negotiations. [src: (CNBC)] [src: (Arab News PK)]
- Rubio announces that Operation Epic Fury, the codename for the initial phase of U.S. military operations in the war with Iran, has concluded. [src: (The Hill)] [src: (Time)]
- Israeli–Palestinian conflict
- Gaza war
- The Israel Defense Forces confirms that Hamas Nukhba commander Anas Muhammad Ibrahim Hamed, who took part in the October 7, 2023 attacks including the Nova music festival massacre, was eliminated in a airstrike yesterday in the central Gaza Strip. [src: (Israel National News)] [src: (Times of Israel)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Ethiopia–Sudan relations
- The Sudan News Agency reports that Sudan has recalled its ambassador to Ethiopia, accusing them of involvement in recent drone strikes targeting the airport in Khartoum. [src: (EWN)]
- Five people are killed and nine others are injured following a drone strike launched by the Rapid Support Forces on two fuel stations in Kosti, White Nile. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Boko Haram insurgency
- Boko Haram militants attack a Chadian military base on the shores of Lake Chad, killing 23 security personnel and injuring dozens of others. [src: (DW)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- At least 27 people are killed and more than 80 injured in Russian drone and missile attacks on Ukraine. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Arts and culture
- Great Israeli Real Estate Event
- Anti-Israeli protests are held outside the Park East Synagogue in New York City, U.S., after the synagogue hosted the Great Israeli Real Estate Event, an expo for land sales in both Israel and the occupied West Bank. [src: (Jewish Insider)] [src: (The New York Times)] [src: (Times of Israel)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
- Kentucky governor Andy Beshear announces emergency regulations in effort to combat the high gas prices in Kentucky as a result of the war. [src: (Kentucky Today)] [src: (Reuters)]
- As a result of the motion of no confidence against Romanian prime minister Ilie Bolojan, exchange rates between the Romanian leu and the euro rise to their highest level in history as the leu's value plummets. [src: (Economica.net )] [src: (Digi FM )]
Disasters and accidents
- More than twenty people are killed over the past 24 hours in storms, heavy rainfall, and lightning strikes across Bihar, India. [src: (The Hans India)]
- Fourteen people are killed in a road accident involving a bus in Mutoko District, Zimbabwe. [src: (The Star)]
- Eight people are killed and 41 others are injured in a fire at a commercial complex in Andisheh, Tehran province, Iran. [src: (AA)]
Health and environment
- COVID-19 drug development
- German biotechnology company BioNTech announces it will halt production of its COVID-19 vaccine due to drastic restructuring plans, leaving sole production of the vaccine to its partner Pfizer. [src: (DW)] [src: (Wall Street Journal)]
Law and crime
- Mass shootings in the United States
- Two people are killed and three others injured in a mass shooting at a Korean supermarket in Carrollton, Texas, U.S., after a 69-year-old man opened fire on his coworkers at a business meeting. The suspect is taken into custody. [src: (NBC News)]
- 2026 Rio Branco school shooting
- Two people are killed and seven others are injured in a school shooting in Rio Branco, Acre, Brazil. A 13-year-old suspect is taken into custody. [src: (Xinhua)] [src: (Central Brasileira de Notícias in Portuguese)]
- In Pasig, Philippines, the National Bureau of Investigation arrests the founder of an online news site, Peanut Gallery Media Network, and four other people, in an entrapment operation for an alleged extortion attempt on former House speaker Martin Romualdez. [src: (Gulf News)] [src: (PNA)]
Politics and elections
- Politics of Romania
- The Parliament of Romania votes 281–4 to pass a motion of no confidence, called by the Social Democratic Party and Alliance for the Union of Romanians, against prime minister Ilie Bolojan. [src: (AP)] [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- President Nicușor Dan refuses the possibility of holding snap elections, saying that a new government will be formed comprising a coalition of pro-Western parties. [src: (Radio Romania )]
- Louise Arbour is announced by prime minister Mark Carney as the next governor general of Canada. [src: (The Guardian)]
- The Ugandan parliament passes the Protection of Sovereignty Bill, which restricts foreign involvement in policymaking without government approval and imposes penalties of up to 10 years' imprisonment for violations. [src: (Reuters)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 May 6
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war
- Pakistani deputy prime minister and foreign minister Ishaq Dar says that Pakistan is focusing on making the current ceasefire between Iran and the United States permanent. [src: (Pakistan Today)]
- Axios reports that Iran and the U.S. are closing in on a one-page memorandum to end the war and set a framework for negotiations regarding Iran's nuclear program. [src: (Axios)] [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- 2026 Iran war regional mobilizations
- France deploys the aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle and its strike group to the Red Sea ahead of a proposed British–French mission aimed at securing maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (AP)]
- Ships attacked during the 2026 Iran war
- French shipping company CMA CGM says that one of its container ships, San Antonio, was attacked yesterday while transiting through the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (AFP via Arab News)] [src: (Times of Israel)]
- The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy says that safe passage on the Strait of Hormuz will be assured with new procedures and guidelines following the U.S. pause in Operation Project Freedom. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 United States military buildup in the Middle East
- USS Gerald R. Ford officially exits the Mediterranean Sea and enters the Atlantic Ocean after its longest deployment since the Cold War during which it participated in both the Iran war and the Maduro raid. [src: (USNI)] [src: (Stars and Stripes)]
- 2026 Lebanon war
- Israeli attacks on the Lebanese health sector during the Israel-Hezbollah conflict
- 16 people are killed and 21 are injured including three paramedics by Israeli drone strikes and airstrikes across southern Lebanon despite the ceasefire. [src: (AA)]
- Israel carries out an airstrike against a building in Beirut, allegedly killing a top commander of Hezbollah's Radwan Force. It is the first strike in the capital since the ceasefire started on April 16. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Mali offensives
- At least 35 people are killed in coordinated attacks in central Mali that are claimed by Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin. [src: (AFP via LBCI)]
- Sudanese civil war
- The Sudan Doctors Network says that the death toll from drone strikes launched yesterday by the Rapid Support Forces in Kosti, White Nile has risen to 235 after laboratory doctor Adel Musa al-Tijani was killed in the drone strike. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Ethiopia and the United Arab Emirates deny Sudan's accusations that they were responsible for the May 4 drone attack on Khartoum International Airport. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Medafrica Times)] [src: (Khaleej Times)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- Gold prices rise to more than a one-week high following reports that Iran and the U.S. may be nearing a peace deal to end the war. [src: (CNBC)]
- Hungary–Ukraine relations
- Ukrainian president announces that Hungary has returned cash and gold seized from Ukraine's Oschadbank after outgoing Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orbán ordered the government to keep the cash and gold for 60 days. [src: (Euronews)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 North Musi Rawas collision
- At least 16 people are killed and four others are injured when a passenger bus crashes into a tanker truck in Sumatra, Indonesia. [src: (AFP via Al Arabiya)]
- At least 12 people are killed and 21 others are injured in two separate road accidents in Eastern Cape, South Africa. [src: (Xinhua)]
Health and environment
- MV Hondius hantavirus outbreak
- Three passengers infected with hantavirus pulmonary syndrome from the Andes virus are evacuated off the cruise ship while it is stationed off the coast of Cape Verde to receive treatment in the Netherlands. At least 145 people remain on board, including two suspected asymptomatic cases. [src: (ABC News)] [src: (NBC News)] [src: (Fox News)]
- Spanish authorities allow the ship to dock at the Canary Islands as several passengers are Spanish citizens. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Reuters)]
International relations
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis, China in the 2026 Iran war, China–Iran relations
- Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi and Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi meet in Beijing, China, to discuss reopening the Strait of Hormuz, among other related topics, ahead of potential Iran–U.S. talks. [src: (Al-Monitor)] [src: (Times of Israel)]
Politics and elections
- Ivory Coast dissolves its election commission following criticism over its management and independence, with authorities planning to establish a new electoral administration system. [src: (Reuters)]
- North Korea drops mention of unification with South Korea from its constitution. [src: (Euronews)]
Business and Economy
- AirAsia purchases 150 Airbus A220 aircraft from Airbus, the largest single aircraft order in Canadian history, with options for 150 more if Airbus develops a stretched version.

title: Portal:Current events/2026 May 7
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- Pakistan foreign office spokesperson Tahir Andrabi says that a ceasefire agreement between Iran and the United States to end the war is expected "sooner rather than later". [src: (Arab News PK)]
- U.S. president Donald Trump says that the ceasefire is still in effect despite the recent strikes on the U.S. destroyers. [src: (ABC News)] [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- A U.S. official tells Axios that Iran and the U.S. have reportedly exchanged fire at the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran claiming to strike three U.S. Navy ships and the U.S. claiming to strike targets on the waterway. [src: (Axios)] [src: (AP)] [src: (Reuters)]
- The Iranian Ports and Maritime Organization says that ports in Iran are prepared to provide maritime services, technical support, supplies, and medical assistance to ships operating in the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (AA)] [src: (The Economic Times)]
- 7 May 2026 United States strikes on Iran
- The U.S. Central Command confirms that the military carried out "self-defense" strikes against military facilities in response to Iran's attacks on the Arleigh Burke-class destroyers USS Truxtun, USS Rafael Peralta, and USS Mason as the three ships were transiting the Hormuz into the Gulf of Oman. [src: (The Asia Business Daily)] [src: (CNN)] [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- Several explosions are heard at a port in Qeshm and Bandar Abbas in Iran's Hormozgan province. Israel denies any involvement in the explosion, while Fox News reporter Jennifer Griffin says that the U.S. military was behind the explosions. Officials say that the explosions does not mean the restart of the war or the end of the ceasefire. [src: (AA)] [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Israeli–Palestinian conflict
- Gaza war
- Azzam Al-Hayya, the son of Hamas Political Bureau chairman Khalil al-Hayya, is confirmed by a Hamas official to have been killed during a Israel airstrike last night. [src: (Reuters)]
- Allied Democratic Forces insurgency, Kivu conflict, Ituri conflict
- Forty people are killed and homes are burned by Allied Democratic Forces militants during attacks in North Kivu and Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo. [src: (AP)]
Business and economy
- 2026 Cuban crisis
- Sherritt International suspends its mining operations in Cuba and withdraws expatriate staff, citing the risk of expanded United States sanctions affecting its operations. [src: (AFP via News Abhiyan)]
- Tariffs in the second Trump administration
- The U.S. Court of International Trade rules that the 10% global tariffs imposed by president Donald Trump are illegal. [src: (The New York Times)] 
- Mastercard says that they are planning to resume services in Syria for the first time in 15 years. [src: (SANA)] [src: (AA)]
Disasters and accidents
- At least 15 people are killed and dozens of others are trapped when a gold mine collapses in West Pokot County, Kenya. [src: (AA)]
- Ten people are killed in a road accident involving a truck carrying a 40-foot container near Freetown, Sierra Leone. [src: (Xinhua)]
- At least five people are killed and more than 12 others are injured in a large fire at a shopping mall in Los Mochis, Sinaloa, Mexico. [src: (BNO News)]
- At least five people are killed in a fire at a fair in Villahermosa, Tabasco, Mexico. [src: (Reuters)]
Health and environment
- Two children are reported to have died from tuberculosis at displacement camps in Tawila, North Darfur, Sudan. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
International relations
- Cambodia–Thailand relations
- 2025 Cambodian–Thai border crisis
- Cambodia and Thailand agree to restore relations following talks mediated by the Philippines on the sidelines of the 48th ASEAN Summit in Cebu. [src: (Bangkok Post)] [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- 2024 South Korean martial law crisis
- The Seoul High Court reduces former South Korean prime minister Han Duck-soo's prison sentence from 23 years to 15 years for crimes related to former president Yoon Suk Yeol's 2024 martial law declaration, citing a lack of evidence that Han played a leading or premeditated role in the declaration. [src: (AFP via CNA)]
- Anti-corruption campaign under Xi Jinping
- Former Chinese defense ministers Li Shangfu and Wei Fenghe are both sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve following their convictions on graft charges. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Politico)]
- 2026 Canvas security incident
- The ShinyHunters cybercrime group claims responsibility for breaching Instructure Canvas, a web-based learning management system, a second time, affecting at least 275 million teachers and students worldwide. [src: (TRT World)]
- Trafficking of Chinese nationals to scam centers abroad
- Sri Lankan authorities arrest 30 Chinese and Vietnamese nationals in Colombo in a crackdown on cyberscams in the country, raising the total number of those detained to 261. [src: (AFP via The Straits Times)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 United Kingdom local elections
- 2026 Scottish Parliament election, 2026 Senedd election
- Voters in England elect six mayors and 5,066 council seats across 136 councils. In Scotland, voters elect 129 seats to the Scottish Parliament. In Wales, voters elect 96 seats to the Senedd. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- Politics of Solomon Islands
- The parliament of the Solomon Islands debates a no-confidence motion against prime minister Jeremiah Manele. The debate is a culmination of a political crisis that started with mass resignations of the cabinet on 16 March, recently escalated by a ruling on 1 May by the Court of Appeal ordering the reconvening of Parliament. [src: (RNZ)]
- Manele is ousted from the premiership following a successful no-confidence motion of 26–22, with two MPs absent. Manele remains as caretaker prime minister until governor-general David Tiva Kapu declares a new prime minister. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2027 Salvadoran legislative election, Right of Salvadoran expatriates to vote
- The Legislative Assembly of El Salvador approves a constitutional reform that establishes an overseas constituency for Salvadoran expatriates. The constituency is allocated 6 seats in the 60-seat legislature. [src: (La Prensa Gráfica in Spanish)]
Sports
- International sporting sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
- Belarus at the Olympics
- The International Olympic Committee lifts restrictions on Belarusian athletes participating in the Olympic Games from 2028, while Russian athletes remain limited to individual neutral participation because of the Russian Olympic Committee's suspension. [src: (AFP via RFI)] [src: (BBC News)]
- 2027 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament, 2027 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament
- In basketball, the NCAA Division I men's and women's tournaments will expand to 76 teams beginning next year. [src: (AP)] [src: (The Athletic via The New York Times)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 May 8
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- 2026 Iran war
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war, Islamabad Talks
- The Wall Street Journal reports that Iran and the United States may resume talks next week in Islamabad, Pakistan. [src: (AA)] [src: (The Wall Street Journal)]
- Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi and Turkish foreign minister Hakan Fidan hold a phone call to review the status of talks between Iran and the United States. [src: (AA)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on the United Arab Emirates
- Three people are injured after the United Arab Emirates defence ministry says that they have intercepted two ballistic missiles and three drones from Iran, increasing the total number of injuries in the country since the war began to 230. [src: (Khaleej Times)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Japanese shipping company Mitsui O.S.K. Lines says that three of their vessels that crossed the Strait of Hormuz last month did not pay transit fees. [src: (Reuters)]
- A Malta-flagged tanker carrying 1 million barrels of crude oil arrived off South Korea’s west coast Friday after passing through the Strait of Hormuz in mid-April. [src: (AP)]
- 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran
- The U.S. Central Command says that a U.S. Navy F/A-18 Super Hornet from USS George H. W. Bush has attacked two Iranian tankers, the M/T Sea Star III and M/T Sevda, as both ships were transiting the Gulf of Oman. [src: (Stars and Stripes)] [src: (Businessinsider)]
- Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters spokesperson Ebrahim Zolfaghari accuses the U.S. of violating the ceasefire after it targeted two ships at the Strait of Hormuz and strikes in the Hormozgan province, including Bandar Khamir, Sirik, and Qeshm Island yesterday. He also confirmed that Iran responded by attacking U.S. military vessels east of the waterway and south of Chabahar port. [src: (AA)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Sudanese civil war
- The Sudan Civil Aviation Authority issues a NOTAM that Khartoum International Airport has reopened to international traffic after previously being suspended due to the May 4 drone attack. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
Arts and culture
- 61st Venice Biennale
- Gaza war protests
- Pavilions at the 61st Venice Biennale close after artists go on a strike in protest of Israel's entry into the event organized by the Art Not Genocide Alliance over Israel's role in the Gaza war. [src: (Times of Israel)]
- Mass media in Niger
- Niger's junta suspends at least 10 French media organizations, including Agence France-Presse and France 24, citing concerns over public order. [src: (AFP via The Punch)] [src: (Xinhua)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Liuyang fireworks factory explosion
- The death toll from an explosion at a fireworks factory three days ago in Liuyang, Hunan, China, rises to 37, with 51 injured and one remaining missing. [src: (Reuters)]
- May 2026 eruption of Dukono
- Three hikers are killed, two are missing and 15 more rescued after the eruption of Mount Dukono on Halmahera, Indonesia. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Frontier Airlines Flight 4345
- An Airbus A321neo operated by Frontier Airlines strikes and kills a person while taking off from Denver International Airport in Colorado, U.S., leading to an engine fire and aborted takeoff that injures 12 passengers. [src: (ABC7)] [src: (BBC News)]
Health and environment
- MV Hondius hantavirus outbreak
- The World Health Organization reports six cases of the Andes strain of hantavirus in connection with MV Hondius. [src: (AFP and Reuters via The Straits Times)]
- The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reports that 115 people on the cruise ship Caribbean Princess have been infected by a norovirus outbreak. [src: (ABC News)]
International relations
- Poland and the European Union, European Defence Union
- Poland becomes the first country to sign a loan agreement under the European Commission's Security Action for Europe defence financing programme, securing nearly €44 billion (US$52 billion) to support military modernization and the domestic arms industry. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Hungary–Russia relations
- Hungary expels a Russian diplomat at the Russian embassy in Budapest identified as a SVR officer who allegedly spent years cultivating contacts in think tanks tied to the government of prime minister Viktor Orbán. [src: (VSquare)] [src: (The New Voice of Ukraine)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 United Kingdom local elections
- 2026 Scottish Parliament election, 2026 Senedd election
- The Labour Party concedes defeat in Wales with Plaid Cymru and Reform UK making significant gains, while the nationalist Scottish National Party claims victory in Scotland. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Welsh Labour leader and First Minister of Wales Eluned Morgan resigns after losing her seat in the Senedd as Plaid Cymru claims victory in Wales. [src: (The National)]
- Reform UK take full control of Havering London Borough Council, making it the first Reform-run council in Greater London. [src: (The Independent)]
- 2026 Bulgarian parliamentary election
- Rumen Radev is sworn in as prime minister of Bulgaria after being elected in a vote of 124–70, with 36 abstentions at the National Assembly. [src: (AP)]
- 2026 Costa Rican general election
- Laura Fernández Delgado is sworn in as president of Costa Rica, succeeding Rodrigo Chaves Robles. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (AP)]
- 2026 Danish parliamentary election
- The bid of Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen to form the new Government fails. King Frederik X asks the leader of the Venstre party, Troels Lund Poulsen, to try it instead. [src: (The Guardian)]
Science and technology
- Investigation of UFO reports by the United States government
- The United States Department of Defense begins releasing classified files, images and videos relating to unidentified flying objects. [src: (The Independent)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 May 9
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russian president Vladimir Putin says that he thinks the Russo-Ukrainian war may come to an end soon after previously vowing victory over Ukraine during the Victory Day military parade in Moscow. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (The Moscow Times)]'
- Kharkiv strikes (2022–present)
- Kharkiv Oblast governor Oleh Syniehubov says that a Russian drone has struck a residential building in Kharkiv during the beginning of the 3-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine. [src: (Kyiv Independent)]
- Mali War
- 2026 Mali offensives
- Sources say that 70 people were killed in a new wave of attacks in central Mali the previous day. Al-Qaeda-linked Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin claims responsibility. [src: (Daily Beirut)] [src: (Times of India)]
- Supporters of the Mali military junta gather in Bamako gather to reaffirm their support of Transitional Council authorities. [src: (Africanews)]
- Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
- 2026 Bannu attacks
- At least 21 police officers are killed and three others are injured in a car bomb, followed by gunfire and other explosions, at a checkpoint in Bannu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Sudanese civil war
- 2026 Blue Nile campaign
- The Sudanese Army announces that it has seized control of the Al-Kili area in the Blue Nile State from Rapid Support Forces and SPLM–N. [src: (AA)]
- Ituri conflict
- The DR Congolese military reports that at least 69 people were killed in an attack by CODECO in Ituri Province in April. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
Arts and culture
- 61st Venice Biennale
- The 61st Venice Biennale in Italy opens to the public without a jury after the jury quit in protest of Israel's and Russia's participation and loud protests outside their pavilions. [src: (AP)]
- Exhibits from over 100 countries are shown on display including Belgium. [src: (Brussels Times)]
- 2026 Moscow Victory Day Parade
- Russia marks the Victory Day with a scaled-down military parade in Moscow. [src: (Sky News)]
Disasters and accidents
- Four miners are found dead following an explosion at a coal mine in Cucunubá, Ubaté Province, Colombia. [src: (AFP via Citizen Digital)]
Health and environment
- MV Hondius hantavirus outbreak
- British Army medics are parachuted from an RAF A400M onto the remote Atlantic island of Tristan da Cunha to deliver vital supplies to a British national with suspected hantavirus. [src: (BBC News)]
Law and crime
- Arrest of Jair Bolsonaro
- Brazilian Supreme Federal Court justice Alexandre de Moraes suspends the implementation of a law that could reduce prison sentences for individuals convicted over the 2022–2023 coup plot, including former president Jair Bolsonaro, pending a constitutional review by the full court. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Bahrain arrests 41 individuals in connection with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, including Shia clerics. [src: (MENA via The New Arab)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Hungarian parliamentary election
- Magyar Government
- Péter Magyar of the Tisza Party is sworn in as the prime minister of Hungary, ending the 16-year tenure of Fidesz's Viktor Orbán. [src: (Reuters)]
- The National Assembly of Hungary reconvenes for the first time since the election as elected members are sworn in. Ágnes Forsthoffer is elected as speaker. [src: (Budapest Business Journal)]
- 2026 Farrer by-election
- Farrer MP David Farley becomes the first One Nation candidate elected to the Australian House of Representatives. [src: (ABC News Australia)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 1
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Iraqi conflict
- Withdrawal of United States troops from Iraq
- Ahmad al-Hamidawi, leader of Kata'ib Hezbollah, announces that the group will suspend military activities in Iraq following the withdrawal of U.S. troops, with the exception of targeting hostile aircraft violating the country's airspace. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- Israeli–Palestinian conflict
- Israeli settler violence, Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Gaza war
- Israeli settlers shoot and kill a Palestinian man at his home in Yasuf, West Bank, and injure another. [src: (Reuters)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Aviation shootdowns and accidents during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- A Russian Su-35 fighter jet shoots down a Russian Mi-8 helicopter over Voronezh Oblast, Russia, in a friendly fire incident. All three crew members are killed. [src: (Kyiv Independent)]
- Sudanese civil war, Kordofan campaign
- War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
- A drone strike by the Rapid Support Forces on a dormitory at the University of Kordofan in El Obeid, North Kordofan, Sudan, kills five people. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Ethiopian civil conflict
- 2026 Ethiopian offensive
- Explosions caused by suspected drone strikes are reported in Ethiopia's capital of Addis Ababa, including one near the Ethiopian National Defense Force' headquarters. [src: (BBC News)]
- 2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war
- Pakistan launches airstrikes in Afghanistan, claiming the killing of 22 Taliban fighters at two locations, while the Government of Afghanistan reports that nine women and children are killed in Kunar Province and Helmand Province by Pakistan airstrikes. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Disasters and accidents
- A medical helicopter transporting a patient crashes off the coast of Santa Catalina Island in Los Angeles County, California, United States, killing two people, injuring two others, and leaving one missing. [src: (AP)]
International relations
- Ethiopian civil conflict, TPLF insurgency in Ethiopia
- Eritrea–Ethiopia relations
- Ethiopia closes its embassy in Eritrea and announces the expulsion of ten Eritrean diplomats from the country, after accusing its neighbour of financing the Tigray People's Liberation Front. [src: (AP)]
- Eritrea's foreign ministry announces that the country will cut off diplomatic ties with Ethiopia in response. [src: (AFP via Al Arabiya)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Egypt–Ethiopia relations
- A diplomat from Egypt is told to leave Ethiopia within 48 hours after being declared as persona non grata. [src: (Reuters)]
- The European Commission stops payments with immediate effect to Sierra Leone, which would have been €18 million for 2026, after the nation refused to cooperate with the extradition of drugs trafficker Jos Leijdekkers. [src: (Het Parool)]
Law and crime
- Censorship in Egypt, Human rights in Egypt
- Egyptian police are arresting six journalists from a fact-checking and investigative media outlet, accusing them of spreading misinformation on behalf of the banned Muslim Brotherhood in Egypt. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 RAF Fairford arrests
- British counter-terrorism police arrest a 25-year-old British-Iranian dual national in Westminster, London, England, on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts linked to the RAF Fairford investigation. Officers also search two properties in the area. [src: (CNN)]
- Sentencing Act 2026
- Hundreds of prisoners begin leaving prison in England and Wales under an early release scheme by the British government to avoid overcapacity in prisons. More than 4,500 "low-risk" prisoners are expected to be released in the coming weeks. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Firstpost)]
- Former Malawian military chief Paul Valentino Phiri is arrested by Malawi's anti-corruption agency for allegedly trafficking weapons to Sudan during his tenure in June and July 2025. [src: (Al-Monitor)]
- Two 18-year-old former students attack a secondary school in Torreón, Coahuila, Mexico, with knives and pyrotechnic devices, killing the vice-principal and injuring three people. Police arrest both suspects. [src: (AFP via RNZ)]
Politics and elections
- Immigration to Japan
- Japan tightens permanent residency requirements for foreign nationals, introducing above-average income and basic Japanese-language standards while raising application fees twentyfold as part of broader changes to immigration policy. [src: (AFP)]
- Gerardo Giovagnoli and William Casali are sworn in as the new Captains Regent of San Marino, succeeding Alice Mina and Vladimiro Selva. [src: (San Marino RTV)]
- Ousted Sudanese leader Omar al-Bashir is sent to a military hospital in Khartoum, Sudan, for medical treatment. [src: (Reuters)]
Science and technology
- SpaceX Crew-13 
- The SpaceX Crew-13 mission to the International Space Station launches, carrying two NASA astronauts, one Roscosmos cosmonaut, and one Canadian Space Agency astronaut, from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, United States. [src: (AFP via France 24)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 10
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Ethiopian civil conflict
- 2026 Ethiopian offensive
- 2026 Eritrean incursion into Ethiopia
- Ethiopian forces regain control of Adigrat in the Tigray Region following a withdrawal of Eritrean forces. Celebrations are reported in the city following the withdrawal. [src: (Oman Observer)] [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (UA News)]
- Yemeni civil war
- Houthi–Saudi conflict
- October 2026 King Khalid International Airport attack
- Twelve people are killed and 309 more injured in a Houthi missile attack against Terminal 3 of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. [src: (The Wall Street Journal)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Zaporizhzhia strikes
- At least 20 people are killed and 32 others are injured in a Russian glide bomb airstrike on a five-story residential building in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine. [src: (Ukrainska Pravda)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
- The National Hurricane Center reports that Hurricane Isaias has weakened to a post-tropical cyclone after making landfall near Destin, Florida, United States. [src: (WVTM-TV)] [src: (NBC News)]
- Four people are killed during Isaias' landfall in the United States, with two deaths in Escambia County, Florida, and another two in Alabama. [src: (The Guardian)]
- 2026 Pacific hurricane season
- Tropical storm Simon strengthens into a category 4 Pacific hurricane with 150 mph (240 kph) winds as it heads towards Mexico's coast. [src: (AP)] [src: (The Rio Times)]
- A man is killed after jumping into a tiger enclosure and being attacked at Yorkshire Wildlife Park in South Yorkshire, England. The tiger was uninjured. [src: (BBC News)]
Law and crime
- Censorship in India
- 2026 anti-CEC protests
- Indian authorities are placing New Delhi under a security lockdown and have been detaining thousands of demonstrators to block a rally organized by the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (The New York Times)]
- 2026 Poland school stabbings
- A woman carries out a mass stabbing at an adult school in Warsaw, Poland, injuring three people. The suspect is arrested. It is the third such attack in the country in a week. [src: (AP)]
Sports
- 2026–27 La Liga
- In association football, the match between Rayo Vallecano and Athletic Bilbao is abandoned by referee José María Sánchez Martínez due to fans throwing objects at the pitch to protest against Rayo president Raúl Martín Presa. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 NCAA Division I FBS football season
- In American college football, the Kentucky Wildcats football team defeats the LSU Tigers 35–34 on a 2-point conversion in overtime, becoming the first team in FBS history to win consecutive overtime games by one point since overtime was introduced in 1996. [src: (The Athletic via The New York Times)] [src: (The Score)]
- 2026 Il Lombardia
- In cycling, French cyclist Paul Seixas wins the 120th edition of the Giro di Lombardia in Italy, becoming the youngest person to do so. [src: (NBC Sports)] [src: (The Guardian)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 11
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Yemeni civil war
- Houthi–Saudi conflict
- October 2026 attacks on Saudi Arabia airports
- Houthis launch an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia, causing a fire, killing one person and injuring multiple people. [src: (Sky News)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- An Indian national injured in yesterday's attack on King Khalid International Airport dies from his injuries, raising the total death toll to 13. [src: (Reuters)]
- The Royal Saudi Air Force launches an airstrike in Sanaa, Yemen, killing a child and wounding seven other people. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- A drone strikes the Nicaragua-flagged tanker MT Petro Dolphin near Sohar, Oman, leaving two Indian sailors missing and prompting the rescue of nine others. Omani authorities conduct search-and-rescue operations for the missing crew members. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- Sudanese civil war
- War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
- Airstrikes are launched at the Egypt–Sudan border targeting an artisanal gold mine in a mountainous area, killing at least 72 people. [src: (Sky News)]
- Mexican drug war
- Three civilians and two police officers are killed in a mass shooting in Jacona, Michoacán, Mexico, while six other people are wounded. Separately, three gunmen are killed in a shootout with police in Zamora. [src: (OEM in Spanish)]
- Colombian conflict
- Four FARC dissidents are killed and 12 rifles seized after an airstrike by the National Army of Colombia against a guerrilla camp in Norte de Santander Department, Colombia. [src: (El Tiempo in Spanish)] 
- A drone strike kills a soldier in La Vega, Cauca Department, Colombia. [src: (Publimetro in Spanish)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Budhi Gandaki flood
- Ten people are reported missing and at least 35 houses and six bridges are swept away in a major flash flood in Gorkha District, Gandaki Province, Nepal. The exact number of casualties is unknown. [src: (ANI via Gulf News)] [src: (Nepal Views)]
- 2026 Djibouti migrant boat sinking
- At least 139 people are killed, 84 more are missing, and over 80 are rescued when a boat carrying migrants shipwrecks off the coast of Djibouti. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Eleven people are killed and 27 others are injured when a tour bus collides with a truck at a toll road of Otoyol 5 in Akhisar, Manisa Province, Turkey. [src: (Türkiye Today)]
- One person is killed and around 19 others are injured, including four critically, when a passenger bus plunges down a slope and crashes into a residential complex in Valparaíso, Chile. [src: (Teletrece in Spanish)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- The Kenyan health ministry reports that no Ebola cases have been reported since one patient died from the disease on October 5, with 293 tests conducted. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Indonesia wildfires
- The Indonesian forestry ministry and International Animal Rescue release eight orangutans rescued from wildfires into a protected wildforest in West Kalimantan after fires destroyed habitat near plantations. [src: (AFP)]
Law and crime
- 2026 anti-CEC protests
- An executive magistrate's court in New Delhi, India, orders the release of Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other leaders, requiring them to avoid breaches of the peace for one year after their detention. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Kraków mayoral election
- Independent candidate Łukasz Gibała wins the Kraków mayoral election in Poland against government-backed Civic Platform senator Monika Piątkowska. [src: (Politico)] [src: (Euronews)]
- 2026 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa state of emergency
- Pakistani president Asif Ali Zardari declares a state of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and suspends its provincial government amid disputes over the province's response to Islamist militancy. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- 2027 French presidential election
- Raphaël Glucksmann is elected as a candidate in the 2027 French presidential election during the Socialist Party primary, receiving more than 66% of the votes in the first round. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- 2026 Slovenian referendum
- Slovenians vote in a referendum to decide whether to overturn the Law on Parliamentary Investigation that was adopted by the National Assembly in May 2026. Voters holded this law by a 49% to 51% vote. [src: (France24)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 12
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Yemeni civil war
- Houthi–Saudi conflict
- October 2026 attacks on Saudi Arabia airports
- The Houthis claim to have attacked King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, with a ballistic missile for a third consecutive day. [src: (Reuters)]
- Delta Air Lines postpones direct flights from Atlanta's Hartsfield–Jackson Atlanta International Airport to Riyadh following attacks by the Houthis on the country. [src: (The Hill)]
- Kivu conflict
- M23 campaign
- Former Congolese president Joseph Kabila announces the formation of a rebel political-military coalition named Front for the Refoundation of the Nation, which includes the March 23 Movement, Twirwaneho and the Congo River Alliance. The group, led by Kabila, says it aimed to coordinate "resistance forces" to topple the Government of President Félix Tshisekedi. [src: (BBC)]
Business and economy
- 2026 Nobel Prizes
- American economists Robert Ernest Hall and Michael Dean Woodford are jointly awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for their work on "microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation". [src: (CNN)]
- American visual images company Getty Images announces that it will file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy. [src: (Reuters)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Pacific hurricane season
- Two deaths are reported after hurricanes Rachel and Simon made landfall on Mexico's coast, with Guerrero governor Evelyn Salgado and Baja California governor Marina del Pilar Ávila confirming their deaths. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Incidents at Six Flags parks
- One person is killed and four others are injured after an accident on the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia in Mableton, Georgia, United States. [src: (BNO News)]
- A fire destroys the historic Marché des Enfants-Rouges food market in Paris, France. [src: (France 24)]
International relations
- International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, Russia–European Union relations
- The Council of the European Union approves the 22nd package of sanctions against Russia, targeting 1,569 individuals and entities of the country's military and industrial complex. [src: (EU Council)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Aubagne school shooting
- A 14-year-old student opens fire at a middle school in Aubagne, France, injuring two staff members, before being detained. [src: (AP)] [src: (France 24)]
- 2026 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa state of emergency
- Pakistan's federal government detains hundreds of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) members, including former Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi and other provincial officials, after suspending the PTI-led provincial administration and imposing emergency rule. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- 2026 French supermarket cyber attack
- A cyber attack without attribution against French supermarkets results in losses worth millions of euros. [src: (BBC News)]
- A woman stabs her husband and her 3-year-old son to death while on vacation at a Great Wolf Lodge in the Pocono Township, Pocono Mountains, Pennsylvania, U.S.. [src: (ABC News)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Estonian presidential election
- Ülle Madise, who was elected by the Riigikogu in September, takes office as President of Estonia, succeeding Alar Karis. [src: (Estonian World)]
Science and technology
- Generative AI chatbot company Character.ai files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, citing costs and litigations including those linked to teen suicides. [src: (The Wall Street Journal)] [src: (CBS News)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 13
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Yemeni civil war
- Houthi–Saudi conflict
- The Royal Saudi Air Force strikes a fuel depot near Sanaa, Yemen. The Houthis launch missiles upon multiple Saudi Arabian cities, including Riyadh and Dammam, in response. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (CNN)]
- An administrative building belonging to Saudi Aramco in Dhahran, Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia, is partially consumed by a fire after a Houthi missile is intercepted over the city by Saudi forces. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Hezbollah–Israel conflict, Funding of Hezbollah
- Hezbollah spokesperson Ali Damoush announces that the group will pay up to US$14,000 in aid to families whose homes in Lebanon were destroyed or rendered uninhabitable during its war with Israel. Families in Beirut and its suburbs will receive $14,000, while those elsewhere in the country will receive $12,000. [src: (AP)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Bulgaria–Russia relations, Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Two merchant ships are hit by unknown drones off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast, with one sinking. Eleven crew members are missing and 20 in total are rescued. Bulgarian prime minister Rumen Radev has blamed Russia and summoned its ambassador. It is the second such attack in six days. [src: (Reuters)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
- Six deaths are confirmed in Florida, United States, from Hurricane Isaias. [src: (Fox Weather)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- 2026 Multan train derailment
- At least seven people are killed and over 40 others are injured in a train derailment near Multan, Punjab, Pakistan. [src: (AA)] [src: (AFP via The Straits Times)]
Health and environment
- Famine in Yemen, Water supply and sanitation in Yemen
- The World Health Organization reports a surge in cholera cases in Yemen over the past three weeks. The country previously had a 6-year-long outbreak due to the ongoing humanitarian crisis. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- Indonesian authorities release 20 protected green sea turtles back into the oceans off Bali after they were seized from an empty boat abandoned by wildlife smugglers last week. [src: (AP)]
Law and crime
- 2024 Cornell University rape allegations
- Cornell University in Ithaca, New York, United States, suspends all fraternity parties and social events for the remainder of the 2026–27 academic year following allegations that seven Chi Phi members drugged and gang-raped a student in 2024. [src: (AFP)] [src: (BBC News)]
- Impeachment trial of Sara Duterte
- Philippine prosecutors in the impeachment trial of vice president Sara Duterte drop three of the four impeachment charges in an attempt to speed up the trial. The Senate, sitting as an impeachment court, approves the move. [src: (AP)] 
- LGBTQ rights in Hungary
- The Hungarian National Assembly passes an amendment repealing most provisions of the anti-LGBTQ child protection law that was previously passed during former prime minister Viktor Orbán's tenure in 2021. [src: (DW)]
- Murder of Tupac Shakur
- The Clark County District Court in Nevada, United States, sentences former Crips gang leader Duane "Keffe D" Davis to a minimum of 40 years in prison for orchestrating the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur in Las Vegas. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (DW)]
- North Korean remote worker scheme
- The United States Federal Bureau of Investigation announces the arrests of two men in Ohio and Pennsylvania over an alleged North Korean remote-work scheme and the seizures of about 187 computers and related devices from more than 40 suspected laptop farms in Texas. [src: (AFP via Malay Mail)]
- Scam centers in Myanmar
- A Chinese court sentences three triad members to death for crimes linked to scam centers in Kokang, Myanmar, including fraud, drug trafficking, illegal gambling, prostitution, and the murders of two Chinese citizens. [src: (AFP via CBS News)]
- Four people are killed and three more injured in a mass shooting at a memorial service in Katlehong, Gauteng, South Africa. [src: (AP)]
- Three Indian nationals are killed and five others are injured in a suspected arson attack in Bochum, North Rhine-Westphalia Germany. A 41-year-old resident is arrested. [src: (tagesschau)]
- Eight people are injured in a mass stabbing at a supermarket in Incheon, South Korea. A suspect is arrested. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (CNA)]
- Students in Tirana, Albania, throw bricks at the Ministry of Education building, prompting riot police to respond. [src: (Reuters)]
Sports
- 2026 World Artistic Gymnastics Championships
- The Netherlands denies visas to Russian artistic gymnasts Anna Kalmykova, Viktoria Listunova, and Angelina Melnikova for the world championships in Rotterdam, while four other Russian gymnasts receive permission to enter the country. [src: (AP)]
- In auto racing, Formula 1 announces a new grand prix in Kigali, Rwanda, to run for at least 10 years starting in the early 2030s with a new track. This would be the first F1 grand prix in Africa since South Africa in 1993. [src: (AP)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 14
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Yemeni civil war
- Houthi–Saudi conflict
- The Houthis claim to have shot down a Royal Saudi Air Force Eurofighter Typhoon aircraft over Saada Governorate, Yemen. Saudi authorities did not comment on the claim. [src: (AFP via AA)]
- The Saudi Civil Defense reports that debris from intercepted Houthi cruise missiles injured four people, including a child, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, and damaged 15 homes. [src: (AFP via CNA)]
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Two cargo ships, the Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride and the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged dry bulk carrier Cape Dao, sink after both are attacked by projectiles near the Strait of Hormuz while trying to navigate through what Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps called an "illegal and dangerous route." At least one crew member is killed in the attacks. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
- A Russian ballistic missile attack strikes a power station in the Dniprovskyi District, Kyiv, Ukraine, leaving more than 1,000 residential buildings without heating. [src: (BBC News)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Darfur campaign
- The Sudanese Armed Forces announces that they have re-captured the Bir Kelekel area of West Darfur, Sudan, from Rapid Support Forces, according to West Darfur state governor Bahr al-Din Adam Karama. [src: (Radio Tamazuj)] [src: (AA)]
- Flamingo Revolution
- Rioters attack government buildings, banks, businesses and other sites as anti-government protests erupt in Tirana, Albania. At least 23 police officers and six others are injured during the unrest, while 35 people are detained. President Bajram Begaj condemns the violence and appeals for calm across the nation. [src: (AP)]
Disasters and accidents
- Three people are killed and four others are missing after torrential rainfall triggers widespread flooding across Istanbul, Turkey. [src: (ABC News)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Southeast Asian haze
- Singapore records its highest air pollution level of 2026 as one-hour PM concentrations reach about 288 micrograms per cubic metre amid haze from Indonesian wildfires. [src: (AFP)]
- Timor-Leste suspends in-person classes nationwide from October 15 to 17 due to worsening air quality from wildfire smoke and pollutant particles across Southeast Asia. [src: (AFP)]
International relations
- Colombia–Israel relations
- Colombia opens an embassy in Jerusalem and restores its free trade agreement with Israel. [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Nord Stream pipelines sabotage
- The Ukrainian citizen accused of sabotaging the Nord Stream pipelines in 2022 faces trial at the Higher Regional Court in Hamburg, Germany, [src: (DW)] [src: (UPI)]
- 2026 Delhi Jantar Mantar protests
- A court in New Delhi, India, remands Cockroach Janta Party spokespeople Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka in custody for five days after police detained them for entering the restricted Jantar Mantar protest site. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- Censorship in Turkey
- Turkish opposition-leaning and independent news channel Halk TV goes offline as it is raided by police and new administrators are appointed by the government. [src: (BBC News)]
- Internet censorship in Mexico
- President Claudia Sheinbaum signs a decree banning violent content on social media to protect minors under the age of 18. [src: (Expansión)]
- Costa Rica inaugurates , a maximum-security prison modeled after El Salvador's CECOT mega-prison, aimed at holding 20% of the country's current prison population, as the homicide rate reached a record high in 2023. [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Irish public sector strikes
- Over 300,000 public sector workers in Ireland, including teachers, health workers, and other civil servants, start a general strike, the first in the country since 2009, to protest against a deadlock in pay negotiations. [src: (Reuters)]
Science and technology
- Kekova shipwreck
- The oldest known shipwreck in the world ( 2700–2400 BC) is excavated in Kekova, Turkey. [src: (CNN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 15
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Yemeni civil war
- Houthi–Saudi conflict
- Saudi Arabia says that it has intercepted a missile intended for Medina. However, the Houthis denied launching a missile at the city. [src: (The Hill)] [src: (France 24)]
- The Houthis launch missiles against Al-Maashiq Palace, headquarters of the Presidential Leadership Council and official residence of President Rashad al-Alimi, in Aden, Yemen, killing five people and injuring 16. No member of the council is harmed in the attack. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Reuters)]
Business and economy
- China–North Korea relations
- The New Yalu River Bridge connecting Dandong, China, and Sinuiju, North Korea, opens following a 12-year delay. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (NK News)]
- The European Central Bank authorizes UniCredit to raise its stake in Commerzbank above 30% without an upper limit, allowing the Italian bank to proceed toward taking control of the German lender. [src: (The Eastern Herald)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Peshawar school roof collapse
- A roof collapses at a school in Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, killing 34 students and a teacher, and injuring 50 more people. [src: (BBC News)]
- 2026 Indonesia wildfires
- Four people are killed fighting wildfires in Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park in East Java, Indonesia, after flames and thick smoke trapped them. Two others suffer serious burns. [src: (AFP)]
- Seven people are missing after a San Marino-flagged tanker catches fire off the coast of Romania amid recent drone attacks on merchant shipping in the Black Sea. Search and rescue operations are underway to locate the missing crew members. [src: (Politico)]
Health and environment
- The United Kingdom declares a severe drought in Cornwall, Devon, Dorset, Somerset, East Sussex, and West Sussex after prolonged low rainfall left more than 80% of England in drought and major reservoirs below 20% capacity. [src: (AFP)]
International relations
- Germany–Iran relations, Antisemitism in 21st-century Germany, Iranian external operations
- A court in Hamburg, Germany, sentences a Danish national to eight years and six months in prison and an Afghan national to four years and six months in prison for plotting to assassinate Josef Schuster, the president of the Central Council of Jews in Germany, on behalf of Iran. [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Silver Rail Elementary School shooting
- Three children and a teacher are killed in a mass school shooting at the Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, United States. Two other people are wounded. The perpetrator, a 16-year-old male, is shot and killed by a bystander. [src: (AP)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- Capital punishment in the United States
- U.S. president Donald Trump announces that the Department of Defense has reversed its plan to livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan, the perpetrator of the 2009 Fort Hood shooting, scheduled for December 3. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (AP)]
- Argentine police arrest at least 25 people after clashes during a university funding protest in Buenos Aires, while eight police officers are injured. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Northern Irish politician and former Democratic Unionist Party leader Jeffrey Donaldson is sentenced to 15 years in prison for child sexual abuse and rape. The offences occurred between 1985 and 2008. [src: (AP)] [src: (BBC News)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Swedish government formation
- The Riksdag votes against the appointment of Social Democratic leader Magdalena Andersson to repeat as Prime Minister of Sweden. Last 28 September, Andersson already returned her mandate to explore forming a new government. [src: (Anadolu Agency)]
Science and technology
- Astronomers discover the first green star, WD J1330+6435, according to a study published by RAS Techniques and Instruments. [src: (Popular Science)]
- At the General Conference on Weights and Measures, the International Bureau of Weights and Measures votes to abolish future leap seconds and make Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) continuous, starting 20 May 2027. To account for future differences between UTC and International Atomic Time, a leap hour will be observed as needed. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (Scientific American)]
Sports
- 2026 Major League Baseball season
- In baseball, the Milwaukee Brewers sweep the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS to advance to the 2026 World Series, their first since 1982. [src: (ESPN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 17
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Yemeni civil war
- Egypt–Saudi Arabia relations, Houthi–Saudi conflict
- Egyptian president Abdel Fattah El-Sisi states that Egypt will take all necessary steps to protect and defend Saudi Arabia should the latter so desire. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- Gaza war
- Israeli settler violence
- Masked Israeli settlers attack a group of European diplomats, including the Belgian consul general, French and Polish diplomats, and Catholic representatives visiting Taybeh in the occupied West Bank, Palestine. [src: (AP)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Kolkata Durga Puja crowd crush
- At least 17 people are killed and 25 others are injured in a crowd crush at a pandal in Kolkata, West Bengal, India. [src: (Hindustan Times)] [src: (Sky News)]
- CFB Wainwright fire
- An explosion and wildfire occurs at the CFB Wainwright, a Canadian Armed Forces base in Alberta. Four people are killed and dozens more injured. [src: (CBC News)] [src: (CTV News)]
- Ten tourists are killed and nine others sustain injuries after a resort catches fire in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh. [src: (AA)]
- Eight people are killed and eight others are injured after a minibus carrying 23 passengers plunges into a drain along the Delhi–Mumbai Expressway near Kota, Rajasthan, India. [src: (The Times of India)]
- A Piper Tomahawk II aircraft crashes near Drymen, Stirling, Scotland, killing the two people on board. [src: (BBC News)]
- A priest is killed after getting struck by a large wooden crucifix during a livestreamed Mass in Guayaquil, Ecuador. [src: (CNN)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- Kenya confirms four additional cases of Bundibugyo ebolavirus, including three health workers who treated Kenya's first patient and one of his relatives, raising the national total to seven. All four are already in quarantine. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Law and crime
- Gen Z protests
- 2026 European unrest
- 2026 French student protests, 17 October 2026 protests
- Over 500,000 people take part in protests across France, according to the national trade union confederation, while clashes and riots erupt in large cities. [src: (FranceInfo)]
- Protesters force their way into Marseille's town hall and vandalize the interior before being dispersed. [src: (CNews)] 
- In Lille, protesters storm the city hall and damage the premises prior to being removed by security forces. [src: (Ouest-France)] 
- Dozens of shops are looted across major French cities amid widespread rioting and civil unrest. [src: (BFMTV)] 
- The Hôtel de Ville in Limoges were partially destroyed by fire. [src: (Le Parisien in French)]
- 2026 French fuel protests
- Yellow vests activists hold mass demonstrations across France against rising fuel prices and join the student protests. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- 2026 anti-CEC protests
- A court in New Delhi, India, orders the release of Cockroach Janta Party founder and activist Abhijeet Dipke on a peace bond, one day after police detained him while he was heading to a protest against the Election Commission of India. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Czech Senate election
- In Czechia, opposition parties win 22 of the contested 27 seats in the Senate. The lead party of prime minister Andrej Babiš's government, ANO 2011, comes in third place. The election is the first time in the country's history where governing parties did not win a single seat in a senatorial election. [src: (AP)]
- Protests against Donald Trump
- The fourth round of No Kings protests are held across the United States against president Donald Trump and his administration and to encourage early voting ahead of the upcoming midterm elections. [src: (AFP)] [src: (USA Today)]
Sports
- 2026–27 NHL season
- In ice hockey, the Florida Panthers become the first team in the National Hockey League to record a natural hat trick in three consecutive games. [src: (The Athletic via The New York Times)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 18
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reports that an oil tanker has caught on fire and exploded in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz after striking a naval mine. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- Haitian conflict
- El Salvador–Haiti relations
- Armed gang members ambush Salvadoran Air Force personnel serving with Haiti's Gang Suppression Force in Port-au-Prince, using gunfire and explosives. Four Salvadoran service members remain missing after escaping their burning armored vehicle. [src: (Reuters)]
Disasters and accidents
- A truck loses control and runs over devotees outside a temple in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, India, killing at least 13 and injuring nearly 40 others. [src: (AFP via Dawn)] [src: (The Indian Express)]
- At least eight people are killed and eight others are injured after a mortar shell explosion in Zawiya, Libya. [src: (Xinhua)]
- A light aircraft crashes into a dry riverbed in Kondariotissa, Pieria, Greece. Two people are killed. [src: (Xinhua)]
Health and environment
- Equatorial Guinea announces that it will expand its program combating malaria to the mainland and Annobón. The program has already heavily reduced malaria cases on Bioko Island. [src: (The Independent)]
International relations
- Cross-strait relations
- The Taiwanese coast guard drives away 16 Chinese coast guard, research, and fishing vessels operating near Taiwan and the Pratas Island, including some that entered restricted waters. [src: (AFP via The Hindu)]
- Free trade agreements of Vietnam
- Vietnam signs a free trade agreement with the European Free Trade Association (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, and Switzerland) that reduces or eliminates tariffs on industrial, agricultural, and fish products and covers services, intellectual property, and sustainable development. [src: (AFP)]
Politics and elections
- Water scarcity in Mexico
- Protests continue for the second week in Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico, over water shortages and widespread contamination. A study in June found that at least 93% of households' water systems contained no residual chlorine, but had elevated levels of lead, mercury, nitrates, and E. coli. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (Türkiye)]
- The Iranian parliament appoints Mehrdad Akhlaghi as Minister of Defence, replacing acting minister Majid Ebn-e-Reza. [src: (Reuters)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 19
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Gaza war
- Israeli settler violence
- Israel Police arrest 10 people in the occupied West Bank over attacks on American photojournalist Heidi Levine and the mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries, France, who were travelling with European diplomats, and seize vehicles and other evidence during raids. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Yemeni civil war
- 2026 Yemen offensives
- 2026 Shabwah missile attack
- A missile attack by the Houthis kills 58 soldiers, injures over 200, and leaves 14 missing at a training center in Shabwah Governorate, Yemen. [src: (Reuters)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Abyei border conflict
- Amiet market massacre
- A drone strike kills at least 73 people at a market in the disputed Abyei area between South Sudan and Sudan. [src: (Reuters)]
- Rapid Support Forces atrocities in Khartoum
- Three children are killed in an alleged Rapid Support Forces drone strike in Khartoum, Sudan. [src: (AP)]
Disasters and accidents
- Mediterranean Sea migrant smuggling
- Twelve migrants, including an infant, are killed when two separate speedboats capsize off the coast of the Lesbos and Samos islands in Greece. [src: (AP)]
- Fourteen miners are killed and seven more injured when an open pit gold mine collapses in Nariño Department, Colombia. [src: (AP)]
International relations
- Andorra–European Union relations, San Marino–European Union relations, Potential enlargement of the European Union
- Andorra and San Marino each sign an association agreement with the European Union. [src: (The Brussels Times)]
- Gaza Strip famine, Palestine and the United Nations
- The World Food Programme cuts monthly food aid for about 500,000 people in the Gaza Strip because of funding shortages, reducing the number of recipients from 1.6 million to 1.1 million. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Law and crime
- Cuba–United States relations
- 1996 shootdown of Brothers to the Rescue aircraft, United States embargo against Cuba
- A judge in Miami-Dade County, Florida, United States, issues a no-bail bond arrest warrant for former Cuban president Raúl Castro after Florida attorney general James Uthmeier charged Castro with conspiracy to commit first-degree murder by directing spies to infiltrate Brothers to the Rescue and ordering the attack on their planes in 1996. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Shakahola Forest incident
- A Kenyan court convicts Good News International Ministries leader Paul Nthenge Mackenzie of murdering 190 children and an adult whose deaths were linked to starvation in Shakahola Forest. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Chihuahua CIA scandal, Mexico–United States relations
- Former Chihuahua attorney general César Jáuregui Moreno is arrested by federal agents on a treason warrant as he leaves a Chihuahua state court, which had declined to order his pretrial detention after state prosecutors arrested him two days earlier on related charges of unlawful exercise of public office. He is accused of allowing U.S. agents, reported to be Central Intelligence Agency officers, to take part in an anti-drug operation in April without federal approval. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Reuters)] [src: (El Universal)]
- Independent Australian MP Helen Haines is deliberately hit by a car outside her office in Wangaratta, Victoria. Police arrest the car's driver, while Haines is airlifted to a hospital. Haines later had both her legs amputated. [src: (AFP)] [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (Reuters)]
- A teacher and a student are injured in a stabbing attack at a school in Bistrița, Romania. The 13-year-old suspect is arrested. [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Alberta referendums
- 2026 Alberta independence referendum
- Albertans vote on ten referendums, including one to decide if Alberta should seek separation from Canada. [src: (Reuters)]
- Albertan voters reject pursuing a future independence referendum, with more than three-quarters supporting the province remaining in Canada. [src: (BBC News)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 2
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Yemeni civil war
- Red Sea crisis
- 2026 Yemen offensives, Strait of Bab al-Mandab crisis
- Reuters reports that Saudi Arabia is planning an offensive on the Houthis in the coming weeks to take back the Bab al-Mandab Strait. [src: (Reuters)]
- Ethiopian civil conflict
- 2026 Ethiopian offensive
- Ethiopian government forces push Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) rebels out of Afar Region after recapturing the towns of Abala, Erebti and Megale. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- Sudan's armed forces announces that they have recaptured the North Kordofan town of al-Mazroub. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
- The death toll in the Rapid Support Forces drone attack on the University of Kordofan in El Obeid rises to 10. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
- A Russian drone strikes Pivdennyi Bridge in Kyiv, Ukraine, for the fourth time in two days. [src: (The Kyiv Independent)]
- Boko Haram insurgency
- Eighteen people are killed as Boko Haram gunmen open fire on villagers collecting firewood in Marte, Borno State, Nigeria. [src: (Reuters)]
Business and economy
- 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
- The G7 countries announce a plan to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil to combat rising fuel prices caused by the Iran war. [src: (The New York Times)]
- Argentina introduces an immigrant investor program allowing foreigners to obtain citizenship through a US$350,000 contribution to the Ministry of Economy or an $800,000 government bond, with lower additional payments required for spouses and children. [src: (AFP)]
Disasters and accidents
- Twenty people are killed and five others are injured after a four-vehicle crash in Plateau, Nigeria. [src: (Xinhua)]
- The United States National Park Service confirms that the Hōlei Sea Arch, located on Hawaii's Big Island, has collapsed into the Pacific Ocean. [src: (The Guardian)]
International relations
- China–Japan relations
- 2025–2026 China–Japan diplomatic crisis, East China Sea EEZ disputes
- A Chinese research vessel leaves Japan's exclusive economic zone after the Japan Coast Guard repeatedly ordered it to halt what Japan described as unauthorized scientific surveys near Ishigaki Island in Okinawa Prefecture. [src: (AFP via CNA)]
Law and crime
- 2026 French lycée protests
- Mass rioting continues for a third day across France with hundreds reportedly injured and over 735 schools shut, while more than 2,000 people are arrested. [src: (BBC News)]
- Riot police clash with protesters in Paris, Montpellier, Nantes and Marseille as justice minister Gérald Darmanin says protests had "gone from high-school student demonstrations to a public order disturbance" and urges an immediate end to violence. [src: (BBC News)]
- French government ministers, including education minister Édouard Geffray, accuse the far-left of inciting the youth-led unrest across the country. Intelligence agencies briefing the government during a crisis meeting on the riots accuse the left-wing La France Insoumise of actively inciting people to join the protests.
