[src: (AFP via NDTV)] [src: (Ynet News)]
- French police near Angers, Pays de la Loire, arrest four Ukrainian nationals suspected of stealing more than €200,000 (US$225,000) in electronics from moving trucks on highways by boarding the vehicles at speed and transferring cargo to an accompanying car. [src: (Vietnam.vn)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Spanish housing protests
- Spain's parliament rejects two government housing decrees that would have expanded protections against evictions, limited some real-estate practices, encouraged rentals through tax incentives, and allowed tenants to renew residential leases automatically. [src: (AP)]
- 2026 Swiss Federal Council election
- Swiss president Guy Parmelin announces his resignation from the Federal Council effective December 31. Parliament is expected to elect his successor on 9 December. [src: (AFP)] [src: (Swissinfo)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 20
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Sudanese civil war
- Abyei border conflict
- Amiet market massacre
- The death toll in the market drone attack in Abyei on the border of South Sudan and Sudan yesterday rises to 220. [src: (Sudans Post)]
- Blue Nile campaign
- The Sudanese Army says that they have repelled an attack by the Rapid Support Forces and Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North (SPLM–N) on the Blue Nile state. [src: (Sudan Tribune)] 
- War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
- The Rapid Support Forces launches a drone strike on a power plant in Tendelti in Sudan's White Nile State, knocking out the main transition line connecting North Kordofan. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
Disasters and accidents
- At least 14 people are killed and 20 others are injured when a bus and a truck collide head-on in Natore District, Bangladesh. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Twelve people are killed and 30 others are injured after a bus crashes into a truck near Cairo, Egypt. [src: (Xinhua)]
- A leak of glycidyl methacrylate from a chemical tank at a terminal in Toledo, Ohio, United States, forces nearly 1,000 residents to evacuate and prompts shelter-in-place orders for more than 50,000 people in Toledo. [src: (Associated Press)] [src: (EPA)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- Nigeria announces its first case of Ebola virus in the epidemic. The victim is a woman who had recently visited Uganda. [src: (The Guardian)]
International relations
- Libya–Turkey relations
- Libya (GNA)–Turkey maritime deal
- Libya's eastern-based House of Representatives approves a 2019 maritime boundary agreement with Turkey and repeals two 2020 decisions that rejected the accord. [src: (Reuters)]
- South Korea–Ukraine relations
- South Korea withdraws additional embassy staff from Ukraine following a dispute over two captured North Korean soldiers who were transferred to South Korea. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- Houthi–Saudi conflict, Saudi Arabia–United Kingdom relations
- United Kingdom says it will deploy RAF Typhoons to help Saudis defend against Houthi attacks. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- 2026 European unrest
- 17 October riots
- Police arrest a 34-year-old man for the arson attack on the Hôtel de Ville in Limoges, Haute-Vienne, France. [src: (BBC)]
- 2022 San Antonio migrant deaths
- A United States federal judge sentences a Guatemalan national to 30 years in prison for helping organize a 2022 migrant-smuggling operation in San Antonio, Texas, that left 53 migrants dead and 11 injured. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Pakistan arrests a man for selling fake postage stamps in the United States that resulted in a $126 million loss to the U.S. Postal Service. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Dawn)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Romanian political crisis
- The Parliament of Romania appoints Luca Niculescu as the new Prime Minister, succeeding Ilie Bolojan who resigned amid a politicial crisis. [src: (Reuters)]
- Malaysia's Registrar of Societies deregisters the opposition coalition Perikatan Nasional, citing internal disputes and breaches of the constitution, preventing its component parties from contesting forthcoming elections under a common coalition banner. [src: (Reuters)]
Science and technology
- Japanese space program
- JAXA launches the Martian Moons eXploration spacecraft from the Tanegashima Space Center toward Phobos aboard an H3 rocket, aiming to collect at least 10 grams of surface material from the Martian moon and return the samples to Earth in 2031. [src: (Reuters)]
- Black October
- PHP2Shell
- A critical vulnerability in PHP allowing for remote code execution is discovered, causing many websites to temporarily go offline while a security update is pushed the following day. [src: (NBC News)]
- Indian certificate authority eMudhra has its private keys compromised, revealing that some of them were extremely insecure single digit numerals. Major web browser developers Mozilla, Google, and Apple subsequently block the certificates. [src: (The Register)]
Sports
- 2026 World Series
- In Major League Baseball, the Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers advance to the World Series, marking the first time in 46 years that neither playoff team has won a championship before. [src: (Yahoo Sports)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 21
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Yemeni civil war
- Houthi–Saudi conflict
- October 2026 Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabian airports
- Two people are killed and eight others are injured in a Houthi attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia. [src: (BBC News)]
- Saudi Arabia–United States relations
- The U.S. Department of State orders non-emergency employees at its embassy in Riyadh to leave the country as Houthi attacks ramp up. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Two people are killed and two others are injured by debris after a suspected Houthi drone is shot down near Shaybah oil field in Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia. [src: (ABS-CBN News)]
- Gaza war
- 2025 Gaza City offensive
- The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) and Shin Bet say that they have killed Musa Abd Muhammad Hamouda, a Hamas Nukhba forces militant that took part in planning the killing of four IDF soldiers in September 2025. [src: (Ynetnews)]
- Haitian conflict
- 2026 Croix-des-Bouquets gang ambush
- Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele announces the start of a military operation to rescue four Air Force technicians. The technicians, attached to the international Gang Suppression Force, were taken hostage after gangs attacked their armored vehicle on 18 October. [src: (Reuters)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war, United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war
- United States special envoy Steve Witkoff arrives in Saint Petersburg to talk with Russian president Vladimir Putin about potentially resolving the war with Ukraine. Putin states he would resume United States-mediated trilateral peace talks with Ukraine, on or after November 10. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (Reuters)]
- American military veteran Stephen Hubbard, who was arrested by Russian authorities in 2022 during the Battle of Izium, is released from custody during the meeting between Putin and Witkoff. [src: (AP)] [src: (BBC News)]
Business and economy
- 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
- South Africa cuts fuel levies by R3.00 (US$0.18) per litre of diesel and R1.50 ($0.09) per litre of petrol from November 4 to December 1 after fuel prices reach record highs. [src: (AFP)]
- The North Sea Transition Authority (NSTA) of the United Kingdom approves production from the Jackdaw gas field after energy secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh authorized the NSTA to grant consent, allowing operator Adura to begin supplying gas by late October. [src: (UPI)]
International relations
- Indonesia, Pakistan, Qatar, and Turkey jointly sign the Badr Memorandum of Understanding, a major agreement to deepen their defence industry cooperation. The agreement aims to support joint military production projects and strengthen cooperation in technical training, research, and development. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Ireland's Dáil Éireann approves legislation removing the requirement for United Nations authorization before deploying more than 12 Defence Forces personnel overseas for peacekeeping missions, while retaining approval by the government and parliament. [src: (France 24)]
Law and crime
- 2026 anti-immigrant movement and xenophobia in South Africa
- A foreign national is beaten to death by a crowd in Durban, South Africa. [src: (BBC News)]
- 2026 Italian unrest
- Italian interior minister Matteo Piantedosi announces a crackdown on truck drivers and farmers protesting in southern Italy over the past month against high fuel prices by blocking highways and transport routes, reporting that they have identified 1,339 individuals, reported 71, and fined 242. [src: (Ansa in Italian)]
- Cross-strait relations
- Taiwanese prosecutors indict five people for allegedly accepting money and planning to injure Huang Yihao, an anti-Chinese Communist Party comedian in New Taipei City. [src: (AP)]
- Lawsuits involving Meta Platforms
- A district judge in New Mexico, United States, orders Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found it guilty of misleading Facebook users about privacy violations, marking its largest fine ever. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Over 80 Americans, British citizens, and Israelis are detained by Israeli soldiers in the Israel-occupied West Bank, including U.S. House of Representatives candidate Brad Lander. [src: (The Guardian)]
- A Tunisian military court sentences politician and businesswoman Olfa Hamdi to four years in prison on state security charges linked to social media posts, including accusations of inciting military personnel to disobey orders. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
Politics and elections
- Gen Z protests
- 2026 European unrest
- Thousands of students and teachers march through Athens, Thessaloniki, and Patras in Greece to protest against the rising cost of living, calling for affordable student housing and more state investment in education. [src: (AP)]
- 2026 Quebec general election, St-Pierre Plamondon ministry
- Paul St-Pierre Plamondon is sworn in as the 34th premier of Quebec, Canada, following the Parti Québécois's victory in the general election. [src: (The Globe and Mail)]
Science and technology
- 2022–2026 video game industry layoffs
- Leveraged buyout of Electronic Arts
- American video game publisher Electronic Arts, which was recently bought-out by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, announces the closing of its Canadian studio BioWare. [src: (Kotaku)]
- Black October
- Node.js releases three security updates to 10 different vulnerabilities, including 4 deemed high-severity, which affect how it handles DNS resolution, TLS handshakes, and Brotli decoding. [src: (Heise Online)]
- A critical security flaw, allowing for remote code execution, in 12 years of GitLab versions is disclosed, requiring updates. [src: (The Hacker News)]
- Open-source artificial intelligence gateway LiteLLM is compromised by attackers, who push a malicious version of LiteLLM to the Python Package Index. [src: (Security Week)]
Sports
- 2026 Canadian Championship
- 2026 Canadian Championship final
- In association football, Forge FC defeats CF Montréal in a penalty shoot-out to become the first Canadian Premier League team to win a Canadian Championship. [src: (CBC)]
- 2026 U.S. Open Cup
- 2026 U.S. Open Cup final
- In association football, St. Louis City SC defeats Columbus Crew in a penalty shoot-out to win the U.S. Open Cup, earning the club its first trophy since beginning play in 2023. [src: (ESPN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 22
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reports that seven oil tankers have been hit in the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Yemeni civil war, Al-Qaeda insurgency in Yemen
- Al-Qaeda gunmen ambush Yemeni Armed Forces soldiers at a mountainous area in the Shabwah Governorate, killing two soldiers and wounding several more. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Haitian conflict
- 2026 Croix-des-Bouquets gang ambush
- El Salvador deploys 100 special forces soldiers to Haiti to assist in the search efforts for the four missing Air Force technicians attached to the Gang Suppression Force. [src: (AP)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Blue Nile campaign
- The Sudanese Armed Forces recaptures two strategic areas in Sudan's Blue Nile state, including the Bukuri base in Ad-Damazin. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
Arts and culture
- British singer Raye wins the 2026 Mercury Prize for her album This Music May Contain Hope. [src: (Billboard)]
- The European Parliament awards its 2026 Sakharov Prize to the International Criminal Court and its officials for their work in global justice and upholding international law. [src: (Reuters)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026–27 European windstorm season
- At least four people are killed and one other is injured by flooding caused by Storm Adam in Bouches-du-Rhône, France. [src: (BBC News)]
- 2026 Tibet earthquake
- A 7.0 earthquake strikes Tibet, with an epicenter in Nagqu, killing 16 people and wounding 32 more. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- At least six people are killed and 25 others are injured when a bus collides with a tree in Manendragarh-Chirmiri-Bharatpur district, Chhattisgarh, India. [src: (Xinhua)]
Health and environment
- France reports the first human case of the livestock Shamonda virus in a patient who died after being hospitalized with an unrelated condition. [src: (Reuters)]
International relations
- Canada–Turkey relations, Free trade agreements of Canada, Free trade agreements of Turkey
- Canada and Turkey open negotiations for a free trade agreement during Canadian prime minister Mark Carney's visit to Ankara. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- 2026 United Nations Secretary-General selection
- Emirati diplomat Lana Nusseibeh announces her candidacy for Secretary-General of the United Nations. [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- Corruption in Ecuador
- Ecuadorian opposition leader and former presidential candidate Luisa González is arrested over allegations of money laundering in campaign financing. [src: (Reuters)]
- LGBTQ rights in Guatemala
- A Guatemalan court sentences seven former police officers to prison terms of up to 60 years for offenses related to the 2024 torture and killing of a gay couple at a police station. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Indonesian authorities capture the Mongolian-flagged MT Global 168 tanker, seize of ketamine, and arrest eight crew members. They also detain the two founders of the ship's company based in Johor Bahru, Malaysia. [src: (Reuters)]
Science and technology
- The Finnish Government grants Posiva an operating license for the Onkalo spent nuclear fuel repository in Eurajoki, making it the world's first licensed deep geological disposal facility for spent nuclear fuel. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Sports
- 2026 World Artistic Gymnastics Championships
- In artistic gymnastics, Japan's Daiki Hashimoto wins his fourth consecutive men's all-around title at the 2026 World Championships in Rotterdam, Netherlands, finishing ahead of China's Zhang Boheng and Japan's Shinnosuke Oka. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- 2026 NFL season
- In American football, the Chicago Bears receive an illegal forward handing penalty in a game against the New England Patriots, the first time in 16 years that the penalty has been handed out. [src: (CBS Sports)]
- 2028 FIFA Women's Club World Cup
- In women's association football, FIFA announces that the United States will host the inaugural FIFA Women's Club World Cup in 2028. [src: (ESPN)]
- The Athletics Integrity Unit bans Ethiopian marathon runner Ruti Aga for six years after she tested positive for methylprednisolone and submitted false information and a forged prescription during an investigation. [src: (AFP via France 24)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 23
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- 2026 drone incidents in Romania
- A merchant ship is hit by drones of unknown origins in the Romanian Black Sea, killing a crew member and leaving three more missing. Nine people are rescued. [src: (Turkiye Today)]
- Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war, Blockade of Oleshky, United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war
- The U.S. government says that Russia and Ukraine reached a humanitarian ceasefire agreement in Oleshky brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump. The ceasefire will take effect on Thursday. [src: (Reuters)]
- Russia and Ukraine confirm the ceasefire agreement for Oleshky, with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy stating that peace talks will begin next month. [src: (The Moscow Times)] [src: (Kyiv Independent)]
- Ukrainian police detain a 17-year-old girl suspected of helping Russia's Federal Security Service send methadone-laced capsules to Ukrainian soldiers, which killed two in Zhytomyr Oblast and allegedly targeting four others. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- Gaza war
- 2026 West Bank lockdown
- Israeli forces launch a multi-day operation around Hebron in the occupied West Bank, conducting searches, questioning suspects, and demolishing structures after Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint. [src: (AFP via Daily Tribune)]
- The Israeli government orders the military to prepare for a complete lockdown of the West Bank. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- 2026 Karak church shooting
- Seven people are killed and 34 others are wounded in a mass shooting during a funeral procession at a Greek Orthodox Church in Hamoud, Karak Governorate, Jordan. All of the gunmen escape from the scene. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (AP)]
- 2026 Trappes and La Verrière shootings
- A person is killed and five other people are injured in a drive-by shooting spree at three separate locations in Trappes and La Verrière, France. A suspect is arrested. The suspected motives behind the shootings are racism and Islamophobia. [src: (BBC News)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Pacific typhoon season
- Typhoon Champi kills a person and injures 163 others in Taiwan as the government evacuates 2,639 people from mountainous areas. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Two Philippine Air Force (PAF) SF-260 aircraft collide during a low-altitude training flight and crash at Basilio Fernando Air Base in Lipa, Batangas, killing all four pilots aboard. The PAF grounds its remaining SF-260 fleet pending investigation. [src: (AP)]
- An 18-storey building under construction collapses in Eastleigh, Nairobi, Kenya, leaving seven people missing and at least one injured. Rescue teams establish contact with some people trapped beneath the rubble. [src: (AFP via The Australian)]
International relations
- Australia–North Korea relations, North Korean remote worker scheme
- The Australian Government imposes financial sanctions and travel bans on two North Koreans and sanctions two companies accused of supporting fraudulent overseas information technology work that funds North Korea's weapons programs. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
Law and crime
- Protesters clash with police in Arunachal Pradesh, India, over the proposed Upper Siang Hydroelectric Project, injuring about 40 officers and damaging a police station, government buildings, and elected representatives' homes. [src: (AFP via Dawn)]
- The Eagle's Nest in Germany is destroyed in a fire. A suspect is arrested. [src: (AP)] [src: (DW)]
Politics and elections
- Online age verification laws by country
- The Greek parliament approves a law banning children and teenagers under 15 from using social media from January 1, 2027, requiring age verification and penalties for platforms that fail to comply. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Sports
- Argentine football player Lionel Messi is awarded the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports for his career at FC Barcelona in Catalonia, Spain. [src: (OneFootball)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 24
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Houthi–Saudi conflict, Yemeni civil war
- Saudi Arabia launches airstrikes against a residential building and a cement factory in Hamdan district, Yemen, killing ten people and wounding many more. [src: (Tempo)]
- Gaza war
- 2026 West Bank lockdown
- The Israeli military raids 15 cities in the occupied West Bank, arresting several Palestinians, forcing over 2,000 from their homes, and destroying a three-storey building in Hebron. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Nigerian bandit conflict
- Unknown gunmen attack a village in Taraba State, Nigeria, killing at least ten people. Locals place the death toll at 20, while Amnesty International claims at least 40. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- 2026 Karak church shooting
- Two people succumb to their injuries sustained the day before during a mass shooting at a Greek Orthodox Church in Karak Governorate, Jordan, bringing the toll to nine killed and 40 injured. [src: (CNN)]
- Unknown gunmen open fire against a group of medics in Bafwasende, Democratic Republic of the Congo, while responding to an Ebola case amid the ongoing emergency, killing a nurse and injuring a health worker. [src: (AP)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Pacific typhoon season
- At least one person is killed and 527 others are injured as Typhoon Champi swept near Taiwan. [src: (DW)]
- Six people are killed and another is injured when a passenger train collides with a minibus in Jewish Autonomous Oblast, Russia. [src: (Reuters)]
- Five people are killed in a fire at the market place of Sorsogon City, Philippines. [src: (PNA)]
- Two people are killed and over 2,000 others are displaced by flooding in Chaco and Corrientes, Argentina. [src: (AA)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Florida A&M University shooting
- Eleven people, including six children, are injured in a mass shooting at Bragg Memorial Stadium at Florida A&M University in Tallahassee, Florida, United States. [src: (CNN)]
- Catholic Church sex abuse cases in the United States
- Survivors of sexual abuse by Catholic clergy reach a settlement with the Archdiocese of New York in the United States, which will see the archdiocese paying at least $250,000 to around 1,300 plaintiffs, totaling over $800 million. [src: (DW)]
- Five people are killed and three more are injured in a suspected gang-related mass shooting at a residence in Lavender Hill, Cape Flats, South Africa. [src: (Smile 90.4FM)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 European unrest
- 2026 French fuel protests
- The Yellow vests hold a second wave of mass demonstrations across France. About 410,000 people participate and over 1,000 people are arrested. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (France 24)]
- About 110,000 protesters march in Paris, France. [src: (France 24)]
- Rioters in Paris attack police with projectiles, but are dispersed with tear gas and water cannons. A gendarmerie helicopter is deployed to locate remaining rioters. [src: (France 24)]
- Party leader Marine Le Pen holds the National Rally congress in Orléans, France. Protesters, including left-wing politicians, marched in opposition. [src: (CBS)] [src: (Euronews)] 
- 2026 Italian unrest
- A new wave of protests is held across Italy. Clashes are reported in Bologna, Turin, Rome and Florence. Protests are also held in Milan, Naples, Padua and Bari. [src: (Rai News)]
- Flamingo Revolution
- Anti-government protests break out in Tirana, Albania. Various government buildings are attacked. [src: (The Guardian)]
- At least 25,000 people gather in Madrid, Spain, in support of the country's state pension fund amid the general election in November. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- A student protest in Barcelona, Spain, ends in riots, looting and clashes with the police, resulting in 128 arrests. [src: (Euronews)]
- 2026 British Columbia general election
- The Conservative Party of British Columbia wins the provincial snap election in Canada, returning to government for the first time in nearly a century and ending nine years of New Democratic Party (NDP) rule. Premier David Eby resigns as NDP leader. [src: (CBC)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Thousands of Israelis rally in Hostages Square in Tel Aviv to protest against the government, prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's cabinet, and the continuation of the Gaza war. [src: (Al Jazeera)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 25
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Houthi–Saudi conflict, Yemeni civil war
- 2026 Houthi attacks on Saudi airports
- Saudi-led coalition air defences intercept a Houthi ballistic missile and two drones targeting Riyadh Province as King Khalid International Airport resumes limited operations after a two-week closure caused by earlier Houthi attacks. [src: (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]
- Gaza war
- Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip
- Three staff members are killed and eight students are wounded in an Israeli airstrike against the Islamic University of Gaza in Gaza City. Four other Palestinians are also killed in more airstrikes in the Gaza Strip. [src: (AFP via Dawn)]
- Colombian conflict
- The Colombian government announces that a military operation in El Tambo, Cauca, in the previous days resulted in the killing of ten National Liberation Army's members, including two key leaders. [src: (AP)]
- Islamist insurgency in Niger, Foreign relations of Algeria, Foreign relations of Niger
- Algeria's parliament approves the deployment of army units to Madama, Niger, to protect energy infrastructure, marking Algeria's first foreign military deployment since 1973. [src: (BBC News)]
Business and economy
- Western Sydney Airport in New South Wales, Australia, commences passenger operations as Greater Sydney's second airport. [src: (The Guardian)]
Disasters and accidents
- Twenty-four people are killed and 24 more are injured after a bus collides with a truck on a highway in Makueni County, Kenya. [src: (AP)]
- Eighty-three people are injured, including seven seriously, in a bus crash in Fogars de Montclús, Catalonia, Spain. [src: (AP)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- The Nigerian health ministry expands contact tracing after confirming an imported Bundibugyo Ebola case in Abuja, identifying at least 44 contacts while investigating additional people who may have been exposed and strengthening infection-control measures. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Brazilian general election
- Brazilians vote in the second round of presidential elections between incumbent left-wing president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of the Workers' Party and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro of the Liberal Party. [src: (AP)] [src: (Reuters)]
- In a vote of 52% to 48%, Lula defeats Bolsonaro to win re-election for a fourth non-consecutive term. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Bulgarian presidential election
- Bulgarians vote in the first round of the presidential election. Incumbent Iliana Iotova wins and will face former acting prime minister Andrey Gyurov in a second round due to record low turnout and no candidate having a majority of the vote. [src: (AP via CNN)] [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Serbian parliamentary election
- Serbians vote for all seats in the National Assembly in a snap election, amid the student-led protests against the incumbent United Serbia government. [src: (AP)]
- The Student List wins the election with 53% of the vote, with former president Aleksandar Vučić conceding defeat. [src: (RFE/RL)] [src: (Reuters)]
- 2027 French presidential election
- French politician Marine Le Pen, leader of the far-right National Rally party, announces her presidential campaign. [src: (Reuters)]
- Crisis in Venezuela
- Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate María Corina Machado announces she has returned to Venezuela from exile. [src: (CNN)]
Sports
- 2026 NASCAR Cup Series
- 2026 YellaWood 500
- In auto racing, American driver Kyle Larson of Hendrick Motorsports wins the YellaWood 500 at the Talladega Superspeedway in Alabama, winning his first NASCAR Cup Series race at the circuit. [src: (ESPN)] 
- 2027 Dakar Rally
- In rally raid, Dakar Rally organizers move the 2027 event from Saudi Arabia because of security concerns regarding the conflict with the Houthis. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- 2026 LPGA Tour
- In golf, Japan's Yuri Yoshida wins her first LPGA Tour title at the BMW Ladies Championship in South Jeolla Province, South Korea, finishing ahead of Australia's Minjee Lee and South Korea's Kim Sei-young. [src: (AFP)]
- International sporting sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
- The International Weightlifting Federation awards Moscow, Russia, the hosting rights to the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships, making it the first IOC-recognised sports federation to grant Russia hosting rights for a world championship since the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine. [src: (AFP via The Straits Times)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 26
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war, Yemeni civil war
- Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war, Saudi Arabia in the 2026 Iran war, Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
- Senior officials representing the members of the Mecca Defence Alliance, including Pakistani military chief Asim Munir, Saudi defense minister Khalid bin Salman Al Saud, and Turkish intelligence director İbrahim Kalın, meet with Iranian leadership, including President Masoud Pezeshkian, in Tehran to discuss efforts to de-escalate the 2026 Iran war and the Yemeni civil war. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (France 24)]
- Gaza war
- Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip
- Israel launches an airstrike against a tent for displaced people in Khan Yunis, Gaza Strip, killing four Palestinians, including a child, and wounding many more. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- The Israel Defense Forces says that they have killed four Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad militants in the Gaza Strip over the weekend. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- Egypt–Saudi Arabia relations, Houthi–Saudi conflict, Yemeni civil war
- 2026 Houthi attacks on Saudi airports
- Egypt's parliament authorizes President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi to provide military support to Saudi Arabia if requested amid Houthi attacks in Saudi territory. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Somali Civil War
- Diplomatic and humanitarian efforts in the Somali Civil War
- The United Nations (UN) announces it will conclude its support for the Transitional Assistance Mission to support the Somali federal government by October 31. The UN will continue supporting Somalia through other smaller agencies. [src: (AA)]
- Sudanese civil war
- War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
- Twenty-one people are killed and 40 more injured in a drone strike in Nyala, Sudan. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- More drone strikes by the Rapid Support Forces are reported across power stations in southeast Sudan, cutting power across the region. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Karak church shooting
- The three gunmen who carried out a mass shooting at a Greek Orthodox Church in Karak Governorate, Jordan, are wounded and arrested after a shootout with security forces at an abandoned building. [src: (BBC News)]
- The Jordanian Armed Forces announces that it has carried out airstrikes against alleged positions of the Islamic State in various areas of Syria's Daraa Governorate and Suwayda Governorate, reporting that the gunmen are linked to the group, claiming the killing of 20 militants. Seven civilians are confirmed killed, including three children and an elderly man. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Internazionale)]
- The Syrian transitional government announces the closure of the Nasib Border Crossing with Jordan, suspending passenger and commercial traffic in both directions, after reporting that the airstrikes were not coordinated. [src: (AA)]
Arts and culture
- Dictionary.com says maxxing has been named its Word of the Year for 2026 following a surge in its use across social media. [src: (BBC News)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026–27 European windstorm season
- Two people are killed and around 90,000 more are left without electricity after the impact of Storm Boelo in Scotland, parts of Northern Ireland, and northern England. [src: (AA)]
Law and crime
- Brazilian police orders senator Flávio Bolsonaro to surrender his passports after Supreme Federal Court justice Alexandre de Moraes barred him from leaving Brazil, one day after Bolsonaro lost the runoff of the general election to incumbent president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. [src: (Firstpost)] [src: (SBS News)]
- A Swiss court convicts former Belarusian security officer Yuri Harauski over the 1999 abduction of businessman Anatol Krasouski, later killed, and gives him a two-year suspended sentence. He is acquitted over Yury Zacharanka's enforced disappearance. [src: (Reuters)]
- The United States Federal Bureau of Investigation announces they have arrested nine people involved in Nigerian scam centers, as part of an international operation targeting organised crime in Nigeria, locating $11 million in funds purloined by the scammers. [src: (OCCRP)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 European unrest
- 2026 Spanish housing protests
- Protests and riots are held in Bilbao, Spain, after and during a political event hosted by far-right commentator Vito Quiles. At least nine people are arrested. [src: (El Constitucional)]
Sports
- 2026 Ballon d'Or
- In association football, English player Harry Kane wins the men's Ballon d'Or for the first time, while Spanish player Alexia Putellas receives the women's award for a record-tying third time. [src: (CNN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 27
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- The Persian Gulf Strait Authority says that vessels belonging to South Korean shipping company Sinokor would face legal action beginning on 1 November. [src: (Reuters)] 
- Gaza war
- Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip
- Three people, including a child, are killed in an Israeli airstrike against a tent in Khan Yunis, Gaza Strip. [src: (AFP via Asharq Al-Awsat)]
- War on drugs
- Colombian conflict
- A bomb explodes near a bridge in Cúcuta, Colombia, at the border with Venezuela, injuring four police officers. [src: (AP)]
- Operation Southern Spear, United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear
- The United States launches an airstrike against an alleged drug boat in the Pacific Ocean, killing five people. [src: (AP)]
- Ethiopian civil conflict, Persecution of Christians in Ethiopia
- The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church reports that at least 60 Christians have been killed in attacks in Oromia, Ethiopia, over the last week. [src: (Reuters)]
- Nigerian bandit conflict
- The casualty toll from the massacre by unknown gunmen four days ago in Taraba State, Nigeria, increases to 62 people killed and 52 more wounded. [src: (AP)]
- Sudanese civil war
- The casualty toll from yesterday's drone strike at a market in Nyala, South Darfur, Sudan, increases to over 100 people killed and 112 more injured. [src: (Reuters)]
Arts and culture
- Eurovision Song Contest 2027
- Netherlands in the Eurovision Song Contest 2027
- Netherlands Public Broadcasting (NPO) withdraws the Netherlands from the 2027 Eurovision Song Contest over concerns about Israel's participation, after AVROTROS withdrew in August and NPO failed to find another broadcaster. [src: (AP)]
Business and economy
- 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
- Villa Vie Residences suspends operations of the Odyssey in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, after running out of money amid sharply higher fuel costs, forcing 203 passengers to disembark with seven hours' notice. [src: (AFP)]
- AI bubble
- China's Shanghai Stock Exchange STAR Market index, which focuses on science and technology companies, plummets 40% in less than four months. [src: (Reuters)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 North Indian Ocean cyclone season
- Indian authorities order nearly 100,000 people to evacuate parts of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha as Cyclone Arnab approaches, with the India Meteorological Department forecasting landfall as a very severe cyclonic storm. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- Four people are killed, two are missing and several homes are destroyed during floods in Haiti and the Dominican Republic. [src: (AP)]
- A construction site is hit by a tornado in Kepez, Antalya, Turkey, killing four workers and injuring another. [src: (AP)]
Health and environment
- 2025 in climate change
- The World Meteorological Organization reports that global concentrations of carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide reached record highs in 2025, with carbon dioxide averaging 426.8 parts per million. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Law and crime
- Crime in El Salvador
- A Salvadoran court issues an order to release former president Antonio Saca from prison after the end of his 10-year sentence for corruption. [src: (La Prensa Gráfica )]
- Gaza war protests at Columbia University
- Algerian-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil returns to Columbia University in New York City, United States, after immigration authorities detained him for more than three months over his role in pro-Palestinian campus protests before a federal judge ordered his release. [src: (AFP)]
- Immigration to Nigeria
- Nigerian police arrest 34 foreigners, including 16 Cameroonians and 18 Nigeriens, suspected of engaging in "illicit activities" in Benue State. The commissioner opens an investigation into their immigration status. [src: (Daily Trust)]
- Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro leaves Brazil for the United States, despite orders to surrender his passports to the Federal Police, two days after his defeat in the presidential election runoffs to incumbent president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The government subsequently cancels Bolsonaro's passports, while the U.S. grants him and his family visas. [src: (AFP)] [src: (Reuters)]
- An Egyptian court orders independent news website Mada Masr to close after convicting editor-in-chief Lina Attalah of operating without a licence. The court also fines her E£3,000,000 (US$53,500) and orders the outlet's equipment confiscated. [src: (DW)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 French fuel protests, 2026 French student protests
- The French Senate passes a bill that would make people who knowingly participate in violent protest groups jointly liable for up to €10,000 (US$11,118) in damage and allow authorities to seize certain welfare payments. The bill heads to the National Assembly for a vote. [src: (AFP via The Straits Times)]
- 2026 Israeli legislative election
- Israelis vote to elect the 120 members of the Knesset. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Reuters)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 3
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Iraq's Oil Tankers Company says that they have transported 2 million barrels of oil from the country through a very large crude carrier in the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (Reuters)]
- Gaza war
- Five people are killed and several more are injured in an Israeli airstrike against a residential building in Gaza City in the Gaza Strip, in violation of the ongoing ceasefire. Three other Palestinians are also killed in more airstrikes. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- The Israel Defense Forces says that they have targeted de facto Hamas leader Ali al-Amoudi in a airstrike, and acknowledge that the results of the strike are under review. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
- Unknown gunmen open fire against a vehicle in Ras al-Maara, Syria, killing three people and wounding seven more. [src: (Hawar News Agency)]
- Ethiopian civil conflict
- 2026 Ethiopian offensive
- Ethiopian federal forces retake control of the Alula Aba Nega Airport in Mekelle, Tigray, from the Tigray People's Liberation Front. [src: (Los Angeles Times)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
- Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko reports that Russian forces have struck the Pivnichnyi Bridge in Kyiv, Ukraine. [src: (Kyiv Independent)]
Arts and culture
- The remains of Samuil, the former Bulgarian tsar during the First Bulgarian Empire who died in 1014, return to Bulgaria following decades of negotiation with Greece. [src: (AP)] [src: (Orthodox Times)]
Disasters and accidents
- Seventeen people are killed and many more injured during the collision of multiple vehicles on a highway in Mombasa, Kenya. Most of the fatalities are Roman Catholic pilgrims traveling on a van. [src: (AP)]
- Five workers are killed and ten more are rescued after the collapse of a gold mine in Chah Ab District, Takhar Province, Afghanistan. [src: (AP)]
- Ten people are injured, including some critically, in a motor vehicle hooning accident in Newcastle, Australia, during a Newcastle Knights procession before the NRL Grand Final. The driver is arrested at the scene. [src: (DW)] [src: (Nine News)]
- A Latitude Air Ambulance Gulfstream G100, flying from St. David's Island, Bermuda, to Boston, United States, goes missing over the Atlantic Ocean with six people on board, including four Canadian crew and two Bermudian passengers. [src: (News 18)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Latvian parliamentary election
- Latvians vote to elect 100 seats of the Saeima amid an uptick of airspace incursions and hybrid warfare during the Russo-Ukrainian war. Preliminary results indicate that the centrist United List, led by incumbent prime minister Andris Kulbergs, won the most seats. [src: (Reuters)]
Science and technology
- Scientists identify a new lizard species, Liolaemus archipensis, in Arequipa, Peru. [src: (AFP via Gulf News)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 4
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Ethiopian civil conflict
- 2026 Ethiopian offensive
- Ethiopian forces capture Mekelle, the capital of the Tigray Region, after the withdrawal of the Tigray People's Liberation Front. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- A drone strikes a displacement camp in Sheraro, Tigray Region, killing at least eight people, including a child, and seriously injuring six others. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Sudanese civil war
- War crimes in the Sudanese civil war, Kordofan campaign
- The World Food Programme reports an airstrike on a United Nations truck in South Kordofan, Sudan, that killed the driver. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- War on cartels
- United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear
- Four people are killed in an American airstrike against an alleged drug boat in the Caribbean Sea. [src: (AP)]
- Yemeni civil war
- 2026 Yemen offensives
- The Houthis take control of Al-Turbah, Yemen, after government troops withdrew earlier in the day. This is the first time the Houthis have held Al-Turbah since the war began. [src: (Yemen Online)] [src: (AP)]
Disasters and accidents
- The United States Coast Guard suspends the search for the Latitude Air Ambulance Gulfstream G100 aircraft that went missing yesterday with six passengers on board after finding a debris field in the ocean south of Nantucket, Massachussetts. All six passengers, including four Canadian pilots and crew and two Bermudian passengers, are presumed dead. [src: (CBC)] [src: (Winnipeg City News)]
Health and environment
- A lab worker in Russia's Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute in Shelekhov, Irkutsk Oblast, Siberia, dies from a pneumonic plague caused by Yersinia pestis, with nearly 200 workers in quarantine. [src: (EuroWeekly News)] [src: (Kyiv Independent)]
International relations
- Nicaragua announces its immediate withdrawal from the Central American Parliament after the Organization of American States approved a resolution on Friday calling for Nicaragua to release political prisoners and restore civil liberties. [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Vienna, Georgia, shooting
- Two people are killed and at least 35 are injured in a mass shooting during a homecoming block party in Vienna, Georgia, United States. [src: (AP)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- Chinese espionage in the United States
- The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation arrests a 34-year-old Chinese American woman at Los Angeles International Airport in California for allegedly acting as an unregistered Chinese agent and surveilling Taiwanese president Lai Ching-te's son and family in the United States. [src: (AFP via RFI)] [src: (The Daily Telegraph)]
- Two people are killed and another is injured in a mass shooting at a hunting party in Halden, Norway. The perpetrator is arrested. [src: (AP)]
- An American Marine stationed at Marine Corps Air Station Futenma in Ginowan, Okinawa Prefecture, Japan, is arrested by Okinawa prefectural police in connection with the alleged robbery and murder of a local woman in Naha. Japanese foreign minister Toshimitsu Motegi summons U.S. ambassador to Japan George Edward Glass regarding the incident. [src: (NPR)]
- Three students are arrested for the murder of a 16-year-old classmate in Yong Peng, Johor, Malaysia. [src: (The Straits Times)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Bosnian general election
- Bosnians vote to elect the three members of the presidency and 42 members of the House of Representatives. Concurrent elections are also held in the Federation to elect 98 seats of the regional legislature and in Republika Srpska to elect the entity's president and the 83 seats of the respective legislature. [src: (AFP)]
- 2026 Brazilian general election
- Brazilians head to the polls to elect their president, vice president, 513 members of Chamber of Deputies and 54 members in the Federal Senate. Incumbent president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is running for the fourth non-consecutive term, where his main opponent is Rio de Janeiro senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. [src: (The Guardian)]
- Flávio Bolsonaro wins the first round and will face Lula da Silva in a runoff on 25 October. [src: (AP)]
Sports
- 2034 FIFA World Cup
- It is reported that Saudi Arabia has cancelled plans for the proposed NEOM Stadium in The Line, Neom, for the upcoming 2034 FIFA World Cup in the country. [src: (Middle East Eye)] [src: (Reuters)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 5
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Yemeni civil war
- 2026 Yemen offensives, Operation Dawn of Yemen
- The Presidential Leadership Council launches a large-scale military operation against Houthis in Yemen, with the aim to capture all Houthi-controlled territories. [src: (Al Arabiya)] [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (TRT World)]
- Turkey and Pakistan agree to deploy troops under the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement to help Saudi and Yemeni forces against the Houthis. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- A Yemeni government offensive pushes the Houthis back from the Bab al-Mandab Strait. [src: (Reuters)]
Business and economy
- 2026 Brazilian general election
- Brazil's benchmark Ibovespa index rises nearly 9% to almost 210,000 points after the first round of the presidential election, surpassing 200,000 points for the first time. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Russian president Vladimir Putin approves the restructuring of UniCredit Bank Russia and the subsequent sale of most of the business to a United Arab Emirates-based private investor, while UniCredit retains its payments operations. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Reuters)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Nigerian Air Force ATR 42 crash
- A Nigerian Air Force ATR 42-500 aircraft crashes in Ondo State, Nigeria, killing all 25 people on board. [src: (DW)] [src: (Reuters)]
- The toll from yesterday's collision between two ships in the Congo River near Lukolela, Democratic Republic of the Congo, increases to 30 people killed and dozens missing. [src: (AP)]
International relations
- United Kingdom–United States relations
- 2026 RAF Fairford arrests
- The United States Air Force withdraws all of its B-1 Lancer strategic bombers from RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, England. The U.S. Department of Defense confirms the bombers have returned to bases in the United States. [src: (BBC News)]
Law and crime
- International Criminal Court investigation in Afghanistan
- The International Criminal Court unseals arrest warrants for Taliban education minister Habibullah Agha and higher education minister Neda Mohammad Nadeem, accusing them of the crime against humanity of gender-based persecution in Afghanistan. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Protesters clash with police in Pristina, Kosovo, after parliament fails to advance legislation limiting the Kosovo Specialist Chambers' powers. One police officer and 11 civilians are injured. [src: (AP)]
Politics and elections
- 2025–2026 Kosovo political deadlock
- In Kosovo, the acting presidency of Albulena Haxhiu becomes de facto due to her having continuously served in the position for more than six months since assuming office on 4 April, violating the third paragraph of Article 90 in the constitution. The Kuvendi has two days left until the presidential election deadline by the Constitutional Court expires. [src: (Kosovo Online)] [src: (RKS)]
- 2026 Quebec general election
- Voters in Quebec, Canada, elect members to the National Assembly. [src: (CBC)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- The Parti Québécois is elected into a minority government while the ruling Coalition Avenir Québec face an electoral wipeout. [src: (CBC)]
- 2026 Romanian political crisis
- Romanian president Nicușor Dan designates diplomat Luca Niculescu to form a government. Niculescu's choice is the fourth attempt by Dan to appoint a Prime Minister to succeed Ilie Bolojan, who lost a no-confidence vote last May. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Spanish general election, 2026 Spanish housing protests
- Spanish prime minister Pedro Sánchez calls a snap general election for 29 November after Parliament voted down two emergency housing decrees that would have restricted evictions, frozen rents, and blocked vulture-fund property buys. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (Reuters)]
- The President of Iran, Masoud Pezeshkian, nominates Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi to the post of Defense Minister. [src: (Gulf News)]
- The National Assembly of Laos approves deputy prime minister Saleumxay Kommasith as the new Prime Minister, succeeding Sonexay Siphandone, who became National Assembly president. [src: (The Laotian Times)]
- The House of Peoples' Representatives of Ethiopia reelects Abiy Ahmed as Prime Minister. [src: (Anadolu Agency)]
Science and technology
- American scientist Karl Deisseroth of Stanford University, and German biophysicists Peter Hegemann of Humboldt University and Georg Nagel of the University of Würzburg are jointly awarded the Nobel Prize in Medicine for "their discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics". [src: (Reuters)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 6
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Yemen offensives
- 2026 Houthi attacks on Saudi airports
- The Houthis launches missiles against the airports of Najran and Jizan, in Saudi Arabia, causing material damages and wounding three people. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Gaza war
- Israeli defense minister Israel Katz says that the military has killed 4,000 militants who took part in the Hamas-led attacks on Israel on October 7, 2023. [src: (The Jewish Chronicle)]
- Somali Civil War
- Piracy off the coast of Somalia
- Four Indonesian seamen return home after Puntland maritime police rescued 17 crew members from the hijacked oil tanker MT Honour 25. Somali pirates had held the crew for more than five months and killed five members. [src: (AFP)]
- Peruvian security crisis
- Three gunmen and a police officer are killed, and another officer is wounded, in a shootout during an operation against illegal miners in Inambari District, Tambopata province, Madre de Dios, Peru. Authorities seize 15 AKM rifles, a pistol, and five grenades. [src: (Evidencia de Perú )] [src: (Infobae )]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Two merchant ships are hit by drones of unknown origins off the coast of Bulgaria. One of the ships has sunk, leaving the crew missing. [src: (Reuters)]
- Boko Haram insurgency
- At least ten soldiers are killed by Islamic State gunmen during an attack at a military base in Kukawa, Borno State, Nigeria. Over 25 attackers are also killed in the shootout. [src: (AP)]
Business and economy
- Acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance
- The merger between American media conglomerates Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery into Skydance takes effect. [src: (AFP)] [src: (CNN)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- Kenya confirms its first imported case of the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebolavirus in Nairobi in a deceased male who traveled from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. [src: (Reuters)]
- The Nairobi Hospital steps up its infection-control measures, tracing, and staff monitoring following Kenya's first imported case of Ebola. [src: (The Star Kenya)]
- Deforestation in Indonesia
- Indonesia halts a program to clear millions of hectares of forest for rice cultivation after achieving rice self-sufficiency, and plans instead to increase yields on existing farmland through improved agricultural methods. [src: (AFP via CNA)]
Law and crime
- 2026 European unrest
- Riots break out in Liège, Belgium, following a day of student protests, resulting in damaged shops and destroyed bus shelters in the city center. [src: (AA)] [src: (Le Soir )]
- August Hanning espionage case
- August Hanning, former head of Germany's Federal Intelligence Service, is arrested at his home in Nordwalde, North Rhine-Westphalia, after being charged by the country's Federal Public Prosecutor General with treason, espionage, and trading state secrets. A former aide of Hanning's is also arrested for aiding and abetting attempted treason and treasonous espionage. [src: (AP)] [src: (DW)]
- A student is killed and seven others are injured in a mass stabbing at a middle school in Istanbul, Turkey. The suspect, a 15-year-old girl, is arrested. [src: (Turkiye Today)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Haitian general election, Haitian crisis
- Haiti's Provisional Electoral Council postpones presidential and legislative elections scheduled for December 13, citing technical, operational, and security requirements. [src: (AFP)]
- 2026 Kosovan presidential election
- The Kuvendi begins the procedure to elect a president on 6 October, finishing the voting process minutes after the constitutional deadline on midnight 7 October. Justina Pula is declared the next president of Kosovo. [src: (AFP via Gulf News)] [src: (Kosovo Online)]
- 2026 Latvian parliamentary election 
- Latvian president Edgars Rinkēvičs asks Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs to form the new Government. Kulbergs' party, the United List, won the plurality in the October 3 parliamentary elections. [src: (LSM)]
Science and technology
- OpenAI bulk release of mathematical papers
- OpenAI releases 377 results on open problems in mathematics in areas such as algebra, number theory, combinatorics and theoretical computer science. [src: (The New York Times)]
- 2026 Nobel Prizes
- Belgian physicist Francis Halzen from the University of Wisconsin–Madison is awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for his "decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin". [src: (CNN)]
- 2026 in archosaur paleontology
- The Royal Society Open Science reports the discovery of the Herugavialis cairensis crocodile species in the Mokattam Formation, which had also provided the rock to build the Great Sphinx in Egypt. [src: (CNN)] [src: (Phys.org)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 7
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Yemen offensives
- October 2026 attacks on Saudi Arabia airports
- Houthi forces claim attacks on Abha International Airport and Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia that killed three civilians and injured 36 others since yesterday. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Israeli settler violence
- Israeli settlers launch an attack in the occupied West Bank targeting Palestinians, killing a man and wounding 16 other people. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Ethiopian civil conflict
- 2026 Ethiopian offensive
- 2026 Eritrean incursion into Ethiopia
- Eritrean forces are reported to have invaded Ethiopia's Tigray Region and are moving south toward Mekelle. [src: (Addis Standard)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russian forces launch a massive ballistic missile and drone attack on Ukraine, killing at least 28 people, including 20 people killed at a single apartment hit by a North Korean KN-23 missile in Pryluky, Chernihiv Oblast, while hundreds more are wounded. [src: (The Guardian)]
- Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Bulgaria halts the search for the 12 Syrian sailors missing since yesterday after a merchant ship sank after being hit by a drone strike in its waters. The perpetrators are still unknown. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Mali War
- 2026 Mali offensives
- The Malian Armed Forces and the Russian Africa Corps retake Kidal, which was captured by the Azawad Liberation Front five months ago, after days of airstrikes and ground operations. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Sudanese civil war
- War crimes in the Sudanese civil war, 2026 Blue Nile campaign
- Four women are killed in a Rapid Support Forces drone strike on homes and a mosque in Ad-Damazin, Blue Nile State, Sudan. [src: (The Washington Post)] [src: (AP)]
Business and economy
- Guinea sets nationwide price ceilings for bottled water after a ban on single-use plastic water sachets causes shortages and higher prices, with retail packs of several bottle sizes capped at 25,000 francs (US$2.84). [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- The Reserve Bank of India raises its benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5%, its first increase since February 2023. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
- Hurricane Isaias
- Tropical cyclone Isaias strengthens into a category 1 hurricane, becoming the first Atlantic hurricane of the season amidst a unusually quiet season caused by the ongoing El Niño phenomenon. [src: (AP)]
- In the United States, Alabama governor Kay Ivey declares a state of emergency for 40 counties ahead of Isaias. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (WVUA-CD)]
Health and environment
- Climate change in Antarctica
- The British Antarctic Survey reports that Zavodovski Island in Antarctica has lost more than 500,000 chinstrap penguins since 2011, ending its status as the world's largest penguin colony as warming waters reduce access to Antarctic krill. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Climate change in Australia, Mining in Australia
- Australia's High Court rejects MACH Energy's appeal to expand the Mount Pleasant coal mine in New South Wales, finding that planning authorities failed to adequately consider greenhouse gas emissions from burning exported coal overseas. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Law and crime
- Elections in Mexico
- Mexican president Claudia Sheinbaum sanctions a constitutional amendment prohibiting Mexicans with dual citizenship from running for president or governor. [src: (AA)] [src: (El Economista in Spanish)]
- Spillover of the 2026 French lycée protests
- For a second consecutive day, riots occur in Liège, Belgium, following earlier student protests, prompting authorities to close the Guillemins railway station and urge local businesses to shut down. Over 100 people are arrested. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (RTBF in French)]
- Libor scandal
- The Court of Appeal in London, United Kingdom, quashes the convictions of five former Barclays traders for manipulating Libor and Euribor, following a 2025 Supreme Court ruling that found legal errors had made similar convictions unsafe. [src: (AFP)]
- 2026 Poland school stabbings
- Nine people are injured in a mass stabbing at a high school in Ostrołęka, Poland. The suspect, a 19-year-old student, is arrested after being injured himself. [src: (Reuters)]
Science and technology
- 2026 Nobel Prizes
- French chemist Henri B. Kagan from the Paris-Saclay University and Japanese organic chemist Kensō Soai from the Tokyo University of Science are jointly awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for "the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis". [src: (Reuters)]
- The Seychelles Islands Foundation (SIF) and University of Exeter in West Country, England, reports that approximately 180,000 Aldabrachelys gigantea tortoises are living on the islands of Seychelles. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (University of Exeter News)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 8
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 United States military buildup in the Middle East
- The returns to San Diego, California, U.S., at the North Island Naval Air Station following its nearly seven-month deployment in the Middle East. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (Los Angeles Times)]
- U.S. president Donald Trump says that the U.S. military will not attack Iran before the midterm elections next month. [src: (AP)]
- Gaza war
- Gaza war hostage crisis
- The Israel Defense Forces announce that they have killed Muhammad Muhsen Nimr Yazji, a Hamas militant who took part in holding Emily Damari, Romi Gonen, and Matan Angrest during an airstrike in Gaza City. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russian forces launch a ballistic missile attack on two buses in the city of Kramatorsk in Ukraine, killing at least 30 people, while 18 others are wounded. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Mexican drug war
- Infighting in the Sinaloa Cartel
- Twelve people, including a 2-year-old, are killed and 16 more injured during a shootout between different factions of the Sinaloa Cartel at El Castillo Penitentiary Centre in Mazatlán, Sinaloa, Mexico. The incident is believed to have been an assassination attempt on Eduardo Jonathan Martínez Larios, a leader of Los Chapitos who was reportedly amongst the dead. [src: (Mexico News Daily)]
Arts and culture
- 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
- Canadian poet Anne Carson is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for "her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms ‌for contemporary literature". [src: (BBC News)]
- The Bank of England announces that the Atlantic puffin, barn owl, buff-tailed bumblebee, and European hedgehog will feature on the next set of pound sterling notes to be issued in the United Kingdom. It will be the first time animals have replaced people on banknotes in England, which is intended to increase awareness of British wildlife. [src: (BBC News)]
Business and economy
- AI boom, Semiconductor industry in Taiwan
- The Taiwanese finance ministry reports that exports reached a record US$87.2 billion in September, while imports rose to a record $63.6 billion and the trade surplus reached a record $23.6 billion, citing demand for artificial intelligence-related hardware. [src: (AFP)] [src: (Reuters)]
- The Hungarian newspaper Népszabadság, which was shut down in 2016 during the government of former prime minister Viktor Orbán, relaunches as an online news site. [src: (Reuters)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
- Hurricane Isaias
- In the United States, Georgia governor Brian Kemp declares a state of emergency ahead of Hurricane Isaias. [src: (Fox 5 Atlanta)]
- Hurricane Isaias strengthens into a category 2 Atlantic hurricane. [src: (AP)]
- Severe rainfall in Chile, particularly in Santiago, causes flooding, river overflowing, mudslides, and power outages, killing one person, injuring six others and damaging over 2,000 homes. [src: (NBC News)]
International relations
- South Korea–Ukraine relations, North Korean involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian war
- South Korea recalls its ambassador to Ukraine after accusing Ukraine of breaching a non-disclosure agreement by disclosing the transfer of two captured North Korean soldiers to South Korea. [src: (AFP via The Straits Times)]
Law and crime
- 2009 Fort Hood shooting, Capital punishment in the United States
- United States secretary of defense Pete Hegseth announces the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan, the perpetrator of the 2009 Fort Hood shooting, will be publicly broadcast. [src: (AFP via RFI)] [src: (CNN)]
- 2026 Poland school stabbings
- A 15-year-old student carries out a mass stabbing against staff members at a primary school in the village of Leszczydół-Nowiny, Wyszków County, Poland, killing one person and injuring two more. The suspect is taken into police custody. [src: (Reuters)]
- Relationship of Prince Andrew and Jeffrey Epstein
- High Court judge Nicholas Hilliard of England and Wales quashes search warrants used on Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes, finding errors in Thames Valley Police's applications and issuing judge Mark Lucraft's consideration of legally protected material. [src: (AP)]
Politics and elections
- Next Guinea-Bissau general election
- The Government of Guinea-Bissau announces that presidential and parliamentary elections scheduled for December 6 will be delayed. [src: (Reuters)]
Sports
- 2026 Nippon Professional Baseball season
- In baseball, Teruaki Satō of the Hanshin Tigers wins the Triple Crown. [src: (Kyodo News)]
- 2026 WNBA season
- In women's basketball, Las Vegas Aces center A'ja Wilson wins a record fifth WNBA Most Valuable Player, becoming the first player in league history to win the award for three years in a row. [src: (ESPN)]
- Swiss and Sunderland A.F.C. footballer Granit Xhaka receives a two-year probation after admitting to obtaining a fake COVID-19 vaccination certificate during the COVID-19 pandemic. [src: (ESPN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 October 9
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- 2026 Iran war
- Casualties of the 2026 Iran war
- The Pentagon raises the U.S. military death toll in the Iran war to 21 after reporting two noncombat deaths. [src: (The Hill)]
- Sudanese civil war
- War crimes in the Sudanese civil war, 2026 Blue Nile campaign
- An RSF drone strike in Blue Nile State, Sudan, kills 41 displaced people. [src: (AP)]
Disasters and accidents
- Tropical cyclones in 2026
- 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
- Hurricane Isaias
- Isaias strengthens into a category 3 Atlantic hurricane. It would later weaken to category 2, with 365,000 people in Alabama and Florida, United States, reported to be without power ahead of its landfall. [src: (AP)] [src: (MS Now)]
- Isaias makes landfall near Destin, Florida, and weakens to a category 1 hurricane. [src: (AP)] [src: (Reuters via The Straits Times)]
- 2026 Pacific hurricane season
- Hurricane Rachel
- Flooding is reported in areas of Southern California, U.S., including Long Beach and Newport Beach, and the National Hurricane Center issues a tropical storm warning for the area. The warning is the first issued for San Diego County, California, since 2023 during Hurricane Hilary. [src: (Los Angeles Times)] [src: (KTLA)] [src: (KNSD)]
- Hurricane Simon
- Simon strengthens into a category 2 Pacific hurricane. [src: (AP)]
- 2026 Panama earthquake
- A magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes Herrera Province, Panama. A nationwide tsunami warning is issued. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (USA Today)]
- A passenger bus collides with a truck on a road in Mkambarani, Morogoro Region, Tanzania, and catches fire, killing 28 people. [src: (AP)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak
- Eight more children in Bangladesh are reported to be killed from measles, bringing the death toll past 1,155. [src: (BSS)]
- South Africa declares the Grassland National Park, which covers 10,225.9242 hectares across 18 properties, as a national park. [src: (Cape Town ETC)] [src: (WWF)]
International relations
- Montenegro–Russia relations
- Montenegro expels Russian military blogger Mikhail Zvinchuk and four other Russian nationals on national security grounds after detaining them in Risan. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- United States and the International Criminal Court
- The U.S. issues sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC) after its former judge Navi Pillay won the Nobel Peace Prize, freezing assets held by the ICC in the U.S. and limiting U.S. companies from conducting transactions with them. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Musée Renoir theft
- Six people suspected of stealing Pierre-Auguste Renoir's paintings Young Woman at the Well and Madame Colonna Romano from the Musée Renoir in Cagnes-sur-Mer, Alpes-Maritimes, France, are arrested, and the artworks are recovered. [src: (AP)] [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
- South African judge and former United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Navi Pillay is awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for "her efforts to promote peace and international law". [src: (DW)] 
- Shootings by U.S. immigration agents in the second Trump administration
- Clashes erupt in New York City, United States, between protestors and police after the shooting of a Dominican Republic national with a criminal conviction by ICE agents. The man, who was in a car alongside a child, was then detained while being wounded. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- 2026 Erie shooting
- Eight people are killed, including the perpetrator, in a mass shooting at a home in Erie, Pennsylvania, United States. [src: (AP)] [src: (BBC News)]
- The Supreme Federal Court of Brazil issues an arrest warrant for Eduardo Bolsonaro, the brother of presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, on charges of lobbying the U.S. to interfere in the trial of his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- A man armed with a knife takes 13 children and staff members hostage at a school in Curitiba, Paraná, Brazil, and threatens to set it on fire, before being shot dead by police. The hostages are rescued, with two children sustaining injuries. [src: (AP)]
Politics and elections
- Next Palestinian legislative election
- Palestinian vice president Hussein al-Sheikh announces that the Palestinian legislative election planned for November 28 will be postponed, possibly until September 2027, along with the also delayed presidential election, because of worsening conditions throughout Palestine. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Czech Senate election, 2026 Czech municipal elections
- Czechs begin voting in the first round to elect one-third of the Senate. Incumbent prime minister Andrej Babiš seeks gains of his coalition in the Senate. Municipal elections are also underway. [src: (AP)]
- The Mauritanian government of Prime Minister Moctar Ould Diay resigns over power outages. However, President Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani reappoints Diay, asking him to form a new government. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- Pope Leo XIV approves Filipino cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle's election as dean of the College of Cardinals, making him the first Asian to lead the body that elects a new pope. [src: (Reuters)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 1
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- September 2026 United States strikes on Iran
- The United States carries out additional airstrikes against Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corp (IRGC) targets in Iran, in response to recent attempted attacks on commercial shipping vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and on U.S. troops in the region, according to the U.S. Central Command. Five members of the IRGC Aerospace Force are killed in Kermanshah. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (BBC News)] [src: (CNN)]
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian says that his country is ready to return to the Islamabad Memorandum signed in June if the United States does the same amidst renewed fighting between the two countries. [src: (Fortune)]
- 2026 Kuhestak wedding airstrike
- Iranian state media reports that five civilians were killed and 63 more were wounded at a wedding party at a home in Kuhestak, Hormozgan province, during an American airstrike against Iranian military targets. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Gaza war
- Four people are killed in Israeli strikes during a ground operation in Gaza. Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu says that Israeli forces captured a senior Hamas internal security official in the operation. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- War against the Islamic State, Yemeni Civil War
- Abu Hudhayfah al-Ansari, the spokesperson for the Islamic State, is killed during a security operation by the Yemeni Armed Forces. [src: (Voice of Emirates)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war, Kyiv strikes
- Ukrainian officials say that Russian missile and drone attacks on Kyiv and surrounding areas killed at least 12 people, including an Indian national, and injure dozens, while damaging residential buildings and other civilian infrastructure. [src: (NDTV)]
- Colombian conflict
- A car bomb explodes outside a police station in Norte de Santander Department, Colombia, killing a person and wounding eleven more. [src: (Reuters)]
Arts and culture
- The 75,000-seater Kingdome, built by the Christian sect Kingdom of Jesus Christ, opens in Davao City, Philippines, becoming the largest indoor arena in the world. It surpasses the 55,000-seater Philippine Arena in Bulacan. [src: (Manila Bulletin)] [src: (MindaNews)]
Business and economy
- Senegal hidden debt scandal
- The International Monetary Fund reaches a staff-level agreement with Senegal on a new US$2.2 billion, 36-month loan program supporting economic reforms after an earlier arrangement was suspended over previously unreported government debt. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Ghana begins requiring artisanal doré bars purchased by privately financed gold buyers to undergo domestic refining before export, with GoldBod considering export applications only after processing at approved refineries. [src: (Reuters)]
- Japan eases overtime enforcement by ending pressure on companies with special labor-management agreements to keep monthly overtime below 45 hours, as businesses face labor shortages. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Nepal–Tibet floods
- Nepal–South Korea relations
- South Korea's foreign ​ministry announces that the country will deploy a 44-member emergency relief team to Nepal to support search-and-rescue operations after flash floods hit the South Asian country. [src: (The Korea Herald)] [src: (Reuters)]
- The Nepali Army reports that around 119 people have been rescued. [src: (The Guardian)]
- 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
- Tropical Storm Edouard makes landfall on the Gulf Coast of the United States. [src: (CNN)]
- Seven people are killed and 13 others are injured when a speeding passenger van, with an Ipil–Pagadian route, crashes into a motorcycle and a wing van in Dumalinao, Zamboanga del Sur, Philippines. [src: (Philippine Daily Inquirer)]
- Four people are killed and more than ten others are injured when a car crashes into a gathering of government and military supporters in Mashhad, Razavi Khorasan, Iran. Traffic police arrest the driver and say the incident was unintentional. [src: (Reuters)]
- Six pilgrims are killed and 14 others sustain serious injuries after a pickup truck carrying devotees collides with a truck along an expressway in Palwal district, Haryana, India. [src: (The Times of India)]
Health and environment
- The New Zealand Conservation Department reports that the amount of critically endangered kākāpō have reached 325 in the country following the addition of 90 chicks, exceeding 300 for the first time in 75 years. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (NBC News)]
International relations
- Germany–Russia relations, Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- 2026 Leipzig Airport drone incidents
- Germany raises its threat assessment to "high", orders the closure of Russia's consulate in Bonn, North Rhine-Westphalia, and the Russian House in Berlin, and tightens entry controls for Russian nationals after attributing the drone attacks at Leipzig/Halle Airport, Saxony, last month to Russia. [src: (CNN)]
- Reactions to the 2026 Iran war
- Peru's foreign ministry says that the country has cut off ties with Iran, accusing it of escalating the war in the Middle East. [src: (AP in Spanish)] [src: (Al-Arabiya)]
Law and crime
- Assassination of Charlie Kirk
- An American judge rules that the case against Tyler James Robinson, accused of murdering political activist Charlie Kirk in September 2025, can go to trial, citing sufficient probable cause. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (CNN)]
- LGBTQ rights in the United States
- The U.S. Department of Justice files a lawsuit against the public schools district of Kansas City, Kansas, over its policies that allow transgender students to share their preferred name, gender, and pronouns with school staff. [src: (KCUR)] [src: (Reuters)]
- A Honduran judge dismisses a corruption case against former president Juan Orlando Hernández, ruling that he neither authorized nor managed the public funds allegedly diverted to finance his 2013 presidential campaign. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Mexican musician Jonathan Meléndez of the band Camilo Séptimo, his pregnant wife, their three-year-old daughter, a domestic worker, and their pet dog are shot dead in a penthouse outside Mexico City, while Meléndez's six-year-old son is found unharmed. Prosecutors arrest two suspects. [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- Death and state funeral of Harald V
- Haakon VIII takes the oath as King of Norway before the Storting following the death of his father, Harald V. His daughter, Ingrid Alexandra, takes the oath as Crown Princess. [src: (AP)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Nicaragua's National Assembly approves on first reading a constitutional amendment barring opposition parties from elections and extending presidential and other elected terms from six to seven years. A second legislative vote is required for ratification. [src: (Reuters)]
- Former British prime minister Keir Starmer resigns as a member of the House of Commons for his appointment to the Chiltern Hundreds; a by-election will be held to fill his parlimentary seat of Holborn and St Pancras. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (BBC News)]
Science and technology
- Syria and weapons of mass destruction
- The International Atomic Energy Agency reports that Syria's former government under Bashar al-Assad failed to declare nuclear material and facilities, confirming that infrastructure at Deir ez-Zor is consistent with an unfinished nuclear reactor and identifying about 73 tonnes of natural uranium. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- The Turkish foreign ministry reports that Turkey has joined the U.S.-led Artemis Accords, becoming the 71st country to do so. [src: (AA)] [src: (Firstpost)]
Sports
- 2026–27 NBA season
- In basketball, the NBA announces that the Los Angeles Clippers had violated the league salary cap by signing Kawhi Leonard in 2022 via a series of external dealings. Penalties include fines of US$30 million for the Clippers and $700,000 for Leonard, the loss of the Clippers' first-round picks in each draft from 2029 to 2033, and a one-year suspension for Clippers owner Steve Ballmer. [src: (AFP via Daily Tribune)] [src: (ESPN)]
- In baseball, the Los Angeles Angels of the MLB are sold to Stan Kroenke of Kroenke Sports & Entertainment for an unspecified price, ending 23 years of ownership by Arte Moreno. The deal is pending regulatory review and is expected to be complete by 2027. [src: (CNBC)] [src: (Reuters)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 10
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Gaza war
- Aftermath of the Second Intifada
