- The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) and Shin Bet confirm that they have killed Hamas senior leader Farah Hamed, a senior member who was accused of carrying out the 2003 attack that resulted in the killing of , the late husband of Limor Son Har-Melech, in a airstrike in the Gaza Strip. [src: (Israel National News)] [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- Israeli airstrikes on the Gaza Strip kill a family of four. [src: (Reuters)]
- Hezbollah–Israel conflict
- 2026 Lebanon war
- Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and defense minister Israel Katz say that the IDF has destroyed a Hezbollah tunnel in Ali al-Taher. [src: (The Financial Times)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- The United States Geological Survey reports that a magnitude 4.1 earthquake has been detected after Israel carried out the strike in Ali al-Taher. [src: (Sky News)]
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 East–West Crude Oil Pipeline attack, Iraq in the 2026 Iran war, Saudi Arabia in the 2026 Iran war
- Multiple projectile explosives launched from Iraq strike pumping stations along the East–West Crude Oil Pipeline in Saudi Arabia, causing a fire. [src: (CNN)]
- Yemeni civil war
- 2026 Yemen offensives
- Houthis capture the port city of Mokha, as government forces retreat from the districts of Hays and Al Khawkhah. A mass exodus of civilians from the area towards Aden is reported. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war, Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russia drone strikes across Ukraine kill at least 15 people and injure 90 others, including victims in Dnipro, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Pavlohrad, and Sumy. Ukraine also strikes gas facilities in Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug, Ural, Russia. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Foreign fighters in the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Amnesty International says that Russia recruited foreign nationals for its war in Ukraine through deception, coercion, and exploitation, including false job offers and threats. The organization concludes that many such cases amount to human trafficking under international law. [src: (The Eastleigh Voice)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
- Crude oil prices in the United States, including from Brent Crude and West Texas Intermediate, reach US$100, the highest since May, amidst the country's renewed tensions with Iran. [src: (CNBC)]
- The European Central Bank raises its three key interest rates by 0.25 percentage points, lifting the deposit rate to 2.50%, as higher energy prices linked to the Iran war increase inflation pressures across the eurozone. [src: (CNBC)]
- The International Monetary Fund reports that the global growth of the global economy is on track to reach 3% in 2026 despite the war in Iran, but also cautioned that risks still remain high. [src: (Reuters)]
Disasters and accidents
- At least 20 people are killed and five others are reported missing after a fire breaks out on a cargo ship in Qingdao, Shandong, China. [src: (CNN)]
- Five people are killed and 40 others are injured after a bus carrying Dutch tourists crashes between Zernez and Susch, Switzerland. [src: (AP)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak
- Seven more children die from suspected measles in Bangladesh in the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of deaths in the country to 1,009. [src: (The Business Standard)]
- Health minister Sardar Md. Sakhawat Husain announces that Bangladesh will resume nationwide vaccinations beginning on September 25 amidst the ongoing measles outbreak. [src: (South Asian Herald)]
International relations
- Algeria–United Arab Emirates relations
- Algeria cuts diplomatic relations with the United Arab Emirates, without specifying a reason. [src: (Reuters)]
- Peru–United States relations, War on drugs
- Peruvian president Keiko Fujimori announces that Peru will join the U.S.-led Shield of the Americas coalition against drug cartels following a visit from U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- Deportation in the second Trump administration
- The United States Alien Terrorist Removal Court orders the deportation of permanent resident Nazira Haji Zada to Afghanistan in its first case, after Haji Zada conceded that she supported an Islamic State-inspired mass-shooting plot planned for the 2024 presidential election. [src: (BBC News)]
- Hutch Organised Crime Gang
- An Irish court charges Jason Hutch, a son of alleged crime boss Gerry Hutch, with facilitating a criminal organisation, the same day he was extradited from Spain. [src: (RTÉ)]
- Sri Lanka's Supreme Court overturns a 2019 presidential pardon granted to Buddhist monk Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara and orders him to serve the remainder of his six-year prison sentence for criminally intimidating human rights activist Sandya Eknelygoda. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Science and technology
- The first robotic surgical system in Kyrgyzstan is introduced at the Kyrgyz State Medical Academy. [src: (Azertag)] [src: (AKIPress)] [src: (Caspian Post)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 11
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Yemeni civil war
- 2026 Yemen offensives
- In Yemen, the Houthis seize Perim Island in the Strait of Bab al-Mandab after government forces withdrew, completing their takeover of the surrounding area and giving them control of territory overlooking a major sea lane between the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- The Houthis announce the end and the success of their offensive, expelling government forces from six districts and seizing major locations. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 East–West Crude Oil Pipeline attack, Saudi Arabia in the 2026 Iran war
- Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy temporarily closes the East-West Crude Oil Pipeline as a precautionary measure following multiple attacks by drones from Iraq on Thursday. [src: (CNBC)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Ukrainian drone strikes kill two people and injure three others in Tula Oblast, Russia, while a separate strike kills a 37-year-old man in Kursk Oblast, according to regional officials. [src: (Reuters)]
- Kyiv strikes, Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russian drone strikes hit two petrol stations in Kyiv, Ukraine, killing two people and injuring 12 others. A separate attack on a residential building injures eight people, while another strike kills a woman in Kyiv Oblast. [src: (Reuters)]
Arts and culture
- Princess Astrid, an older sister of the late Norwegian King Harald V and daughter of Olav V, dies at the age of 94. [src: (Nine.com.au)] [src: (Sky News)]
Business and economy
- Kyrgyzstan's central bank starts domestically printing banknotes of the Kyrgyz som, the country's currency, for the first time since independence. [src: (24.kg)] [src: (Kursiv)]
Disasters and accidents
- MV June Aster ship fire
- The death toll from the MV June Aster ferry fire off Coron, Palawan, Philippines, rises from five to 35 after firefighters boarded the burned vessel and recovered 30 additional bodies. The coast guard continues searching for dozens of missing passengers and crew. [src: (Reuters)]
- At least 16 people are killed in a fire in a retirement home near Pitrufquén, Cautín, Chile. Ten people are rescued and hospitalized. [src: (DPA via Yahoo News)]
- Thirteen people are killed and eight others are injured when a minibus collided with a car and a logging truck in Kholmogorsky District, Arkhangelsk Oblast, Russia. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (Xinhua)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- A case of Ebola is reported in the Sud-Ubangi province, making it the seventh province in the Democratic Republic of the Congo the outbreak has spread to. [src: (The Independent)] 
- 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
- The U.S. Food and Drug Administration and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention declares an end to the cyclosporiasis food poisoning outbreak, which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis and linked to iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms, in the United States. [src: (CNBC)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Endangerment of orangutans, India–Indonesia relations
- Indonesia works with Indian authorities to repatriate five baby orangutans found in an Odisha forest after suspected trafficking. Odisha Police and India's Wildlife Crime Control Bureau examine how the apes, which are native to Borneo and Sumatra, reached India. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
International relations
- Nigeria–South Africa relations, Xenophobia in South Africa
- Nigeria's National Assembly suspends all official visits and virtual engagements with South Africa in protest over repeated anti-migrant attacks there, including violence against Nigerians. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Israel–United Kingdom relations
- In retaliation to British sanctions on goods from Israeli settlements earlier this week, the Israeli government orders a team of British soldiers who train and advise Palestinian Authority security forces in the West Bank to leave the country. [src: (The Telegraph)]
Law and crime
- The Gambia bans protests without official permits after demonstrations over prolonged power outages damaged a police post and utility offices. Police arrest 11 people in connection with the unrest and warn that they will disperse unauthorized gatherings. [src: (Reuters)]
- A Hong Kong court sentences pro-democracy activists Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung to seven years in prison each for inciting subversion under the national security law for leading the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China. [src: (AFP)] [src: (Reuters)]
- The Lebanese Army arrests Suleiman Hilal Al Assad, a cousin of former Syrian president Bashar al-Assad, along with two other men, on drug trafficking charges. The men are now under the custody of Lebanon's defence ministry. [src: (AP)] [src: (Gulf News)]
- The Seoul Central District Court acquits former South Korean president Yoon Suk Yeol on charges that he appointed his defense minister, Lee Jong-sup, as ambassador to Australia to obstruct an investigation into a South Korean marine's drowning during the 2023 floods. [src: (AP)]
- South Africa extradites six Nigerian nationals allegedly belonging to Black Axe to the United States, where they face wire fraud and money laundering charges linked to online romance scams that allegedly defrauded more than 100 victims. [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- September 11 intelligence before the attacks
- The U.S. Central Intelligence Agency releases 71 documents warning of a threat from Al Qaeda prior to the September 11 attacks, including presidential daily briefs during the administrations of former U.S. presidents Bill Clinton and George W. Bush from 1998 to the day after the attacks. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 12
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 East–West Crude Oil Pipeline attack, Iran–Iraq relations, Iraq in the 2026 Iran war
- Iraq closes three border crossings with Iran after Iraqi and Saudi officials said that a drone attack on Saudi Arabia's East–West Crude Oil Pipeline originated from Iraq. [src: (AFP via The Times of Israel)]
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire, Iran–United Arab Emirates relations
- Iran and the United Arab Emirates sign a joint statement calling for restraint in the war. Additionally, Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian and Abu Dhabi ruler Khaled bin Mohamed Al Nahyan meet at the BRICS summit, the highest profile meeting between the two countries since the war started on February 28. [src: (Al-Monitor)] [src: (Hindustan Times)]
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan, China in the 2026 Iran war
- The Wall Street Journal reports that Iran had received Chinese satellite images before launching a July 17 strike on the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan that killed three United States Army soldiers. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- Yemeni civil war
- 2026 Yemen offensives, Strait of Bab al-Mandab crisis
- Yemeni government forces strike Houthi positions near the port of Mokha, Taiz Governorate, and along the Mokha–Dhubab road, reporting that they destroyed vehicles and weapons and killed Houthi fighters after the group captured the city. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Kryvyi Rih strikes, Odesa strikes, Zaporizhzhia strikes
- Russian drone strikes across Ukraine kill eight civilians, including two people in Zaporizhzhia, two people at a grocery store in Zhytomyr, one person in Kryvyi Rih, while a "massive attack" targeting the Port of Odesa and surrounding areas wounds at least 28 people. [src: (AP)]
- Eastern front of the Russo-Ukrainian war
- A Russian drone strikes a civilian vehicle in Kramatorsk, Donetsk Oblast, killing three people. [src: (AP)]
- Mexican drug war
- Four gunmen and a National Guard agent are killed and another is wounded after an attempted ambush against authorities in Jilotlán de los Dolores, Jalisco, Mexico. [src: (La Jornada in Spanish)]
Arts and culture
- 83rd Venice International Film Festival
- May el-Toukhy's film Woman Unknown wins the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival in Italy, while Lee Chang-dong's Possible Love and Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor's NAZA win the competition's Grand Jury Prize and Special Jury Prize, respectively. [src: (Japan Today)]
- Rukidi IV, the late king of Uganda's Tooro Kingdom, is buried. [src: (Reuters)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2024 Atlantic hurricane season
- The sheriff's office of Washington County, Tennessee, U.S., announces that the remains of the last victim of Hurricane Helene has been found, two years after the hurricane has hit East Tennessee. [src: (Knoxville News Sentinel)] [src: (WHNS)]
- MV June Aster ship fire
- The Philippine coast guard confirms that 41 more bodies have been discovered aboard the burned vessel MV June Aster off Coron, Palawan, bringing the death toll from the fire to 76. [src: (AFP via Philippine Daily Inquirer)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
- The Atlantic hurricane season reaches a 103-day record in the satellite era without a hurricane after the season started on June 1, the first since 1941, with the El Niño in the Pacific Ocean being a big factor. [src: (CNN)] [src: (The New York Times)] [src: (USA Today)]
International relations
- North Korean missile tests
- North Korea launches a series of SRBM missile tests from Wonsan in response to trilateral Freedom Edge military exercises conducted by Japan, South Korea, and the United States. [src: (Korea JoongAng Daily)] [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- Cléon derailment
- French officials investigate if the derailment in Cléon, Seine-Maritime, was caused by sabotage after a fragment of rail was found on the tracks. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (BBC News)] [src: (RTÉ)]
- Libya's RADA Special Deterrence Forces seize about 100,000 MDMA pills moulded with former leader Muammar Gaddafi's likeness after tracking a shipment smuggled from Europe. Officers find the drugs hidden in a cargo van and refer several suspects to prosecutors. [src: (The Independent)]
- Several residents are arrested after riots erupted yesterday in Kobani, Syria, over the murder of a Kurdish citizen that was blamed on an Arab man, while a prison riot and fire at Kobani prison leaves seven inmates dead. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reports the violence erupted over plans to transfer some prisoners to another prison in Aleppo. [src: (AP)] [src: (ABC News)]
Politics and elections
- Protests against Donald Trump
- Protests against the 2026 Iran war, Gaza war protests, Protests against the second Trump administration
- Thousands of demonstrators gather in Dublin and Doonbeg, Ireland, against U.S. president Donald Trump's visit to the country and protest against his role in the wars in Iran and Gaza. [src: (Irish Times)] [src: (The New York Times)]
- 2026 Saxony-Anhalt state election
- Protesters gather in Germany across 20 cities against the Alternative for Germany following its victory in the Saxony-Anhalt state election. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Sports
- 2026 US Open
- In tennis, Elena Rybakina wins the women's singles title at the US Open, her third major title, after defeating two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka in the final, 6–4, 5–7, 6–2. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Christian Harrison and Neal Skupski win the men's doubles title at the US Open without dropping a set in the tournament after defeating Kevin Krawietz and Tim Pütz, 6–4, 7–6(8–6) in the final. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- 2026 Summer Youth Olympics
- The Olympic flame arrives in Dakar, Senegal, ahead of the upcoming Youth Olympic Games, which will be the first Olympic Games held in Africa. [src: (AP)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 13
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Hezbollah–Israel conflict
- The Ghana Army says that Battalion 92 of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon will return to Ghana following a year of duty in southern Lebanon. [src: (GhanaWeb)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- A Russian drone attacks a train bound for Warsaw, Poland, at Yahodyn station in western Ukraine, shortly after former UK prime minister Boris Johnson and top EU security officials had passed through the airspace. Former U.S. CIA director David Petraeus was also at the station at the time of the strike but was unharmed. [src: (BBC News)]
Disasters and accidents
- Shipwrecks in 2026
- Sinking of the Virgo Transport 8
- Six people die, 97 are rescued and 140 remain missing after the sinking of the Virgo Transport 8 ferry in the Java Sea, Indonesia. [src: (BBC News)]
- Sinking of the MV Matui
- One person dies, 12 are rescued, and more than 30 remain missing after the sinking of the MV Matui ferry off Espiritu Santo, Vanuatu, during rough seas. [src: (ABC News Australia)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- A multiple-vehicle collision on a major highway in Western Cape, South Africa, kills at least 21 people and leaves four others injured, according to the Road Traffic Management Corporation. [src: (AP)]
International relations
- Myanmar's Union Government revokes Kyaw Moe Tun's status as the country's permanent representative to the United Nations, accusing him of illegal activities, as the UN Credentials Committee prepares to consider the country's disputed representation. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Law and crime
- Datu Usman Mampen Elementary School shooting
- Three people are killed and 15 others are injured when gunfire erupted outside a school in Cotabato City, Bangsamoro, Philippines, used as a polling station for the Bangsamoro Parliament election the following day. Police say that members of rival political factions clashed while competing to be first in line to vote. [src: (AFP via The Star)]
- Mexican drug war
- Law enforcement agents rescue eight people who they say were forcibly recruited by the Jalisco New Generation Cartel from a clandestine clinic in Tecalitlán, Jalisco, Mexico. Police arrest six suspected guards and seize drugs, weapons, and ammunition. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- An attack on the Panguna mine in the autonomous region of Bougainville, in Papua New Guinea, injures personnel and destroys equipment amid opposition to plans to reopen the copper mine. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Turkish police detain at least 63 people in raids targeting LGBTQ+ organizations and venues across several provinces. The justice ministry says investigations involve 162 suspects, nine associations and 13 businesses over alleged offences including prostitution and obscenity. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Politics and elections
- 2025–2026 Kosovo political deadlock
- The Assembly of Kosovo is declared constituted by acting president and speaker Albulena Haxhiu, but without the deputy speaker from the PDK. The Assembly then accepts the fourth cabinet of incumbent prime minister Albin Kurti. The PDK and the AAK both challenge the legitimacy of Kurti's government at the Constitutional Court. [src: (AP)] [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Swedish general election
- Swedes vote to elect all 349 seats of the Riksdag. Incumbent prime minister Ulf Kristersson, who seeks to lead the Moderates to a second consecutive government while including the right-wing populist Sweden Democrats in his cabinet, is being challenged by the former prime minister and SAP leader Magdalena Andersson. Preliminary results indicate that the Red-Greens and the Centre Party are projected to have a combined total of 175 seats, while the four Tidö parties are projected to have a total of 174 seats. [src: (AP)] [src: (DW)]
- Disinformation in the Russian invasion of Ukraine
- Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy sanctions his former press secretary, Iuliia Mendel, and nine others for allegedly spreading Russian propaganda and supporting Russia in its war against Ukraine. The 10-year sanctions include asset freezes and trade restrictions. [src: (Reuters)]
Sports
- 2026 Formula One World Championship
- 2026 Spanish Grand Prix
- In Formula One racing, Kimi Antonelli wins the inaugural Spanish Grand Prix at the Madring in Madrid, Spain. [src: (ESPN)]
- 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup
- In basketball, the United States women's team defeats France 97–79 in the final to win the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin, Germany, further extending its lead of 12 total wins. [src: (USA Today)]
- American player Breanna Stewart is awarded MVP of the tournament, while Belgian player Emma Meesseman is the top scorer, averaging 21 points per game. [src: (USA Today)]
- 2026 US Open
- In tennis, Alexander Zverev wins the men's singles title of the 2026 US Open after defeating Ben Shelton in the final, 6–3, 7–6(7–2), 5–7, 6–2. It is his first US Open title and second major title overall. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- 2026 Women's Twenty20 Asia Cup
- In cricket, the India women's team wins its eighth Asia Cup title by defeating Sri Lanka by 72 runs, but refuses to accept the trophy from Asian Cricket Council president and Pakistani interior minister Mohsin Naqvi during the presentation ceremony. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- 2026 World Athletics Ultimate Championship
- In athletics, British middle-distance runner Josh Kerr wins the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship in the 1500 metres event in Budapest, Hungary's National Athletics Centre. [src: (The Independent)]
- Melissa Jefferson-Wooden and Kenny Bednarek win the inaugural women's and men's 200 metres at the World Athletics Ultimate Championship. [src: (The Athletic via The New York Times)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 14
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Yemeni civil war
- 2026 Yemen offensives 
- Houthi forces seize control of the Hanish Islands in the Red Sea consolidating the group's control of the strategic sea lane off Yemen's western coast. [src: (AP)]
- Houthi forces advance towards the PLC-controlled cities of Marib and Taiz with heavy clashes underway. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Iranian support for the Houthis
- Gulf states call off planned peace talks with Iran in response to Houthi ballistic missile attacks on Saudi Arabia and Yemeni government forces. [src: (Reuters)]
- Mexican drug war
- At least seven suspected gunmen are killed and two others are detained after an armed group attacks Nuevo León police and soldiers in General Treviño, Mexico. Police later arrest three additional suspects. [src: (La Jornada in Spanish)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Sudan's Popular Congress Party and Sudan Liberation Movement faction led by Abdul Wahid al-Nur agree to broaden talks aimed at ending the three-year civil war in the country. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
Arts and culture
- 78th Primetime Emmy Awards
- American actress Jean Smart wins a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series for her role in Hacks, becoming the first actress to win for every season of a show. [src: (Entertainment Weekly)] [src: (Variety)]
- Canadian–American actor Michael J. Fox wins the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award for his contributions to research and advocacy on Parkinson's disease. [src: (Reuters)]
- American comedy horror television series Widow's Bay wins 14 Emmys including Outstanding Comedy Series, surpassing the record set by The Studio last year. [src: (The Hollywood Reporter)] [src: (Los Angeles Times)]
Business and economy
- Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the Catholic Church
- Pope Leo XIV restores salaries for cardinals and senior Vatican City officials to pre-COVID-19-pandemic levels, ending reductions introduced by Pope Francis in 2021. The change took effect September 1, 2026, without retroactive compensation. [src: (The Sun)]
- Nigeria's Dangote Group launches an initial public offering (IPO) of 4.1 billion shares at ₦525 (US$0.40) each, seeking to raise about ₦2.15 trillion ($1.6 billion) to fund the expansion of the Dangote refinery in Lekki, Lagos State. The sale is set to become Africa's biggest IPO. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd announce that they will sail more container ships through the Suez Canal. [src: (Reuters)]
Disasters and accidents
- Indonesia extends the search for eight people, including five journalists, after their speedboat disappeared in the Sunda Strait during a reporting mission on Anak Krakatoa's eruption a week prior. Police await test results to identify a body found on Enggano Island. [src: (AFP via Malay Mail)]
Health and environment
- 2026–2027 El Niño event
- The World Food Programme reports that Sudan's Darfur region is having its driest rainy season since the 1980s, worsening famine conditions amidst the ongoing civil war. [src: (AFP via Free Malaysia Today)]
- Chile becomes the first country in South America to eliminate dog-transmitted rabies, with the World Health Organization confirming the milestone. [src: (AP)]
International relations
- Separatism in the United Kingdom, Decolonization
- The First Ministers of Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales meet in Cardiff at a summit to call for their independence from the United Kingdom. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (The Guardian)]
Law and crime
- Immigration policy of the second Trump administration
- United States district judge F. Dennis Saylor IV of Massachusetts postpones new rules limiting stays for international students and journalists, preventing the measures from taking effect while a legal challenge proceeds. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Bangsamoro Parliament election
- Parliamentary elections are held in the Bangsamoro autonomous region, Philippines, its first since its establishment in 2018. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Science and technology
- Militarisation of space
- The United States confirms for the first time that it has deployed a weapon in Earth's orbit. Air Force secretary Troy Meink says the highly classified weapon is necessary to "safeguard U.S. forces" against potential enemy action. [src: (BBC News)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 15
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Oman's maritime security centre reports that two sailors are reported to be missing after the Panama-flagged oil tanker El Gaia was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz near the Musandam Peninsula. [src: (BBC News)]
- Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war
- The Kuwaiti energy ministry reports that Kuwait's electrical grid has held despite attacks from Iran against it. [src: (Arab Times Kuwait)] 
- Yemeni civil war
- 2026 Yemen offensives 
- The United Nations reports that more than 100,000 people have fled their homes in western and southern Yemen due to the ongoing Houthi offensive against Yemeni government forces, and that 2,400 refugees have arrived in Djibouti in the last four days alone. [src: (Kurdistan 24)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- A drone crosses from Belarusian airspace into Lithuania before being shot down by a NATO fighter jet over the village of Pratkūnai, Kaišiadorys District Municipality, near Kruonis Pumped Storage Plant, two days after an unidentified object flew over Lithuanian airspace from Belarus to Kaliningrad Oblast, Russia. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (LRT)]
Business and economy
- 2026–2027 El Niño event
- The Panama Canal Authority reduces daily ship transits through the canal from 36 to 32 as below-average rainfall and a strengthening El Niño lower water levels in reservoirs supplying the waterway. [src: (DW)]
- Kenya announces bans on exports of unprocessed gold and establishes at least three refineries, seeking to maximize its economic value by increasing domestic processing. [src: (Nairametrics)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Chatsworth Eurocopter AS350 crash
- Three people die when a telecopter operated by KNBC in Los Angeles, California, United States, crashes while covering a traffic collision in Chatsworth. [src: (AP)] [src: (BBC News)]
- Six people die while 17 others are injured after an Elf truck, with an Isabela–Benguet route and carrying 27 passengers, plunges into a ravine in Bontoc, Mountain Province, Philippines. [src: (Philippine Daily Inquirer)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- The United Nations reports that daily Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo declined from about 120 to 80, while 10 of 62 affected health zones record no new infections for more than 22 days. [src: (The Independent)]
- Aging of Japan
- Japan's health ministry reports 107,677 people aged 100 or older, exceeding 100,000 for the first time since records began in 1963. [src: (AFP via The Manila Times)] [src: (CNN)]
International relations
- Denmark–Russia relations
- A Russian Navy warship fires two flares at a Danish military helicopter in the Baltic Sea. [src: (The Guardian)]
Law and crime
- 2024 Bangladesh quota reform movement, Controversies related to Sheikh Hasina, Capital punishment in Bangladesh
- A court in Bangladesh sentences seven Awami League leaders who were former officials in former prime minister Sheikh Hasina's government to death in absentia over their role in deadly crackdowns on the anti-government protests in 2024. [src: (DW)]
- Death of Noah Donohoe
- The Northern Irish jury in the inquest returns a narrative verdict, criticising the Department for Infrastructure for failure to prevent public access to the tunnel Donohoe was found in and the police for failures in their investigation. [src: (RTÉ)]
- Femicide in Latin America, Gender inequality in El Salvador
- A court in El Salvador sentences a man to life imprisonment for aggravated femicide and stalking, the first such sentence for femicide in the country's history. [src: (DW)]
- Phillips family disappearances
- A New Zealand inquiry finds that police and Oranga Tamariki failed to act on warnings that Tom Phillips might abduct his three children and possessed firearms, contributing to missed opportunities to prevent or end their nearly four-year disappearance. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- The Brazilian public prosecutor's office files a civil action against Vale, the world's largest iron ore producer and one of Brazil's biggest companies, as well as the national mining agency and the Minas Gerais state government. The lawsuit is based on a containment overflow of two sumps at the Mina de Viga site in Congonhas in January, which caused the site to be shut down. [src: (Mining Reports)] [src: (The Rio Times)] 
- China implements new travel regulations allowing exit bans on citizens who violate technology import or export controls or commit national-security-related offences abroad. Returned citizens can face bans lasting six months to three years. [src: (AFP via Dawn)]
- Former Golden Dawn spokesperson Ilias Kasidiaris is released from prison in Domokos, Phthiotis, Greece, after serving part of a 13-year sentence for leading a criminal organization and announces plans to return to politics, although he remains barred from office until 2033. [src: (AFP)] [src: (The National Herald)]
- ProRail services across northern and central parts of the Netherlands are disrupted by a sabotage operation after pipes are attached to tracks, resulting in the failure of railway signals. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Politico Europe)]
- Romanian farmers clash with gendarmes in Bucharest during protests against live export restrictions due to ovine rinderpest and other policies. The confrontations leave 24 people injured, including eight gendarmes, while police detain 26 protesters. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Bloomberg)]
Politics and elections
- Reactions to the 2026 Iran war
- United States representative Thomas Massie files articles for impeachment against defense secretary Pete Hegseth for allegedly violating the War Powers Resolution by declaring war against Iran without congressional approval. [src: (Hindustan Times)] [src: (Military.com)]
Sports
- 2026 Asian Games
- The Italian cruise ship Costa Serena docks in Nagoya, Japan, to house about 4,000 Asian Games athletes and officials as delegations report accommodation problems, including undersized beds, leaking sinks, and room shortages. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- In association football, UEFA announces that the Champions League finals in 2028 and 2029 will be held at the Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany, and Camp Nou in Barcelona, Spain, respectively. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- The World Athletics Championships in 2029 and 2031 are awarded to Nairobi, Kenya, and Munich, Germany, respectively. 2029 will mark the first time the event is held on the continent of Africa. [src: (The Star Kenya)] [src: (AP)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 16
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Gaza war
- Twenty-one people are killed, 45 are injured, and about 100 others are missing after a residential building in Gaza City collapses after it was previously hit by an Israeli airstrike. Twelve children are among the fatalities. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Arts and culture
- 2026 Americana Music Honors & Awards
- The Americana Music Honors & Awards are held at the Ryman Auditorium in Nashville, Tennessee, United States, with the Heartbreakers performing for the first time since lead vocalist Tom Petty's death in 2017. [src: (The Independent)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026–2027 El Niño event
- Guatemala announces food aid for about 1.2 million families affected by severe El Niño-related drought, which damages crops and livestock across the Dry Corridor. The programme distributes maize, beans, and rice with World Food Programme support. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- At least 82 people are killed when a gold mine explodes in West Kordofan, Sudan, an area under control of the Rapid Support Forces. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Sky News)]
Health and environment
- 2026 United Kingdom heatwaves
- The United Kingdom records its second-best butterfly season in 16 years amidst record heat waves in the country. [src: (The Independent)]
- Fiji declares HIV a national crisis after reporting 2,016 new diagnoses in 2025, sixteen times the 2019 total. The government estimates that one in 60 adults lives with HIV and expands testing, prevention, and treatment services. [src: (AFP via New Straits Times)]
- In a study published by the Nature Medicine journal, scientists report that the PANXEON blood test helps detect pancreatic cancer at early stages and treat the disease before it spreads. [src: (Scientific American)] [src: (Discover)]
International relations
- Canada–European Union relations
- European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen invites Canada to become the first associate member of the European Union amidst the ongoing trade war between Canada and the United States. [src: (CNBC)]
- International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war
- The United States House of Representatives passes a bipartisan sanctions bill that imposes sanctions on Russia's energy revenues, financial institutions, officials, and shadow fleet, while authorizing tariffs of up to 100% on major buyers of Russian oil and gas. The bill will head to president Donald Trump's desk for his signature for it to become law. [src: (Kyiv Independent)] [src: (Reuters)]
- The first summit between South Korea and the five countries of Central Asia is held in Seoul. [src: (Euronews)] [src: (AFP via Korea Times)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Law and crime
- North Korea–South Korea relations
- Inter-Korean Liaison Office bombing
- A district court in Seoul, South Korea, orders North Korea to pay KRW44.6 billion (US$32.5 million) in damages for destroying the Inter-Korean Liaison Office in Kaesong in 2020, in South Korea's first damages lawsuit against North Korea. [src: (AFP via CNA)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Human rights in Macau
- Macau begins its first closed-door national security trial against former legislator Au Kam San, who faces charges including subversion of state power and alleged ties with foreign groups and media outlets. He faces up to 25 years in prison. [src: (AFP via RTL Today)]
- War crimes in the Kosovo War
- The Kosovo Specialist Chambers sentences former prime minister Hashim Thaçi to 25 years in prison after convicting him on charges of murder, torture, cruel treatment and arbitrary detention committed during the Kosovo War. [src: (AP)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Bangsamoro Parliament election
- The Philippine Commission on Elections proclaims all 78 elected members of the Bangsamoro Parliament, with four parties given all seats for party representation. The Bangsamoro Federalist Party, earning most of the seats, fails to secure a majority, leading to a hung parliament. Meanwhile, six sectoral seats are given to the United Bangsamoro Justice Party. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Manila Bulletin)]
Science and technology
- Discoveries of exoplanets
- Astronomers confirm the existence of Elias 2-24 b, the youngest known exoplanet, which is less than one million years old and located approximately 450 light-years from Earth. The discovery was observed through the W.M. Keck Observatory in Mauna Kea, Hawaii, U.S., using a coronagraph. [src: (Space.com)]
- NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter discovers a recently formed crater on the moon larger than the Colosseum in Rome, Italy. [src: (Phys.org)]
- A study published by the Science Advances scientific journal find that the Tyrannosaurus had a temperature of . [src: (Scientific American)]
Sports
- In association football, Clearlake Capital buys out Todd Boehly and Mark Walter's stakes to gain full control of Premier League club Chelsea. The deal is valued at around £950 million (€1.1 billion) for the 25% share. Chelsea is now worth about £5 billion (€5.8 billion). [src: (BBC Sport)] [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (ESPN)]
- The Women's Tennis Association (WTA) announces that its finals will move from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, to the Spectrum Center in Charlotte, North Carolina, United States, for three years beginning in 2027. The WTA also relocates its global headquarters from St. Petersburg, Florida, to Charlotte. [src: (BBC)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 17
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Gaza war
- Israeli government response to the October 7 attacks
- Lt. Col. "Aleph", the chief police officer in the Southern Command's Gaza Division, is dismissed following his role in the failures leading to the Hamas-led October 7 attacks on Israel. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- The Israel Defense Forces confirm that they have killed a Al-Qassam Brigades Nukhba Forces commander who took part in the October 7 attacks in a airstrike and a Hamas navy officer in another airstrike in Gaza City. [src: (Israel National News)] [src: (JFeed)]
- 2026 Iran war
- US war crimes in Iran strikes
- The UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission finds "reasonable grounds" that the United States military may have committed war crimes with attacks on the Minab school and Lamerd sports hall in southern Iran. [src: (Reuters)]
- Yemeni civil war
- 2026 Yemen offensives
- Al-Akhbar reports that Saudi Arabia has sent a proposal for Oman to mediate a two-week ceasefire with the Houthis. [src: (AzerNews)]
- A Yemeni resident is reported to be killed by debris from a drone in Taif, Mecca Province. [src: (Arab News)]
- Aftermath of the South Sudanese Civil War
- Twenty-six people are killed and 82 more injured during clashes between two rival communities in Abyei, at the border between Sudan and South Sudan. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Fifteen civilians are killed during an armed attack by unknown individuals in Madegoua, Far North Region, Cameroon. [src: (Reuters)]
Arts and culture
- France–Mexico relations
- The 16th-century Codex Azcatitlan goes on display in Mexico City after France loaned two folios nearly two centuries after the manuscript left the country. Mexico continues seeking the codex's permanent return from France. [src: (AFP)] [src: (BBC News)]
Disasters and accidents
- Seventeen people are killed and two others are injured after a passenger vehicle collided with a truck in Inhambane, Mozambique. [src: (Xinhua)]
Health and environment
- Environmental policy of the second Trump administration
- The United States Fish and Wildlife Service narrows its enforcement of the Endangered Species Act by excluding unintentional wildlife deaths from its definition of prohibited take, including foreseeable deaths linked to activities such as commercial fishing and logging. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Biologists publish a study in the journal Current Biology describing a new species of wild cat belonging to the genus Leopardus, commonly called the "tilcayo", in the Yungas cloud forests of Bolivia. This discovery marks the first new cat species in over 100 years. [src: (Cell)] [src: (Reuters)]
- The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence approves the Trastuzumab deruxtecan drug for women in England with metastatic or incurable HER2-breast cancer that cannot be removed surgically, making it the first licensed targeted treatment for patients, two years after it was rejected due to its cost effectiveness. [src: (Sky News)] [src: (The Independent)]
International relations
- Eighty-First session of the United Nations General Assembly, Palestine and the United Nations
- The United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) votes 152–3, with four abstentions, to allow Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas and other senior Palestinian officials to address UN meetings, including the general debate of the eighty-first session of the UNGA, by video for one year after United States visa restrictions prevented their travel to New York City, where the UN headquarters are. [src: (Reuters)]
- Israel–Serbia relations
- Serbian president Aleksandar Vučić inaugurates a factory for Israeli-made drones that will be produced by the country's Krušik company, with Vučić stating that it will employ 100 people and produce advanced equipment for the Serbian military. [src: (AP)]
Law and crime
- Human rights in Pakistan
- Pakistan's Supreme Court suspends 17-year prison sentences imposed on human rights lawyer Imaan Mazari and her husband over anti-state social media posts, and grants them bail pending an Islamabad High Court ruling. [src: (Reuters)]
- Malawian police rescue a 47-year-old British woman after her abduction in Blantyre. Four suspected kidnappers are killed in a shootout with officers, while a senior police officer is injured and hospitalized in stable condition. [src: (AP via ABC News)]
- Thirty-seven suspected illegal gold miners die in custody of Nigeria's civil defence agency in Minna, Niger State. Survivors say overcrowding and poor ventilation caused breathing difficulties, while an intelligence report links the deaths to those conditions. The government orders an investigation. [src: (AFP)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Swedish general election
- Ulf Kristersson announces his resignation as Prime Minister of Sweden after his right-wing bloc wins 173 seats in the Riksdag, compared to 176 won by the opposition, led by Magdalena Andersson. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (BBC News)]
- Censorship and media control during the Venezuelan presidential crisis
- Venezuela restores access to 17 news websites that were previously blocked, including EFE, El Nacional, NTN24, and Semana, as the interim government and opposition resume political transition talks that include freedom of expression. [src: (AFP via Gulf News)]
- Visa policy of Australia
- Australia tightens visa rules for international students and working holidaymakers, restricts visa switching, and increases enforcement against overstayers as it seeks to reduce net overseas migration to 225,000 by 2027–28 and ease pressure on housing. [src: (AFP via France 24)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 18
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- The IRNA reports that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has hit the Togo-flagged oil tanker Trend as it attempted to pass the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (AFP via FMT)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
- 2026 Kohat attack
- A suicide car bombing outside a mosque located inside a police station in Kohat District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, kills at least 31 people, including 16 policemen, and injures at least 100 more. The Hafiz Gul Bahadur Group claims responsibility. [src: (AFP)]
- Mali War
- 2026 Mali offensives
- At least 100 Malian soldiers are reported to have been killed in a attack on the Dioura central army base in Mali over the past weeks. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- Sudanese civil war
- 2026 Blue Nile campaign
- The Sudanese Armed Forces says that they have killed several Rapid Support Forces militants in Sudan's Blue Nile state. The country's defence ministry also confirms the attacks. [src: (Radio Tamazuj)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
- The Bank of Japan raises its benchmark interest rate by 0.25 percentage points to 1.25%, the highest level since 1995, citing inflation pressures from rising energy costs and a weak yen, and signals further increases. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Russia places the local assets of Auchan and Nestlé under temporary administration, transferring their control to Russian firm L.E.V. Management, headed by interior minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev. The government cites the companies' origins in countries it designates as "unfriendly" amid broader seizures of foreign-owned businesses. [src: (CNN)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2024–2026 Cuba blackouts
- Millions of people are left without electricity in Cuba as a result of a collapse of the country's energy power grid. [src: (AP)]
Health and environment
- Zealand Pharma's drug Zeydovio receives approval by the European Medicines Agency's Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use to treat short bowel syndrome. [src: (Reuters)]
International relations
- Denmark–United States relations
- Greenland crisis
- Denmark and the United States reach a deal allowing the U.S. to expand its military presence in Greenland and granting permanent basing, overflight, and access rights, while barring non-NATO countries from establishing bases and restricting sensitive investments on the island. [src: (Reuters)]
- International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war, United States sanctions against Iran
- U.S. president Donald Trump signs the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which authorises and expands statutory sanctions, tariffs, and prohibitions on Russia and extends existing sanctions on Iran until 2031. [src: (Middle East Eye)] [src: (Kyiv Indepedent)]
- Polish prime minister Donald Tusk announces that Poland has joined the Anti-Ballistic Missile Coalition to develop a joint anti-ballistic missile defence system with some other European countries. [src: (Firstpost)]
Law and crime
- 1MDB scandal
- King Sultan Ibrahim of Malaysia grants former prime minister Najib Razak a conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, following his corruption conviction linked to 1MDB. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Ceuta migrant crisis
- Spanish police begin moving more than 3,000 migrants from beaches in Ceuta to temporary accommodation at the port. The operation prompts crowding and clashes, with officers firing warning shots and several people sustaining injuries. [src: (News.Az)]
- 2026 South Cotabato school shooting
- Three students, including the perpetrator, are killed ‌and eight others are injured ​in ​a mass shooting at a ⁠secondary ​school in ​Banga, South Cotabato, Philippines. [src: (AA)]
- Afghanistan–Pakistan relations
- Pakistan's medical regulator orders Afghan students enrolled in medical and dental programs to leave their colleges and return to Afghanistan. Dozens challenge the directive in court, while a Lahore judge temporarily suspends expulsions in Punjab. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Protests erupt in Minna, Niger State, Nigeria, after 37 miners died yesterday in custody of the Security and Civil Defence Corps following raids on suspected illegal mines. Niger state governor Mohammed Umar Bago imposes a curfew. [src: (Reuters)]
- Russia designates filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev a foreign agent, subjecting him to financial restrictions, reporting requirements, and mandatory labels on published material. Zvyagintsev, who lives abroad, has criticized the Russo-Ukrainian war and president Vladimir Putin. [src: (Reuters)]
- Vietnamese police arrest three men, including Norwegian and Australian citizens, on terrorism and document-forgery charges after authorities say they attempted to enter Vietnam illegally from Cambodia while carrying out activities linked to Việt Tân. [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Russian legislative election
- Russians begin voting to elect 450 seats of the State Duma over a period of three days following Ukrainian attacks upon oil infrastructure. The elections are also held under strict control during the Russo-Ukrainian war, combined with an ongoing crackdown on anti-war opposition and the anti-war party Yabloko being disqualified from running. [src: (AFP via RNZ)] [src: (AP)]
- The Senate of Bolivia ratifies an agreement to take a US$1.9 billion loan from the International Monetary Fund amid a deep economic crisis in the country, with trade unions threatening renewed protests in response. [src: (AP)]
Science and technology
- Investigation of UFO reports by the United States government
- The U.S. Defense Department releases a sixth batch of classified files related to unidentified flying objects, including videos of several orbs flying over Washington, D.C. in 1952 and orbs flying near Tremonton, Utah, also in 1952. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (CBC News)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 19
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire
- Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaee says that Iran has set seven conditions for resuming ceasefire negotiations with the United States. [src: (Iran International)]
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- United States Central Command commander Brad Cooper says that oil, cargo, and liquefied natural gas shipments in the Strait of Hormuz have hit a six-month high. [src: (Bloomberg)] [src: (Middle East Eye)]
- Gaza war
- Israeli airstrikes kill at least three Palestinians in Gaza, including the eldest son of the Gaza Health Ministry director-general. Israel says it targeted militants, while medics report additional deaths in Sheikh Radwan and Shuja'iyya. [src: (Reuters)]
- Operation Southern Spear
- United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear
- The U.S. military strikes a vessel in the Caribbean Sea, killing four people whom the Southern Command says were involved in drug trafficking. [src: (Reuters)]
- Islamic State insurgency in the Philippines
- A series of clashes, involving combined police and military forces and remaining wanted members of the Dawlah Islamiya and the Bangsamoro Islamic Freedom Fighters, erupts in Tugunan, Special Geographic Area of the Bangsamoro, Philippines. Seven members from both groups are killed. [src: (The Philippine Star)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
- Tropical Depression Six forms in the Atlantic Ocean near the Azores amidst an unusually quiet Atlantic hurricane season caused by El Niño. [src: (Fox Weather)] [src: (WTSP)]
- 2026 Indonesia wildfires, Indonesia–Malaysia relations
- Indonesia accepts Malaysian assistance to combat wildfires in Kalimantan, including a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters, and 52 personnel, as the fires cause transboundary haze affecting Southeast Asia. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
International relations
- Eritrea–United States relations
- The U.S. treasury department lifts the sanctions against Eritrea's ruling party previously imposed by former U.S. president Joe Biden's administration. [src: (AP)]
- 2026 United Nations Secretary-General selection
- Chilean Michelle Bachelet announces that she is withdrawing from the race to become UN Secretary-General after losing support, and that in the latest informal poll, Costa Rica’s Rebeca Grynspan is reported in the lead. [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- Domestic violence in South Africa, Sexual violence in South Africa
- South Africans hold memorial runs and protests after police find the bodies of nine women in Ekurhuleni, Gauteng, over two months. Police investigate possible links between the killings, which renew public concern over violence against women. [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Russian legislative election
- Russian election commission chairperson Ella Pamfilova reports cyberattacks targeting Russia's online voting system during the second day of the parliamentary election and says they are repelled. The Minkomsvyaz separately reports thwarting a sabotage attempt on Far Eastern communication lines. [src: (ABC News Australia)]
- 2026 South Ossetian presidential election
- Marat Kambolov is declared the winner of the presidential elections in the partially recognized South Ossetia. [src: (Reuters)]
- Donald Trump's conflict with the news media
- United States president Donald Trump's executive office denies journalists from CNN, MS NOW, and Politico access to the White House and confiscates or disables their press passes, citing their coverage of his administration. [src: (AFP via Philippine Daily Inquirer)]
Sports
- 2026 Asian Games
- The 20th Asian Games are opened by Emperor Naruhito in Nagoya, Aichi Prefecture, Japan. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 WNBA season
- In women's basketball, Atlanta Dream player Angel Reese becomes the first player in Women's National Basketball Association history to reach 500 rebounds in a single season. [src: (Bleacher Report)]
- 2026 World Rugby Pacific Nations Cup
- In rugby union, hosts Japan win their fourth Pacific Nations Cup title after defeating the defending champions Fiji 20–15 in the final at Chichibunomiya Stadium in Tokyo. [src: (AFP via RFI)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 2
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Israeli–Palestinian conflict
- Israeli settler violence
- Palestinian officials say two teenagers were killed during an incident involving Israeli settlers and soldiers in al-Mughayyir, Ramallah and al-Bireh Governorate, West Bank. The villiage council states that the Palestinian teenagers were killed when they were trying to prevent the Israeli settlers from stealing livestock. Israel's military says troops shot stone-throwers while protecting an Israeli civilian and police retrieving livestock. [src: (BBC News)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- 2026 SBUHUR Kyiv shootout
- In Kyiv, Ukraine, the Security Service of Ukraine and Defence Intelligence of Ukraine (HUR) have a shootout, injuring three HUR officers. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Kyiv Independent)]
- Sudanese civil war
- War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
- The World Food Programme reports that an airstrike hit two UN food aid trucks in Dilling, South Kordofan, Sudan, over the weekend, destroying emergency supplies. [src: (AFP via Arab News)] [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Insurgency in Balochistan
- Twenty-one insurgents and six Pakistani personnel, including five security forces and a customs official, are killed in separate shootouts across multiple districts in Balochistan, Pakistan. [src: (Dawn)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- The global stock index rises following recent declines amidst the war in Iran including renewed tensions with the Japanese yen gaining against the United States dollar. [src: (Reuters)]
- The Dutch central bank reallocates 86 tonnes of gold reserves from Ottawa, Canada, and New York City, United States, to London, United Kingdom, increasing the share held there to 32.1%, citing "increasing geopolitical unrest". [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Seoul Economic Daily)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Dahab-Nuweiba bus crash
- At least 22 people, including ten Jordanians, are killed and 28 others are injured in a bus accident in South Sinai, Egypt. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- The MV Tuğberk İmamoğlu cargo ship sinks in the Marmara Sea after a collision with an oil tanker, leaving ten people missing. [src: (Euronews)]
- At least 13 people are killed and five others sustain critical injuries after two minivans collide head-on in Greater Accra, Ghana. [src: (Xinhua)]
- Five people are killed and 20 others injured after a passenger bus collides with a tanker truck on the National Highway 39 in Rewa District, Madhya Pradesh, India. [src: (Times of India)]
- An explosion at the Augsburg train station in Swabia, Germany, injures two people. The cause is unknown. [src: (Euronews)]
- A crew member is killed, six others are missing, and one is rescued when a tugboat capsizes and sinks off the coast of Busan, South Korea. [src: (AP)] 
International relations
- Norway–Russia relations, Russian shadow fleet
- Norway seizes the Russian-owned Professor Molchanov ship near Svalbard to enforce a US$4.22 billion compensation award owed to Ukraine's Naftogaz for assets expropriated in Crimea. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Leipzig Airport drone incidents
- Following the drone attacks at Leipzig/Halle Airport last month, German security authorities are focusing on several suspects with ties to Russia. According to investigations by the NDR, WDR, and SZ, the suspects are two men from Belarus and Lithuania who are also said to hold Russian passports. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (DW)]
- Birthright citizenship in the United States
- U.S. federal judge Deborah Boardman of Maryland's district court blocks an attempt by the Trump administration from implementing an executive order aimed at ending birthright citizenship in the country. [src: (The New York Times)] [src: (Reuters)]
- A Maltese jury acquits businessman Yorgen Fenech of complicity in the 2017 car-bomb killing of journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia and of criminal association, finding him not guilty by an 8–1 vote. [src: (AP via NPR)]
- Three people are killed, including the perpetrator, and six others are injured in a mass shooting in Loring Park, Minneapolis, United States. [src: (AP)] [src: (DW)]
- Digital rights organization SHARE Foundation documents at least 14 Serbian students and opposition activists targeted with Pegasus or NoviSpy spyware in 2026, while Citizen Lab confirms Pegasus infection in at least one case. [src: (Financial Times)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Estonian presidential election
- Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise, the only candidate, is elected by the Riigikogu as President of Estonia. She will be sworn into office on October 12, succeeding Alar Karis. [src: (ERR)] [src: (Reuters)]
Sports
- 2027 U.S. Open Cup
- In association football, Major League Soccer announces that all 27 teams from the United States will return to the U.S. Open Cup beginning in 2027, making it the first full participation in the tournament since 2023. [src: (ESPN)] [src: (The Guardian)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 21
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Yemeni civil war
- Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict, 2026 Yemen offensives
- Saudi Arabia–United Kingdom relations
- British prime minister Andy Burnham says that the United Kingdom will offer Saudi Arabia aerial refueling in its ongoing conflict with the Houthis. [src: (The Hill)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Egypt–Sudan relations, Egypt–United States relations, Sudan–United States relations
- U.S. senior advisor Massad Boulos says that he has held talks with Sudanese foreign minister Mohieddin Salem and Egyptian foreign minister Badr Abdelatty at the United Nations General Assembly meeting in an effort to end the three-year long civil war. [src: (Arab News)] [src: (Sudan Horizon)]
- Darfur campaign
- The Sudanese military at night launches heavy airstrikes against Rapid Support Forces targets in Nyala, South Darfur. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Kordofan campaign
- An attack on a gold mining market in North Kordofan by the Rapid Support Forces kills five citizens, including a goldsmith worker. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- The United Nations's International Organization for Migration reports that 5 million displaced people have decided to return to Sudan despite the civil war. [src: (Arab News)]
- 2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war
- Pakistan's military launches strikes over the Afghanistan–Pakistan border in retaliation for the 2026 Kohat attack. Afghanistan's government and the UNAMA report that a family of three was killed in the strikes, while Pakistan says the strikes killed 28 Pakistani Taliban militants. [src: (Reuters)]
Arts and culture
- Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict
- The Red Sea International Film Festival in Saudi Arabia is postponed to 2027 due to the ongoing conflict with the Houthis. [src: (Arab News)] [src: (Gulf News)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- Economic D-Day, United States sanctions against Iran
- Turkish Airlines suspends flights to and from Iran until March 2027 ahead of new U.S. sanctions against Iran. [src: (Iran International)]
- Ceer Motors unveils the EXOBOT SUV and sedan in Saudi Arabia, its first electric vehicles in the country. [src: (Electrek)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 California wildfires
- Two pilots are killed in a helicopter crash while fighting a wildfire in Yosemite National Park, California, United States. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Nepal–Tibet floods
- The Nepalese government announces that they are discussing resettling victims of flooding from Bhotekoshi Rural Municipality to safe places in the country. [src: (Daily Pioneer)]
- Korean conflict
- An explosion injures three South Korean military officers during an operation inside the Demilitarized Zone, south of the military demarcation line. The Joint Chiefs of Staff says the cause remains unknown. [src: (AFP via The Peninsula)]
- A helicopter crashes in a mountainous area of Urubici, Santa Catarina, Brazil, killing the five occupants, including singer Rick Sollo. [src: (Metrópoles )] [src: (Xinhua)]
Health and environment
- New Zealand's critically endangered black robin wins Forest & Bird's Bird of the Year competition with more than 26,000 votes out of about 105,000 votes. [src: (AFP)]
International relations
- International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian war, Russia–European Union relations
- European Union ambassadors agree in principle to remove Russian oligarchs Mikhail Fridman and Alisher Usmanov from sanctions imposed over Russia's invasion of Ukraine, while renewing restrictions on about 3,000 other Russian-linked individuals and entities for three years. However, Latvia later blocks the deal. [src: (Billionaires.Africa)] [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- 2023 Vermont shooting of Palestinian students
- Jason Eaton is found guilty for shooting and critically wounding three Palestinian students in Burlington, Vermont, United States, who wore keffiyehs in solidarity with Palestine in the wake of the beginning of the Gaza war. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (IndyStar)]
- Singapore's Land Transport Authority introduces fines of up to S$500 (US$390) for eating on public buses or placing feet on seats, while severe cleanliness or safety violations can incur penalties of up to S$5,000 (US$3,900). [src: (AFP)]
Politics and elections
- Mexico's Secretariat of Public Education introduces nationwide rules restricting cellphone and tablet use throughout the school day in public primary and secondary schools, effective November 3. High schools set their own limits for educational use. [src: (AFP via The Star)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 22
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Ethiopian civil conflict
- 2026 Ethiopian offensive
- The Ethiopian National Defense Force launches 21 airstrikes in Alamata, Tigray Region, killing 14 civilians and wounding 22 more. Two empty schools are also hit. [src: (BBC News)]
- Yemeni civil war
- Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict
- 2026 Yemen offensives
- Saudi airstrikes against the Houthi-held city of Mokha, Yemen, kills six civilians. [src: (AFP via CNA)]
- Colombian conflict
- Colombian president Abelardo de la Espriella deploys troops to Santa Marta, Magdalena Department, after members of the Conquering Self-Defense Forces of the Sierra Nevada (ACSN) attack businesses and burn vehicles following a security operation that killed 13 ACSN members, including a senior commander. [src: (AFP)]
Arts and culture
- Silver Roman coins dating back to the 2nd century are discovered by an amateur archaeologist in Germany. The coins are placed on display at the Rheinisches Landesmuseum Bonn museum in Bonn. [src: (The Guardian)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Pacific hurricane season
- The National Hurricane Center reports that Hurricane Polo has strengthened into a category 5 Pacific hurricane. [src: (The Independent)] 
- 2026 Pacific typhoon season
- Typhoon Dujuan kills at least four people and injures 22 others in Japan, while six remain missing after landslides. More than 45,000 households in Chiba Prefecture lose power, and over 460 homes are damaged. [src: (AFP via Taipei Times)]
- Moldova's parliament approves a 60-day state of emergency in the energy and water sectors as low levels in the Dniester and Prut rivers threaten water supplies and global conflicts raise energy costs. [src: (AP)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
- The Atlantic hurricane season breaks a 112-year record without a hurricane, due to a strong El Niño event in the Pacific. [src: (AccuWeather)]
- Tunisia's meteorological service reports that summer 2026 is the country's hottest since records began in 1950, with average temperatures above the previous record and repeated heat waves contributing to water shortages and power cuts. [src: (AFP)]
International relations
- Eighty-first session of the United Nations General Assembly
- 2026 Iran war
- 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
- Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi and U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff hold three hours of Qatar-mediated talks at the UN General Assembly in New York City, the first contact between the countries since U.S. vice president JD Vance met an Iranian delegation in Switzerland in June. [src: (The Guardian)]
- Sudan–United States relations
- Diplomatic sources and the United Nations say that the United States refused to issue Sudanese military chief and de facto leader Abdel Fattah al-Burhan a visa to attend the UN General Assembly. Sudan asks the UN to intervene. [src: (AFP)]
- United States–Venezuela relations
- United States president Donald Trump and Venezuelan interim president Delcy Rodríguez meet on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, marking the first in-person meeting between the countries' leaders following the 2026 U.S. intervention in Venezuela and capture of Nicolás Maduro. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Afghanistan–Turkmenistan relations
- Afghanistan and Turkmenistan agree to establish a joint commission on road transport and to facilitate transit between the two bordering countries. [src: (Trend News Agency)]
- Belgium–Rwanda relations
- Belgium and Rwanda restore diplomatic relations 18 months after severing ties over the Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda conflict. The countries plan to reopen their embassies following months of meetings facilitated in part by Qatar. [src: (Reuters)]
- Greenland crisis, Decolonization of the Americas
- Denmark, Greenland, and the United States sign an agreement expanding U.S. military access to Greenland, permitting new defence areas and a missile defence system while reaffirming Greenland's self-determination and amending the 1951 defence agreement. [src: (DW)] [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- Crime in South Africa
- Eleven people are killed, including a pregnant woman, and three others are injured after three men open fire at a gathering inside a house in KwaMakhutha township, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. [src: (BBC News)]
- Three men are killed in a shooting in Gugulethu, Cape Flats, South Africa. Police are investigating it as a triple homicide. [src: (Cape Town ETC)]
- 2019 Sri Lanka Easter bombings
- Sri Lanka's High Court convicts 15 men involved in the Easter bombings in 2019. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- 2026 Turgutlu school shooting
- Eleven people are wounded in a mass shooting at a high school in Turgutlu, Turkey. The perpetrator is arrested. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Human trafficking in Papua New Guinea
- Papua New Guinea police rescue 39 Indonesians allegedly trafficked through false job offers and held in Port Moresby. Officers arrest four Chinese nationals and investigate possible links to a wider transnational trafficking network. [src: (AFP via The Straits Times)]
- Three lawsuits are filed against the Six Flags Magic Mountain amusement park in Valencia, California, U.S., after 100 riders suffered brain injuries after riding the X2 roller coaster. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (CBS Los Angeles)]
- Cybercrime group ShinyHunters says it has breached the website of the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and stolen personal data on current and former employees, including addresses and Social Security numbers. The FBI investigates the claim. [src: (Reuters)]
- At least three people are killed in an after-curfew ambush in Mangu, Plateau State, Nigeria. [src: (Daily Trust)]
Science and technology
- Hundreds of flights are delayed at five primary airports across northeastern United States, namely Newark Liberty, Teterboro, Philadelphia, LaGuardia, and JFK, due to technological issues after a construction crew accidentally severed numerous cables, including fiber-optic ones used for communication with air traffic control. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (CNN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 23
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran
- The United States Central Command says that the U.S. military has redirected 115 commercial vessels since the reinstatement of its blockade on July 14. [src: (Gulf News)]
- An Indian wiper is killed during an attack on the bulk carrier MV Cape Dao near the Strait of Hormuz, with Oman's navy confirming that 27 crew members have been evacuated. [src: (AFP and Reuters via Arab News)] [src: (The Indian Express)]
- Iran reopens schools and universities after months of closures caused by the war. About 16.5 million schoolchildren begin the new academic year, with reopening ceremonies held across the country. [src: (AFP via Channels Television)]
- Acting United States Navy secretary Hung Cao reports that eight sailors on the have attempted suicide during its long deployment including during the Iran war. [src: (BBC News)]
- Ethiopian civil conflict
- 2026 Ethiopian offensive
- The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) seizes several airports in Tigray, while clashes are ongoing in the nearby regions of Afar and Amhara. The TPLF says that it has started a "defensive war" against the federal government of Ethiopia. [src: (Reuters)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Kharkiv strikes, Kyiv strikes, Odesa strikes
- Russian drone and missile attacks across Ukraine kill at least eight civilians, including six agricultural workers in Kharkiv Oblast and two people in Kyiv, while strikes also hit Odesa. Ukraine says it intercepts or suppresses 119 of 161 drones. [src: (AP)]
- Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Poland deploys fighter jets into its airspace after a Russian helicopter intruded near Braniewo, Warmian–Masurian Voivodeship. [src: (Chronicle Live)]
- Colombian conflict
- Threats and attacks by the Conquering Self-Defense Forces of the Sierra Nevada (ACSN) bring Santa Marta, Magdalena Department, Colombia, to a standstill, closing businesses and public transport. The group orders the shutdown after security forces kill 13 ACSN members. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Communal conflicts in Nigeria
- Fifteen people, including a village head, are killed in an armed ethnic clash in Bagudo, Kebbi State, Nigeria. Six suspects are arrested following the attack. [src: (Daily Post)]
- Islamist insurgency in Niger
- Islamic State militants kill at least 20 gendarmes in an ambush near Abala and Filingué in Tillabéri Region, Niger. [src: (Reuters)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war, United States sanctions against Iran
- Iranian airlines suspend services to Azerbaijan, Baghdad, Georgia, Muscat, and Qatar, after new U.S. sanctions target Iran's aviation sector. [src: (AFP)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
- Tropical Storm Fay re-emerges as a tropical depression with a sustained wind of 35 mph amidst a unusually quiet Atlantic hurricane season caused by El Niño. [src: (Sun Sentinel)]
Health and environment
- 2026–2027 El Niño event
- The Atacama Desert in Chile reports blossoms of flowers amidst the ongoing El Nino event in the Pacific. [src: (Phys.org)]
International relations
- Eighty-first session of the United Nations General Assembly
- Sudanese civil war
- Africa–United States relations
- The United States and African Union hold the first joint Quad-Quintet talks at the United Nations General Assembly sidelines in a effort to end the ongoing civil war in Sudan. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Belarus–Poland relations
- Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski and Belarusian Foreign Minister Maxim Ryzhenkov meet at the United Nations General Assembly, making it the first meeting between Poland and Belarus in a decade. [src: (UA News)] [src: (Notes from Poland)]
- Azerbaijan–France relations
- Azerbaijani president Ilham Aliyev pardons a French national who served a 10-year prison sentence for espionage, and orders his release as one of 20 pardoned prisoners. [src: (BBC News)]
- Cross-strait relations
- Taiwan's coast guard increases patrol capacity around the disputed Pratas Island in the South China Sea by stationing a new 100-tonne patrol boat and regularly deploying larger vessels, citing increased China Coast Guard activity near the Taiwan-controlled outpost. [src: (Reuters)]
- North Korean involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian war, South Korea–Ukraine relations
- Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy says that Ukraine transferred two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea after capturing them in Kursk Oblast, Russia, in January 2025. [src: (UPI)]
Law and crime
- Harvey Weinstein sexual abuse cases
- A court in New York, United States, sentences former film producer Harvey Weinstein to 15 years in prison for committing a criminal sexual act against former production assistant Miriam Haley. [src: (BBC News)]
- Mexican drug war, missing persons in Mexico
- Congresswoman Margarita López Pérez reports that, since 2021, Searching Mothers have found around 1,600 milk teeth, among other skeletal remains, in a mass grave in Zacapu, Michoacán. The state prosecutor's office denies having reports on the case. [src: (Guillermo Ortega)]
- War crimes in the Myanmar civil war
- Human Rights Watch reports that women held as political prisoners in Myanmar face torture, sexual violence, and inadequate medical care. The group says more than 6,600 women and 640 children are among over 30,000 political prisoners detained since 2021. [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Israeli legislative election
- The Central Elections Committee votes to disqualify Ra'am and all parties on the Joint List from running, alleging they promoted terrorism against Israel. Balad leader Sami Abu Shehadeh and MK Ofer Cassif are also specifically barred from running. [src: (Times of Israel)]
- 2026 Moroccan general election
- Moroccans vote to elect all 395 members of the House of Representatives. [src: (AP)]
- Second impeachment of Sara Duterte
- The Philippine Senate, sitting as an impeachment court, rules that only senator-judges able to participate count toward the conviction threshold in vice president Sara Duterte's trial, reducing the required votes from 16 to 14. [src: (Reuters)]
- The United Kingdom establishes a National Centre for Information Defence to detect and counter foreign disinformation, including AI-generated content. Prime Minister Andy Burnham says the centre will address disinformation attacks to states such as Russia. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Science and technology
- 2026 OpenAI infiltration of Medicare
- Australian prime minister Anthony Albanese says that an OpenAI-deployed agent accessed public and restricted files on a Medicare database during testing in June. OpenAI notified the government in September, while investigations continue into the breach. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- Croatia joins the U.S.-led Artemis Accords, becoming the 74th country to do so. [src: (Croatia Week)]
Sports
- 2026 Asian Games
- North Korea at the 2026 Asian Games, Weightlifting at the 2026 Asian Games
- North Korean weightlifter Ri Song Gum wins gold in the women's 49kg category at the 2026 Asian Games while setting three world records: 94kg in the snatch, 121kg in the clean and jerk, and 215kg overall. [src: (AFP via France 24)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 24
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Yemeni civil war, France–Saudi Arabia relations
- Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict
- 2026 Yemen offensives
- France announces that it will deploy its soldiers and air defense systems to Yanbu, Saudi Arabia, to support the Saudi military against the Houthis. [src: (Reuters)]
- Gaza war
- The Israel Defense Forces and Shin Bet say that they have killed Hamas's chief financial officer in the Khan Younis area of the Gaza Strip. [src: (Israel National News)] [src: (The Yeshiva World)]
- Ethiopian civil conflict
- 2026 Ethiopian offensive
- Fano fighters launch several attacks in the Amhara Region. Shootouts with the Ethiopian National Defense Force are ongoing, causing several casualties, while a colonel is captured. [src: (Daily News Egypt)]
- 2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war
- Pakistan's military launches ten air strikes on Afghan military sites, claiming they were used to store and launch drones. At least four people are killed in the strikes. [src: (AP)]
Arts and culture
- The beatification ceremony for the late American Catholic prelate and Rochester Archbishop Fulton J. Sheen is held at The Dome at America's Center in St. Louis, Missouri, United States. [src: (Bastille Post)] [src: (Vatican News)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
