- The European Commission reports that the average diesel price across the European Union reaches a record €2.23 (US$2.54) per litre, up from €2.16 ($2.46) the previous week. Nineteen member states record new highs. [src: (AFP via Bangkok Post)]
- Economic D-Day, United States sanctions against Iran
- The Emirati General Civil Aviation Authority announces the suspension of all flights between Iran and the United Arab Emirates amidst new U.S. sanctions until further notice. [src: (Gulf News)]
- Economic impact of the Gaza war
- UN Trade and Development reports that Gaza is experiencing the most severe economic crisis on record, with 92% of economic establishments damaged or destroyed, daily per capita GDP at US$0.58, and unemployment exceeding 90% among working-age residents. [src: (AFP)]
Disasters and accidents
- At least nine people are killed and many others are injured as a sleeper bus catches fire on the Yamuna Expressway in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India. [src: (Deccan Herald)] [src: (DW)]
- Twelve Kazakh military personnel are killed, three are rescued and two are missing after being swept into the Caspian Sea during a naval training exercise in the Mangystau Region. [src: (Reuters)]
Health and environment
- Hungary's food chain safety office confirms the European Union's first detection of the invasive spotted lanternfly in Bács-Kiskun County. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
International relations
- 2026 state visit by Xi Jinping to the United States
- Chinese leader Xi Jinping says that China will send two pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, to the Zoo Atlanta in Atlanta, Georgia, U.S. [src: (PBS)]
Law and crime
- Chromebook procurement scandal
- A court in Jakarta, Indonesia, reduces former education minister and Gojek co-founder Nadiem Makarim's prison sentence from 10 to nine years for corruption involving Chromebook procurement, while lowering restitution from Rp809 billion (US$45 million) to Rp548 billion ($30 million). [src: (Reuters)]
- Croatia–Germany relations, Nord Stream pipelines sabotage
- A Croatian court approves Ukrainian national Volodymyr Zhuravlov's extradition to Germany over his alleged involvement in sabotaging the Nord Stream 1 and Nord Stream 2 pipelines in 2022. [src: (AP)]
- Donald Trump's conflict with the news media
- American news outlets CNN, MS NOW, and Politico regain access to the White House after U.S. federal judge Timothy J. Kelly temporarily blocked the ban by President Donald Trump, ruling that the outlets are likely to show that their press passes were revoked without adequate due process. [src: (BBC News)]
- Mary Jane Veloso drug smuggling case
- Philippine president Bongbong Marcos grants an absolute pardon to Mary Jane Veloso, a former overseas worker in Indonesia who was arrested for drug trafficking and sentenced to death in 2010, but was later granted a reprieve and extradited back to the Philippines. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (Philippine Daily Inquirer)]
- Belarusian president Alexander Lukashenko says that he has pardoned 15 political prisoners. [src: (Reuters)]
- A priest is killed and four other people are injured in a mass stabbing by a Ukrainian national at a Benedictine abbey in Jarosław, Podkarpackie Voivodeship, Poland. [src: (AP)] [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Moroccan general election
- Morocco's Authenticity and Modernity Party, led by Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, wins the most seats in yesterday's parliamentary election, taking 97 of 395 seats, followed by the ruling National Rally of Independents with 66 and the Istiqlal Party with 65, according to preliminary official results. [src: (Reuters)]
- Hijab and burqa controversies in Europe, Islam in Italy
- Italy's government approves a decree capping foreign students with limited Italian proficiency at 30% per classroom and banning burqas and niqabs in schools. The measure takes effect immediately but requires parliamentary approval within 60 days. [src: (AP)]
Sports
- 2026 Asian Games
- Japan at the 2026 Asian Games, Swimming at the 2026 Asian Games
- In swimming, Japan's Shin Ohashi wins gold in the men's 200-metre breaststroke at the 2026 Asian Games in 2:04.83, breaking China's Qin Haiyang's 2023 world record of 2:05.48 by 0.65 seconds. [src: (AFP)]
- 2026 Major League Baseball season
- In baseball, the Major League Baseball's Chicago White Sox clinches the upcoming playoffs for the first time since 2021, following three-straight 100-loss seasons. [src: (AP)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 25
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- The Sudanese Armed Forces announces that they have recaptured Sodri, North Kordofan. [src: (Radio Tamazuj)]
- Two civilians are killed in a drone strike by Rapid Support Forces in El Obeid. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Sudanese refugee crisis
- The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees reports a sharp increase in refugees fleeing from Sudan to Chad in a effort to escape the civil war and dire conditions, with 400 people a day crossing eastern Chad. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iran war ceasefire, 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- The Wall Street Journal reports that United States president Donald Trump has rejected Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and halt regional fighting within seven days in exchange for easing U.S. sanctions and releasing Iranian frozen funds. [src: (Reuters)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Kyiv strikes, Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russian drone and missile strikes on residential buildings and other civilian sites in Kyiv, Ukraine, kill seven people, including a 14-year-old boy, and injure 46 others. [src: (AFP via News.com.au)]
- Somali Civil War
- Piracy off the coast of Somalia, Anti-piracy measures
- The Puntland Maritime Police Force successfully frees the oil tanker Sibu 1 following a multi-day counter-piracy operation near Garacad, Mudug, Puntland, after it was seized by Somali pirates in August. [src: (Idil News)] [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war
- Pakistan says that its military has killed 13 Afghan security forces during shootouts at the border. Afghanistan's government denies the claim. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (AP)]
Business and economy
- Gambling in Brazil
- Days before the general election, Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva issues a provisional measure banning online betting in Brazil, immediately halting new deposits. Users may withdraw remaining funds until October 5, and Congress must approve the measure within 120 days for it to remain in force. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (BBC News)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Kenge Let L-410 crash
- A military-leased Let L-410 carrying 17 people, including two generals, crashes near Kenge, Kwango, Democratic Republic of the Congo, while on route to Kinshasa, killing all passengers. [src: (AA)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Seven people are killed and 13 others are injured when a bus overturns on a road near Iraquara, Bahia, Brazil. [src: (G1)]
- Six people are killed and two others injured during the collapse of a two-storey building in Plaka, Athens, Greece, after an explosion caused by a suspected gas leak. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (AP)] [src: (BBC News)]
- Two people are killed and 13 more injured in a fire at a residential building in Lucca, Tuscany, Italy. [src: (ANSA)]
Health and environment
- 2023–2026 mpox epidemic
- A laboratory-confirmed mpox case from a 21-year-old woman is reported in Bunia, Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo. [src: (Reuters)]
International relations
- China–United States relations
- China–United States trade war, 2026 state visit by Xi Jinping to the United States
- China and the United States reach an agreement to cut tariffs on $30 ‌billion of goods and launch a dialogue on artificial intelligence. [src: (Reuters)]
- Humanitarian impact of the Sudanese civil war
- Chad–Sudan relations
- Authorities in the Darfur region open the Tina crossing at the border with Chad for aid deliveries across North Darfur. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
Law and crime
- 2026 political prisoner release in Venezuela
- Venezuela releases at least 29 detainees whom rights groups classify as political prisoners following a second round of talks between the interim government and opposition, while organizations continue verifying the number and identities of those freed. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- Mary Jane Veloso drug smuggling case
- Mary Jane Veloso is released from a prison in Mandaluyong, Philippines, after president Bongbong Marcos's absolute pardon of her was approved yesterday. [src: (Arab News)] [src: (Rappler)]
- Four people are killed and four more injured in a mass shooting on a street in Kingstown, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. The perpetrators are on the run. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- A court in Paris, France, sentences Loik Le Priol to 26 years in prison and Romain Bouvier to 19 years for murdering former Argentine rugby union player Federico Martín Aramburú in 2022. Le Priol and Bouvier had links to the dissolved far-right group Groupe Union Défense. [src: (AP)] [src: (BBC News)]
- Sri Lanka's parliament approves a constitutional amendment extending the terms of senior judges by two years as part of efforts to reduce an estimated 1.1 million-case backlog. [src: (Reuters)]
Sports
- 2026 Asian Games
- China at the 2026 Asian Games, Swimming at the 2026 Asian Games
- In swimming, China's Zhang Zhanshuo becomes the first athlete to win seven gold medals at a single Asian Games, securing his seventh title in the men's 400-metre freestyle with a Games-record time of 3:41.28. [src: (AFP)]
- In association football, an independent Premier League commission finds Manchester City F.C. guilty of 114 of 115 alleged financial-rule breaches spanning the 2009–10 to 2022–23 seasons. [src: (CNN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 26
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- War on terror
- Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
- 2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war
- A Pakistani Taliban suicide bomber self-detonates at a police checkpoint in Dera Ismail Khan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, killing twelve people and wounding 30 more. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (AP)]
- Islamist insurgency in Niger
- Islamic State militants kill more than 30 Nigerien soldiers in an attack near Birni-N'Konni, Tahoua Region. [src: (Reuters)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Bangkok floods
- In Thailand, Bangkok governor Chadchart Sittipunt declares a flood disaster across the city as severe flooding kills at least two people and affects more than 84,000 nationwide. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (AP)]
- September 2026 nor'easter
- A nor'easter is reported along the East Coast of the United States, forcing the cancellation of 400 flights and leaving more than 68,000 homes without power. One person is killed in New York City. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (WABC-TV)]
- Seven sailors are injured and 25 are rescued after a fire breaks out aboard the Russian fishing vessel Triumf off the Kamchatka Peninsula in the Far East. [src: (Reuters)] 
International relations
- Eighty-first session of the United Nations General Assembly
- Germany–Russia relations
- German foreign minister Johann Wadephul and Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov hold talks during the United Nations General Assembly, the first talks between Germany and Russia since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine. [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- Crime in South Africa
- Eighteen people are killed and 14 more are injured in a mass shooting carried out by eight gunmen at a tavern in Wedela township, Gauteng, South Africa. Police launch a manhunt for the gunmen. It is suspected that the shooting is linked to a dispute over illegal gold mining. [src: (The Citizen)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Four people are killed in a mass shooting by unknown gunmen on a street in the township of Khayelitsha in Cape Flats, South Africa. [src: (Smile)]
- The body of a murdered woman is found in Ekurhuleni, South Africa. She is the tenth woman found killed in the city in the last three months. Police says that it can not rule out the possibility that the killings are carried out by a serial killer. [src: (BBC News)]
Politics and elections
- India's Election Commission orders a review of its voter-roll software after concerns arise over changes that excluded millions of voters. A committee will examine whether the software complied with election laws and rules. [src: (Reuters)]
Sports
- 2026 AFL Grand Final
- In Australian rules football, the Brisbane Lions defeat the Fremantle Dockers to win the 2026 Australian Football League season by seven points, winning their third consecutive premiership and sixth overall. [src: (AFL)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- 2026 Billie Jean King Cup finals
- In tennis, Ukraine reaches its first Billie Jean King Cup final after defeating defending champion Italy 2–0 in the semifinals, with Elina Svitolina securing the decisive victory over Jasmine Paolini. [src: (AFP)] [src: (AP)]
- 2026 UCI Road World Championships
- In cycling, the Netherlands' Demi Vollering wins the women's road race world title in Montreal, Canada, defeating Poland's Katarzyna Niewiadoma-Phinney in the final sprint, while Italy's Elisa Longo Borghini takes bronze. [src: (AFP)]
- Bids for the 2036 Summer Olympics
- Germany's Olympic committee selects Munich as its candidate to host the Summer Olympics and Paralympics in 2036, 2040, or 2044. [src: (AP)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 27
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Yemeni civil war
- Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict
- 2026 Yemen offensives
- Saudi Arabia's air force carries out an airstrike at a market in Taiz, Yemen, killing seven people and wounding 40 more. [src: (Reuters)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war, Kyiv strikes, Odesa strikes, Zaporizhzhia strikes
- Russian and Ukrainian forces exchange strikes that kill at least eight people in Ukraine and one in Russia, hitting Kyiv and its outskirts, the Kharkiv and Odesa Oblasts, Sumy, and Russian-occupied Enerhodar, all in Ukraine, as well as Russia's Belgorod Oblast. [src: (AP)]
- Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
- Russian strikes hit Kyivstar's headquarters and multiple data centres in Kyiv, including a facility struck twice that injures two children and an adult. Russia also says it targeted a Vodafone Ukraine data centre. [src: (India Today)]
- 2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war
- Islamic State–Taliban conflict
- The Afghan military kill 28 fighters allegedly linked to the Islamic State in Nuristan Province. The Minister of Defense reports that the gunmen entered from Pakistan. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Ethiopian civil conflict
- 2026 Ethiopian offensive
- A drone strikes Tigrai Television's headquarters in Mekelle, Tigray Region, Ethiopia, forcing the station off air, while Tigray People's Liberation Front forces capture Erebti, Afar Region, and advance toward Afdera. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Arts and culture
- 2026 MTV Video Music Awards
- American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift's song "The Fate of Ophelia" wins the MTV Video Music Award (VMA) for Video of the Year, and surpasses Beyoncé for the most amount of VMAs won with 32 total. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (NBC News)]
- Thai rapper and singer Lisa wins the VMA Award for Best Pop with her song Dream, becoming the first K-pop solo artist and first Thai artist to win this award in VMA history. [src: (The Nation)]
Business and economy
- Turkish economic crisis
- Former Turkish family minister Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya resigns from her positions in the ruling Justice and Development Party amid scrutiny over alleged links to an investment-fund scandal that prompted the Capital Markets Board to liquidate 131 funds and led to 51 arrests. [src: (AFP)] [src: (AP)]
Disasters and accidents
- A bus carrying Filipino tourists veers off a highway near Munich, Germany, killing two people and wounding 25 more. [src: (AP)] [src: (Demócrata)]
Health and environment
- Healthcare in Ireland
- The Irish public healthcare system announces they will limit influenza vaccines to people aged 65 and above due to a shortage across the country. [src: (RTÉ)]
International relations
- China–United States relations
- Panda diplomacy
- Two giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, arrive at Zoo Atlanta in Georgia, U.S., as part of an agreement signed between China and the U.S. during Chinese leader Xi Jinping's state visit last week. [src: (AFP via Dawn)] [src: (AP)]
Law and crime
- 2026 RAF Fairford arrests 
- Five men are arrested in relation to a 'major incident' at the RAF Fairford air base in England. They are arrested on suspicion of committing offences that violate the Explosives Act 1875 and preparation of a terrorist act. [src: (CNN)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- Crime in South Africa
- Ten people are killed and 11 others are injured in a mass shooting at a store in Lwandle, City of Cape Town, South Africa. Police search for the perpetrators. A business dispute is suspected to be the main motive. [src: (Euronews)]
- Kidnapping in Nigeria
- It is reported that armed gangs have kidnapped at least 47 farmers in Niger State, Nigeria, yesterday and 40 women in Zamfara State on today. Separately, Abia State police announce on that they have discovered 28 human skulls and bones after raiding camps suspected to be owned by criminal gangs, with police speculating they may belong to kidnapped victims. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- List of mass shootings in the United States in 2026
- Three people are killed and four more injured in a mass shooting after an altercation at a strip club in Detroit, Michigan, United States. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 French Senate election
- The National Rally clears the 10-seat threshold in the Senate of France, allowing the party to meet qualifications to form a far-right parliamentary group. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (RFI)]
- 2026 São Toméan parliamentary election
- São Toméans vote to elect 55 members of the National Assembly. [src: (AFP via Macau Business)]
- 2026 Serbian parliamentary election
- Serbian president Aleksandar Vučić resigns in order to run for prime minister in the upcoming parliamentary election. Speaker of the National Assembly Ana Brnabić becomes acting president. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Swiss referendums
- Swiss voters reject an initiative that proposed to enshrine a stricter form of Swiss neutrality, which would have prevented Switzerland from imposing economic sanctions and cooperating with NATO. [src: (Reuters)]
Sports
- 2026 Berlin Marathon
- The Berlin Marathon is held in Germany, with Guye Adola and Tigst Assefa winning their respective marathon races although Assefa sustained cramps prior to the finish line. [src: (AP)] [src: (BBC News)]
- 2026 Billie Jean King Cup
- In tennis, the Czech Republic wins its 12th Billie Jean King Cup title and first since 2018 after defeating Ukraine 2–0 in the final in Shenzhen, Guangdong, China. [src: (AFP)]
- 2026 UCI Road World Championships
- In cycling, Brandon McNulty of the United States wins the men's road race world title in Montreal, Canada, becoming the first American champion in 33 years after finishing 13 seconds ahead of Australia's Michael Matthews. [src: (AFP)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 28
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Kyiv strikes, Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
- At least three people are killed and 24 others, including the former secretary of the National Security and Defence Council, Volodymyr Horbulin, are injured by Russian drone strikes on the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine building, a health clinic, and a residential building in Kyiv, Ukraine. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (Ukrainska Pravda)]
- Polish military jets are scrambled in response to Russian airstrikes on Ukraine. Individuals in Lublin Voivodeship, Poland, are briefly urged to seek shelter before an alert is lifted. [src: (Reuters)]
- Somali Civil War
- Constitutional crisis in Somalia, Controversies of Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
- At least 23 people are killed and others are injured as heavy clashes breaks out across the South West State of Somalia, as forces loyal to former president Abdiaziz Laftagareen launch a major armed assault on troops of Aden Madobe and Hassan Sheikh Mohamud. The assault starts with gunfire, explosive drones and a suicide vehicle bomb, spreading through the regional capital Baidoa. [src: (Garowe Online)] [src: (Horseed Media)] [src: (Bluewin)]
- Myanmar civil war
- Rakhine offensive
- At least 50 people are killed and 58 others are injured in a Tatmadaw airstrike on a market area in Kyauktaw, Rakhine State, Myanmar. The strike targeted the Arakan Army, which controls Kyauktaw. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Haitian crisis
- Gang members kill at least eleven civilians in Gros Morne, Grand'Anse, Haiti, after exchanging fire with a Gang Suppression Force patrol, which kills three attackers before the remaining gunmen flee. [src: (Demócrata)]
Business and economy
- Russian president Vladimir Putin places German retailer Metro AG's Russian assets under temporary administration, removing Metro's operational control amid broader Russian restrictions on businesses from countries it classifies as unfriendly. [src: (AP)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Bangkok floods
- Flooding and landslides kill at least eight people each in Myanmar and Thailand, while 20 to 30 people remain missing in Tanintharyi Region and more than 1.7 million people across Bangkok and 27 Thai provinces are affected. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- 2026 Pacific hurricane season
- Hurricane Polo causes flooding, power outages, coastal flooding, and evacuations in Baja California Sur, Mexico, as the Category 3 storm approaches the Pacific coast, becoming the first Pacific hurricane of the 2026 season to make landfall. [src: (AFP)]
- Eighty-one people in Uttar Pradesh, India, and 21 more in Nepal are killed during heavy floods and landslides in the past three days. [src: (Euronews)]
- An avalanche kills four climbers and leaves 12 others missing at the base camp of the Himalayan mountain Nemjung in Manang District, Nepal, as heavy snowfall hampers rescue operations. [src: (BBC News)]
Health and environment
- Sudanese cholera epidemic
- United Nations Secretary-General spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric reports a sharp drop in cholera cases in Sudan despite the ongoing civil war in the country following vaccinations and extensive efforts to treat the disease. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- The government of Delhi, India, announces a six-week construction ban from December 10 to January 20, along with traffic restrictions, staggered office hours, and higher parking fees, as part of measures to reduce winter air pollution. [src: (AFP via Gulf Times)]
Law and crime
- Two people are shot and killed inside a vehicle in Kent, Washington, United States. [src: (KOMO)]
- Five people are arrested in a police raid against suspected Islamic State members in Skopje, North Macedonia. Guns, knives and the group's flag are recovered. [src: (Vesnik)]
- Dutch police arrest cybersecurity specialist Pepijn van der Stap in connection with an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacker group. Van der Stap's employer identifies him as the suspect, while police say he will appear in court in Rotterdam, South Holland. [src: (CBC News)]
Science and technology
- Starship flight 14
- SpaceX's Starship Flight 14 launches into orbit from Starbase, Texas, United States. The ship is successfully returned to Earth early out of an abundance of caution. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (AP)]
Sports
- The United States Senate votes 77–22 to pass the Protect College Sports Act, a bill that will establish federal rules governing name, image, and likeness (NIL) compensation, NCAA eligibility, and athlete transfers in college sports. [src: (ESPN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 29
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Gaza war
- Israeli settler violence, Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Gaza war
- More than 100 Israeli settlers attack the Palestinian village of Jalud in the occupied West Bank, burning two homes and injuring three Israeli security personnel while preventing a displaced Palestinian family from returning home. [src: (AFP via The Manila Times)]
- An Israeli airstrike kills Izz al-Din al-Beik, the head of Hamas's Al-Qassam Brigades in the northern Gaza Strip. [src: (Reuters)]
- Somali Civil War
- Piracy off the coast of Somalia, Anti-piracy measures, Controversies of Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
- The Puntland Maritime Police Force successfully frees another hijacked oil tanker, the MT Honour ​25, following an ongoing week-long counter-piracy operation near Bayla, Karkaar, Puntland, after it was seized by Somali pirates on 21 April ​around 30 nautical miles off Puntland's coast with 17 crew members on board. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (Somali Guardian)]
- Five crew members aboard the MT Honour 25 are killed and four more injured by the pirates before the rescue. The fatalities are three citizens of Pakistan and one each from India and Myanmar. It is the first time in over a decade that people are killed by the pirates. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Arts and culture
- The coronation ceremony for Nyabongo I of Uganda's Tooro Kingdom is held, formally making him king. [src: (Reuters)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- The Reserve Bank of Australia raises its cash rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4.60%, the highest level since 2011, citing persistently high inflation above its 2–3% target range. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Julius Baer Group controversies
- The Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) concludes its investigation into the Julius Baer Group, finding serious risk-management and anti–money laundering failures. FINMA orders additional capital requirements, compliance reporting through 2032, and the confiscation of about CHF10 million (US$12 million) in profits. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Disasters and accidents
- A vehicle crashes through a fence and plunges into the River Wear in Sunderland, Tyne and Wear, England, killing three teenagers. The driver of the vehicle, also a teenager, is later arrested by Northumbria Police. [src: (Sky News)]
Health and environment
- The Japan Meteorological Agency reports rainfall in Tokyo for 34 consecutive days through today, the longest streak since records began in 1886 and one day longer than the previous record set in 2019. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Bloomberg)]
- The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issues two recalls for more than 25,000 bottles of chlorthalidone, a diuretic antihypertensive drug, created by Indian-based Inventia Healthcare Limited, due to faulty dissolution times in the human body. [src: (USA Today)]
International relations
- North Korea–South Korea relations
- Korean conflict
- South Korean defense minister Kang Shin-chul says that land mines planted by North Korea likely caused two explosions last week that injured three South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone south of the military demarcation line, potentially violating the armistice. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- Haitian crisis
- The United Nations Security Council extends the mandate of the Gang Suppression Force in Haiti by six months, allowing the multinational force to continue supporting Haitian security forces against armed gangs. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- Malaysia–Myanmar relations, Myanmar civil war
- Malaysia begins repatriating about 1,500 Burmese nationals from immigration detention centres under the first phase of a programme covering 5,000 people. [src: (AFP via RTL Today)]
Law and crime
- Myanmar civil war
- Twenty-one people are arrested in Myanmar for allegedly donating to the in-exile National Unity Government-linked People's Revolution Supply Family fundraising platform as the government identifies more than 2,700 alleged contributors. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Staškov school stabbing
- A teacher is killed and a student and another teacher are wounded in a mass stabbing at a secondary school in Staškov, Slovakia. The perpetrator, a fellow student, is arrested. [src: (Euronews)]
- Crime in Mexico
- The Supreme Court of Mexico invalidates the state of Chihuahua's authority to annul elections due to interference by organized crime and instructs the local legislature to instead include the annulment of elections due to foreign interference. [src: (El Sol de México)]
- Seventeen people are arrested during a security operation involving 800 police officers against a "suspected organised crime group" in five cities in the United Kingdom, including London. A police officer is stabbed and wounded during one of the raids. [src: (Sky News)]
- The Six Flags Magic Mountain amusement park in Valencia, California, U.S., announces that the X2 roller coaster will close permanently after several lawsuits alleged that over 100 riders sustained brain injuries while riding the attraction. [src: (BBC)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Moroccan general election
- King Mohammed VI appoints Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as the first female prime minister of Morocco after her victory in the general elections on 23 September. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Reuters)]
Science and technology
- Scientists identify and name a new penguin species, the southeastern gentoo penguin (Pygoscelis kerguelensis), in the Kerguelen Islands near Antarctica. Previously classfied as a standard gentoo penguin due to its nearly identical appearance, it is now differentiated through genetic sequencing. [src: (BBC News)]
Sports
- 2026 Asian Games
- Badminton at the 2026 Asian Games, South Korea at the 2026 Asian Games
- In badminton, South Korea's An Se-young wins the women's singles gold medal at the 2026 Asian Games, becoming the first woman to win two singles titles and the first to defend the title, defeating Japan's Akane Yamaguchi 21–17, 21–9. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- Manchester City F.C. financial breaches scandal
- In association football, an independent Premier League commission finds Manchester City guilty of almost all 115-plus financial charges, including inflating revenue by more than £900 million (US$1.19 billion) and failing to cooperate with the investigation. [src: (AP)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 3
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war, United Arab Emirates in the 2026 Iran war
- Iran's military launches drones and missiles on Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base in Kuwait and Al Minhad Air Base in the United Arab Emirates, targeting United States military facilities and equipment to retaliate for the recent U.S. bombardment of Iran that killed at least 19 people. [src: (AFP via South China Morning Post)]
- 2026 Kuhestak wedding airstrike
- U.S. vice president JD Vance says that the country will investigate its military strike against a wedding in Bandar Sirik that killed five people. [src: (Middle East Eye)] [src: (The Jerusalem Post)]
- 2026 Lebanon war
- 2026 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire
- Israel releases prisoner Malek Ghazi and hands him over to the Lebanese army, the first release since the war started in March, as part of an effort to revive peace talks. [src: (AP)] [src: (Arab News)]
- Yemeni civil war
- 2026 Yemen offensive
- The Houthis launch an offensive in western Yemen, clashing with the Yemeni Armed Forces and aiming to reach and cut the road linking Taiz to Al-Makha district. Fourteen balistic missiles and several drones are launched in Taiz and Hodeidah. At least 18 Houthi fighters and 13 government troops are killed in the clashes. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Russo–Ukrainian war
- Kharkiv Oblast campaign
- Russian forces say they have captured several settlements in northeastern Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine, encircling Ukrainian forces. [src: (ISW)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Sudanese refugee crisis
- The International Organization for Migration reports the first operation of a voluntary repatriation flight for stranded migrants in Khartoum, Sudan, since the war started three years ago. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Colombian conflict
- A Colombian judge orders president Abelardo de la Espriella's government to suspend airstrikes on guerrilla camps in the Guaviare Department when intelligence indicated that minors may be present, after recent bombings killed at least three teenagers. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Insurgency in Cabo Delgado
- At least one person is killed and no less than 11 people are abducted by ISM militants in an attack on a hunting camp in Niassa Province, Mozambique. [src: (AP)]
- Nigerian bandit conflict
- Five people are killed and several other residents are abducted during a bandit attack in Kebbe, Sokoto State, Nigeria. [src: (Daily Post Nigeria)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Indonesia wildfires
- 2026 East Malaysia haze, Endangerment of orangutans
- Authorities in Indonesia rescue a mother orangutan and her baby from wildfire smoke on the island of Borneo. [src: (AFP via RFI)] [src: (The Borneo Post)]
- 2026 Nepal–Tibet floods
- United Arab Emirates president Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan announces that the country will deploy an emergency relief mission to Nepal to support people affected by the deadly floods and landslides. [src: (Gulf News)]
- At least 37 people are killed after inhaling petroleum fumes while allegedly siphoning fuel from an illegally tapped pipeline in Rivers State, Nigeria. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Six crew members are referred to court as part of the investigation into the ship collision in the Sea of Marmara yesterday, while the search continues for the ten Turkish crew members aboard the sunken MV Tuğberk İmamoğlu cargo ship. [src: (BBC News)]
Health and environment
- 2026 East Malaysia haze
- Malaysia's disaster agency, meteorological agency, and air force launch cloud-seeding operations in Sarawak to reduce haze and increase water reserves. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
International relations
- Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
- Syrian chemical weapons program, Use of chemical weapons in the Syrian civil war
- Officials at a United Nations Security Council meeting say that Syria has started the process of destroying clandestine chemical weapons from former president Bashar al-Assad's regime. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Germany–Russia relations
- 2026 Leipzig Airport drone incidents
- Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov says that Russia will close Goethe-Institut cultural centers in Moscow, Saint Petersburg, and Yekaterinburg in response to Germany closing Russia's consulate in Bonn and the Russian House in Berlin following the drone attacks at Leipzig/Halle Airport last month. [src: (AP)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Tacloban school shooting, 2026 Ateneo de Zamboanga University shooting
- The Philippine education department initiates nationwide school safety drills to prepare students and staff for armed intruders, involving police and emergency responders after two school shooting incidents. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- A court in Moscow, Russia, places children's hospice founder Lida Moniava under judicial supervision, imposing a nightly curfew, internet ban, and contact restrictions over a 2023 post prosecutors said spread false information about the military. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Politics and elections
- 2025–2026 United States redistricting
- In the United States, the Supreme Court of Missouri blocks the use of a congressional map intended to favor Republicans, despite the map having already been used for primary elections in the state. A referendum on the 2025 map will appear on the ballot for the November election in the state. [src: (AP)] [src: (The Guardian)]
Science and technology
- AI boom
- OpenAI releases GPT-6 Astra, the latest version of ChatGPT. [src: (AFP via ABS-CBN News)] [src: (Axios)]
- 2026 in spaceflight
- The BepiColombo begins its final mission to Mercury, eight years after its launch by the European Space Agency and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency. [src: (Space.com)]
- NASA discovers a 10–sided pattern on the south pole of Saturn using its Hubble Space Telescope from the Goddard Space Flight Center in Maryland, United States. [src: (The Peninsula)] [src: (ScienceDaily)]
- Ig Nobel Prize
- The 36th Ig Nobel Prize ceremony is held in Zürich, Switzerland. The ceremony, normally held in the Greater Boston area, was the first held outside the United States due to due to safety concerns about international visitors entering the country. [src: (Ars Technica)]
Sports
- In association football, the French Football Federation upholds Bordeaux's relegation to Régional 1, the sixth tier of the French football league system, rejecting the club's request for reinstatement in National 2 following its exclusion from national competitions over financial concerns. [src: (AFP via France 24)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 30
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Iraqi conflict
- Withdrawal of United States troops from Iraq
- American troops complete their withdrawal from Iraq, ending their 23-year presence in the country that started with the 2003 U.S. invasion, and also the 12-year U.S. intervention against the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria. [src: (AP)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir
- Hashim Moosa, a top Lashkar-e-Taiba commander and the mastermind of the 2025 Pahalgam attack is killed in an encounter with security forces in Budgam, Jammu and Kashmir.[src: (The New Indian Express)]
- Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
- Unknown gunmen open fire against a bus carrying employees returning home from work in Homs, Syria, killing seven people and wounding four more. [src: (Middle East Eye)]
Business and economy
- Proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance
- A United States federal judge approves media conglomerate Paramount Skydance's settlement with 12 states that challenged its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on antitrust grounds, allowing the $81 billion merger to proceed toward completion. [src: (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]
Disasters and accidents
- A helicopter crashes in Marondera, Zimbabwe, killing all six people on board, including businessman Wicknell Chivayo and his wife. [src: (AFP via Daily Sun)] [src: (The Citizen)]
- Seven workers are killed in a gas incident inside a mining tunnel in Itogon, Benguet, Philippines. [src: (Manila Bulletin)]
Law and crime
- Capital punishment in the United States
- Capital punishment in Tennessee
- The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit halts Christa Pike's execution in Tennessee shortly before it was scheduled, to allow for further review of whether evidence of childhood sexual abuse was adequately considered at sentencing; the U.S. Supreme Court shortly after lifts the Sixth Circuit's stay order, allowing the execution to proceed. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Turkish LGBTQ raids, Censorship in Turkey, Censorship of LGBTQ issues
- A Turkish court orders the closure of independent news website T24 and its social media accounts after the justice ministry reported that T24 had published 118 items during the previous year which the court classified as "LGBTQ propaganda". [src: (AFP via RTL Today)]
- Flydubai Flight 1073
- A Flydubai flight from Dubai, United Arab Emirates, to Tel Aviv, Israel, is landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, by a relief crew after the copilot violently attacked the captain in an attempted aircraft hijacking. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (CNN)]
- Bolivian police arrest attorney general Roger Mariaca and Santa Cruz de la Sierra prosecutor Alberto Zeballos after the U.S. State Department accused them of corruption and links to drug trafficking. Police also raid prosecutors' offices in several cities. [src: (AFP)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Romanian political crisis
- Romania's parliament rejects prime minister-designate Siegfried Mureșan's proposed government, receiving 182 of the 233 votes required for approval, prolonging the political crisis that began after Ilie Bolojan's government fell in May. [src: (AFP)] [src: (AP)]
- 2026 French lycée protests
- At least 450 people are arrested and 76 people are injured after students in France protest over class overcrowding and teacher shortages. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (The New York Times)]
- Temukisa Auina Penehuro Hauma is sworn in as the first woman Governor-General of Tuvalu. [src: (RNZ)]
Science and technology
- AI boom
- The Tokyo District Court rules that a person's voice can receive protection under publicity rights, in Japan's first case involving alleged audio deepfake, while dismissing actor Kenjiro Tsuda's request to remove already-deleted TikTok videos. [src: (AFP via France 24)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 4
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Gaza war
- Aftermath of the Battle of Sufa
- The Israel Defense Forces state that Mohammad Mahmoud Marshad al-Qadi, a Nukhba Force commander who participated in the October 7 attacks on the Sufa post, was killed in an airstrike in Khan Yunis, Gaza Strip. [src: (The Times of Israel)]
- 2026 Lebanon war
- 2026 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire
- Israel frees four prisoners, including two Syrian citizens, via International Committee of the Red Cross as part of efforts to revive U.S.-backed peace talks signed between Israel and Lebanon. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (The Hill)]
- Yemeni civil war
- 2026 Yemen offensive
- Over 120 people are confirmed to have been killed since yesterday during the clashes between Houthis and the Yemeni Armed Forces in western Yemen. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Kyiv strikes
- A Russian drone strikes the Security Service of Ukraine (SSU) headquarters in central Kyiv, injuring five people. Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy says the attack targeted acting SSU head Oleksandr Poklad, who was unharmed. [src: (CNN)]
- Colombian conflict
- At least three soldiers are killed and four are wounded by explosives dropped from drones in Ocaña, Norte de Santander, Colombia. Local authorities blame the attack on the National Liberation Army. [src: (AP)]
- Insurgency in Balochistan
- The Pakistani military says it has killed 48 Baloch separatists in a series of raids on hideouts over the past 72 hours in Balochistan, Pakistan. [src: (AP)]
- Kidnapping in Nigeria
- Nine people, including five Department of State Services personnel, are killed during a security operation to rescue kidnapped victims in Oyo State, Nigeria. [src: (Vanguard)]
Arts and culture
- An Argentine judge orders the repatriation of Giacomo Ceruti's 18th-century painting Portrait of a Lady, looted by Nazi Germany from Dutch Jewish art dealer Jacques Goudstikker during World War II, to Goudstikker's daughter-in-law Marei von Saher. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Business and economy
- Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
- The American Automobile Association reports that the average U.S. diesel price reached a record $5.85 per gallon, up from $3.71 a year earlier, amid disruptions to global energy markets caused by the Iran war. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- 2026 European drought, 2026 European heatwaves
- France allocates more than €1 billion to support farms affected by drought and heatwaves, including compensation for crop losses, liquidity assistance, tax relief, and support for fertilizer and agricultural diesel costs. [src: (The Peninsula)]
- Tajikistan's capital Dushanbe begins construction on the 340-meter-high Dushanbe Tower, which is set to become the tallest building in Central Asia. President Emomali Rahmon and Mayor Rustami Emomali lay the building's foundation stone. [src: (Asia-News)] [src: (Caspian Post)] [src: (The Gulf Observer)]
- The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opens an investigation into whether Tesla's new Cybercab robotaxi models are properly certified and demonstrate compliance with motor vehicle safety standards. [src: (Reuters)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Nepal–Tibet floods
- The Nepali Army rescues two people from a tunnel at the Upper Trishuli 3A Hydropower Station in Rasuwa District, a week after floods ravaged the country. [src: (NBC News)]
- Around 22 people are killed in a blaze of unknown origin at a wedding party in Lingwala, Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo. [src: (AP)]
- At least two people are killed, 62 others sustain injuries, and 14 others remain unaccounted for after a blast at a military base storing pyrotechnic material in Viacha, Bolivia. [src: (Reuters)]
Health and environment
- 2026 East Malaysia haze
- Malaysia declares a state of emergency in Serian Division, Sarawak, after haze from wildfires in nearby Kalimantan, Indonesia, pushed air pollution above hazardous levels, closing 647 schools. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- The Democratic Republic of the Congo issues an updated 180-day response to the Ebola outbreak in the country. [src: (Xinhua)]
- New Zealand becomes the second country after Australia to authorize pharmaceutical-grade MDMA for severe post-traumatic stress disorder, with Medsafe allowing two psychiatrists to prescribe it alongside psychotherapy in controlled clinical settings. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
International relations
- Cambodia–United States relations
- The Royal Cambodian Army announces that they will resume joint military exercises with the United States beginning in February 2027 after they were suspended in 2017. The exercise will be codenamed Exercise Angkor Sentinel. [src: (AP)]
- The United Nations General Assembly adopts a resolution supporting the Equal Earth map projection over the Mercator projection, with 164 countries voting in favor, one against (United States), and six abstaining. [src: (The Guardian)]
- European Union enlargement chief Marta Kos cancels a visit to Serbia after a Serbian government plane took the remains of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladić to Belgrade for his funeral. [src: (AP)] [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- Killing of the Clancy children
- In the United States, Massachusetts Superior Court associate justice William F. Sullivan declares a mistrial in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial after jurors were deadlocked following more than 38 hours of deliberations, with the panel split 11–1. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- Mexican drug war
- Mexico's navy, the attorney general, and the Secretariat of Security and Citizen Protection seize approximately 16.8 tonnes of methamphetamine and dismantle three clandestine drug laboratories in Sinaloa. [src: (AFP via Arab News)]
- Mexican federal deputy Zenyazen Escobar García is found dead inside his vehicle in his home state of Veracruz with at least one gunshot wound. State prosecutors open an investigation without determining whether his death is suicide or homicide. [src: (AFP via The Manila Times)]
- A Philippine regional trial court issues an arrest warrant for vice president Sara Duterte on three counts of grave threats against president Bongbong Marcos, first lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and former House speaker Martin Romualdez, setting bail at ₱120,000 (US$2,000) per count. [src: (Reuters)]
- Police in Guangxi, China, arrest 52 Singaporeans over suspected involvement in illegal pyramid-scheme activities as part of a broader law-enforcement operation. Singapore's foreign ministry says it is providing consular assistance. [src: (Reuters)]
- Sri Lankan MP Namal Rajapaksa is arrested over alleged corruption involving SriLankan Airlines' 2013 Airbus purchases. A court in Colombo remands him until September 18. [src: (Reuters)]
- A Tunisian judge orders journalist Mohamed Ali Yousfi detained on allegations of illicit enrichment, money laundering, and conspiracy after police arrest him outside Express FM in Tunis. [src: (DW)]
Politics and elections
- Meloni government
- Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government becomes the longest serving in Italy during the postwar era. [src: (DW)]
- The remains of King Rukidi IV of the Tooro Kingdom return to Uganda for his burial. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Reuters)]
Sports
- 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup
- The opening ceremony for the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup is held in Berlin, Germany, with the defending champions United States defeating China 94–61. [src: (AP)]
- Palestinian sports during the Gaza war
- Palestinian football resumes after nearly three years due to the Gaza war, with the Palestinian Football Association launching a tournament involving more than 200 teams from refugee camps. [src: (AFP via France 24)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 5
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war, United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russia and Ukraine agree to halt strikes on Kyiv and Moscow, respectively, during United States-mediated peace talks, as U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff meet Russian president Vladimir Putin in Moscow before traveling to Kyiv. [src: (AFP via Dawn)]
- Kyiv strikes
- A Russian missile strike kills two people and damages multiple residential buildings in Bucha, Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine. [src: (UA News)]
- Russian occupation of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast
- A Russian airstrike on Kamianske, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Ukraine, kills four people and injures five others, including one critically, according to Dnipropetrovsk governor Oleksandr Hanza. [src: (SANA)]
- 2026 Iran war
- The United States Central Command says its forces have destroyed three Iranian oil tankers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, including one in the Gulf of Oman, after alleged Iranian missile attacks on U.S. naval vessels. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (BBC News)]
- Mexican drug war
- Two federal agents are killed in a shootout with an armed group in Omealca, Veracruz, Mexico. [src: (Demócrata)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Pacific typhoon season
- Typhoon Saudel
- One person is killed and eleven others are reported missing after a mudslide buries a village and damages 12 homes in Suichuan County, Jiangxi, China. [src: (AP)]
- 2026 Indonesia wildfires
- Indonesia's disaster agency and air force conduct aerial firefighting operations to contain wildfires near the planned capital Nusantara in East Kalimantan, following a request from the Nusantara Capital City Authority. [src: (AFP via Philippine Daily Inquirer)]
- Cape Verde bus crash
- Twenty-five people are killed and several others are injured after a bus carrying mostly secondary school students plunges down a slope in Fogo island, Cape Verde. [src: (AP)]
- Ten people are killed and 64 others are injured after an accidental fireworks explosion during a religious celebration in a parish in Temascalcingo, Mexico. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Ten people are killed and six others are injured after a tank truck suffers a brake failure and explodes on the Hamedan–Sanandaj highway, Iran. [src: (AFP via The Star)]
- A Greek F-4 Phantom jet crashes during an air show at Tanagra Air Base near Athens, Greece, killing both pilots. [src: (Reuters)]
- A five-story hostel building collapses in New Delhi, India, killing seven people. At least 12 people are rescued from the rubble. [src: (AP)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Ebola epidemic
- Uganda's health ministry bans mourners from the Democratic Republic of the Congo from attending the burial ceremony of the late Tooro Kingdom king Rukidi IV amidst the Ebola outbreak. [src: (The Independent Uganda)] [src: (Uganda Mirror)]
- Tens of thousands of people rally in Zagreb, Croatia, demanding the removal of about 37,000 tonnes of illegally dumped hazardous waste from Gospić and a ban on waste imports amid concerns over soil and groundwater contamination. [src: (AP)]
- The National Food Agency of Indonesia reports that nearly 2,000 people, mostly students, have fallen ill across the country this week in suspected food poisoning outbreaks linked to president Prabowo Subianto's new Free Nutritious Meals program. [src: (AP)]
International relations
- The 128 parties to the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons agree on a non-binding text defining lethal autonomous weapons systems, potentially enabling negotiations on international rules governing their use. [src: (Reuters)]
Law and crime
- Peruvian security crisis
- Peru declares a 60-day state of emergency in five supermax prisons, authorizing police and military forces to control the facilities and surrounding airspace and communications to disrupt criminal organizations operating from prisons. [src: (Reuters)]
- United Kingdom anti-immigration protests
- Hundreds of masked anti-immigration protesters block the Port of Dover in Kent, England, and chant "stop the boats", causing massive disruption to traffic and train services. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (CNN)]
- Philippine vice president Sara Duterte posts ₱360,000 (US$5,740) bail on three counts of grave threats, prompting a regional trial court to lift her arrest warrant. The charges concern alleged threats against president Bongbong Marcos, first lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and former House speaker Martin Romualdez. [src: (AP)]
- In Egypt, twelve people are sentenced to death for drugs trafficking, including television presenter Sarah Khalifa. [src: (AFP via ABC News Australia)]
Sports
- 2026 Formula One World Championship
- 2026 Italian Grand Prix
- In Formula One, Aston Martin driver Lance Stroll becomes the first driver to be knocked out in Q1 100 times after doing so at the 2026 Italian Grand Prix. [src: (Motorsport)]
- At the same Grand Prix, Alpine driver Pierre Gasly achieves his maiden pole position after qualifying first, the first French driver to do so since Jean Alesi in 1997. [src: (F1)] [src: (USA Today)]
- 2026 Diamond League
- 2026 Memorial Van Damme
- In track and field, Swiss athlete Audrey Werro wins the women's 800 metres at the Diamond League's Memorial Van Damme in Brussels, Belgium, with a meeting record of 1:54.75. [src: (Athletics Weekly)]
- 2026 China GT Championship
- Dutch Loek Hartog rescues fellow driver from a burning car following an accident at the Shanghai International Circuit. [src: (Motorsport Network)]
- 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup
- In women's basketball, the Mali women's national basketball team upsets Spain 82-73, making it Mali's second ever victory in the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup after its 2010 victory against Senegal. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (ESPN)]
- 2026 MLS season
- In association football, Major League Soccer's Columbus Crew wins their 400th game in franchise history. [src: (The Columbus Dispatch)] [src: (Our Sports Central)]
- In women's boxing, Katie Taylor retires as the undisputed super lightweight champion after defeating previously unbeaten Flora Pili by unanimous decision before a crowd of 83,000 at Croke Park in Dublin. [src: (ESPN)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 6
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Gaza war
- Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip
- Israeli strikes in Gaza City kill at least four Palestinians, including an eight-year-old girl and a three-year-old boy, and injure six others. Israel says one strike targeted a Hamas member and that it is reviewing the outcome. [src: (Reuters)]
- Hezbollah–Israeli conflict
- Seven people are killed and 20 more injured in a series of Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon. [src: (Al Jazeera 1)] [src: (Al Jazeera 2)] 
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war, United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war
- U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner make their first visit to Kyiv, Ukraine, to meet with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy for talks amidst renewed efforts to end the war. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (CNBC)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- The Sudanese Armed Forces and Joint Forces advance in Sudan's North Kordofan state, and recaptures the town of Hamrat al-Wiz. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- The International Committee of the Red Cross reports that over 11,000 people have been reported missing since the civil war. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
Arts and culture
- 78th Primetime Emmy Awards
- 78th Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards
- Rob Reiner wins a posthumous award for Outstanding Guest Actor in a Comedy Series for his role in The Bear nine months after his killing. [src: (The New York Times)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Pacific hurricane season
- A state of emergency is declared in Hawaii, United States, as Hurricane Lowell approaches the state as a Category 3 storm, with heavy rain, high surf, and dangerous coastal conditions forecasted. Tropical storm warnings are issued for Kauaʻi and Niʻihau. [src: (The Guardian)]
- 2026 Pacific typhoon season
- The death toll from mudslides caused by Typhoon Saudel in Suichuan County, Jiangxi, China, increases to three. [src: (AP)]
- 21 Air Flight 7598
- A Boeing 767-300 cargo plane operated by 21 Air, contracted by Amazon Air, overshoots the runway and strikes vehicles while landing at Miami International Airport in Florida, United States, killing five people and injuring five others. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (The New York Times)]
- Eleven people are killed and seven others are injured when a fuel tanker hits other cars and explodes, reportedly due to a faulty brake system, near Sanandaj, Kurdistan province, Iran. [src: (AP)]
- Eleven climbers are killed and six others are injured after an avalanche struck a group of 33 on Mount Mizhirgi in Kabardino-Balkaria, Russia. Six other climbers are missing as rescuers continue search operations. [src: (Firstpost)]
- Jakarta's Soekarno–Hatta International Airport, Indonesia's busiest airport, suspends flight operations after volcanic ash from Anak Krakatoa reaches the airport. [src: (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]
Health and environment
- 2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak
- Three more children are reported to die from suspected measles in Bangladesh in the past 24 hours, bringing the total death toll to 997. [src: (The Daily Star)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Saxony-Anhalt state election
- Exit polls show the far-right Alternative for Germany party winning the Saxony-Anhalt state election in Germany but failing to secure an absolute majority of seats. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (The Guardian)]
Sports
- 2026 Formula One World Championship
- 2026 Italian Grand Prix
- In Formula One racing, Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli wins the Italian Grand Prix, becoming the first Italian driver in 60 years to win on home soil after Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966. [src: (Reuters)]
- 2026 Leagues Cup
- 2026 Leagues Cup final
- In association football, Toluca defeat Monterrey 2–0 in the final to claim their first Leagues Cup championship. [src: (USA Today)]
- 2026 NASCAR Cup Series
- 2026 Cook Out Southern 500
- In NASCAR racing, Joe Gibbs driver Christopher Bell wins the Southern 500 race at Darlington Raceway in South Carolina, U.S., snapping a 33-race winless streak. [src: (ESPN)]
- 2026 World Nomad Games
- The final day of the World Nomad Games is held, with hosts Kyrgyzstan defeating Kazakhstan 12–0 to win the kok-boru final in Cholpon-Ata. Kyrgyzstan wins the gold medal in kok-boru, Kazakhstan wins the silver, and Russia wins the bronze. [src: (The Times of Central Asia)] [src: (24.kg)]
- Kazakhstan finishes first in the medal standings at the World Nomad Games. [src: (Qazinform)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 7
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
- Oman's navy says that they have rescued 16 crew members from a Saudi Arabia-flagged oil tanker SIDR that was attacked a week ago in the Strait of Hormuz. [src: (MENA via The New Arab)]
- Hezbollah–Israeli conflict
- 2026 Lebanon war, Israeli attacks on the Lebanese health sector during the Israel-Hezbollah conflict
- Nine people, including two children, are killed, and five others are injured in an Israeli airstrike on a residential building in Kfar Reman, Lebanon. Separately, in the same city, two medics are killed in another airstrike on a vehicle. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
- Ecuadorian conflict
- Operation Southern Spear, United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear
- The United States Southern Command says that they have sunk a vessel allegedly belonging to the Los Choneros. [src: (AP)]
- Yemeni civil war
- 2026 Yemen offensive
- More than 300 people are killed amid the deadliest fighting in the war since 2022. [src: (AFP via Barron's)]
- Amid the offensive, Saudi Arabia launches an airstrike against a prison in Al-Jawf Governorate, killing seven people, including a child, and trapping 35 more under the rubble. [src: (AP)]
Business and economy
- Tourism in Tokyo
- The government of Shinjuku, Tokyo, Japan, announces plans to prohibit more than half of its vacation rentals in residential areas and near schools after complaints increase over noise, smoking, trespassing, and improper waste disposal. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Disasters and accidents
- Eleven people, including six children, are killed in a fire at a fire at a market in Paniai, Central Papua, Indonesia. Forty kiosks and houses are destroyed. The causes are unknown. [src: (AFP via The Straits Times)]
- The death toll from an explosion at military barracks in Viacha, Bolivia, three days ago, increases to nine people. [src: (Reuters)]
- A private Piper PA-34-200T Seneca aircraft goes missing off Andros Island, the Bahamas, with four people on board. A search and rescue operation is ongoing. [src: (NBC News)]
- A PAC P-750 XSTOL aircraft operating a passenger flight for Niugini Aviation crashes near Simbai, Madang, Papua New Guinea, during approach. All four people on board are killed. [src: (ASN)]
Health and environment
- 2026 East Malaysia haze
- Malaysia lifts the state of emergency in Serian Division, Sarawak, after air pollution fell below hazardous levels, although several areas remain "very unhealthy" because of smoke from wildfires in Indonesia. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
International relations
- Greenland and the European Union
- European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen announces that Greenland and the European Union have reached a €200 million (US$232.5 million) partnership deal. [src: (Reuters)]
- North Korea–Russia relations
- North Korea and Russia opens the Yakov Novichenko Bridge at its border, the first road bridge connecting the two countries. [src: (DW)] [src: (The Independent)]
- Serbia–European Union relations
- A military funeral and burial is held for convicted war criminal Ratko Mladić in Belgrade, Serbia, despite objections from the European Union due to concerns that the honors glorify a person convicted of genocide and crimes against humanity. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (The Guardian)]
Law and crime
- Flood control projects scandal in the Philippines
- The Philippine Sandiganbayan appellate court issues an arrest warrant for Leyte's 1st district representative and former House speaker Martin Romualdez after the Office of the Ombudsman filed charges of plunder against him for the alleged ₱7.44 billion (US$118.62 million) worth of kickbacks he received from flood control, infrastructure, and other government projects. [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- Kenya grants temporary legal status to undocumented East African nationals who registered with their embassies, after president William Ruto ordered the closure of small businesses operated by foreign traders without work permits. [src: (Reuters)]
Sports
- In Australian rules football, the Australian Football League introduces limits on contact training from the 2027 preseason to reduce concussion risk, capping weekly contact at 120 minutes initially and 160 minutes later while prohibiting high-intensity sessions on consecutive days. [src: (AFP via France 24)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 8
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Yemeni civil war
- 2026 Yemen offensive, Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict
- September 2026 Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia
- Houthi forces launch ballistic missiles and drones at several locations in Saudi Arabia, injuring 73 people, including civilians, and causing fires that temporarily halt operations at some energy facilities. [src: (Reuters)]
- The confirmed toll of the offensive in western Yemen increases to 500 people killed, including 278 Houthi fighters, 216 soldiers of the Yemeni Armed Forces and 29 civilians. [src: (AFP via LBC Group)]
- The toll from yesterday's Saudi airstrike against a prison in Al-Jawf Governorate increases to 17 people killed and seven more wounded. [src: (Saba News Agency)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Kyiv strikes, Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russia launches drones and missiles at Kyiv, Ukraine, following a weekend pause in strikes, killing five people and injuring at least 10. The attacks damage civilian infrastructure at at least 16 locations and cause fires in five districts. [src: (The Pioneer)] [src: (Reuters)]
- Sudanese civil war
- Kordofan campaign
- Around 13 people are killed in a drone strike by the Rapid Support Forces on a courthouse in Umm Ruwaba, North Kordofan. [src: (Sudan Horizon)]
- Peace talks are held by mediators from the African Union, the Intergovernmental Authority on Development, the Arab League, the European Union and the United Nations, in Khartoum, Sudan, in an effort to end the three-year long civil war, with UN envoy Pekka Haavisto attending the talks. [src: (Arab News)]
Business and economy
- Canada–United States relations
- 2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico
- Canada's retaliatory tariffs of 15% to 50% on CA$27.6 billion (US$19.9 billion) of U.S. goods, including steel, dairy products, appliances, agricultural equipment, paper products, and electronics, take effect in response to U.S. tariffs on Canadian imports. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- In response, the United States announces a ban on the imports of Canadian alcoholic drinks, motorcycles, and dairy products beginning September 29. [src: (Reuters)]
- International sanctions against Iran
- United States sanctions against Iran, Economic D-Day
- The U.S. treasury department imposes sanctions against 27 Iranian airlines, including flag carrier Iran Air, in an effort to squeeze Iran's economy. [src: (Al-Monitor)]
Disasters and accidents
- 2026 Nepal–Tibet floods
- The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority reports that 13,583 people have been rescued so far since flash floods ravaged Nepal. [src: (The Rising Nepal)]
- A MBB Bo 105 helicopter operating for the Flying Doctors of Malaysia crashes near Long Lellang, Sarawak, Malaysia, killing all five onboard. [src: (Reuters)] [src: (The Star)]
- Indonesia reopens its airport in Jakarta and four others after previously being closed due to ashes from Anak Krakatoa. [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Health and environment
- 2026 North American heat wave
- A third-year student in the marching band at the University of Iowa in Iowa City, U.S., dies after collapsing during extreme heat at the Iowa Hawkeyes season opener at Kinnick Stadium. Temperatures reached at the time of the game. [src: (The Guardian)] [src: (The Athletic via The New York Times)]
- Famine in Sudan
- A famine is reported across Sudan's Jebel Marra area in the Darfur region, with 20 people dying from hunger and diseases. [src: (Sudan Tribune)]
- Health effects arising from the September 11 attacks
- Mayor Zohran Mamdani says that New York City, U.S., has released over 170,000 documents detailing that city officials knew about the air quality and unsafe conditions at the time of the September 11 attacks including at Ground Zero. [src: (CNN)] [src: (The Guardian)]
- Indonesia's food agency suspends nearly 2,000 kitchens in its national free meals programme after they fail to register for mandatory sanitation inspections, as the agency strengthens food safety measures following widespread food poisoning cases. [src: (Reuters)]
International relations
- Morocco–Spain relations
- 2026 Ceuta migrant crisis
- Spain declassifies around 40 intelligence reports concerning the July migrant crisis into Ceuta, during which more than 70,000 people crossed from Morocco, amid scrutiny of whether Moroccan security forces facilitated the crossings and whether Spanish security services had prior warning of the influx. [src: (AFP via RFI)]
- Israel–United Kingdom relations, Israeli occupation of the West Bank, Legality of Israeli settlements
- The United Kingdom announces it will ban imports of all goods from Israeli settlements in the West Bank, as well as some services, including financing, construction, infrastructure, real estate, and advertising. [src: (Telegraph India)]
- To reciprocate the UK sanctions, Israel announces it will close the UK consulate in East Jerusalem. Israel also forbids the UK from participating in the U.S.-led mission for Gaza, and bans some British officials, including former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn, from entering the country. [src: (The North West Star)]
- Bosnia and Herzegovina–Serbia relations
- Bosnia and Herzegovina declares two Serbian embassy diplomats, military attaché Milan Dulanović and Security Intelligence Agency representative advisor at the embassy Darko Maksimović, as personae non gratae after attending the funeral of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladić in Belgrade. [src: (Reuters)]
- Nicaragua v. Germany, German support for Israel in the Gaza war
- Nicaragua urges the International Court of Justice to reject Germany's objections to its case, stating that German arms exports to Israel breach the Genocide Convention and international humanitarian law. Germany responds by saying that the court lacks jurisdiction over parts of the case. [src: (AFP via France 24)] [src: (Al Jazeera)]
Law and crime
- 2026 Musée Renoir theft
- Thieves steal and by Pierre-Auguste Renoir from the in Cagnes-sur-Mer, Alpes-Maritimes, France. The works have an estimated value of €9 million. [src: (BBC News)]
Science and technology
- AI boom
- OpenAI says that it has solved the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize problem, with the announcement raising questions about plagiarism. [src: (BBC News)] [src: (Scientific American)]

title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 9
text:
Armed conflicts and attacks
- Middle Eastern crisis
- Yemeni civil war
- 2026 Yemen offensive, Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict
- September 2026 Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia
- Saudi Arabia launches 32 airstrikes in four governorates in Yemen against the Houthis. [src: (UA News)]
- The death toll from the Saudi airstrike against a prison in Al-Jawf Governorate, two days ago, increases to 23 people. [src: (AP)]
- Gaza war
- Aftermath of the Second Intifada
- Hamas claims that the Israel Defense Forces has killed Farah Hamed, a senior member who was accused of carrying out the 2003 attack that resulted in the killing of , the late husband of Limor Son Har-Melech, in a airstrike in the Gaza Strip. [src: (The Jerusalem Post)] [src: (Israel National News)] [src: (VINnews)]
- 2026 Iran war
- 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
- Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launch missiles at the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Azraq, Jordan, reporting damage to maintenance facilities, deployment areas, and hangars. Jordan says its forces have intercepted 18 Iranian missiles, following United States strikes that destroyed five Iranian oil tankers. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
- Operation Southern Spear
- United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear
- The United States Southern Command's Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere kills three people in a strike on an alleged narcotrafficking drug boat in the Caribbean Sea. [src: (Stars and Stripes)] [src: (SOUTHCOM)]
- Russo-Ukrainian war
- Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
- A Russian drone strike hits a shopping centre in Sumy, Ukraine, killing two people and injuring 20 others. [src: (Reuters)]
Arts and culture
- Death and state funeral of Harald V
- The state funeral of King Harald V takes place at the Oslo Cathedral in Oslo, Norway. [src: (CNN)] [src: (The New York Times)]
- The Tooro Kingdom in western Uganda selects Prince Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma, a television news anchor and editor, as its new monarch following the death of Rukidi IV last month. [src: (Reuters)]
Disasters and accidents
- MV June Aster ship fire
- Five people are killed and 87 others are reported missing when a fire breaks out aboard a passenger ferry off Coron, Palawan, Philippines. The coast guard rescues 42 people from the vessel, which carried 117 passengers and 17 crew members. [src: (AFP via The Straits Times)]
- Sokolniki Suche train collision
- A train collides with a truck at a level crossing in Sokolniki Suche, Poland, killing one person and injuring 20 others. [src: (TVP World)] [src: (Xinhua)]
- Fourteen people are killed and eleven others are injured in an explosion at a weapons depot in Sarmada, Syria. [src: (AP)]
- Two people are killed and extensive damage is caused after an explosion at a hydroelectric power station in Piotta, Ticino, Switzerland. [src: (Reuters)]
Health and environment
- 2026 heat waves
- 2026 European heatwaves
- Peninsular Spain records its hottest summer since the State Meteorological Agency's measurements began in 1961, with an average temperature of and 61 heatwave days from June through August. [src: (Arab News Pakistan)]
- 2026 North American heat wave
- The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration reports that the United States has experienced its hottest summer on record from June to August with a , surpassing the Dust Bowl. [src: (Al Jazeera)] [src: (CBS News)]
- The Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) reports that August 2026 is the hottest month globally since measurements began, with an average temperature of , exceeding the previous record set in July 2023. [src: (AP)]
- 2026 Indonesia wildfires
- The C3S reports that wildfires in Kalimantan and Sumatra, Indonesia, produced more than 19.7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions from September 1 to 7, the world's highest total and more than one-third of global fire emissions. [src: (Reuters)]
- Sudanese cholera epidemic
- The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs announces that a 10-day cholera vaccination campaign has been launched in Tawila, North Darfur in a effort to immunize 95,000 people in the area. Additionally, 16 deaths are reported from cholera in Sudan's West Kordofan state. [src: (Sudan Tribune)] [src: (Radio Dabanga)] [src: (AllAfrica)]
International relations
- Israel–Slovenia relations
- Israel opens its first embassy in Ljubljana, Slovenia. [src: (AP)]
- Syria and weapons of mass destruction
- The International Atomic Energy Agency ends its investigation into Syria's nuclear activities after the new government granted inspectors access to nuclear sites. Its board terminates a 2011 resolution that found Syria in non-compliance with its nuclear safeguards obligations. [src: (AFP via France 24)]
Law and crime
- Reform UK financial allegations
- The Metropolitan Police launch a criminal investigation into Reform UK over allegations that it broke foreign funding laws in the United Kingdom, following an investigation by Channel 4 News. [src: (AP)] [src: (BBC News)]
- Brazilian Supreme Court president Edson Fachin suspends conflicting rulings by two justices, allowing Federal Police chief Andrei Rodrigues to remain in office while the court reviews allegations that police monitored justice André Mendonça and other government authorities. [src: (Reuters)]
Politics and elections
- 2026 Serbian parliamentary election
- Serbian president Aleksandar Vučić dissolves the National Assembly and calls a snap parliamentary election for October 25, following a government proposal amid prolonged political tensions. The ruling Serbian Progressive Party nominates Vučić as its lead candidate and candidate for prime minister. [src: (Xinhua)]
Science and technology
- 2026 in archosaur paleontology
- Scientists at the Denver Museum of Nature and Science in Colorado, U.S., and Liverpool John Moores University in England discover the first adult Tyrannosaurus trackway at Hell Creek Formation in North Dakota, U.S. The study is published in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology. [src: (Phys.org)] [src: (Axios)]
